description: Derived release contract: names, members, constraints, presence, enum ownership, encoding, units, ordering, open slots and canonical/signature bindings.

contract.description: Decrypted plaintext value of the holder-private ak.account.blocklist account-data key. It is written only through ak.account_data.set as an encrypted value; the whole-value replacement uses that write's expected_server_revision CAS and the value carries no revision of its own. Omitting an entry in the next value removes it, and entries=[] clears the list. It never enters shared Realm state or federation payloads.

entry_id.description: Blocklist entry identity. This is the registered ak:block:<uuidv7> typed id of id-kind-registry.json, not a document-local symbol: the wire form owns the ak: namespace, so common-fields.md 2.1 classifies it as typed_object_id and the terminal MUST pin that form.

mode.description: block denies a new holder-facing interaction on the selected surfaces and filters shared durable content only after canonical receive/store; mute keeps content visible but suppresses attention surfaces; hide keeps canonical content but omits it from default holder rendering/search. None of the modes revokes a Realm capability or rewrites shared history.

contract.description: Principal-private Account Data value committed client-side. Services validate and store this envelope but never receive the account secret or plaintext.

Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface actor-private account_data operations (ak.self.account_data.*). PUT builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write; the server stores content verbatim (clients own canonical encoding and, for sensitive keys, client-side encryption). Every key is a server-versioned compare-and-set whole-value register: writes carry expected_server_revision and the accepted revision is expected_server_revision + 1, so concurrent multi-device writes converge instead of silently overwriting each other. See spec/v1/zh/models/account-data.md §5. account_data_key keys are dot-delimited namespaces validated against account-data-key-registry.json.

account_data_key.description: Dot-delimited account_data namespace key (e.g. ak.contacts.realm.<realm_id>, ak.account.blocklist). Control chars / whitespace / path separators are forbidden so the key is URL- and log-safe.

revision.description: Monotonic per-key revision counter. 0 means the key has never been written. Each accepted write or delete stores expected_server_revision + 1. The counter is a high-water mark: it MUST NOT go backwards, not even after a tombstone is garbage-collected, so a stale offline write can never resurrect a superseded value.
Revision of this stored value. Pass it back as expected_server_revision inside the caller-signed ak.account_data.set payload to replace or delete the entry.

content.description: Caller-supplied opaque payload, stored verbatim. Any JSON value.

account_data_replace_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.account_data.set Event and nothing else. The actor-private current state subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so the subject *is* the owner: the Event MUST be signed by the holder and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. key, expected_server_revision, and body / encrypted_payload live exclusively in set_event.event.payload and MUST NOT appear at the request top level. A tombstone payload is rejected here: erasure goes through ak.self.account_data.resource.delete.v1, which enforces the registered deletion_mode.

account_data_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event and nothing else. Same subject rule as the replace body: composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key] makes the holder the only legal signer. expected_server_revision is the payload's, not a query parameter -- one CAS precondition, one place. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused on this endpoint.

revision.description: Revision of the stored tombstone (expected_server_revision + 1). Recreating the key requires this value as the next expected_server_revision.

account_data_cas_conflict_details.description: Closed error.details payload for cas_conflict and not_found on ak.self.account_data.resource.*. It always carries the current revision so the caller can decrypt, re-apply its domain merge rule and issue exactly one new compare-and-set write without a second round trip.

current_entry.description: Present only when the key currently holds a live value. Omitted when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; current_revision is still authoritative in that case.

contract.description: Immutable Human account_device evidence for the existing directory/current-query contract. The authority_forward sibling in $defs alone also supports accepted Applet-managed real Account Devices, with its independent Event-bound original source. Neither branch adds a member to AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence. signer_evidence_ref is SHA-256(RFC 8785 JCS of the complete object). Conformance vector ak.vector.device.account_device_signer_evidence.v1 checks the exact closure and negative mutations.

forward_account_device_signer_evidence.description: authority_forward-only complete original Station closure for Human or accepted Applet-managed real Account Devices, independently proven from accepted PCR purpose and original authorization. Never appears in current keys/query or peer directory; not an Agent, Service, controller or native authorization source.

contract.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations and Account Authority issuer-ledger account-status publication and resolution.

account_subject.description: Deployment-local, non-reversible authentication subject: SHA-256 over utf8('ak.account-subject.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of the issuer identity and issuer-local authentication row key. It is confined to the private Account Authority boundary, is always issuer-scoped, and is never an AccountId or resource-owner selector.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the holder key, encoded base64url without padding.

status.description: Lifecycle projection only, matching device-lifecycle.md section 14.1. revocation_pending is authority-derived from a durable accepted ak.device.revoke security transaction; trust/evidence quality is reported separately in verification_state.

verification_state.description: Trust verification of the device authorization evidence, separate from lifecycle status. A consumer MUST NOT interpret lifecycle status=active as usable authority unless verification_state=verified.

verification_source.description: Closed provenance of the verification checkpoint behind verification_state, per device-lifecycle.md section 10.1. genesis is the PCR genesis first device, pairing_code an accepted-device pairing or re-verification ceremony, and recovery an accepted recovery unit replacement device. Login factors, SSO sessions, ordinary session grants and bare server projections MUST NOT mint a checkpoint. Required when verification_state is verified, retained when a previously verified checkpoint went stale, and absent when verification_state is unresolved.

revocation_states.description: All gate-relevant durable revoke records for the exact device/generation, sorted by acceptance_sequence and Event id. At most 128 distinct unresolved transactions may be admitted; exact replay consumes no slot, a terminal rejected result removes one pending slot, and an already revoked generation accepts no new transaction. Committing one record makes lifecycle status revoked but MUST NOT hide other surviving pending records.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

audience_id.description: Stable target-service authorization identity. A service DID used for signature verification is supplied separately and MUST project to this did_core_id.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

account_registration_control_proof.description: Fresh current-control authorization for complete published-DID account registration. It is valid only with published_identity. The request_canonical_digest binds that complete branch, including its lease/fence, full anchor, evidence draft, ordered genesis and initial session. The signature is UTF8(ak.account_registration_control_proof.v1 followed by LF) followed by RFC8785_JCS of this complete object with only signature omitted. No method-derived field is injected into the signed object. The verified terminal active update key signs; the verifier independently checks high-tier currentness at challenge and first registration admission. The explicit anchor/genesis/session/lease fields are reconstructed from the frozen published_identity request and separately compared at Station PCR admission; request_canonical_digest does not substitute for these bindings.

request_canonical_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete account_register_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

account_subject.description: Service account subject this identity is being bound to. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed to bind the same identity to a different account.

principal_id.description: Stable did_core_id echoed by the challenge and equal to project(did).

did.description: Complete DID resolved by the Account Authority and signed by the holder; it MUST equal the register request did byte-for-byte.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined versionId of the entry whose current active update key signed this proof.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the verified current active update key.

registration_anchor_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete principal_registration_anchor. The verifier recomputes it from the submitted anchor.

pcr_realm_id.description: Principal Control Realm id obtained only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id; it is not derived from principal_id and MUST equal the pcr_genesis_unit create Event's retyped id.

realm_create_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the ak.realm.create payload only. Event ids and envelope digests MUST NOT be added as separate proof members; the existing request_canonical_digest still commits the complete closed request.

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the founding ak.device.authorize payload only. Event ids and envelope digests MUST NOT be added as separate proof members; the existing request_canonical_digest still commits the complete closed request.

initial_session_request_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS InitialSessionGrantIntent. The embedded session_public_key MUST thumbprint to dpop_jkt; this binds the first Standard grant intent without turning it into a separate root-signed object.

dpop_jkt.description: DPoP holder thumbprint echoed by the durable challenge.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

verification_method.description: Exact control-key verification method derived from the validated terminal anchor entry, including a method-native did:key controller method when applicable. It is not a device key or a DID Document authentication/assertion method.

account_handoff_authentication_proof.description: OIDC authorization-code exchange proof used only to create a DPoP-bound account handoff. The signature is made by the same Ed25519 holder key as the request DPoP proof over utf8('ak.account_handoff_authentication_proof.v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS(this object with signature omitted).

challenge.description: Account Authority-generated challenge persisted with the OIDC authorization transaction and consumed by this exchange.

request_canonical_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete account_handoff_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 signature encoded base64url without padding.

reserved_identity_creation.description: Server-persisted identity-creation checkpoint, readable only by the authenticated current holder of the owning service account's identity-creation lease. It is NOT public: an unfinished reservation would otherwise leak that a specific account is mid-registration, and abandoning it would leave a permanent public trace. Once registration completes the public artifact is the published method-native anchor itself, so this checkpoint never needs to become public. It contains the exact unpublished or already-published registration anchor, never recovery words, seed material, private keys, or an encrypted root export.

binding_kind.description: Frozen reservation purpose. It cannot be switched by renewal, takeover, replay or abandonment.

registration_anchor_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete principal_registration_anchor object.

state.description: Account-Authority-authored durable identity-creation saga state. Clients MUST derive their onboarding phase from this value and MUST NOT infer a phase from local checkpoint presence. reserved_identity MUST be absent only in active and present in every later state. identity_creation uses did_published; published_did uses did_validated, meaning durable independent validation, never registry acceptance. These alternatives cannot be converted into one another.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

reserved_identity.description: Holder-authenticated identity-creation checkpoint carried while a reservation exists. It MUST be omitted once the provisional identity has been explicitly abandoned through ak.gate.account.command.abandon_identity_creation.v1: after abandonment the checkpoint MUST NOT remain readable on this or any other holder-readable surface, because leaving it would keep publishing that some account once tried to create an identity. That is a security property, not a cleanup policy.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the conflicting live identity-creation lease. The client uses this authenticated upper bound for waiting UI; it conveys no holder identity or authority.

account_handle.description: Canonical handle of the authenticated service account. This unsigned UX hint is only for display and local artifact naming; it MUST NOT be treated as principal identity evidence, authorization, or a service-account-to-principal binding.

account_subject.description: Stable subject for the authenticated service account. The client freezes this value from the DPoP-bound handoff and MUST require the identity-binding challenge to echo it byte-for-byte before signing.

preferred_locale.description: Optional private UI-language preference of the authenticated service account. It is returned only in this DPoP-bound handoff response so the client can continue the just-completed authentication flow in the selected language; it MUST NOT be copied into a public actor profile.

account_handoff_grant.description: Opaque, short-lived credential bound to the request DPoP key. It is not ak.session.grant and has no refresh-token semantics.

allowed_operations.description: Closed set of operations this handoff may be presented at. The abandonment command is a member because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can carry them. The device-pairing finalize command is a member for the mirror reason: a fresh device of an already bound account has no accepted-device signer yet, so this handoff is the only sender-constrained credential that can supply the exact AccountId its target proof must sign. Membership here does not widen the handoff into a session credential.

did.description: Complete standard DID whose registered method adapter MUST project to the principal_id the Account Authority derives from principal_registration_anchor.

identity_binding_challenge_response_body.description: Only fresh challenge material and domain separation. The authority durably retains the full request, account/handoff subject, lease/fence, DID operation and independently derived pins, PCR/genesis/session digests, audience/origin/trust-domain, and rechecks all of them atomically at registration. The client reconstructs the proof from its frozen submission and authenticated onboarding context.

pcr_genesis_unit_kinds.description: Closed ordered declaration copied into the identity-root creation transcript.

identity_creation_control_proof.description: Fresh proof signed by the WebVH registration root control key. The verifier derives that key from the accepted did:webvh entry's parameters.updateKeys[0] in principal_registration_anchor and MUST NOT treat a request-supplied key or a DID Document verificationMethod as authority. proof_kind is fixed to did_webvh_inception_update_key and MUST agree with anchor_kind=webvh_registration. The Ed25519 signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.identity_creation_control_proof.v1; signature_algorithm is part of those signed bytes.

proof_kind.description: Closed registration root-key derivation discriminator. v1 permits only did_webvh_inception_update_key paired with anchor_kind=webvh_registration.

registration_anchor_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete principal_registration_anchor. The verifier recomputes it from the submitted anchor.

pcr_realm_id.description: Principal Control Realm id obtained only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id; it is not derived from principal_id and MUST equal the pcr_genesis_unit create Event's retyped id.

realm_create_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the ak.realm.create payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the founding ak.device.authorize payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

initial_session_request_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS InitialSessionGrantRequest. The embedded session_public_key MUST thumbprint to dpop_jkt; this binds the first Standard grant intent without turning it into a separate root-signed object.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 identity-root signature encoded base64url without padding.

registration_did_evidence_draft.description: Dedicated registration-time control proof and frozen method evidence. It is distinct from identity_creation_control_proof, it is a receipt rather than primary material, and it MUST bind the exact coordinates re-derived from principal_registration_anchor.

binding_kind.description: Frozen registration branch: new DID publication or complete already-published DID account initialization.

did.description: Verified DID whose registered adapter projects to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined version identifier pinned when the account binding was accepted.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the verified current control key that authorized this binding.

identity_creation_lease_id.description: Required in both registration branches; identifies the account initialization lease/fence.

lease_fence.description: Required in both registration branches; identifies the account initialization lease/fence.

operation_status.description: identity_creation preserves the exact registry accepted/duplicate status. published_did uses accepted for the first durable validation acceptance and replays that same value; it never claims publication or invents a registry duplicate.

registration_anchor_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC8785 JCS of the exact complete typed anchor submitted and independently verified for the selected branch. The authenticated result must match the client frozen anchor.

proof.description: Account Authority detached proof. payload_digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete receipt with proof omitted, including binding_kind, principal_id, did, did_version_id, control_key_digest, registration_anchor_digest, and the account initialization lease/fence in both branches. JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.account_binding_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, account_authority_id, account_subject, principal_id, did, did_version_id, control_key_digest, verification_method, created_at}); proof.created_at MUST equal issued_at and verification_method MUST be an assertion method of account_authority_id valid at issued_at.

propertyNames.description: ak.self.account.command.update_profile.v1 only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

account_materialized_profile.description: Materialized Actor Profile returned on the account surface. id is the actor_profile ID derived by retyping the accepted ak.profile.create Event ID; realm_id is the exact Principal Control Realm that carries the profile Event lineage.

profile.description: Present only when the authenticated principal has exactly one unambiguous accepted Actor Profile across its account-local-lineage PCR lineages. Because this request has no authority selector, multiple accepted lineages MUST fail closed by omitting profile; the service MUST NOT choose an implicit current PCR.

is_server_admin.description: True when the authenticated principal is a deployment server administrator (the server's configured admin principal set). Operator-only product surfaces (e.g. organization creation) gate their UI on this. Reducer/config-derived, not a stored account field; absent or false means non-admin.

account_register_request_body.description: Complete Human account initialization. Exactly one closed branch: identity_creation, or proof together with published_identity. A proof alone is invalid. Both branches establish one account-local PCR, its founding device and initial Standard session under the same live account/holder/lease/fence. Repeated DID/principal coordinates must agree and project(did)=principal_id. Top-level device_id is forbidden; the device is bound inside the genesis descriptor and initial_session.

did.description: Required for both externally created and account-first identities. The server verifies the method evidence and project(did)=principal_id before persisting the PCR resolution state.

pcr_genesis_commits.description: Required two accepted genesis RealmCommits in registered order in either successful registration branch. No binding-only success exists.

preconditions.description: This account self-service surface forbids Event preconditions. ak.profile.update concurrency is expressed only by the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest.

account_profile_event_submission.description: Holder-signed ordinary Actor Profile Event. (event.actor_id, event.station_id) MUST equal the authenticated session's exact account authority pair, and event.realm_id MUST select that pair's local unique PCR lineage. Accepted-profile presence is evaluated only within that lineage. With no accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.create and its materialized actor_profile ID is derived by retyping event.event_id; the create payload MUST NOT carry id. With an accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.update and payload.target_ref MUST equal that accepted create-derived ID. On create payload.object.principal_id MUST equal event.actor_id; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id MUST equal it. Holder direct proof is required without executed_by, authorization_ref or Applet provenance. Event preconditions MUST be empty; update concurrency uses only the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service submits the exact bytes through authority Event submission and MUST NOT author, rebuild, co-sign, choose an ID or add a concurrency guard. Success exists only after the current PCR governance Station atomically accepts the Event, materializes the profile result and signs its RealmCommit; exact retry returns the stored outcome and the same Commit.

account_update_profile_request_body.description: Carries exactly one holder-signed profile create-or-update Event and no unsigned profile patch.

account_update_profile_response_body.description: Stored outcome after the profile Event is authority-committed and its effect is materialized. profile.id is the create-derived ActorProfile ID, profile.realm_id is event.realm_id, and an update projects updated_by/updated_at from event.actor_id/event.created_at. commit is the exact RealmCommit covering the submitted Event. Exact Event replay returns the byte-identical stored outcome and emits no second account-aggregate delta.

account_status_record.description: Immutable Account Authority issuer-ledger record. account_status_record_id is the suite-tagged full digest of RFC 8785 JCS over every field except account_status_record_id and proof. The proof uses context ak.account_status_record_proof.v1 over that same closed unsigned core. principal_control_realm_id is a verified account-binding coordinate only and is never a finality scope.

binding_version.description: Monotonic Account Authority-local account-to-principal binding generation.

issued_at.description: Account Authority signing time and historical-key lookup instant, not a scheduled activation time. Current status follows the atomically committed issuer-ledger head or the accepted monotonic replica head, irrespective of local wall clock. effective_at is forbidden, including equal, future or backdated values; receivers must reject it without writes, never strip it or reconstruct signed bytes.

account_status_publication.description: Constrained carrier for one exact AccountStatusRecord. Initial publication carries record only; downstream fanout carries the byte-identical record plus prior receiver receipts. No receiver rebuilds or re-signs the record.

account_status_receipt.description: Receiver-signed receipt proving durable monotonic replication of one exact AccountStatusRecord. It grants no authority. proof uses context ak.account_status_replication_receipt_proof.v1 and payload_digest over RFC 8785 JCS of every field except proof.

account_status_resolve_request_body.description: Service-authenticated bounded issuer-ledger range request used for freshness checks and predecessor-gap recovery. Unauthorized or unrelated callers receive the operation's non-enumerating authority outcome.

account_status_resolve_response_body.description: Contiguous Account Authority issuer-ledger range. Records are ordered by status_sequence, begin exactly at from_status_sequence when present, and retain the Account Authority's original bytes and proofs.

account_status_publication_response_body.description: Durable replica operation state. accepted/duplicate are terminal for this receiver and dependency_missing performs zero writes while identifying the exact next sequence required for gap recovery.

did.description: Complete standard DID whose registered method adapter MUST project to the principal_id the Account Authority derives from principal_registration_anchor.

did_binding_challenge_request_body.description: Freeze complete published-DID account initialization intent under the live lease/fence. The caller supplies the full anchor as primary material; the designated fact owner independently resolves the DID at high tier and requires the current verified head/key and exact anchor to agree. Caller history is never trusted as a resolution result. No registry write or PCR effect occurs here.

did_binding_challenge_response_body.description: Durable single-use published-DID challenge. Existing echoed identity/key/holder fields are compared with the frozen request and authenticated account context. The record additionally retains the entire request, lease/fence, anchor and PCR/genesis/initial-session digests. Register requires proof plus published_identity, rechecks currentness before first acceptance and freezes the exact outcome. No witness_evidence string substitutes for independently verified method-native witness/freshness.

account_subject.description: Service account subject that will own the binding. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed against another account.

did.description: Server-resolved did echoed into the signed proof transcript; it MUST project to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the entry the Account Authority resolved as current; the proof MUST be signed by that entry's active update key.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

identity_abandonment_request_body.description: Single explicit command using a fresh holder-bound account handoff grant. The authority MUST verify a successful authentication event later than the frozen reservation creation, not merely a refreshed token. Current account, lease/fence, holder binding and never-accepted PCR are rechecked atomically. Authentication strength and cooldown remain deployment governance.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the abandonment. Replaying it returns the recorded terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second orphan-anchor tombstone.

identity_abandonment_response_body.description: Exact terminal outcome of explicitly abandoning the frozen local registration reservation before any PCR acceptance. identity_creation retains the orphan-anchor rule. published_did cancels only this account initialization attempt and tombstones its request/challenge: it never deactivates, globally tombstones or makes the external DID unusable. Both suppress the old holder-readable checkpoint and release the lease atomically; unresolved PCR dispatch must be reconciled first.

principal_id.description: Principal of the abandoned local reservation. Only binding_kind=identity_creation has provisional orphan-anchor consequences; published_did retains its independent DID and may start a fresh authorized registration.

account_request_erasure_request_body.description: Record the authenticated account holder's explicit request to erase the account (ak.gate.account.command.request_erasure.v1; zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). The Account Authority accepts it directly on the gate surface; acceptance only records the intent and continues the Account Authority's existing erasure_pending issuance flow within the same service — it is neither the signed AccountStatusRecord nor a completion receipt. The Account Authority MUST treat this as a high-risk action and require fresh high-risk action authentication (recent login, WebAuthn, recovery key or a deployment equivalent), judged locally by the Account Authority; re-authentication strength, risk checks and cooldown are deployment governance.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the erasure request. Replaying it returns the recorded acceptance outcome and MUST NOT record a second intent; the same request_id with different canonical bytes is duplicate_conflict with zero writes. A different request_id while a live intent whose erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord is not yet signed exists is failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending.

account_request_erasure_response_body.description: Acceptance confirmation of a self-initiated account erasure request. At most one live intent record exists per account while the erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord is unsigned. This outcome proves only that the intent is durably recorded; it MUST NOT be read as record issuance or physical erasure completion. Completion is observed through the existing account-status read surface, and physical completion through the erasure receipt rail (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8).

principal_id.description: The authenticated principal whose account erasure intent was recorded.

recorded_at.description: Time the intent was durably recorded; an exact replay returns the first recording's value.

withdrawal_window_ends_at.description: Present only when the deployment grants a withdrawal window. The Account Authority MUST NOT sign the erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord before this time; once the record is signed the request is irreversible (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3 rule 3) and no withdrawal is possible.

registration_did_evidence_draft.description: Dedicated client registration-evidence control signature over the full terminal-derived method evidence. It is distinct from the outer account_registration_control_proof, is not primary method material, and must bind the same verified anchor coordinates and applicable witness evidence.

published_identity_registration.description: Complete already-published Human DID account initialization material. Submitted together with the outer proof, never alone. The live lease/fence reserves this Station account initialization, not publication of another DID. The exact anchor, evidence draft, ordered PCR genesis and initial session are all bound by proof.request_canonical_digest. No DID operation is published, replayed to a registry or hosted by this branch.

contract.description: Account Station view of authority-committed typed current state selected by closed domain selectors.

governance_generation.description: Station tenure these entries and stream heads were read under.

contract.description: Single NDJSON frame on the ak.self.account.stream.subscribe.v1 streaming channel (GET /_arkret/self/account/subscribe, Content-Type: application/x-ndjson). Each newline-delimited line is one frame object. Discriminated by the `kind` field: `delta` carries account-aggregate data (per-Realm stream heads, to_device, account_data, agent_draft_pending_intents, device_lists, notifications, unread counts); the other kinds are control frames that mirror ak.self.committed_event.stream.subscribe.v1 (`catchup_complete`, `checkpoint`, `heartbeat`, `dropped`, `resync_required`, `unauthorized`). Agent draft pending intents use their own holder-private baseline/delta channel and never reuse account_data.events, account_data.station_cas, notifications, or to_device. Encrypted broadcast signals use the optional Signal Extension rail and never appear in this durable/account aggregate stream. `dropped` and `resync_required` MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms` as a server-directed minimum delay before opening another account subscribe stream for the same principal/device/filter scope.

cursor.description: Stream cursor (purpose='stream'). On `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `checkpoint` frames it points to the position covered by this frame; pass back as `after=` on the next subscribe call to resume. REQUIRED on `dropped` frames as the account-aggregate catch-up start for `GET /account/subscribe?after=<cursor>&catchup=true`. MUST be present on `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `checkpoint` / `dropped`; absent on `heartbeat` / `resync_required` / `unauthorized`. This one stays opaque even though each individual stream now has a total order: the account aggregate spans N independent streams so there is no scalar position to state in the clear, a cleartext position vector would let the caller infer private streams it cannot see from the gaps (zh/sync/client-sync.md §4), and the server-side handle also binds filter_digest and device so a changed filter cannot silently skip events. Single-stream reads do NOT use a cursor — see zh/sync/api-conventions.md §7.2.

realms.description: Per-Realm map on `delta` frames. Keys are `ak:realm:*`; values are that Realm's aggregate entry: per-stream window boundaries (streams[]), delivered commit rows (committed_events[]), projection state and account data. Membership state (`join` / `knock` / `leave` / `ban`) is carried by the events inside the Realm entry; pending Invite lifecycle remains a caller-private inbox projection and is not membership.

device_lists.description: Principal DID sets whose authoritative device list changed or left the caller's visibility scope on `delta` frames.

account_data.description: Account-scoped private data on `delta` frames, split by authority: holder-authored durable Events remain in events[], while registry-declared station_cas registers use the closed station_cas branch.

agent_draft_pending_intents.description: Dedicated controller-holder-private Agent draft pending-intent baseline/delta channel. It is authorized for an authenticated active device of the exact controller AccountId and is never an account-data, notification or to-device carrier.

notifications.description: Account-private notification projection deltas on `delta` frames. They are not Realm Events: the channel is authorized by the authenticated account context and is never filtered by the detail Realm window. Ordinary source-Event rows are additionally re-evaluated against the recipient's current read authorization on every frame, frozen baseline pages included.

partial.description: This frame contains at least one limited stream window (some streams[].limited is true). Missing older history is loaded on user demand through ak.self.committed_event.read.scan.v1 with before_position; partial does not describe account baseline completion.

priority.description: Optional server-side priority hint for the frame (UX scheduling).

reconnect_after_ms.description: Optional server-directed minimum delay, in milliseconds, before opening another `ak.self.account.stream.subscribe.v1` stream for the same principal/device/filter scope. MAY appear only on `dropped` and `resync_required` frames. This is a stream reconnect hint, not a generic error retry field; it does not apply to unrelated API calls. Clients MUST wait at least this delay before reconnecting, and servers MUST reject earlier reconnect attempts with `429 rate_limited` plus `Retry-After`.

events.description: Holder-authored ak.account_data.set Events only. Station-CAS rows MUST NOT be synthesized as Events.

station_cas_account_data_container.description: Bounded holder-readable Station-CAS upserts/removals. Initial completeness is carried only by baseline.channels/completed_channels; never clear absent keys on an intermediate page.

station_cas_account_data_removal.description: Explicit physical-delete delta. The revision is the per-key tombstone high-water revision; updated_at is diagnostic only and never selects a winner.

agent_draft_pending_intent_key.description: Stable pending-intent item key. All three components are compared byte-for-byte and are never inferred from account-data digest-key components.

agent_draft_pending_intent_removal.description: Explicit removal after terminal metadata retention. The stable key, source Event identity, canonical Event digest, content digest, expiry and exact last terminal outcome remain visible so a client cannot interpret the removal as permission to resurrect or recreate the intent.

agent_draft_pending_intent_container.description: Independent pending-intent projection page. A frame carries at most 100 ordered changes in one items array; each upsert value's canonical JSON is at most 1 MiB and the complete canonical frame remains at most 8 MiB. The account cursor covers the independent pending-intent projection position.

agent_draft_pending_intent_change.description: One ordered pending-intent projection change. The closed union and one shared items array make the per-frame 100-change bound apply to upserts and removals together.

projection_position.description: Highest independent pending-intent projection position covered by this container and its enclosing account cursor.

snapshot_cut_position.description: Frozen pending-intent projection cut shared by every page under the enclosing baseline.snapshot_cursor.

next_page_offset.description: Next offset in the same frozen cut, or null on the terminal page. Completion still requires baseline.completed_channels to name agent_draft_pending_intents.

notification_delta.description: One account-private notification projection delta. The `id` form is the only branch discriminator: `ak:notification:<uuidv7>` selects the Agent runtime approval branch, `ak:notification_projection:<44-char token>` selects the ordinary source-Event current-row branch. Both branches share one projector, one channel position and the section 2.3 per-frame budget; there is no second notification list operation. See spec/v1/zh/sync/client-sync.md#31-account-notification-deltanormative

oneOf.description: Agent runtime approval branch.
Ordinary source-Event branch. The recipient recomputes it from its own complete AccountId plus data.realm_id, data.source_event_id and data.notification_kind.

ordinary_notification_removal_data.description: Why one ordinary source-Event notification projection left the recipient's current set. It is a server-observable cause only: inbox disposition (read / dismissed / archived) stays in holder-private account data and never removes a current row.

recipient_delivery.description: One exact recipient-private queue item. The discriminator selects an unchanged DeviceMessageEnvelope or producer-signed MlsWelcomeDelivery; neither payload is rewritten into the other.

acknowledgement_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever deliveries[] is non-empty. Bound server-side to the authenticated recipient endpoint and queue high-water position of this batch, covering both delivery kinds and all earlier queue items. NOT a cursor. The client passes it verbatim to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1 only after durably processing every covered delivery (client-sync.md §10.1).

lost.description: SHOULD be true only when durable evidence proves a historical gap or failure since this recipient endpoint's last acknowledged position. Normal expiry and capacity MUST NOT delete unacknowledged deliveries of either kind; clients MUST NOT silently assume completeness when lost is true.

limited.description: True when this account subscribe recipient-delivery batch is truncated by the stream frame budget. When true, `next_cursor` is REQUIRED and the client MUST continue the same queue with ak.self.device_messages.read.list.v1?after=<next_cursor>.

next_cursor.description: Read-only to-device queue continuation cursor for ak.self.device_messages.read.list.v1?after=... . It is not an acknowledgement and MUST NOT delete queued messages; queue deletion happens only through `acknowledgement_token` passed to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

realm_stream_window.description: Per-stream delivery window for one visible authority stream of this Realm bucket. Realm, each Circle and each Sidecar are independent commit streams, so every window boundary marker is per stream: a bucket-level 'there is more history' boolean has no referent once the bucket spans N streams, and a bucket-level one would make one stream's window a function of activity on streams the caller cannot see (zh/sync/client-sync.md §4).

head_commit_ref.description: Current head commit of this stream as known to the server at window freeze. Same {head_commit_ref, next_position} progress shape as zh/sync/service-surface.md §4.6.

next_position.description: Next stream_position this stream expects, i.e. head stream_position + 1. Positions are never compared across streams.

limited.description: Gap marker for THIS stream: history this caller is permitted to read exists below this stream's window start. It is read against the caller's permitted range, never against the physical stream: history below the caller's readable floor MUST NOT set it, and it MUST NOT be cleared because the remaining history happens to be unreadable. Within one frozen baseline window every segment repeats the same value; it must not change because the current segment could not fit the remaining items. Backfill goes through ak.self.committed_event.read.scan.v1 with before_position — there is no second pagination mechanism on the subscribe surface.

window_limit.description: Cumulative item ceiling of the frozen window for THIS stream after merging the request targets (account_filter.window_limit), not the count emitted in one frame. Constant within a window; byte budgets only decide segmentation and must never lower it. Per stream, so one stream being limited never depends on how much budget the other streams consumed. 0 is a boundary-and-context-only window: the server delivers no ordinary event rows for this stream, limited and complete still describe the caller's permitted range (complete true means the zero-row window was delivered in full, never that the stream was scanned to its start), and the client MUST NOT read a zero-row window as an empty or exhausted stream.

complete.description: The server has delivered every segment of this stream's frozen window. Independent of realm_detail_baseline.complete, account baseline completed_channels and catchup_complete. Completion proves delivery only: not per-event authentication, decryption, display dependencies, full history or any read/write permission, and never that the stream was read down to position 0 — the window is bounded by window_limit and by the caller's permitted range.

preview_only.description: Per-stream display fallback: when a window starts after position 0 and this frame lacks a window_start_basis sufficient to verify THIS stream start, preview_only MUST be true regardless of limited. A position-0 start has no basis and is not preview for that reason. Realm-level state_at_window_start cannot substitute for this basis. A preview window MUST NOT feed reducer input or MLS install. Repeat identically in every segment of a frozen window.

window_start_basis.description: Verifiable material only for THIS stream window starting after position 0. It names the exact committed prefix the state is valid after (all Commits of THIS stream through anchor_position) and an authority-signed realm-state-snapshot slice whose head on THIS stream is that Commit; the server must retain the exact snapshot throughout the actual lifetime of the Account stream cursor carrying the window (issued_at through expires_at, at most 7 days), while current disclosure authorization still applies. The client fetches and verifies the basis before persisting the Account frame. Without sufficient basis, this stream is preview_only regardless of limited. A position-0 window has no basis and starts verification at genesis. No cross-stream order or typed-current client reconstruction is implied.

anchor_position.description: stream_position of anchor_commit_ref on THIS stream; the basis state is valid after every Commit of THIS stream through this position. A window that starts at the caller readable floor Commit (floor > 0) has no Commit of the caller readable range before it and therefore carries no basis: that stream is preview_only. Positions are never compared across streams.

anchor_commit_ref.description: commit_id of the Commit at anchor_position.

snapshot_ref.description: The authority-signed realm-state-snapshot whose per-stream slice carries this basis. The client verifies that snapshot's signature and generation and reads the slice for this stream_ref; a slice missing the security or MLS context this stream needs means preview_only for this stream and no other.

governance_generation.description: Station tenure the anchor and snapshot slice are bound to. A client MUST resolve this historical generation and its Station through a fresh verified genesis-to-current authority bundle; an unknown generation or Station is invalid. The snapshot_ref names the exact signed object from this tenure, not a substitute current head.

accepted_dependency_refs.description: Exact accepted cross-stream authorization dependencies the anchor's prefix relied on, each a closed four-coordinate committed_event_ref. They are explicit references, not an ordering: listing them introduces no cross-stream total order and no comparison of positions across streams. Omitted or empty means the prefix depended on no accepted reference outside this stream.

e2ee_epoch.description: Projection-only MLS epoch of THIS stream at its window start. Each Circle and each Sidecar owns an independent MLS group and epoch, so this cannot be a Realm-level scalar. null when the stream has no MLS group. Not part of any state hash, checkpoint or causal graph.

streams.description: Per-stream window boundaries for the streams of this Realm bucket that the caller is authorized to see and whose Commit chain is already established. A container with no Commit yet MUST NOT appear here: head_commit_ref and next_position have no value to carry before position 0 exists, and the server MUST NOT fabricate a window with an empty head. Such a container becomes visible through stream enumeration (ak.self.realm.read.streams.v1) or a later frame once its first Commit lands. Entries MUST be sorted by unsigned bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(stream_ref) and stream_ref MUST be unique. Delivery rows live in committed_events[]; this array carries only the window scalars, which are per stream because Realm / each Circle / each Sidecar are independent commit streams. The caller MUST NOT infer anything about streams absent from this array other than what streams_limited states: an authorized-but-absent stream and a stream the caller cannot see are indistinguishable here by construction.

streams_limited.description: True when the caller is authorized to see more streams in this Realm than the 64-entry streams[] ceiling admits. Truncation is deterministic and depends only on the caller's own visible stream set: the Realm stream (stream_ref.kind='realm') MUST be retained whenever the caller can see it, and the remaining slots are filled in ascending unsigned-byte order of JCS(stream_ref). The server MUST NOT silently drop streams — a client that reads this as false may treat streams[] as the complete visible set, while true means it MUST fetch the remainder through the per-stream surfaces (ak.self.committed_event.read.scan.v1 and Realm detail) and MUST NOT conclude that an absent stream does not exist. Omitted means false.

window_snapshot_cursor.description: Identifies and binds the frozen window generation of this Realm bucket. Repeated identically in every segment of that window. It is an identity, not a position: never used as the account `after` parameter, never parsed, never compared as an ordered token. Distinct from realm_detail_baseline.snapshot_cursor, which freezes a different generation.

event_states.description: Per-event protocol-state views (event_id + event_state) for reducer-input events carried by this entry. Ordinary current-value projection concurrency is resolved by the governance Station's {commit_id, stream_ref, stream_position} plus the domain revision — within one stream stream_position is a total order, and there is no cross-stream order to resolve. See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_state_reason_code.description: Optional registered reason code for failure detail beyond the enum.

committed_events.description: Caller-visible committed Event views delivered by this Realm bucket. Each item carries its RealmCommit, so there is no cross-stream protocol order.

state_at_window_start.description: Derived projection-only state at the window start, Realm-level display context only. NOT part of state hash, checkpoint, or causal graph, and never a security basis: it is a display preview and MUST NOT be presented as, or accepted in place of, an authority-signed snapshot. The verifiable rebuild material is per stream in realm_sync_entry.streams[].window_start_basis, and the presence of this object MUST NOT clear any stream's preview_only. The MLS epoch is NOT here either: each Circle and each Sidecar has its own group and epoch, so e2ee_epoch lives on realm_sync_entry.streams[] instead.

actor_profiles.description: Window-start profile rows keyed semantically by the complete ActorId. Entries MUST be sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(actor_id), and duplicate ActorIds MUST be rejected even if display fields differ. A principal DID alone is not a key: accounts on distinct Stations remain distinct rows with their own display projections.

collaboration_role.description: Projection-only strong Realm role, emitted only after the server validates the registered Realm profile and discriminator.

invited_member_count.description: Count of caller-private pending Invite inbox entries associated with this Realm. This is not derived from ak.member.state, does not imply membership, and MUST NOT create roster rows.

member_roster.description: Lightweight roster page derived from effective ak.member.state, effective ak.member.identity.update references, and currently visible handle-claim evidence. Entries MUST NOT carry display fields or naked handle strings directly; handle strings may appear only inside signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects.

limited.description: True when entries[] is truncated and MUST NOT be treated as the complete Realm roster.

next_cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor for continuing member roster retrieval.

membership.description: Effective membership rows visible in the roster. Invite lifecycle records are not membership and MUST NOT appear here.

subject_account_id.description: Optional exact account identity disclosed for this member. Omit when subject disclosure is only available inside encrypted MemberIdentity or not authorized for the caller. Required whenever handle claim evidence or digest hints are included.

identity_event_ids.description: Effective ak.member.identity.update event ids for this actor after replacement refs are applied.

member_display_state_digest.description: Digest over the effective identity event references plus the current visible handle claim digest set for this roster entry.

identity_events.description: Optional inline effective ak.member.identity.update Event envelopes. When present these are the original events, not query-time re-encryption or projection rewrites. MUST be omitted unless subject_account_id is disclosed, because plaintext or decryptable identity events can disclose the same member subject.

handle_claim_digests.description: Digests of currently visible effective ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects for this member in the current Realm context. MUST be omitted unless subject_account_id is disclosed, because stable claim digests are linkable across contexts. Absence is not proof that the member has no handle.

handle_claims.description: Optional inline signed handle claim status evidence. MUST be omitted unless subject_account_id is disclosed, and every included status view MUST have claim.subject_account_id byte-for-byte equal to the entry subject_account_id across both components. Services may omit this for privacy, size, or freshness. a claim whose principal_id matches but whose station_id differs MUST be discarded.

handle_claims_limited.description: True when handle_claims[] is truncated or replaced by digest-only hints. Clients MUST NOT interpret missing claims as no handle.

stream_refs.description: Optional explicit stream selection for the selected Realms, at most 64 per window. Entries MUST be unique, MUST each name a Realm present in realm_ids, and MUST each be a stream this caller is permitted to see; a member that is not is rejected rather than silently dropped. The Realm stream occupies one slot like any other entry when a group includes it, and a group that omits it is a valid selection. Omitted keeps the current behaviour: the server fills streams[] up to its own 64-entry ceiling and reports streams_limited. When present, the window is the selected set: the server advances the tail of exactly those streams, an omitted stream counts as not delivered rather than delivered-and-empty, and the cursor handle binds filter_digest to this selection, so switching groups needs a new filter and a new cursor while the position each group reached stays retrievable. Discovery of streams added or removed since the selection was made travels through ak.self.realm.read.streams.v1 or the visible discovery delta.

window_limit.description: Per-VISIBLE-STREAM item ceiling after merging the request targets, same name and same meaning as the response-side realm_sync_entry.streams[].window_limit. For a frozen baseline window it is the cumulative ceiling across every segment of that window; for live delta it applies per frame. Byte budgets only decide segmentation and never lower it. It is deliberately not a per-Realm budget: a bucket-level quota would force the server to divide it across N streams, so one stream being marked limited could mean only that another stream consumed the budget.

account_filter.description: An absent or empty realm_ids collection selects no Realm detail. Global account and Realm-summary changes remain subscribed. stream_refs belongs to selected Realms: absent keeps the bounded first screen, while present makes the selected set the window. Event-kind and Strand display filtering is client-side only and MUST NOT interrupt Commit continuity.

account_revision_stale_problem.description: Registered pre-NDJSON RFC 9457 recovery carrier for ak.self.account.stream.subscribe.v1 only. After session, live cursor and current disclosure validation, a recoverable verified serving prefix is behind an accepted head bound to after. continuation_cursor MUST echo that exact after byte for byte. No checkpoint installation, baseline reset, new authority, private state deletion or delivery ACK follows from this refusal; only ordinary verified Account frames can advance the cut. Unknown, forked, irrecoverable or unavailable authority is not this producer condition. See client-sync section 12.3.2.

realm_list_page.description: Only next_cursor presence indicates another page. A nonterminal page MUST contain at least one item; no duplicated terminal flag is carried.

channels.description: Global baseline channels carried by this segment. agent_draft_pending_intents is independent from account_data_events, station_cas, notifications and to_device.

completed_channels.description: Channels whose complete frozen snapshot has been delivered. A pending-intent channel is complete only on its terminal page with next_page_offset=null; absent items on an earlier page never remove local records.

oneOf.description: Account aggregate data frame.
This bounded catchup round completed. Per-channel and Realm baseline completion is declared separately.
Cursor-only checkpoint advancement; no data fields are allowed.
Account stream gap signal; cursor is the account catch-up start. No data fields are allowed. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Keepalive frame; cursor and data fields are forbidden.
Hard reset signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Authorization-loss signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden.

contract.description: Issuer-signed endorsement used to verify Actor Profile accountable_principal_ids entries. This is the payload contract for ak.identity.accountability_grant.

issuer_id.description: Stable principal did_core_id accepting accountability for subject. Verifiers MUST take the proof verification-method DID URL's bare controller did, validate it with the registered method adapter, and require project(did) to equal issuer; direct DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden.

accountability_scope.description: Non-empty duplicate-free closed set used only for display and accountability governance; never grants authorization. A string is the singleton-set wire form. Array order has no semantic meaning. Canonical authors emit singleton sets as strings and multi-value sets in ascending raw UTF-8 byte order; receivers accept every schema-valid ordering and normalize only for current state-subject derivation, domain equality, and projection union.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the accountability grant is non-expiring and governed by grant_status revocation and controller lifecycle cascade.

proof.description: Detached proof by issuer over utf8('ak.accountability-grant-v1\n') || canonical_json(the object with proof omitted). Its verification method MUST be the same <issuer DID>#ak:device:<device_id> method as the carrying Event producer proof, active in the issuer Principal Control Realm at the admission cut (zh/models/actor.md section 3.3.1). The sole service-issuer exception is a closed Applet managed-actor creation aggregate in the provision Collaboration Realm: both this detached proof and the Event producer proof use the exact registration-epoch Service method verified against the exact install. Ordinary issuers retain the PCR/device rule; no standalone Service ingress is permitted.

accountability_projection.description: Canonical business value of the identity_accountability current state. zh/models/actor.md section 3.3.1 fixes these six members and keeps two things out on purpose: the inner proof, and any source event reference. The head Event and its accepted proof already carry where this endorsement came from, so copying an event id into the value would make two endorsements that say the same thing compare unequal. Both registered writers -- the independent ak.identity.accountability_grant and ak.agent.provision's atomic accountability projection -- MUST reach this shape through a declared value_projection rather than a renaming state_projection.value.field path.

issuer_id.description: Principal accepting accountability. ak.agent.provision maps its controller_principal_id here.

subject_id.description: Endorsed actor principal. ak.agent.provision maps its agent_id here.

accountability_scope.description: The normalized set, always an array even when the wire form was the singleton string, deduplicated and sorted by ascending raw UTF-8 bytes. This is the same normalization the composite subject digests under ak.accountability_scope_set.v1, which is what makes a provision projection and a later independent grant address one current state rather than two.

not_before.description: ak.agent.provision derives this from the carrying envelope's created_at, which is why its admission requires payload.created_at to equal it byte-for-byte.

expires_at.description: Optional, and absent is the meaning rather than the absence of a meaning: the grant is non-expiring and governed by grant_status. A writer whose payload omits it MUST leave this member out; writing JSON null is not the same statement.

contract.description: Authorized anti-enumeration display view of a co-member global Actor Profile, served by the authenticated own Station. The profile Event and its covering RealmCommit are accepted provenance, not a complete projection proof. The operation grants no identity, capability or membership authority.

resolve_request_body.description: Resolves current global Actor Profiles for actors the caller currently shares realm_id with. The caller MUST be an effective joined member of realm_id and every returned actor MUST also be one at evaluation time; realm_id is the authorization basis, not a display hint.

realm_id.description: Shared Collaboration Realm establishing the relationship. A Principal Control Realm MUST NOT be used here: PCR co-membership is the owner's own devices and would make this operation a self-read with an outward shape.

profile_event.description: The exact eligible profile Event that is the source of the deterministic current display projection. It is provenance only: retained losing writes and patch ancestry are not proven complete by this one Event. The service must return profile_unavailable if no eligible and disclosable source Event exists. Its Realm is the owner PCR; this limited disclosure never permits other PCR Events.

resolved_actor_profile.description: One actor display projection from the authenticated own Station, the exact accepted profile Event sourcing its deterministic current value and that Event's covering RealmCommit. The Station verifies commit.event_ref == profile_event.event_id, the PCR stream binding, authority generation and signature before serving it. A single patch Event plus Commit does not prove the full retained evidence set, patch ancestry, historical completeness or global freshness. An independent verifier needs the complete authorized projection closure; this DTO makes no such proof claim. No field is a grant, selector authority or identity-resolution authority.

profile_commit.description: The exact RealmCommit that accepted profile_event in the owner's Principal Control Realm stream. commit.event_ref MUST equal profile_event.event_id.

resolve_failure.description: Per-actor failure. The reason vocabulary is deliberately single-valued: unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, actor that is not an effective joined member of realm_id, and a caller not authorized for that actor MUST all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot be used to probe membership or account existence.

resolve_response_body.description: Closed outcome. Every requested actor_id appears exactly once across profiles and failures, so a caller cannot distinguish an omitted actor from a withheld one.

account_status_projection.description: Optional AccountStatusRecord projection served beside the profile. The durable Actor Profile object used to carry a status member, which was unwritable by construction: zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3 keeps AccountStatusRecord out of every authority stream, RealmCommit, Control Proposal and reducer, so no registered state_writes[] row could ever produce it and no author could be allowed to. It is a read-side projection and lives here. The Station MUST have verified the exact record it is projecting -- the same account_id, the record's own proof, and the status_sequence against its durable monotonic replica head -- and MUST omit this member entirely when it holds no verified record. Omission means unknown. A caller MUST NOT read a missing member as active, and MUST NOT cache a status across a profile revision: the record changes on the Account Authority's clock, not on the profile's.

status.description: The closed AccountStatusRecord lifecycle value of zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3. Implementations MAY coarsen or withhold the projection, but MUST NOT invent a value.

status_sequence.description: status_sequence of the exact record projected, so the caller can order and re-check it.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

actor_kind.description: Closed Actor classification. agent is reserved exclusively for a controller-provisioned Agent; Applet-created or Applet-hosted automation uses bot; Ghost Actor is provenance rather than an actor_kind and uses integration for an external account/integration mirror or bot for an external bot mirror. MUST NOT include device: a device is an endpoint rather than an Actor principal. actor_kind alone grants no authority; authorization still requires the normative DID, provisioning/registration, Grant and Constraint evidence. See zh/models/actor.md.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped Agent label backed by the current agent_selector_claim current state written by ak.agent.provision. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ak.profile.agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle, free-text mention address, authorization subject, attribution key, or Directory discovery key. A client may verify this label only after obtaining the exact full Agent AccountId from an authorized source.

resolution.description: Read-only current principal did projection derived from the PCR identity resolution current state. It is not writable through Actor Profile create/update patches and is not an authorization root.

actor_profile_definition.description: Closed Profile owner: ordinary principal_id branch or Realm actor_id branch, mutually exclusive. Realm owners are exact full actors and may not carry Account handles or Agent/accountability fields. Profile identity is Event-derived and owner/actor_kind are create-locked.

actor_kind.description: Closed Actor classification. agent is reserved exclusively for a controller-provisioned Agent; Applet-created or Applet-hosted automation uses bot; Ghost Actor is provenance rather than an actor_kind and uses integration for an external account/integration mirror or bot for an external bot mirror. MUST NOT include device: a device is an endpoint rather than an Actor principal. actor_kind alone grants no authority; authorization still requires the normative DID, provisioning/registration, Grant and Constraint evidence. See zh/models/actor.md.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped Agent label backed by the current agent_selector_claim current state written by ak.agent.provision. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ak.profile.agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle, free-text mention address, authorization subject, attribution key, or Directory discovery key. A client may verify this label only after obtaining the exact full Agent AccountId from an authorized source.

contract.description: Closed Profile owner: ordinary principal_id branch or Realm actor_id branch, mutually exclusive. Realm owners are exact full actors and may not carry Account handles or Agent/accountability fields. Profile identity is Event-derived and owner/actor_kind are create-locked.

Portable Agent signer evidence carried to a Station or peer verifier: the Agent Authority state evidence over one exact confirmed RealmCommit state, and the Account Authority controller gate. Both objects anchor their own local detached signature under their own registered domain separation; neither reuses the shared Event proof leaf. Agent and controller private keys, MLS private state, service-local account_id and raw account typed current state never appear here.

detached_jws.description: Local detached signature leaf of this file. The signing bytes are the registered domain separation label, a newline, then the JCS bytes of the enclosing object with this member jws removed; kind stays covered like every other closed member.

jws.description: Compact detached JWS. Its verification method is the enclosing object verification_method, resolved through the published DID document of the signer at the signing instant.

controller_account_gate_basis.description: Private Account Authority current basis. account_binding_default is stable absence or the exact initial active binding record; account_status_record binds the original immutable signed AccountStatusRecord current head. It is not an Event, RealmCommit or Station checkpoint, and the record body remains private.

status_record_digest.description: SHA-256 of JCS of the complete original signed AccountStatusRecord, including account_status_record_id and proof; not the unsigned core, a reconstructed record or an aggregate checkpoint.

controller_account_gate_attestation.description: Account Authority answer to one question: is the controller principal behind an Agent key authorization still eligible? Signed under ak.controller_account_gate.v1. Member order is byte-for-byte the binding_fields order of that domain_separations row; proof follows as the detached signature over exactly those bound members. It is privacy minimised by construction: a service-local account_id, a raw account current state or a caller-asserted active boolean is a schema violation, not an optional member.

principal_id.description: Controller principal did_core_id. The consumer independently derives the complete controller AccountId from the key authorization Event and MUST reject a gate whose principal does not match it.

eligibility.description: The only decision a consumer acts on. It is active if and only if status is active.

basis_digest.description: SHA-256(JCS({principal_id:gate.principal_id,accepted_id:gate.authority_id,status:gate.status,basis:gate.basis})), without a domain prefix. accepted_id is a derived preimage key equal to the original internal request agent_authority_id and owning AA/Station; it is not another wire member. Consumers MUST recompute exact equality from these public Gate fields, independently of signature verification; this does not authenticate the hidden original Record/current ledger head.

authority_id.description: Owning Station of the Account Authority. The consumer derives the expected Station from the complete Agent AccountId; a self-asserted authority is not a source.

expires_at.description: Positive validity window bound: expires_at is strictly after issued_at and at most 300 seconds after it.

allOf.description: status active holds exactly when eligibility is active; every other status is inactive.
Stable absence or exact initial binding Active is the only default basis. Every non-active status, and restored Active after any successor, requires the original signed record basis.

commit_lineage.description: Complete, duplicate-free predecessor closure connecting one witness RealmCommit to source_commit_id inside the same stream. An unknown, forked, cross-Realm or unsigned predecessor, or a missing link, rejects the whole evidence.

predecessor_commit_ids.description: Ordered inclusive path from witness_commit_id to source_commit_id, increasing stream_position by exactly one at each step. Every ID addresses the matching complete member of state.commits.

agent_key_authorization.description: Projection of the key authenticated by one complete ak.agent.key.authorize Event. It is never a second wire certificate and never an authority source: the consumer separately verifies the Event producer proof and the authority-signed RealmCommit that covers it.

public_key.description: Closed Ed25519 profile. kid MUST equal verification_method and key MUST decode to exactly 32 octets.

public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the decoded 32 raw Ed25519 octets. It is never a hash of the PublicKey DTO, a JWK, a multibase form or a hex string.

accepted_commit_id.description: MUST equal key_state_witness.commit_id and the id of key_state_witness.commit.

accepted_at.description: Instant the authorization took effect through accepted_commit_id. MUST equal key_state_witness.commit.committed_at; the storage time of a receiving service creates no runtime key authority.

agent_key_state_witness.description: Signed RealmCommit plus the closed agent_key current state it covers. v1 has no state_root, leaf digest, index, count or Merkle inclusion proof: the Commit itself is the commitment.

agent_lifecycle_provenance.description: Closed provenance branch of the witnessed lifecycle value. Each branch carries only the accepted status Event ID of its own transition; a provision Event ID or a predecessor lifecycle pointer has no independent proof carrier and MUST NOT appear.

agent_lifecycle_witness.description: Signed RealmCommit, the closed agent_status current state it covers, the accepted status Event and its closed provenance branch. The receiver recomputes the lifecycle result and its transition from the signed Event before trusting any of them.

agent_authority_state.description: One exact confirmed RealmCommit state of the Agent Principal Control Realm, carrying the complete PCR genesis Event, key authorization Event, key authorization, key state witness and Agent lifecycle witness together.

authority_id.description: The immutable owning Station of the user-managed Agent PCR, Agent Account and controller Account pair. Derive it from the complete AccountId.station_id and accepted agent_control genesis/provision, never from a self-reported authority. No PCR handoff is permitted; every Commit is generation zero.

source_commit_id.description: The exact confirmed RealmCommit this state is read at. Every witness lineage terminates here.

commits.description: Exact union of genesis, witness and lineage Commits through source_commit_id, sorted by stream_position. No gaps, duplicate IDs/positions, forks or unrelated Commits.

signer_dependencies.description: Exactly the recursive producer proof dependencies used by genesis, authorization, lifecycle and authority transition Events. Sorted by signer_resolution_evidence_ref UTF-8 bytes. Missing ref is unresolved; duplicate ref, conflicting bytes, cycle or surplus is rejected.

agent_authority_state_attestation.description: The single Agent Authority state signature, made under ak.agent_authority_state_evidence.v1 by the authoritative service DID of that PCR. It binds the exact authority, verification method, state digest and observation window verbatim; the controller proof, the Account Authority gate and the RealmCommit signatures each stay separate.

issued_at.description: The real instant the authoritative state was read. Forwarding, re-wrapping, reconnecting, disk recovery or re-signing an old observation MUST NOT restart this clock.

expires_at.description: Strictly after issued_at and at most 300 seconds after it.

agent_authority_state_evidence.description: Portable Agent Authority state evidence. state_digest is the RFC 8785 JCS SHA-256 of state alone, so a compact transport root MAY omit state when the receiver already holds that exact digest fully verified; the receiver MUST restore the complete state before recomputing any digest or verifying any signature.

controller_account_gate_attestation_issu.description: Deployment-authenticated request an Agent Authority sends to obtain the Account Authority-owned controller gate. Caller identity comes only from the authenticated deployment relationship: the body carries no service resolution carrier, and a self-asserted DID, URL, bearer subject, public key or account-active boolean is a schema violation rather than an identity source.

principal_id.description: Controller principal whose eligibility is asked about.

agent_authority_id.description: Agent Authority the gate is issued for. It MUST equal the authenticated caller and the Station of the controller's complete AccountId; a mismatch is an unenumerable not_found.

controller_account_gate_attestation_issu.description: Byte-stable issuance result. A replay of the same request_id and canonical intent returns these original bytes; a different intent under the same request_id is a duplicate_conflict with zero issuance.

agent_accepted_authority_bundle.description: Minimal accepted-at genesis-only authority projection for a user-managed Agent PCR fixed to its Account Station at generation zero. No authority_transitions member, online nonce/current assertion or routing authority. signer_histories contain exactly the original Station method-native history needed at each actual signature time; key rotation is not governance transfer. Unused records are surplus. It does not authorize other Events or controller binding.

agent_producer_evidence.description: authority_forward Agent sibling.
