The retained producer signer_resolution_evidence_ref addresses the six-member authenticated_signer_evidence alone; authority state and controller gate are independent signed siblings. authority_resolution supplies method-native history for the state attestation and controller gate at their respective observation times. It carries no participation selection. Canonical persistence restores compact state first.

oneOf.description: Ref is the JCS SHA-256 content address of account_device_signer_evidence. Validate the original accepted producer at its accepted_at, not against a newly issued current device projection.
Ref addresses authenticated_signer_evidence alone. Verify its exact method/key/subject using the carried method-native history at the original accepted-at instant.
Ref addresses agent_evidence.authenticated_signer_evidence alone. Recursively validate the complete accepted-at Agent closure; repeated refs are deduplicated and cycles rejected.

contract.description: Closed controller-private Agent draft plaintext and Station-private pending-intent contracts. The top-level schema is the plaintext encrypted by the controller holder inside ak.schema.account_data_encrypted_value.v1; Station never receives that plaintext.

agent_draft_account_data_key.description: Canonical Agent draft Account Data key. The two 43-character unpadded base64url components are SHA-256 digests, not reversible encodings: agent_component = BASE64URL_NOPAD(SHA-256(UTF8('ak.agent-draft.account-data-key.agent-id.v1\n') || UTF8(canonical agent_id))) and draft_component = BASE64URL_NOPAD(SHA-256(UTF8('ak.agent-draft.account-data-key.draft-id.v1\n') || UTF8(draft_id))). A parser validates the exact prefix, total length, exactly two components, canonical 32-byte base64url round-trip and no padding; it returns opaque digest components, never guessed literals. Station obtains literals only from source_pending_event_id's accepted pending row, recomputes both components and requires byte-for-byte key equality before writing.

content.description: Candidate content whose RFC 8785 JCS digest equals content_digest.
Controller-visible proposal content recovered from the HPKE handoff. Its RFC 8785 JCS digest MUST equal content_digest before encryption and after decryption.

agent_draft_pending_intent.description: Closed live | terminal-redacted union. A live available record carries the HPKE content_handoff. A terminal-redacted consumed/expired record permanently omits ciphertext while retaining the create-once identity, source Event, canonical Event digest, expiry and exact terminal metadata.

agent_draft_pending_intent_terminal_reda.description: Terminal metadata retained after HPKE ciphertext GC. content_handoff is not a property and is therefore forbidden by the closed object.

contract.description: Closed binding and durable cleanup state for Agent Realm membership. Effective membership is the AND of the Agent member current state, the exact controller membership generation, Agent lifecycle and provision/accountability validity. Canonical Agent leave transitions are always caller-signed; a service never synthesizes them.

membership_lifecycle_cause.description: Closed audit-only lifecycle cause. It never supplies authorization or proves reducer provenance.

controller_membership_generation_ref.description: Exact controller ak.member.state join Event that establishes the bound membership generation. It must already be accepted, except that the complete controller-Agent Direct Conversation founding unit explicitly references its preceding staged founder join and activates all four Events atomically. A later rejoin has another Event ID and never revives this binding.

controller_terminal_event_ref.description: Required only on an explicit controller-membership-ended cleanup Event. It identifies the accepted terminal controller transition whose pre-state determines the exact Agent set and one-shot cascade authority.

expected_agent_ids.description: Exact set of active controlled Agent ActorIds frozen from terminal pre-state, sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of each RFC 8785 JCS ActorId. Every element MUST identify an Agent in that pre-state; a bare principal DID or a different Station is not the same member.

cleanup_intent_digest.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical record fields through expected_agent_ids. It is the durable idempotency key for emergency cleanup.

cleanup_due_at.description: Governance alert deadline only. Crossing it changes pending to overdue but never restores controller or Agent authority.

contract.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account pairing and Agent management operations.

agent_slug.description: Required controller-scoped Agent label slug. Used only to verify or display an already-known authorized full Agent AccountId; not a free-text mention address, global handle, or authorization subject. The accepted ak.agent.provision is the only writer of the agent_selector_claim current state that binds this label.

opaque_local_id.description: Deployment-local short-lived account/auth artifact id. It is an opaque_correlation value, so its lexical space is disjoint from the ak: typed-ID namespace: a value MUST NOT begin with ak:.

pairing_secret.description: One-time eight-digit decimal pairing code generated uniformly by a CSPRNG, including leading zeroes. It is accepted only with the matching opaque pairing_request_id; the code alone is never a lookup credential. It is transmitted only in JSON bodies, never in URLs or logs.

device_pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style code carrying 40 CSPRNG bits. The minting service MUST keep it unique across its whole live pending window, because it is also the sole lookup key of the authenticated code claim; it is bound to a short-lived pairing challenge transcript and protected by a ten-failure lockout.

agent_runtime_key_possession_proof.description: Closed Ed25519 proof that the submitter controls the proposed Agent runtime key and possesses the authoritative pairing secret. Canonical transcript, equality, freshness, and final-commit re-verification rules are defined in key-management.md section 3.6.2.

audience_id.description: Stable target-service authorization identity; any verification_method remains a DID URL whose bare DID MUST project to this did_core_id.

signature.description: Unpadded base64url encoding of the 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature over the canonical transcript.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey DTO. Defined once in public-key.schema.json so device, agent and account surfaces share one definition.

agent_runtime_public_key.description: Closed v1 Agent runtime signing-key profile. Ed25519 is the fully-specified JOSE algorithm identifier from RFC 9864; polymorphic algorithm identifiers are rejected.

agent_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent axis. Closed enum; only the controller's pause / resume / deactivate lifecycle events change it. Pairing and key facts are reflected through the generic readiness axis and open-handle fields, never through a fourth generic state axis (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_runtime_state.description: Operation-local diagnostic enum used only by agent_runtime_approval_status_response_body on the unauthenticated pairing poll. It is mechanically derived from the polled handle and key facts, is never writable, and MUST NOT appear in generic Agent list/get/key_state projections: no active accepted key authorization with an unexpired bootstrap handle is pending_runtime_key; no active key with the bootstrap handle expired is pairing_expired; an active key with no unconsumed replacement handle is ready; an active key with an unexpired replacement handle is replacing.

agent_presence.description: Short-lived reachability signal only. It never substitutes for lifecycle or readiness and does not use a protocol-wide fixed five-minute refresh interval.

realm_id.description: Realm that owns the capability grant current state and therefore the required ak.capability.revoke write surface.

key_state.description: Controller-private key, pairing-handle and authorization material for a generic Agent view. Active authorization delivers the exact accepted current authorize Event and covering RealmCommit in current_key_authorization, separately from the compact current_signer_evidence; original pairing custody is immutable and is not a substitute for replacement authorization scope, audience or expiry. No lifecycle, readiness, presence, runtime_state or backup-readiness field is carried here.

requested_scope.description: Controller-private projection of the required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling captured at provision time, not a grant. Content actions are the maximum actions that later key scopes, Realm-scoped grants and sessions may allow; an omitted action cannot be added later. Participation is a separate action-time deny gate and cannot add authority. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants. Receiver authority comes from a valid agent-requested-scope-disclosure whose digest matches the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, not this service projection.

pairing_request_id.description: Current unconsumed, unexpired pairing handle. Omit it and pairing_code/pairing_expires_at after consumption or expiry. Attach versus replace is derived from current active authorization dots, never historical rows.

pairing_expires_at.description: Authoritative pairing expiry instant in the shared byte-canonical UTC millisecond profile. The projection and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1.expires_at use the same exact string; offset or sub-millisecond wire spellings are schema violations and MUST NOT be normalized by a verifier.

authorized_public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key using the unique agent_signing_public_key_digest helper; the runtime compares it to its own key.

current_key_authorization.description: Complete accepted current ak.agent.key.authorize Event and its covering RealmCommit; the full Event branch is required, never withheld. Required when an active authorization exists and omitted otherwise. Event id, actor Account, controller execution/delegation, PCR, method, raw key digest, expiry and covering Commit must match the active dot and sibling compact signer evidence. The source grants no authority and cannot replace current lifecycle, accountability or immutable provision ceiling checks. It carries neither private requested_scope disclosure nor raw pairing PoP.

agent_current_signer_evidence.description: Complete content-addressed Agent signer root for the currently authorized runtime key. signer_resolution_evidence_ref MUST equal SHA-256(RFC8785-JCS(authenticated_signer_evidence)) in the registered ak:signer_evidence form, and MUST equal the sibling signer_resolution_evidence_ref of the carrier object byte for byte. authenticated_signer_evidence is the compact six-member signer-resolution evidence and carries no closure of its own; the portable Agent Authority closure travels as agent-authority-evidence.schema.json#/$defs/agent_authority_state_evidence, never inside this root.

account_device_pair_request_body.description: Account Authority terminal pairing command. The Station TCB validates the sole pending ledger and current-device authority, admits the exact authorize_event once, stores its unique RealmCommit, consumes pending/code once, and stores a byte-identical terminal outcome. Exact retry returns the same Event, Commit and outcome; changed intent conflicts with zero writes. The request does not carry a client-selected Station, receipt, internal recovery state or private coordination member.

authorize_event.description: Fully signed ak.device.authorize initial submission authored by a current accepted device. The service MUST admit this exact Event through the Event validation/reducer path; it MUST NOT mint an Event id, rewrite the Event, or directly insert a device projection. Its typed payload is the sole source of hpke_key and the target-device possession device_signature, MUST match new_device_public_key by device id and Ed25519 key bytes, MUST set authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, and MUST name the approving current device id in authorized_by. The proof.verification_method bare DID component MUST project through its registered adapter to Event.actor_id.account_id.principal_id and its fragment MUST equal authorized_by; appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden. That Event proof, not the target device_signature, binds the exact account actor, authorized_by, not_before, expires_at and scopes, because only the approving device knows those values.

device_pairing_request_id.description: Required pairing identity bound by the single target device_signature over the full final-account challenge descriptor, including metadata digest with explicit nulls. The verifier reconstructs and compares the transcript digest. Exact replay returns the durable terminal outcome without re-reading pending state.

account_device_pair_response_body.description: Byte-identical terminal outcome stored by the Account Authority only after the owning Station RealmCommit has been verified and the local fence reaches completed. Exact replay returns these bytes without another Event submission or pending read.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_response_body. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Controller-signed private disclosure addressed to the authoritative pairing verifier. The endpoint MUST consume its presentation challenge once, match agent/controller/audience, recompute the public DID commitment digest, and use the disclosed scope for the subset check. It MUST NOT copy the disclosure into authorize_event or any durable/public history.

authorize_event.description: Fully-signed ak.agent.key.authorize initial submission approved by the controller or policy engine. Its Event MUST target the Agent Principal Control Realm, carry actor_id equal to agent_id, executed_by equal to the controller DID, authorization_ref equal to the controller delegation DID URL bound by the Agent DID Document, and a proof verification method belonging to the controller or one of its currently authorized devices. The submission MUST carry ordinary publication authority evidence without rewriting the Event. Its payload.agent_key_scope MAY be narrower than, but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of, the immutable provision requested_scope; every provision constraint remains mandatory. Required so key activation never depends on an unaudited pairing side effect. authorize_event.event.event_id is the pair operation idempotency identity.

agent_key_pair_request_body.description: One controller approval command bound to the frozen candidate and handle. The signed authorization Event supplies Agent, key, method, scope, expiry and exact supersedes. Verifiers load possession proof and candidate from the authoritative confidential record, never caller echoes. Accepted RealmCommit processing automatically advances the durable command; exact retries only observe or recover it.

activation_state.description: Durable command state. awaiting_source_commit waits for the exact authorization Event covering RealmCommit; accepted RealmCommit processing activates automatically without another pair command. active preserves lifecycle intent and does not itself issue a session. cancelled is terminal after handle invalidation, expiry, changed authority or failed activation fence. Replays never revive a cancelled command.

agent_runtime_approval_request_body.description: Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for Agent-agent key pairing. The runtime proves possession of the local key and the short pairing code; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize and submitting agent_key_pair_request_body. The service computes ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 from agent_id, pairing_request_id, verification_method, public-key digest and attestation digest. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable binding: same-binding retry is idempotent and refreshes the full request while retaining approval/notification ids; a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_response_body. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_controller_projec.description: Authenticated minimal frozen candidate projection. Raw key/method and optional attestation are public approval inputs; approval_request_id and stable digest do not change when a fresh PoP is accepted for the same candidate. Full possession proof and pairing secret are not included. Controller must inspect exact Agent, key fingerprint, scope/expiry and supersedes in the Event before signing.

agent_human_approval_problem_extensions.description: Closed RFC 9457 extension set returned by ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.v1 when an agent_key_proof request needs out-of-band controller approval. The enclosing Problem type MUST be https://arkret.org/problems/claim_required. The agent runtime MUST NOT be given CAPTCHA, OTP, browser-login, or other interactive human challenge material.

agent_runtime_approval_status_request_bo.description: Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id, pairing_code, and agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. A record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and stop polling after pairing expiry.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_response_body. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_status_response_b.description: Operation-local status for the exact handle/candidate. Authorization and signer-evidence fields are present only after durable RealmCommit activation. The runtime checks its own method/raw-key digest, validates the complete current_signer_evidence closure, independently rebuilds its authenticated root and signer_resolution_evidence_ref with the SDK canonical helper, then persists both for offline Event authoring; authorized_event_ref is provenance and MUST NOT be used as the signer evidence ref. Expired, unknown or invalidated handles use uniform anti-enumeration behavior. Status never authorizes a key by itself.

authorized_public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key using the unique agent_signing_public_key_digest helper; the runtime compares it to its own key.

signer_resolution_evidence_ref.description: Content address of current_signer_evidence.authenticated_signer_evidence. The runtime MUST recompute it from the complete canonical root and reject a mismatch.

agent_provision_request_body.description: Controller-authored Agent bootstrap. Before prepare, the controller publishes a signed, PCR-independent did:webvh inception whose document contains the managed-controller delegation but no ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service. prepare receives that did, verifies the accepted inception and returns its exact initial_resolution plus an opaque allocation. The controller freezes the Agent PCR genesis with that commitment, derives principal_control_realm_id, and commits one ak.agent.provision Event. After PCR acceptance, the controller publishes the pre-rotation-authorized DID update containing the create-locked Realm binding. The service exposes the Agent and pairing handle only after that update is accepted.

did.description: Controller-authored Agent did:webvh whose accepted inception is independent of the future PCR Realm id.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived as retype(event_id) of the Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope it froze locally, and signed into provision_event. A service MUST NOT choose it; commit MUST reject any value that differs from the provision payload byte for byte. It is distinct from the controller PCR that carries provision_event. This transport field is not inside any digest preimage; the ordering the controller MUST follow is key-management.md 3.6.3 and the named encoding.md §3.1 exemption on the payload field.

requested_scope.description: Required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling, not a grant. Later key scopes, Realm grants and session requests MUST NOT exceed its actions, resource selectors or mandatory constraints. Participation is an independent action-time deny gate and cannot restore authority omitted here. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants.

controller_station_id.description: Authenticated controller account Station. Together with the session principal_id this selects the controller authority; PCR identifiers are not exposed.

agent_provision_response_body.description: Four-stage outcome. prepare returns awaiting_controller_event with an accepted inception commitment. An accepted ak.agent.provision moves it to awaiting_pcr_genesis. PCR acceptance moves it to awaiting_did_binding until the controller-authored continuous WebVH update publishes the exact Realm service entry. The Agent, pairing handle and list/get projection become visible only at complete.

did.description: Complete Agent DID whose registered adapter projection is agent_id; Agent PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST commit this value and its verified method head.

initial_resolution.description: Exact verified accepted inception position. It is immutable across all provisioning outcomes and is copied byte-for-byte into Agent PCR genesis.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived locally as retype(event_id) of the Agent PCR genesis it froze, and declared in the provision payload. Until that genesis is accepted this is a claim, not a live Realm.

controller_realm_id.description: Authenticated controller PCR in which the provision Event must be authored. Present only while status is awaiting_controller_event.

allocation_handle.description: Service-signed opaque allocation binding returned only by prepare and presented unchanged by commit.

agent_renew_pairing_request_body.description: Re-open bootstrap pairing or replace an agent runtime. The service issues a fresh one-time pairing_request_id + pairing_code; every previously issued pairing handle for the agent becomes permanently unresolvable. An Agent with no active accepted runtime-key authorization re-opens bootstrap pairing; an Agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle active or paused) performs runtime replacement re-pairing with a different raw Ed25519 signing key. Reusing the replaced key is rejected; same-key reauthorization is not pairing. Lifecycle intent, existing keys and grants stay untouched until the new controller-signed authorization with an exact supersedes set is accepted atomically, and completion preserves lifecycle intent. deactivated rejects.

agent_renew_pairing_response_body.description: Fresh single-use opaque pairing handle and uniformly generated eight-digit decimal CSPRNG code. Attach or replacement is derived at approval from the complete current authorization set. Renew does not change principal, slug, lifecycle, keys, grants or history and never gates on sibling slug availability.

requested_scope_digest.description: Unchanged digest of the immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID binding; the complete scope remains controller-private.

agent_pairing_bootstrap.description: One-time bootstrap material handed to an Agent runtime after provisioning. New resolver responses MUST include runtime_identity; its omission is only for reading older stored bootstrap material. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret.

agent_pairing_runtime_identity.description: Identity context obtained from the accepted Agent/controller binding. It does not authorize the runtime key. The verification method controller MUST project to bootstrap.agent_id; its fragment is a key label, not a human device identity.

agent_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for short agent pairing handoff links. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.self.agent.pause Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. The service submits these exact bytes through authority Event submission and never synthesizes an Agent-authored Event. Its optional payload.reason MUST equal the request reason exactly (both absent or the same string).

Closed ak.self.agent.resume Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. Sidecar desired membership is re-derived from accepted lifecycle and exact Realm membership after admission; the request carries no writable Sidecar roster or acknowledgement.

The single controller-authorized terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Event. Once accepted, lifecycle is an unavoidable AND gate that makes every subordinate runtime key, session, pairing handle, capability grant, KeyPackage, presence and future submission ineffective. Cleanup Events are not part of this request. Optional payload.reason MUST equal request reason.

provisioning_phase.description: Closed reconciliation phase. Clients derive localized explanatory text from this phase; no parallel reason string is carried.

authority_stream_head.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted accepted Event IDs for Sidecar genesis, ownership, Agent lifecycle/runtime-key authorization, and exact Realm membership. It excludes action grants, participation selections, and MLS/key-readiness results. Same value and bound as the signed mls_governance_binding.authority_stream_head.

current_controller_device_ready.description: True only when the authenticated controller session device is the accepted genesis creator device or has completed matching Welcome and KeyPackage consume evidence.

desired_agent_ids.description: Read-only projection derived at the Sidecar stream's committed head: active, runtime-key-authorized Agent principals owned by the Sidecar controller and also active members of sidecar.realm_id. It is not caller-authored or reducer-stored and cannot be edited through Sidecar operations.

effective_agent_ids.description: Desired Agent principals that are members of the current accepted Sidecar MLS epoch and have completed target-device Welcome/KeyPackage consumption and key readiness. Reducer/service MUST enforce this set is a subset of desired_agent_ids. The controller is represented by sidecar.controller_account_id and is not duplicated in either Agent array.

version.description: Account Authority CAS version for this exact agent/scope selection.

expected_version.description: Value to echo verbatim into the next participation replace for this exact agent/scope selection.

next_replace_input.description: Verbatim prepare input for the next ak.self.agent.participation.resource.replace.v1 of this entry; member names match the replace request byte-for-byte per the service-http-binding.md 2.2.2 echo-container discipline. A first-ever selection has no entry row and uses expected_version 0. At the maximum signed-64 version it MUST be absent: the selection is exhausted and no next replace can be prepared.

contract.description: Controller-authored payload that creates one Agent provisioning fact. One accepted reducer transaction atomically writes FOUR typed current state from it -- the provisioning fact, the accountability endorsement, the controller-scoped selector binding and the principal_control_realm_id claim -- and MUST NOT expose a partially completed state. zh/identity/key-management.md sections 3.6 and 3.6.3, zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md, zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md and zh/extensions/applet-integration.md all enumerate the same four; this description used to name only two, which reads as a licence for the accountability/selector two-Event fan-out that conformance-profiles.md explicitly forbids. The containing Event proof is the only signature; this payload carries no nested proof.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id this provision forward-declares. The controller freezes the Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope locally, computes its event_id and writes retype(event_id, "realm") here; that genesis Event is not yet submitted when this payload is authored, and it MUST be submitted separately afterwards rather than alongside this Event. This is the named class C exemption ak.exemption.preimage_identity.agent_provision_principal_control_realm_id.v1 registered under encoding.md §3.1: the genesis preimage carries no reference to this Event, so the dependency stays one-way. Genesis admission reverse-looks-up this declaration; a service MUST NOT choose the value.

contract.description: Controller-signed, verifier-bound private disclosure of an Agent's immutable requested_scope. This object is authorization evidence, not a grant. It MUST travel only over an authenticated confidential presentation/operation channel and MUST NOT be written to a public DID Document, durable Realm Event, public registry, pairing code, or notification. The verifier consumes request_id/challenge once, validates the short presentation window, verifies a current controller proof, recomputes the requested-scope commitment against the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, and then applies the Agent ceiling subset rules. After successful one-time admission, an implementation MAY retain the object only as encrypted verifier-private evidence keyed by the recomputed digest, verifier_id and audience.

request_id.description: Identifier of the verifier's authenticated private challenge request. It is single-use at verifier_id.

requested_scope.description: Complete immutable Agent ceiling disclosed only to the bound verifier. It does not grant any action or resource.

verifier_id.description: Exact verifier named by the presentation request. A different verifier MUST NOT accept or forward this disclosure as its own evidence.

audience.description: Exact origin, service audience, or canonical operation audience requested by verifier_id.

challenge.description: Verifier-generated unpredictable challenge. The (verifier_id, request_id, challenge) tuple is single-use; replay MUST fail closed.

expires_at.description: Presentation admission expiry. expires_at MUST be later than issued_at and expires_at - issued_at MUST NOT exceed 300 seconds. It does not change the immutable ceiling; it only bounds disclosure delivery/replay.

proofs.description: At least one current controller proof. The proof verification method MUST belong to controller_principal_id or one of its currently authorized devices. payload_digest is sha256(canonical_json(this object with proofs omitted)); detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.agent_requested_scope_disclosure_proof.v1', payload_digest, agent_id, controller_principal_id, verifier_id, audience, challenge, verification_method, created_at}).

contract.description: Closed typed binding that ties one native-Sidecar-scoped Message event to one source-routed exchange. It is legal only inside encrypted metadata plaintext of an event whose scope_ref.kind is sidecar. It is the only normative way to declare an explicit user-facing response; invalid or absent bindings are non-echo. See zh/models/sidecar.md.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity copied verbatim from the request binding. It is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT appear in shared events, plaintext metadata, publish output, push previews, notifications, public telemetry, account-data keys, or any public/shared surface.

role.description: Closed disposition. request: the controller's private request event itself. user_facing_response: an Agent response the controller MAY echo after validation. internal: exchange-scoped Agent collaboration/tool output that MUST NOT be echoed. Consumers MUST fail closed to non-echo on any value not listed here.

request_event_id.description: Accepted Event id of the private request event of the same exchange. Event id is the only canonical reference form; Message ids MUST NOT be used here.

completes_exchange.description: Optional coordinator completion request; legal only with role=user_facing_response. It does not itself make the exchange terminal. A controller device validates the actor against coordinator_assignment_event_id and, on success, authors a durable ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event with action=close.

coordinator_assignment_event_id.description: Request Event id for the initial coordinator assignment, or the accepted reassign_coordinator control Event id. Required only when completes_exchange=true.

request_context.description: Write-once exchange identity carried only on role=request. It is the single durable source of the projection's write-once fields: any controller device rebuilding the projection copies these values verbatim, so cross-device bit-identity is anchored to the accepted request event instead of device-local state. Forbidden on response/internal roles.

coordinator_agent_id.description: Initial coordinator. It MUST be one of addressed_agent_ids. It MAY be omitted only when addressed_agent_ids contains exactly one item, in which case that sole item is implied.

contract.description: Closed plaintext encrypted inside the payload of ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. Only the Sidecar controller may author this durable private-Strand Event. It is the sole source of coordinator reassignment and terminal exchange state.

basis_event_ids.description: Canonical UTF-8 byte-order sorted maximal causal heads of exchange facts observed when this control was authored. The outer Event refs MUST contain role=after for every id, and the request Event must be causally covered.

response_event_ids.description: Exact canonical set of validated user-facing response Event ids causally covered by basis_event_ids. Required for every terminal action, including an empty array.

failure_reason_code.description: Required only for action=fail. close/cancel derive empty-response failure codes controller_closed_empty/controller_cancelled.

coordinator_agent_id.description: New coordinator for action=reassign_coordinator. It MUST be addressed by the request and eligible at authoring time.

contract.description: Disposable controller-device-local cache for one source-routed native Sidecar exchange. Every field is a deterministic fold of accepted Sidecar-scoped Events. This object is not wire truth, is not Account Data, is never merged across devices, and may always be deleted and rebuilt.

source_event_id.description: Optional accepted Event id copied from the request context as the source Event for this exchange. This identifies one Event, not a checkpoint or trust anchor.

terminal_event_id.description: Controller-authored ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event that produced complete or failed.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity; it is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT be copied into shared events.

folded_checkpoint.description: Local cache coverage. event_ids are the canonical sorted maximal causal heads of all contributing accepted exchange facts. event_set_digest commits to the canonical sorted complete contributing Event-id set. max_hlc is display/cache metadata only and never proves causal dominance.

contract.description: Controller-private encrypted account-data plaintext for one hosted Sidecar context. It changes only private presentation and never mutates either Strand, Track, access, read state, notifications, search, or event ownership.

Controller-account-owned private AI workspace bound one-to-one to (realm_id, controller_account_id). Agent Sidecar is a first-class native protocol scope, not a Circle profile, backing Circle, or editable membership container. See spec/v1/zh/models/sidecar.md.

current_binding.description: Same-cut current effective installation of the authenticated Service in the exact Applet scope. Historical material access and creation confirmation do not require active status. Unknown authority or dependencies fail the entire read.

contract.description: Closed preview, commit, and outcome DTOs for receiver-side Applet-managed Bot provisioning. The commit carrier is exactly the signed authoring request plus its role-neutral managed-actor bundle.

execution_response_body.description: Runtime may return a signed creation candidate Event; created/reused is permitted only with the original governance acceptance Commit. Candidate generation is not identity acceptance. Administrator intent is bound to the exact candidate before approval and Event submission.

contract.description: base64url_no_pad(JCS) metadata for an accepted Realm Bot/Ghost Device HTTP signature. Exact full actor, current generation, Device bounds and current installation are checked at the owning Realm current governor; no AccountId or SessionGrant is inferred.

nonce.description: Independent random request nonce with at least 128 bits of entropy, signed inside the closed metadata.

contract.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Applet edge and bridge operations.

applet_transaction_request_body.description: Body for ak.edge.applet.command.transaction.v1. Transport-layer requirements are mandatory but not body fields: RFC 9421 Signature/Signature-Input, Source-Service-ID, Destination-Service-ID, Content-Digest, Idempotency-Key, received_at audit metadata, and a persisted delivery_authentication_record. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md section 7.3.1. Event/Signal delivery and managed-actor completion are mutually exclusive closed branches. Completion is allowed only in the node-to-Applet direction.

status.description: Closed transaction result: all items accepted, a mixed result, or all items rejected.

committed_event_refs.description: Exact committed references for every durable Event accepted by this transaction. The array is empty when only Signals were accepted. A successful or partial outcome cannot be represented by status alone.

applet_event_transaction_request_body.description: Producer Event submission, committed Event delivery, and/or Signal delivery under the existing per-delivery source authentication rules; at least one non-empty array is required. events is Applet-to-Station only; committed_events is Station-to-Applet only.

applet_id.description: Exact active Applet registration selected for signature and epoch verification; service_id alone is not unique.

source_id.description: Must exactly match the Source-Service-ID header and the signed source-service-id component. It identifies the source service only; each Event still requires independent actor/applet/capability signature verification.

events.description: Original producer-only business Events; native Realm actor control Events use the registered self submission controller authentication, not Applet Service transport as a substitute.

signals.description: Optional encrypted Signal Extension envelopes. Exact applet payload types and targets remain inside ciphertext.

applet_committed_event.description: Original committed business Event. Account Device actual producers require producer_device_evidence only; Realm Device actual producers require producer_signer_fact only; all other producers forbid both. Actor, method, EventId and fact digest must match the original covering Commit. Private realm_control delivery uses exact material only.

producer_device_evidence.description: Required exactly when the original actual producer is an Account whose proof verification_method fragment is an ak:device: id; forbidden otherwise. The immutable complete origin Station evidence is retained at original admission and its attestation/native Service history and original Event JWS are verified at the covering Commit committed_at, never receiver current time. It conveys no PCR log, current device authority, new read right or SessionGrant.

applet_managed_actor_authoring_context.description: Current governor signed exact own control material. The runtime verifies request/audience/nonce, original Event/Commit and its retained private keys before using an accepted identity. No PCR or separate source Station.

applet_authoring_transaction_request_bod.description: Exclusive node-to-Applet completion delivery. The reverse direction is forbidden. The Applet persists the whole authoring context and exact source binding before returning accepted; partial installation is forbidden.

contract.description: Closed preview, commit, and outcome DTOs for receiver-side Applet-managed Ghost provisioning. The commit carrier is exactly the signed authoring request plus its role-neutral managed-actor bundle.
The single closed Station preview to Applet authoring carrier for install_bot and provision_ghost. No install-only operation, branch-specific bundle aliases, or derived request identifier exists.

managed_actor_proof.description: Closed Applet managed-actor request/bundle proof. audience_id is the exact recipient service DidCoreId: basis.service_id for the request and basis.target_station_id for the bundle. It is an identity binding, not a generic string or multi-audience selector.

install_authoring_request_basis.description: Administrator-authored service installation intent. No Bot or Ghost is created by service installation.

ghost_authoring_request_basis.description: Bounded creation intent at the owning Realm current governance Station. Runtime creates one independently controller-signed candidate and Service-signed Event; governance verifies the exact candidate and commits it via the standard Event submission. No Account/PCR aggregate.

governance_station_id.description: Current governance Station service identity for the target Realm. The Station signs the resulting RealmCommit after revalidating the authoring request at the stream head.

bot_authoring_request_basis.description: Bounded creation intent at the owning Realm current governance Station. Runtime creates one independently controller-signed candidate and Service-signed Event; governance verifies the exact candidate and commits it via the standard Event submission. No Account/PCR aggregate.

contract.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ak.self.applet.install.command.preview.v1, ak.self.applet.command.install.v1, and ak.self.applet.command.revoke.v1. The InstallPlan body itself is defined in applet-install-plan.schema.json.

capability_revoke_events.description: Exactly one caller-signed ak.capability.revoke initial submission for every active grant in the recomputed plan.

membership_state_events.description: Caller-signed membership removals in the plan, or an empty array when the install owns no managed membership.

expected_revision.description: Exact revision of the same active capability_grant current state returned by the governing Station in this preview plan. It is covered by the canonical plan digest and MUST be copied byte-for-byte into the caller-signed ak.capability.revoke payload.

revoke_plan.description: Canonical exact revoke plan. The preview carries no revoke_plan_digest: the caller computes SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of this plan and submits that value as applet_revoke_request_body.revoke_plan_digest.

applet_revoke_step.description: Closed state-dependent saga step. Event steps use the immutable submitted EventId before acceptance and the exact CommittedEventRef only after acceptance or duplicate resolution. Local effects always use a non-Event typed resource reference.

applet_revoke_effect_ref.description: CommittedEventRef for a durable revoke Event, or a local typed resource reference for service-local widget token or fence effects. Bare EventId and RealmCommitId strings are not valid effect references.

applet_revoke_local_effect_ref.description: Typed service-local revoke effect reference. EventId and RealmCommitId are forbidden because only Event admission can produce a committed Event coordinate.

contract.description: Canonical plan returned by ak.self.applet.install.command.preview.v1 and recomputed by ak.self.applet.command.install.v1 before commit. plan_digest is calculated over the canonical InstallPlan object with plan_digest omitted.

Controller-signed package used to install an Applet. The package is a distribution object, not Realm history truth and not a grant. The Station authorization capability derives ak.applet.registration and capability grants during ak.applet.install.

package_id.description: Distribution identifier only. Not a grant subject.

controller_principal_id.description: Accountable human or organization publisher principal. The Applet runtime service_id is never accepted as this controller.

proof.description: Controller DID detached proof over the canonical package or derived registration object. proof.payload_digest MUST equal package_digest (proof over canonical package) or the derived registration object digest. Empty object is invalid.

detached_proof.description: Controller-DID detached-JWS proof shape, aligned with event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof (the generic non-Event signed-object proof). Non-Event objects bind their canonical payload via payload_digest; Event proofs MUST instead use event_digest and event_proof.

webhook_signature_policy.description: HTTP message signature verification policy for transaction push. key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used to verify the app/bridge->arkret inbound HTTP message signature. Verifiers MUST take its bare controller did, validate it with the registered method adapter, and require project(did) to equal service_id (did_core_id); direct DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden. The key is bound to the effective registration_epoch. accepted_signature_algorithms pins the acceptable RFC 9421 signature algorithms.

key_ref.description: DID URL under an Applet service did whose registered adapter projection equals service_id. For app/bridge->arkret inbound transaction push, Signature-Input keyid MUST equal this value. Node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service did/key binding selected by the Source-Service-ID did_core_id, not this field.

endpoint_policy.description: Supported Applet API endpoints and their auth requirement.

limits.description: Service-side resource hints derived into the registration manifest.

ghost_policy.description: Ghost Actor support and accountability template. enabled defaults to false semantics; an explicit boolean is required.

delegation_policy.description: Delegated native-user acting request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

e2ee_policy.description: MLS join request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

widget.description: Optional Applet widget declaration. When present, it MUST validate ak.schema.applet_widget_declaration.v1.

contract.description: Versioned Applet service DID evidence used to derive a stable registration epoch and Service signer evidence root. Only did:webvh and did:key are accepted; did:web current snapshots cannot support historical producer verification.

Closed, normalized security transcript hashed to produce an Applet registration_epoch. The hash input is the UTF-8 domain separator arkret-applet-registration-epoch-v1\n followed by the JCS bytes of this object. Applet producer identity is restricted to versioned did:webvh or stable did:key so the same accepted state can form a historical Service signer root.

string_set.x-arkret-canonical-order: Sort by canonical encoded element bytes; elements MUST be unique.

did.description: Complete service DID whose adapter projection MUST equal derived_registration.service_id.

contract.description: Closed declaration for an Applet UI widget origin, CSP, scoped token capability scope, and consent gate.

widget_origin.description: Canonical HTTPS Web Origin only: lowercase scheme and host plus an optional valid non-default port. Userinfo, path (including a trailing slash), query, fragment, explicit :443, and out-of-range ports are forbidden.

csp.description: Content-Security-Policy that the host client MUST enforce for the widget document.

token_scope.description: Maximum capability scope for the short-lived widget token.

contract.description: Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ak.applet.* MUST use the typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json; this object is not a loose transport envelope and is closed at the top level except for x_* extensions.

applet_id.description: Stable canonical Applet identifier. Service identity is carried separately in service_id.

service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the service that hosts the applet runtime; current resolution is supplied by its authenticated service definition.

contract.description: The single approval evidence type of v1 (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2). One approver signs one exact target: either a fully authored Event that has not been submitted yet, or the original typed RequestBody of one operation whose evidence carrier is registered in capability-action-registry.json. The object is not an Event, never enters Realm history, and MUST NOT be written into an EventEnvelope, a signed payload or an Event semantic_refs[] entry. It travels in the carrier registered for the approved action. It proves that an approver approved that target; it proves nothing about the initiator's own authority.

approval_signature_input.description: The complete signed semantics. signing_bytes are UTF8("ak.approval.signature.v1") || 0x0A || JCS(input): the registered primitive is the signing input itself, never a JSON digest that is signed in a second step. JCS orders object keys, so this schema fixes no field order. Every member is required and the object is closed: a missing or extra member is a schema_violation, not a signature_invalid, and an absent member MUST NOT be reconstructed as null or as a local default.

request_canonical_digest.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the original input selected by approval_target: the complete authored Event including its own producer proof for the event branch, the original typed RequestBody for the operation branch. The evidence container is outside that original input and never contributes to this digest. This digest and the HTTP Content-Digest over the actually transmitted body, which does include the evidence container, are two independent checks; each MUST be performed and neither substitutes for the other.

operation.description: The registered operation token of the entry point that carries this execution, as listed in registry/operation-registry.json. An unregistered value is a schema_violation. It pins which entry point the approval was given for, so the same action replayed through another operation MUST fail.

action.description: The approved capability action token, identical to the element of the grant actions[] array that the execution matches (zh/authz/capabilities.md section 5).

realm_id.description: The Realm the approved action happens in. It stops cross-Realm replay of one approval.

initiating_actor_id.description: The exact ActorId that initiates this execution, carrying the complete account identity rather than a bare principal. One approval does not authorize another Account of the same principal: replay from a different Station MUST be rejected.

approver_did.description: The approver that issues this approval. The verification method in proof MUST resolve through this DID, and it MUST have been unrevoked at approved_at.

approved_at.description: The signing instant. A reducer MUST apply the future-only guard registered as ak.time_tolerance.approval_approved_at.v1 in contract-registry.json#protocol_time_tolerance_registry. For the grant context it MUST also reject approved_at earlier than that grant's issued_at, and earlier than the not_before of that grant's temporal grant-constraint when it carries one. A capability grant has no top-level not_before of its own: its validity window lives on grant-constraint.schema.json with constraint_kind temporal, so an implementation MUST read the bound from there rather than from a grant member that does not exist. Accepted history is verified against the accepted-at evidence, so a later approver key rotation or revocation MUST NOT invalidate an already accepted Event.

nonce.description: Approver-private, per-approval unique random string carrying at least 128 bits of entropy. Its namespace is (approval_context, approver_did) and it MUST NOT be shared with the ak.agent.action_approve confirmation nonce, with any challenge, or with any other signature evidence. It is consumed only when the target is successfully accepted, in that same transaction.

approval_signature_proof.description: The single detached signature over signing_bytes. It is a locally anchored signing domain, not the shared event-envelope detached-proof leaf: that leaf signs a binding object carrying a payload_digest, whereas this domain registers the signing input itself. proof is never a member of input, so no container field outside input is covered. verification_method is not signed and carries no authority of its own: it only selects a key, and it MUST resolve through the signed approver_did, so substituting it yields an invalid signature.

verification_method.description: Selects the approver key through authenticated history at input.approved_at. For a WebVH principal, identity-did.md section 3.4 also permits the exact native did:key:<multibase>#<multibase> of an effective updateKeys member at that instant; its bare did:key is never the approver identity. No caller-supplied key or synthetic fragment can establish this control relation.

jws.description: Compact detached JWS whose payload is signing_bytes. The signature algorithm comes from registry/signature-alg-registry.json; this domain introduces no second proof suite and no locally assembled key material.

approval_context.description: Which independent requirement this signature answers. The closed branches are grant, realm_governance, list_wip and management. A qualified grant-context vote MAY count separately toward grant and Realm governance requirements; each quorum remains independent. List WIP binds the exact List metadata revision and cannot cross-count. Management binds a private durable request ledger, its exact operation and effective scope; neither other contexts nor Agent confirmation replace it (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2; zh/authz/managed-governance.md section 3).

grant_id.description: The approval requirement carried by one specific capability grant (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.1). It MUST be one of the satisfied dependency grants of this execution.

approval_target.description: The exact approved target, which also selects the original input of request_canonical_digest. An approval MUST NOT bind a bare principal, a displayable target name or part of a payload instead.

event_id.description: The complete content-bound id of the target Event. The target Event is fully authored and producer-signed but not yet submitted when the approval is signed, so this id is already fixed when the approver computes signing_bytes and is never a function of the approval. This object is not an Event and this field sits outside the preimage of every Event digest, so no content-addressing order is constrained by it. Attaching approval signatures MUST NOT change event_id: they ride in the submission container, outside the Event.

contract.description: Compact signer-key evidence binding a resolved key to one authority-committed stream revision.

submit_request_body.description: One ordinary producer Event with the approval signatures its two approval layers require for the Event action or for this registered submit operation, or one atomic MLS Commit plus all recipient Welcome deliveries required by that Commit. The ordinary branch is EventAdmissionSubmission itself, not a second declaration of it: the approval evidence a constraint demands has to be carriable on the primary ingress, otherwise no execution could ever satisfy the constraint (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.5).

self_submit_request_body.description: Closed self Event-submit union: single producer Event, MLS Commit, and exactly the registered ordinary Realm bootstrap, Direct Conversation founding, membership compensation or audit_paired_event unit. Shared atomic execution rules are in authority-commit-log section 5.1 and contract-registry.atomic_unit_registry; each registered branch retains its own typed shape and admission policy. No arbitrary events[] or atomic=true.

self_submit_response_body.description: Closed self Event-submit outcome union. Aggregate outcomes cannot be parsed as an ordinary single-Event outcome.

peer_submit_request_body.description: Closed authority-forward, committed-replication and registered-atomic-unit ingress. Ordinary Account and Agent evidence rules remain. Realm actor first admission routes directly to its owning Realm governor, whose original control/Device facts are local; committed replication uses original minimal realm_device signer facts. No foreign Applet Account/PCR provenance or scope-confirmation carrier.

mls_genesis_material.description: authority_forward event branch only. Required when event_submission.event.kind is ak.mls.genesis and forbidden for every other kind: the raw GroupInfo and ratchet_tree bytes of the two content-addressed Blobs the Genesis references, read by the forwarding Station (the creator's Account Station) from its own Blob store. The governance Station hashes each under its ref's embedded suite, compares with the Genesis payload refs, rejects a mismatch with digest_mismatch and zero writes, and stores both as public Blobs inside the acceptance transaction (zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 5.1.2).

producer_device_evidence.description: authority_forward only. Complete account_device evidence for a cross-Station real Account Device producer (Human or accepted Applet-managed), freshly signed by the forwarding Station (the producer's account Station) from the same durable cut as its live gate before every forwarding attempt and persisted with its ref before sending; never a cached or keys/query-returned object. The governance Station verifies Source-Service-ID equals attestation.account_id.station_id, the attestation signature under the carried Service history at attested_at, now earlier than attestation expires_at, the original authorization_window covering both Event created_at and now, device_status active, and exact producer AccountId/device fragment/key binding, and persists the complete object and ref inside the acceptance transaction for audit only. An exact duplicate Event returns its original outcome before evidence freshness is checked. event_authorization is required, covers the exact original Event and destination/canonical body, and freezes independent original authorization coordinates, revision, PCR tenure and source accepted_at. The complete evidence remains private audit; only the separately committed minimal fact is replicated.

peer_submit_response_body.description: Closed peer Event-submit outcome union. Replication reports one same-order item result for every input; registered units report exactly one indivisible outcome.

committed_event_submission.description: One exact source canonical Event inside an EventAdmissionSubmission containing only event, paired with the source-signed RealmCommit that accepted it. Private approval_signatures are forbidden on committed replication and stay in the governance Station's accepted-at audit. event_submission.event.event_id MUST equal source_commit.event_ref; realm and stream coordinates, governance generation, current source authority signature and previous_commit_ref continuity MUST verify exactly. The receiver does not redo the source admission approval. This shape accepts only the full producer Event, never a withheld or projection-only read view. For every ak.mls.commit, genesis_event_ref is required, frozen from the exact accepted group Genesis in the governance acceptance transaction, and covered by the authenticated canonical peer request; it is forbidden for other kinds. The receiver binds it to the exact Commit and immutable group provenance in the same replica transaction and never infers it from base_group_state_ref. welcomes is allowed only when the source Event is ak.mls.commit and carries exactly the MlsWelcomeDelivery objects of that Commit whose recipients the destination Station hosts, in submission order; the destination re-verifies each claim against its own claim ledger and queues the passing Welcomes in the same replica transaction as the Commit (zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 2.2). Every source Commit carrying producer_signer_fact_digest requires exactly the matching immutable historical_producer_signer_fact branch for its actual producer; a fact without the digest is forbidden. Receiver checks exact Event/actual producer/method and sender-specific device or registration/install/scope, original Commit digest and true Event Ed proof, retaining fact with canonical Event/Commit atomically. The fact does not replace admission/current membership or approval evidence.

event_submission.description: Only the exact source Event; approval_signatures is forbidden in committed replication and remains in the governance Station's private accepted-at audit.

genesis_event_ref.description: Immutable exact accepted Genesis EventId for the effective scope and MLS group of an ak.mls.commit. Required for every replicated MLS Commit, forbidden otherwise; signed peer-body metadata, not a recipient guess or a replacement for governance-side provenance verification.

welcomes.description: Exact producer-signed Welcome deliveries of this ak.mls.commit for recipients hosted by the destination Station, written into this outbox intent by the governance Station inside the Commit acceptance transaction. Absent for every other Event kind and when the destination hosts no recipient of the Commit.

mls_genesis_material.description: Raw epoch-0 public material of one forwarded ak.mls.genesis: the exact bytes of the GroupInfo and ratchet_tree Blobs named by the Genesis payload group_info_ref and ratchet_tree_ref, as unpadded base64url. It carries no ref or digest echo; the refs in the signed Genesis are the only digest carrier. Each member is at most 5592406 characters, so each decodes to at most 4194304 bytes and the two together never exceed 8388608 bytes, the ak.peer.mls.read.group_state_material.v1 response bound; a longer member is schema_violation and there is no separate aggregate bound.

peer_committed_replication_response_body.description: Per-item replication outcome. replication_outcomes has exactly the same length and order as request.replications. Input order identifies each row, so an outcome does not repeat an index or source coordinates. rejected means that item was not stored. Transport retry replays the complete request body and returns the same outcomes. This branch has no accepted finality vocabulary.

ordinary_realm_bootstrap_unit_submission.description: Self-only ordinary Collaboration Realm bootstrap. The caller submits the complete registered ordered unit to one current governance Station. Slot 0 derives the Realm ID; all following Events use that Realm and the same actor authority. The optional alias and conditional plaintext-visible-services slots retain registry order. The Station validates all slots against staged state, then atomically stores one consecutive RealmCommit per Event, every registered typed result, idempotency outcome and outbox or stores none. No batch-level authority artifact or receipt exists.

idempotency_key.description: UUIDv7 whole-unit replay fence. Same key and identical canonical request return the original ordered RealmCommits; same key with different request bytes is duplicate_conflict.

events.description: Exactly the ordinary_collaboration ordered slots in contract-registry.json.realm_bootstrap_registry. Runtime validation also checks the conditional visibility slot, all producer/approval proofs, staged authority-root evidence, exact Realm and actor bindings, and the final creator join.

ordinary_realm_bootstrap_creator_join_su.description: The final slot is the genesis actor's explicit member.state join with expected_revision null; the Station verifies payload and actor bindings against slot 0.

ordinary_realm_bootstrap_acceptance_outc.description: One indivisible ordinary Realm bootstrap outcome. The ordered commits match the submitted Events and form one consecutive source Realm stream chain. Exact whole-unit replay returns the same commits. No per-item partial success or batch-level receipt exists.

direct_conversation_founding_unit_submis.description: Self-only caller-authored Direct Conversation founding unit. The current Station recomputes authority from current evidence and therefore rejects a founding_authority_evidence echo. The four Events are accepted atomically in this exact order with consecutive RealmCommits: realm create, founder join, peer join, strand create. realm_id is retyped from events[0].event.event_id and main_strand_id from events[3].event.event_id.

idempotency_key.description: UUIDv7 founding-slot fence. Byte-identical replay returns the same four byte-identical source RealmCommits without changing the fourth committed_at; the same key with different canonical unit bytes is duplicate_conflict.

allOf.description: payload action MUST be join. The first occurrence is the founder and the second is the peer; the pair and Realm bindings must match the realm-create Event.

direct_conversation_founding_federation_.description: Peer-only source-committed Direct Conversation founding unit. The four committed rows have the same Event order as the self unit; their source commits have one Realm/generation/stream, consecutive positions and exact previous_commit_ref linkage. The receiver derives every coordinate from the four Events, verifies the source commits and bounded authority evidence, then materializes all four rows or none without re-signing commits or creating fanout. No second acceptance receipt or finality object exists.

direct_conversation_founding_acceptance_.description: One indivisible Direct Conversation founding outcome. Self first success, peer success and exact replay return the same four verified source commits. The commits are ordered like the unit and form one consecutive source chain; the fourth committed_at is the founding acceptance time. No receipt or per-item partial result exists.

peer_registered_atomic_unit.description: Closed source-committed atomic-unit union: Direct Conversation founding, membership compensation and audit_paired_event. No first admission or arbitrary Event collection.

membership_compensation_unit_submission.description: Self-only membership compensation aggregate. The enclosed Event is an ak.member.state leave/remove whose authorization_ref equals evidence.delegation.delegation_id. Evidence is transport-only and excluded from Event canonical bytes. The destination authority claims (admission_id, delegation_id) once in the same transaction as Event acceptance; mismatch, already absent, prior use or a superseding J2/new join is membership_compensation_conflict with zero writes.

membership_compensation_federation_submi.description: Peer-only source-committed membership compensation unit. The receiver verifies the full source Event/Commit pair and the unchanged compensation evidence, then atomically claims the same single-use binding and stores the source fact without re-signing a commit or fanout.

membership_compensation_evidence.description: Closed transport-only compensation evidence. The verifier recomputes delegation_id as ak:membership_compensation_delegation:sha256:<lowercase_hex SHA-256(JCS(core))>, verifies both signatures and exact join/admission/commit/executor bindings, and compares single_use_binding byte-for-byte. It is never inserted into Event canonical bytes.

membership_compensation_acceptance_outco.description: Atomic compensation outcome. committed and duplicate both carry the one authority-signed source commit. Exact full-body replay returns the same outcome; no per-item partial exists.

direct_conversation_founding_dependency_.description: Closed HTTP 409 application/problem+json response for a registered Direct Conversation founding unit whose bounded exact dependencies are not locally available. It is retryable only after canonical backfill/resolve and a new full-body request evaluation; no partial unit write occurred.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The closed endpoint problem retains the RFC literal type/title/status/detail/instance member vocabulary and adds one registered details member.

stream_scan_request_body.description: Positional single-stream scan request. Pagination is by stream_position, not by an opaque cursor: within one stream the governance Station's stream_position is a strict +1 total order, so the position IS the continuation token. Exactly one of after_position / before_position MUST be present; the exclusivity is structural (the oneOf below), so a request carrying both or neither is a schema violation and MUST NOT be repaired by picking a default direction. Both bounds are read inside the range this caller is permitted to read, never over the physical stream: null means 'from the oldest position this caller may read' (after_position) or 'from the newest position this caller may read' (before_position). Continuation is the caller's job: take the largest stream_position of this batch for after_position, the smallest for before_position.

after_position.description: Scan toward newer commits: return commits whose stream_position is strictly greater than this value, ascending. null starts at the oldest position this caller may read, which is position 0 only when that floor is the physical stream start; see stream_scan_response_body.readable_floor.

before_position.description: Scan toward older commits (history backfill): return commits whose stream_position is strictly smaller than this value, descending. null starts at the newest position this caller may read, which is not necessarily the physical stream head. The scan stops at the caller's readable floor; positions below that floor are unreadable rather than missing and are not a gap (zh/sync/client-sync.md section 12.3.3).

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of one caller's readable range on one stream. The anchor lets a member whose history is trimmed verify that its permitted prefix is complete without ever holding position 0: it proves where the accepted chain that caller may read begins, and it proves nothing about whether the Station holds further history below it or further updates above it.

oldest_position.description: Smallest stream_position this caller is permitted to read. Positions below it are unreadable, not missing: their absence MUST NOT be treated as a gap and MUST NOT be used to infer activity, membership or existence below the floor.

floor_commit_id.description: commit_id of the RealmCommit at oldest_position, so the boundary binds to the chain the caller has already accepted. The commit at the floor is the only readable commit allowed to carry a previous_commit_ref the caller cannot resolve, because its predecessor is outside that caller's range.

floor_reason.description: Why the range starts here. stream_start means the floor is the physical start of the stream and oldest_position is 0; the other two are trimmed ranges and MUST NOT be reported as stream_start. Retention never moves a floor: v1 never deletes an accepted RealmCommit and expired Events are returned through the withheld CommittedEventView branch.

stream_scan_response_body.description: Positional scan result over caller-visible committed Event views. There is no cursor or cross-stream order; continuation uses stream_position from committed_events[].

committed_events.description: Contiguous caller-visible committed Event views for the requested stream, ordered by RealmCommit stream_position. Full and withheld rows preserve the same verifiable Commit chain.

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of this caller's readable range on the requested stream. It MUST be present on every page whose scan reached that bottom (a before_position page with truncated false, and an after_position page whose first row is at it), MAY be present on any other page of the same stream, and MUST be omitted only when the caller may read no commit of this stream at all, which is also the only case in which an empty committed_events[] with truncated false is legal.

truncated.description: True when at least one further commit that this caller is permitted to read exists beyond this page in the requested direction, i.e. the scan stopped on limit. It is a statement about the caller's permitted range, never about the physical stream: a scan that stopped on the newest readable position (after_position) or on readable_floor.oldest_position (before_position) MUST set it false even when the Station holds further commits this caller may not read. History outside the caller's range MUST NOT set it, a page that stopped on the floor MUST NOT be presented as truncation, and truncated MUST NOT be used to conceal a floor. An empty committed_events[] with truncated false means the caller's permitted range is exhausted in that direction, never that the physical stream is empty or absent.

committed_event_ref.description: Closed exact reference to one authority-committed Event. All four coordinates are verified against the returned RealmCommit; none is a hint.

final_stream_heads.description: Private state-transfer manifest whose canonical digest equals handoff.final_stream_heads_digest. It is not included in the public authority bundle.

historical_signer_facts.description: Private complete canonical inventory at the frozen authority handoff cut: exact target set equals all imported digest-bearing Full Commit originals, without duplicates, missing or extra entries. Canonical order: JCS UTF-8 stream_ref, numeric stream_position, UTF-8 event_id, UTF-8 commit_id. Authority handoff covers all authorized streams; ordinary peer member floors remain separate. Existing request budget applies: limit_exceeded rejects without partial authority startup. No private PCR bodies. New handoffs require the inventory, including empty array.

realm_authority_handoff_request_body.description: Eligible Organization PCR only when this is a PCR: verified accepted genesis provenance must satisfy the PCR profile pcr_governance_policy before any freeze/export/import/acceptance/activation. Human, user-managed Agent and unresolved provenance reject without effects; no subject flag in this DTO grants eligibility.  Direct Conversation accepted genesis is permanently ineligible, even with valid signatures and complete imports; rejection has no effects.

account_device_historical_signer_fact.description: Minimal immutable original Account Device signer source, binding the complete Account actor, Device, actual verification method, key and original accepted time. Applet Realm Bot/Ghost devices use realm_device_historical_signer_fact instead. Native provenance is verified at acceptance, never inferred from proof shape. No current permission, verified flag or private PCR bytes.

peer_stream_scan_response_body.description: Peer-only authorized original rows and exactly one ordered original Commit-bound producer fact for every digest-bearing Full original, using the matching historical_producer_signer_fact branch for its actual producer. Withheld/redacted rows carry no fact. Handoff inventory covers the complete imported digest-bearing original target set, independent of member floors.

committed_events.description: Contiguous caller-visible committed Event views for the requested stream, ordered by RealmCommit stream_position. Full and withheld rows preserve the same verifiable Commit chain.

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of this caller's readable range on the requested stream. It MUST be present on every page whose scan reached that bottom (a before_position page with truncated false, and an after_position page whose first row is at it), MAY be present on any other page of the same stream, and MUST be omitted only when the caller may read no commit of this stream at all, which is also the only case in which an empty committed_events[] with truncated false is legal.

truncated.description: True when at least one further commit that this caller is permitted to read exists beyond this page in the requested direction, i.e. the scan stopped on limit. It is a statement about the caller's permitted range, never about the physical stream: a scan that stopped on the newest readable position (after_position) or on readable_floor.oldest_position (before_position) MUST set it false even when the Station holds further commits this caller may not read. History outside the caller's range MUST NOT set it, a page that stopped on the floor MUST NOT be presented as truncation, and truncated MUST NOT be used to conceal a floor. An empty committed_events[] with truncated false means the caller's permitted range is exhausted in that direction, never that the physical stream is empty or absent.

service_historical_signer_fact.description: Minimal immutable Applet Service producer source: original key, exact accepted registration epoch and installation authorization coordinates/scope. Frozen at target governance acceptance and bound by original Commit digest; no runtime completion, private Profile/control/history bodies or private signing material. This does not grant access to the source Events.

historical_producer_signer_fact_entry.description: Complete target association derived only after the original governance Commit exists. Fact digest excludes this outer target.

audit_paired_event_unit_submission.description: Exactly one producer-signed cross-actor business Event followed by its producer-signed audit Event. The same Realm, effective stream, complete actor and actual producer/key must bind both slots. Runtime checks the registered pair, one-way critical audit_pair ref, canonical Event IDs, current authorization and business CAS. Full canonical unit bytes and unique business/audit Event IDs are the replay fence; no caller-selected atomic batch or parallel UUID is added.

audit_paired_event_acceptance_outcome.description: Original source RealmCommits in business/audit order. Same stream, generation and consecutive positions; exact replay preserves the first outcome bytes. No unit-level acceptance receipt or new Event identity.

audit_paired_event_federation_submission.description: Source-committed business/audit pair only.
