Original proofs, signer facts, same-stream consecutive source Commits and authorized disclosure of both slots are verified before atomic materialization. Approval signatures, first-admission producer evidence and private audited-read outcomes are not copied. Missing/conflicting slot is zero-write refusal, never partial materialization or new finality.

atomic_slot_producer_evidence.description: One fixed admission slot actual-producer closure. Human Device reuses exact Event-bound forward evidence; Agent reuses its complete closure; a Service producer uses the empty branch and its existing Service history. Presence follows the actual producer, never caller choice. Exactly one family per slot.

audit_pair_producer_evidence.description: Fixed business/audit order; fresh actual-producer evidence for each original Event at one origin cut. Each Human event_authorization.event_id binds its own slot. Each forward_body_digest binds the entire canonical peer request with atomic_producer_evidence omitted. Empty slot is permitted only for actual Service producer. Same producer/key identity does not replace either Event-specific authorization.

pcr_private_handoff_manifest.description: Eligible Organization PCR only when this is a PCR: verified accepted genesis provenance must satisfy the PCR profile pcr_governance_policy before any freeze/export/import/acceptance/activation. Human, user-managed Agent and unresolved provenance reject without effects; no subject flag in this DTO grants eligibility. Private salted commitment to the complete frozen native-state export, retained only by verified old/new PCR governors; it never replaces actual complete import.

public_key_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes; this is public material, not reusable current authorization.

contract.description: A recovery or admission signer policy materialized by the current governance Station. It is not an offline publication lease.
Closed response DTOs for authorization query operations that need operation-specific list envelopes.
Closed request/response DTOs for blob service operations whose wire shape is not the full blob metadata resource.

kid.description: DID URL of the concrete issuer verification method. Bare DID is not accepted because the receipt must pin one already accepted service key binding.

content.description: The binary blob content part in multipart/form-data. This field is not JCS-canonicalized as JSON; content_digest covers the bytes.

media_type.description: The stored-byte MIME declaration. If the content part also declares a different MIME, reject before storage. Ciphertext uses application/octet-stream.

encryption.description: Required JSON multipart part, null for plaintext or minimal scheme classification for ciphertext. Persist before publishing the Blob; ciphertext is never eligible for bearer presign.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit event.

Content digest of the accepted ak.mls.genesis or winning ak.mls.commit Event, using the Event ID canonical preimage and digest suite. Re-encode the complete suite and digest bytes as EventId and use the same authenticated authorized winning-state resolution; possession is not authorization. The original key_ref remains AAD-bound.

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification.

content_key_salt.description: Canonical base64url-no-pad encoding of a fresh 32-octet CSPRNG per-object salt. MLS-Exporter and immutable AAD binding are defined in zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md section 3.0; this is public input, never the content key.

encrypted_attachment.description: Closed authenticated ContentBlock attachment descriptor. Required content_key_salt binds the per-object MLS-Exporter key and AEAD AAD; it is never upload metadata.

storage_encryption.description: Storage-visible encryption classification only; no plaintext MIME, plaintext size, nonce, group or key reference. Private attachment descriptors remain in authenticated Content Blocks.

realm_id.description: Owning Realm for authorization, asset privacy policy enforcement, retention and GC. MAY be omitted only for global / cross-Realm service blobs (e.g. avatar previews) explicitly authorized by the Blob Service deployment policy.

contract.description: Schedule subtree carried at Strand metadata.fields.calendar and activated by ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 in Strand.schema_refs. Both directions of that binding are enforced by strand.schema.json. All intervals are half-open [start, end). Timed events carry RFC 8984 LocalDateTime wall-clock anchors resolved through timezone plus tzdb_version; this schema never carries an absolute instant.

start.description: Inclusive lower bound of the event interval, and the recurrence anchor. Narrowed to local_date when all_day is true and to local_date_time when it is false.

end.description: Exclusive upper bound of the event interval, in the same shape as start. MUST be strictly later than start in both branches; a single all-day event spells end as the following date. JSON Schema cannot express the cross-field comparison, so reducers and profiles enforce it with schema_violation.

timezone.description: Canonical IANA Zone name in the release named by tzdb_version. Producers MUST resolve Link aliases to their canonical Zone before signing per calendar-timezone-registry.json; this pattern only constrains shape.

tzdb_version.description: IANA TZDB release tag (for example 2026a) whose rules resolve timezone and every derived instant. Signed with the schedule so receivers never silently substitute their locally installed release.

all_day.description: True selects the date branch of start/end/recurrence.until; false selects the whole-second LocalDateTime branch.

status.description: Whole-event schedule status. Required with no implicit default; distinct from the generic Strand stage and state axes. cancelled rejects new RSVPs and is schedule-relevant for notification.

call_id.description: Soft reference to an Arkret call session. It never widens access: an unresolvable or invisible call_id MUST NOT leak call state.

attendees.description: The single canonical schedule roster. Membership and invite projections are producer inputs only, never a second projection truth source. actor_id uniqueness is enforced by the reducer; at most one organizer is enforced here by maxContains.

recurrence.description: RFC 8984 RecurrenceRule snake_case subset. Omitted interval means 1, omitted first_day_of_week means mo, rscale is Gregorian and skip is omit; the JSCalendar @type discriminator is implied by this schema and MUST NOT appear on the wire. Unlisted RecurrenceRule members, excluded rules, overrides, RDATE and EXDATE are rejected rather than ignored.

until.description: Inclusive termination bound compared against the occurrence local start with <=. Narrowed to the same branch as start/end by all_day, and MUST NOT be earlier than the base start.

role.description: Attendance role. Omitted means required. organizer is display and scheduling semantics only and grants no capability.

display_name_snapshot.description: Identity-revealing display snapshot. It MUST be encrypted together with the rest of the schedule whenever Strand metadata is encrypted.

contract.description: Closed transient invitation relation, holder-authority cut and token join context. Does not extend the encrypted Signal envelope. Conformance: ak.vector.consent.call_invitation_admission.v1.

media.description: Exact normalized invitation media. Omitted screen in decrypted CallMediaSelection normalizes to false. At least one media flag is true; video or screen selects video_call, otherwise audio selects voice_call.

invitation_envelope.description: Producer-signed directional relation for one exact encrypted invitation and one holder. It is transient, not a Signal ID, Consent ledger, Call creator inference or participant authorization.

admission_request_body.description: Only the authenticated holder hosting Station or exact currently authorized media issuer may request a verdict from the current holder PCR authority. Not a requester API. A new nonce and current evaluation are required for every actual release cut.

authority_generation.description: Actual holder PCR governance tenure, independently verified from accepted inception and eligible authority continuity. Human stays at the account Station; same-Station endpoint/key changes do not advance this value. Never an authority-root delegation or device generation.

admission_decision.description: Minimal audience/request/stage-bound verdict, consumed only as the direct response to the outstanding fresh authorized request. Signature/TTL alone never authorize another cut. No Consent ID, revision, value, PCR head, existence or history is disclosed.

delivery_view.description: Own-Station delivery material attached only after the holder product gate. Client independently reads complete holder-private Consent current before ringing. This material never replays as a media-token verdict.

voluntary_join_context.description: Explicit affirmative join intent signed by the requesting actor/device over the complete token RequestBody with this proof omitted. It cannot be selected by receipt of an invitation, background retry, push handler or automatic fallback.

refresh_join_context.description: An authenticated request names the current accepted participant_id. The issuer independently resolves the exact full ActorId, real DeviceId, Realm, Call, focus and media from current accepted roster; this carrier alone grants no admission.

contract.description: Canonical metadata for a call recording artifact after it has entered the Arkret blob pipeline. It binds the blob, recording start event, MLS exporter recording key context, retention policy and deletion audit surface without introducing a ak:recording or ak:artifact storage key.

produced_by.description: Media service DID or recorder service DID that produced the encrypted recording bytes.

recording_initiator_capability_ref.description: Capability grant reference proving the recording was initiated by an actor holding ak.call.record.

deletion_audit.description: Present only after a delete attempt is scheduled, completed, or blocked. The referenced erasure receipt remains the durable audit proof.

call_recording_retention.description: Retention contract for a recording or transcript capture artifact. retention_expires_at is the earliest deletion time; deletion_trigger declares the only accepted purge cause; audit_lock blocks all purge paths until an audit-grade release is accepted; consent_confirmed records the required second client-side capture confirmation.

retention_expires_at.description: Earliest time the artifact MAY be purged. Absent = governed by retention_policy_id. MUST NOT be in the past at write time.

audit_lock.description: When true the artifact is under audit / legal hold; purge MUST be rejected with legal_hold_active until the lock is released by an audit-grade action.

consent_confirmed.description: Records that the second client-side confirmation required before recording or transcript capture was obtained.

trigger_event_id.description: Durable event that caused this delete attempt, when the trigger is event-backed.

erasure_receipt_ref.description: ak.audit.erasure_receipt event, ak.schema.erasure_receipt.v1 object, or digest proving the deletion outcome.

contract.description: Closed top-level plaintext object carried inside a SignalEnvelope encrypted_payload for ak.call.signal. The signal_kind-specific data object is validated by the corresponding normative branch in zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_actor_id, sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref); arbitrary forward gaps are accepted. The complete ActorId is part of the sequence domain. It is independent of seq, the per-call anti-rollback sequence monotonic over (realm_id, call_id, actor_id, device_id).

data.description: Signal-kind-specific payload. Producers and consumers MUST additionally validate the closed field rules for the selected signal_kind in webrtc-signaling.md; this extension point is encrypted end-to-end and is not interpreted by the Signal service.

owned_agent_authority_ref.description: Explicit terminal owned-Agent execution source, not general regrant or Realm root control. Exact controller and Agent join generations are pinned; current controller authority is reevaluated at each use. See zh/authz/owned-agent-authority.md.

issuer_id.description: Exact issuing actor. Its closed ActorId shape already contains the account routing authority when one exists; no parallel station sidecar is permitted.

items.description: Canonical action vocabulary. MUST be of the form ak.<segment>.<segment>... matching capabilities.md §5. Bare names without the ak. prefix are not permitted; consult capabilities.md before introducing new action names. Wildcards within a segment are not permitted in this schema; the resource selector controls scope, not action expansion.

constraints.description: Constraints applied to this grant. Re-grant control MUST be expressed via constraint_kind='authority_control' and max_authority_depth (see capabilities.md §10). A top-level 'delegable' field is forbidden and MUST be rejected as schema_violation. With no authority_control constraint the grant cannot be re-granted (equivalent to max_authority_depth=0).

issued_at.description: Grant issuance time — carries the 'creation time' semantics for a Capability Grant in place of the generic created_at (models/common-fields.md §3.2). Retention / audit / ordering queries MUST use issued_at, revoked_at and the expires_at of a temporal grant-constraint rather than falling back to created_at; this object carries no top-level not_before or expires_at, because validity windows are expressed by grant-constraint.schema.json with constraint_kind temporal.

status.description: Reducer-derived lifecycle status of this Grant (zh/authz/capabilities.md section 12.1). It is absent from the closed authoring body of ak.capability.grant and is materialised by the registered capability_status derivation, so an author-supplied value MUST be rejected rather than trusted. The two terminal values stay distinct because section 10.4 gives them different authorities: revoke is issuer or root-controller authority, relinquish is the target subject's own signature and MUST NOT require ak.capability.revoke. Collapsing them into revoked_at alone would erase which authority closed the Grant. A terminal value is final -- section 12.1 forbids resurrecting a closed grant_id -- and compaction MUST preserve it.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

updated_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp for the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

issuer_authority_refs.description: The signed semantic authority lineage this grant was issued under. A root controller's grant anchors on the accepted Realm authority Event; any further grant anchors on grants its issuer already holds. These closed refs intentionally carry no producer-selected current-state revision, authorization-state digest, Station id or commit basis: the governing Station resolves their current typed results at acceptance, fails closed when current authority cannot be proved fresh, and records the accepting RealmCommit as the decision basis. Authorization is recomputed from these refs on every decision, so revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants without a cascading write. The sole owned_agent ref is an explicit non-regrant exception; it pins ownership membership and continuously bounds the Agent by current controller authority.

oneOf.description: A grant the issuer holds. The issuer MUST be that grant's subject, and the ref MUST be active both at acceptance and evaluation time; its capability, resources and constraints all bound this child. Its current-state revision is an acceptance-time Station input, not a signed wire member.

authority_event_ref.description: The accepted Realm genesis or owner-transfer Event that established the issuing controller.

authority_generation.description: Realm authority-root delegation generation at issuance, read from the realm_authority_root current state. A ref stays valid only while that value's current authority_generation still equals this one, and the read MUST use the registered inclusion proof at a RealmCommit basis, never an unproven cache. ak.realm.authority.reset is the only kind that advances it, so it is the only act that invalidates a whole delegated generation; ak.realm.owner.transfer preserves it and therefore leaves every child grant valid. This is NOT the governing Station tenure, which is governance_generation on RealmCommit -- a planned Station handoff MUST NOT invalidate any grant.

oneOf.description: A committed authority root in the same Realm as the grant. It is terminal for cycle checks. The accepting Station verifies the named Event/controller/generation against durable current authority; the ref does not carry a Station-local commit wrapper.

authority_depth.description: Reducer-derived absolute distance from the authority root: a realm_root ref counts 0, so a root controller's grant is 1 and a member's re-grant is 2. Derived from the refs, never author-declared, so it cannot be misreported — which is what makes it safe to answer 'how far did this authority spread' with a single field instead of a recursive join. Taken at issuance and not recomputed on revocation; a later chain may be shorter than the recorded value, which is the conservative direction for a max_authority_depth decision. A dedicated terminal owned_agent source has depth 1 and cannot become a parent grant.

authority_root_refs.description: Reducer-derived set of committed authority roots this grant ultimately descends from: direct realm_root refs plus the union of every parent grant's roots. Deduplicated on (realm_id, authority_event_ref, authority_generation) and sorted canonically by unsigned-byte order. For an owned_agent source the sole root is that exact owned_agent ref; it never confers Realm root-control authority.

authority_generation.description: The delegation generation of the root this grant descends from, carried verbatim from the realm_root ref. Part of the dedup key, because the same root at a different generation is a different authority.

contract.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Circle administration operations (ak.self.circle.*). Every write operation carries the caller-signed ak.circle.* Event and the service submits those exact bytes through authority Event submission; the durable Circle object model is circle.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md. Read-receipt policy has only the ak.scope.read_receipt_policy writer and scope_read_receipt_policy current carrier; it is not a Circle object or metadata patch member.

circle_view.description: Circle projection returned by create/get/lifecycle operations. MLS activation is derived from an accepted ak.mls.genesis in this Circle stream.

profile_ref.description: Create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it; profile-specific Circles expose it so clients can apply mandatory filtering.

mls_group_id.description: Reducer-derived from this Circle's circle-branch effective scope; both realm_id and circle_id enter the scope key bytes.

viewer_membership.description: The caller's own Circle membership state when one exists.

member_ids.description: Active Circle member ActorIds (strict subset of parent Realm.members). Empty after tombstone. The member count is derived as member_ids.length and is never carried as a separate wire field; directory-only previews never carry member_ids and use the privacy-bucketed preview contract instead.

circle_preview.description: Fixed directory-only response to a joined parent-Realm member who is not a Circle member. It never carries a private Circle field or Event reference.

circle_create_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event and nothing else. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service cannot name the Circle and MUST NOT synthesize the Event: every actor-supplied field lives in create_event.event.payload.object, and the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md. Read-receipt policy has only the ak.scope.read_receipt_policy writer and scope_read_receipt_policy current carrier; it is not a Circle object or metadata patch member.

create_event.description: Closed ak.circle.create Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. Admission requires the payload closed union and forbids id/mls_group_id. The reducer derives both identifiers. The Circle scope stays plaintext until its own ak.mls.genesis is accepted.

circle_member_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event and nothing else. The target actor and the membership value live in member_event.event.payload; the Circle is payload.circle_id and MUST equal the path circle_id. The service MUST NOT add a capability verdict to the payload it submits: circle_member_state_payload is closed, and the ak.circle.member.manage decision is the admission path's, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through authority Event submission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that payload.circle_id names the path Circle. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed by allowed_circle_ids. Every join payload carries parent_membership_revision, the exact typed revision of the target's current parent-Realm member_state join, and admission rejects it unless that current is join at exactly that revision (zh/models/circle.md §9.1); knock requires join_rule=knock. A self-service join is gated on the Circle join_rule instead.

circle_member_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state leave Event and nothing else. The path circle_id and actor_id MUST respectively equal member_event.event.payload.circle_id and payload.member_id; member_event.event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. The path name actor_id is a route selector only; the canonical Event payload identity field is member_id. The service submits the exact signed Event through authority Event submission and MUST NOT rebuild it or synthesize a leave Event.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with membership fixed to leave and expected_membership carrying the concrete current membership as the signed expected_revision guard. Admission MUST bind the Event proof to the exact account-local lineage selected by the authenticated session; matching only the caller DID is insufficient. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to the path Circle; self-service leave uses ak.circle.member.add.

note.description: Reducer-emitted reason code on Ignored / Rejected, or unsupported-feature note while MLS scope rotation is not wired end-to-end.

contract.description: Circle — an intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary with its own membership, history_access and optional independent MLS group. Parent Realm membership supplies only the current-membership intersection gate; history_access is never dynamically inherited. Read-receipt policy is not a Circle object member or metadata patch: ak.scope.read_receipt_policy is its sole writer and scope_read_receipt_policy its sole current carrier (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5).

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm. create-locked; Circle never re-binds to another Realm.

profile_ref.description: Optional create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it. Profile-specific creation paths MUST persist their registered profile id. Agent Sidecar is a separate ak.schema.agent_sidecar.v1 object and MUST NOT be represented by this field.

directory_visibility.description: Who may see this Circle exists as a directory entry. 'members' means only Circle members see its title/display/member_ids. 'realm_members' exposes directory metadata only and does NOT grant event or history access.

join_rule.description: public permits parent-Realm members to self-join; invite requires an authorized administrator using ak.circle.member.add.others with the required same-unit audit. v1 has no Circle invitation or acceptance workflow. All joins bind the exact current parent membership revision.

history_access.description: Circle's own governance history range ratchet, initialized by Circle create. The only state-changing update is all_history_for_current_members to since_join; widening is permanently forbidden. It is never dynamically inherited from or capped by the parent Realm history_access, while current access still requires active parent-Realm membership. Standard MLS requires since_join.

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped five-bit Agent ceiling. When present every bit is explicit and may only tighten the parent Realm ceiling.

mls_group_id.description: Reducer-derived from this Circle's circle-branch effective scope; both realm_id and circle_id enter the scope key bytes. Present only on the materialized MLS-backed Circle and forbidden in the actor-supplied create payload.

state.description: Circle lifecycle state. v1 defines active, archived, and tombstoned only; Circle has no independent freeze or destroy state because parent Realm freeze/destroy applies at the Realm boundary.

short_name.description: Human-facing short name. Unique per (realm_id, short_name) case-insensitive — reducer-enforced. Circle naming has no Sidecar-reserved prefix because Sidecar is a separate native scope.

color_token.description: Color token from the spec-controlled palette. Clients MUST map token -> theme color (light/dark/high-contrast) consistently across devices; clients MUST NOT reassign tokens.

contract.description: Closed frame union emitted by ak.self.committed_event.stream.subscribe.v1 over NDJSON or an Arkret WebSocket channel.

Shared ID and reference pattern $defs referenced cross-file by multiple object schemas so a single form change propagates without inline drift. Defs-only: not an object or event schema. See zh/models/common-fields.md and artifacts/registry/id-kind-registry.json for the authoritative ID kind registry.

event_id.description: Complete Arkret Event cryptographic identity. The suffix is the canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of exactly 33 octets: fixed current-v1 suite code 0x01 followed by all 32 octets of the SHA-256 Event digest. Regex validation is only lexical; receivers MUST decode, require 33 octets, require byte 0 == 0x01, canonical re-encode, and verify the full digest before use. Other registered digest suites remain available only to the typed domains that explicitly select them and MUST NOT appear in Event IDs.

realm_id.description: Retyped ak.realm.create Event token. It therefore carries the same fixed current-v1 0x01/SHA-256 content-address identity and is not selected by Realm state.

realm_commit_id.description: Content-addressed identity of a closed unsigned RealmCommit body. The suffix uses the fixed v1 digest suite and the same canonical 33-octet token encoding as Event IDs.

realm_authority_handoff_id.description: Content-addressed identity of one closed old-to-new Realm authority handoff.

realm_snapshot_id.description: Content-addressed identity of an authority-signed typed Realm snapshot.

mls_group_id.description: RFC 9420 group_id as base64url_no_pad(SHA-256(UTF8("ak.mls.group_id.v1") || 0x00 || canonical_effective_scope_key_bytes(effective_scope))), so exactly 43 characters. Derived by the reducer and the SDK from the effective scope alone; actors never submit it. The v1 formula is the only one: the earlier reversible base64url of the scope key bytes MUST NOT be accepted alongside it. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.2.

push_target_id.description: Canonical typed pairwise push pseudonym. The suffix is the unpadded Base64URL encoding of the complete 32-octet HMAC-SHA256 output for one (account_id, device_id, push_route_id, salt_epoch_id) tuple under the registering Station private secret. account_id is the complete closed AccountId. The route binds the selected Gateway and device channel. Receivers MUST decode exactly 32 octets and require canonical re-encoding. The same route/epoch target is reused across Realms and is linkable within that window; it is not an identity or authorization proof and does not prevent provider-token, device-id or timing correlation.

account_status_record_id.description: Account Authority issuer-ledger record identity derived from the complete closed unsigned AccountStatusRecord core.

account_id.description: Complete protocol identity for a principal at one Station, including human, Organization and personal Agent accounts. It does not imply a human login, provisioning workflow, credential class or authorization. Equality is byte-for-byte equality of both canonical did_core_id components; neither component may be inferred from a DID Document, route, session audience, current service, handle, or local database key. Accounts with the same principal_id at different station_id values are permanently distinct. Principal equality MUST NOT establish account equivalence or any permission inheritance, merging, delegation, substitution or recovery relationship. Account-scoped authority requires independent authorization for the exact AccountId. Permanent loss of a Station does not permit its accounts or PCR lineages to migrate to or revive at another Station; Realm takeover and RealmCommit recovery do not waive this boundary. See models/common-fields.md section 4.2.

actor_id.description: Closed complete actor identity: account binds a principal permanently to one Station; service acts as itself; realm binds an Applet Bot/Ghost permanently to one owning Realm. Full tagged-object equality is required. No authority is inferred from a discriminator, shared principal, key, route or DID controller.

web_origin.description: Canonical HTTP(S) Web Origin: lowercase scheme/host plus an optional valid non-default effective port. Userinfo, path (including a trailing slash), query, fragment, explicit :80 on HTTP, and explicit :443 on HTTPS are forbidden.

blob_id.description: Producer-allocated identity of one Blob metadata resource. A blob_id never commits to content bytes and MUST NOT be used where a content-addressed blob_ref is required.

blob_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to exact Blob bytes. The embedded suite and digest are the sole wire commitment to those bytes; sibling content/ciphertext digest mirrors are forbidden.

did_core_id.description: Canonical stable DID-derived identity core. The lowercase DID method name follows ak:did_core:, and the remaining method-adapter-defined core is opaque to generic consumers. The did:web v1 adapter uses the complete canonical method-specific-id, never a digest or truncated host. Principal-core and service-core equality is byte-for-byte equality of the complete did_core_id. Event actor and Realm membership equality instead use the complete closed ActorId, and account-scoped equality uses the complete AccountId; neither may be reduced to a principal core. A did_core_id is not a DID and cannot be resolved without a did or AuthenticatedServiceResolution.

did.description: Canonical bare DID used for registration, DID method resolution and owner-published current resolution. It contains no path, query or fragment and MUST project through the registered method adapter to exactly one did_core_id.

webvh_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identifier used at method-native registration, document and evidence boundaries. Role admission is enforced separately.

human_principal_did.description: Canonical bare DID for a v1 human principal anchor. The method set is derived from role_requirements.human_principal_anchor and contains exactly did:webvh. Every other method, including did:key and did:web, MUST fail closed with unsupported_did_method here rather than inside a method parser or history replay. Capability checks for relocation, DID-root recovery and ongoing governance are separate.

agent_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identity of a durable Agent. Its accepted bootstrap history is controller-authored and must contain a continuous inception followed by the create-locked PCR binding update.

applet_id.description: Stable canonical Applet installation identity. Applet service authority is carried separately by service_id.

did_key_did.description: Canonical bare did:key identifier used at method-native key and witness evidence boundaries. This is a registered method-specific Did subtype, not a business ActorId and not a DID URL.

did_url.description: Arkret verification-method DID URL profile (identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2): lowercase method name, no query, required fragment, fragment limited to ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. Every verification_method-family field and every kid/key_ref a schema declares to be a DID URL MUST resolve to exactly this definition; values compare byte-for-byte with no URI normalization or percent-decoding.

realm_actor_id.description: Stable Realm-owned Bot/Ghost identity. Both components are required for equality; governance handoff does not change either. No Station binding or AccountId is implied.

contract.description: Closed request/response DTOs for holder-private consent state serialized by the current governance Station.

consent_view.description: Holder-private display summary only. Includes every stored scope regardless of effective window; empty scopes is a present current. Complete editing input requires current read.

consent_replace_request_body.description: One caller-signed complete ak.consent.replace Event, submitted unchanged under holder root-control-only authorization and exact expected_current CAS.

consent_event.description: One caller-signed complete ak.consent.replace Event, submitted unchanged under holder root-control-only authorization and exact expected_current CAS. Never delegate, merge, rebuild or co-sign.

consent_request_request_body.description: Body for opaque contact/consent request submission. The peer is the exact authenticated ActorId and is never caller-supplied. Holder existence is deliberately not a precondition visible to the caller.

holder_account_id.description: Exact target AccountId. The same principal hosted by another Station is a different holder and MUST NOT hit this request or its rate-limit/cache key.

consent_scope.description: Requested scope, taken from the section 4 enum minus invite. An invite-scope request has no carrier here: it would have to become a holder_quarantine entry whose surface_kind is consent_request, and that branch pins consent_scope away from invite because an invite belongs to invite delivery. Rejecting it at the request boundary keeps the server from inventing a behaviour for a scope it can never store.

consent_request_response_body.description: Constant anti-enumeration response. Missing holder, denial, rate-limit drop and quarantine acceptance all return this exact shape; no current state id, state, dots, timestamps or expiry are exposed.

consent_current_read_response_body.description: Signed same-cut exact subject assertion: request_digest binds holder/peer/audience/nonce; PCR/generation/head binds the actual authority cut. Present contains complete original value including empty, expired, future and unevaluable entries. Never_written asserts no accepted current ever existed, never position zero or missing scope.

contract.description: Only for verified transferable non-Human PCRs with a separated governor under the PCR profile pcr_governance_policy. Human uses owning-Station native acceptance/read/notification and rejects these cross-Station operations without effects. This schema grants no new holder-session eligibility. Closed holder-hosting-Station proxy to the current PCR authority. Never a generic RPC, arbitrary account-data write or cached permission. Every command preserves its original authorization and atomically executes its private effects at the PCR authority.

body.description: Exact original accepted replacement source for historical retry; never a native consent_id lookup or current authorization.

effects_publish_request_body.description: Only the independently verified current PCR authority publishes accepted private effects to the exact holder hosting Station; this is a display and wakeup projection, never a private CAS command.

contract.description: Closed request/response DTO bundle for the Contact lifecycle: request, respond, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, the portable Contact round evidence bundle, acceptance receipts and the peer Contact carrier, plus the contact-list projection.

recipient.description: Exact Contact participant receiving this private delivery. The delivery Station is derived from the human account_id.station_id or the agent controller_account_id.station_id and is not carried as a parallel identity field.

service_resolution.description: First-hop transport material for the Station derived from recipient.

route_assistance.description: Optional transport-only hints for recovering the same recipient_id route during Contact delivery bootstrap. They are not part of the signed Contact Event, Contact projection, Realm member current state or authority state; they do not extend any token/receipt TTL or authorize delivery.

sorted_pair_member_ids.description: Exactly two distinct full ActorIds, strictly ascending by their RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 unsigned bytes. Validation rejects noncanonical order without sorting the received array.
Exactly two distinct full ActorIds, strictly ascending by their RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 unsigned bytes. Validation rejects noncanonical order without sorting the received array.

requests.description: Exactly two distinct request_event_ref values, strictly ascending by the complete typed EventId wire string UTF-8 unsigned bytes. Receipt digest is not a sort key or tiebreaker. Duplicate refs are invalid even with different digests. Receivers reject unsorted input without normalization. The signed request Event author ActorId of requests[0], not the Station receipt issuer_id, is the root-round founder.

current_operations.description: Exactly one original confirmed head operation for each opposite directional proof. Scope origins and round Events alone do not necessarily contain the latest head.

contact_round_evidence_bundle.description: Current normal/glare establishment plus immutable first identity and two opposite directional currents. No intermediate round chain. The first identity determines founder; current scope instances authorize separately.

contact_current_proof.description: Complete source-authenticated directional current at one durable cut. Only a new committed holder operation advances version; establishment, peer closure and proof refresh do not. Same-version conflicts compare immutable operation bytes, not proof bytes. Refresh never replaces known closures. The expected Station is independently derived from holder; no shared tombstone head or per-round completeness chain.

contact_lineage.description: Source-confirmed exact holder operation projection. issuer is the complete holder ContactPeer, not the signing Station. version is monotonic for holder/peer/trust-domain across all Contact operations and rounds. contact_round_id exists only for post-establishment operations. Original accepted_at and producer descriptor remain immutable.

request_message.description: The exact verified request Event message, present only for pending_incoming and only when that Event carries message.

effective_scopes.description: Optional shorthand. When present, MUST equal bidirectional_scopes.

contact_next_prepare_input.description: Server-provided exact next operation cursor: same contact_round_id, version=current lifetime holder direction version+1 and predecessor_event_ref=own exact current operation head. Copy verbatim; do not derive from list summary refs. Accepted rows carry it; pending/terminal rows do not. Normal requester and glare heads are their original requests, without synthetic accepted Events.

contact_scope_update_payload.description: Holder full-set replacement in a nonterminal established round. version advances the holder lifetime direction, retained scope instances retain their grant Event. Empty scopes remain accepted; pure narrowing does not wait for remote freshness.

block_peer.description: Holder-private commit side effect. true adds the peer to invite receive policy denied_subjects; false only tombstones the Contact lineage. This field is reservation-bound and is not copied into the public Contact Event payload.

direct_conversation_summary.description: Contact-list projection of an already materialized stable Direct Conversation. Coordinates and binding identity are immutable; state only says whether the same conversation is currently sendable. Creation progress is exposed only by direct_conversation_resolve_response_body; there is no durable creation operation, draft or reservation.

subject_id.description: Exact Contact participant whose Station issued this directional attestation.

issuer_id.description: Station service authority that signed this attestation at observed_at.

glare_concurrency_attestation.description: The source durably chooses glare for these exact requests in the same transaction as this attestation. version is the subject request operation version; finalizing glare does not increment it. No cumulative observed Event list, no later normal/reject choice, no unilateral authorizing success.

normal_response_acceptance_receipt.description: Source Station attestation issued only after the exact response Event's command unit is committed and its Contact effect atomically installed. Pending admission or proposal acknowledgement is not this receipt.

response_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted response Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel response_digest is carried.

outgoing_slot_absence_digest.description: H('ak.contact.no_outgoing_slot.v1', outgoing_slot_absence_transcript) over the exact closed transcript defined by identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 2.

peer_contact_authoritative_mirror_receip.description: Only an accepted or duplicate mirror receipt proves that the immutable signed Contact fact is durably mirrored. A deferred receipt is never authority for proof refresh or glare finalization.

control_material_digest.description: H('ak.peer-contact.control-result.v1',{request_digest,state_kind,glare_concurrency_attestation?,current_proof?,material?}) over the exact closed successful result.

peer_contact_control_receipt.description: The recipient signs every field except signature. This receipt is only for current_refresh, glare_finalize or continuity_checkpoint and cannot stand in for a signed Event mirror receipt.

peer_contact_event_submit_response_body.description: Only the five signed Contact Event request kinds use this branch. The receipt event coordinates and state_kind must match the submitted Event exactly. Request/response may return a current proof; accepted or duplicate scope/tombstone must return one; reject and deferred never do.

signed_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the mirrored signed Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; request_digest remains the distinct digest of the peer submit request.

peer_contact_submit_request_body.description: Closed Contact-only peer carrier. Each Event branch carries existing source Station attestation of a truly RealmCommit-committed Contact projection; pending admission cannot produce an authorizing receipt or receipted outbox. The original holder producer remains independently authenticated. No private PCR bootstrap, RealmCommit or new confirmation field is carried.

oneOf.description: Exact-pair source-current read with no prior mirror receipt prerequisite. The Message-Signature Station must host requester and may read only the opposite exact participant. Zero known_version is local unknown, not never-written proof. Optional initial identity is an assertion to match, not a caller-selected root. Hidden admission and quota outcomes remain opaque.

reject_acceptance_receipt.description: Source Station attestation of the committed Contact rejection Event, which is a successful terminal domain command. A RealmCommit-rejected command or pending Event cannot produce this receipt.

reject_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted reject Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel reject_digest is carried.

request_acceptance_receipt.description: Source Station attestation issued only after the exact request Event's command unit is committed and its Contact effect atomically installed. It may seed normal/glare round evidence; a pending admission receipt cannot occupy this type.

request_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted request Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel request_digest is carried.

request_acceptance_receipt_core.description: Frozen original request confirmation, signed before the future round exists. initial_contact_round_id is present exactly after a first established identity; version is the holder lifetime Contact operation version. Recontact does not reset it.

contact_producer_signer.description: Exact-Event source-signed producer projection. Closed direct and delegated branches are distinguished by delegated_actor_did presence, with no new wire tag. Enclosing carrier validation MUST select delegated if and only if the original Event is a legal Agent controller-device Event with executed_by; human and Agent runtime use direct. Method/raw32 authenticate the original producer, while delegated_actor_did only locates the independently verified Agent public identity. No reusable authorization, new endpoint or private PCR disclosure is created.

public_key_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of the exact Ed25519 raw32 key independently verified by the source for this confirmed Contact Event.

contact_direct_producer_signer.description: Closed direct producer branch for human-device and Agent-runtime Contact Events. The original Event has no executed_by; its producer method already locates its Actor DID. No delegated_actor_did is permitted.

public_key_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of the exact Ed25519 raw32 key independently verified by the source for this confirmed Contact Event.

delegated_actor_did.description: Complete public DID locator of the exact Agent Event actor, frozen from the source-verified native identity binding when the original Event has executed_by. It is not the executor DID, a core-derived locator, or authorization.

contact_delegated_producer_signer.description: Closed delegated producer branch, required exactly for a legal Agent controller-device Contact Event with executed_by. The receiver verifies the original producer signature and separately validates this complete Agent DID history against exact actor/controller/Station and the create-locked tuple.

contact_peer_endpoint.description: Exact selector mechanically derived from the verified peer producer of the selected accepted Contact round. Not current Device or MLS authority. Omit when no verified source exists.

contact_round_basis.description: Immutable normal/glare establishment evidence. No freshness, terminal acknowledgement, or history-chain root traversal is encoded here.

contact_initial_identity.description: Unsigned deterministic preservation of the first confirmed establishment originals. Founder is derived from round; this is not a newly signed root certificate. Exact Event refs, original producer signatures and original source receipts MUST cross-match.

contact_scope_instance.description: One current continuous directional scope instance. Retaining a scope retains its grant Event; removal closes it and re-addition selects the new grant Event. No independent generation counter.

contact_operation_evidence.description: Exact original holder-signed Contact Event plus its original branch-specific source confirmation. Pending or rejected command units cannot produce this evidence.

contact_round_closure.description: Original source tombstone closing this exact round. The receiving holder does not replace its own operation head or increment its own version. Validate the inner source and producer independently.

contact_scope_interval.description: Exact requested historical scope instance and its first actual removal/tombstone, if closed. The source result binds the completeness of this interval at its cut. Missing evidence is unknown, never an open interval invented from current scope equality.

contact_current_material.description: Bounded source material for the exact pair. All current proof refs, scope origins, original source confirmations and producer keys cross-match. Pending/reject never fabricate a round; root is absent only before first establishment. The signed control result covers the full material. Historical intervals are exact-requested, not an enumeration.

contract.description: Closed decrypted plaintext shape for the principal-private ak.contacts.actor.<principal_key> account-data value described by zh/discovery/client-preferences.md section 3.6. A producer validates the final plaintext before it encrypts and signs; a consumer validates after it opens the AEAD and before it applies the value. The recipient Station holds no key and cannot validate this shape, so nothing here is a server-side admission check. Structural validity proves nothing about where a name came from: the display-name confirmation evidence, the tag namespace and the storage-key binding are domain rules the same client also enforces.

version.description: Value format version of this remark. v1 has exactly one value, so a different number is a rejected value rather than a negotiated variant.

kind.description: Aligned with the human branch of the Contact list. Organization, device, service and Realm actors MUST NOT reuse this record.

principal_id.description: The human Contact peer this remark is about. After decryption the consumer recomputes the storage key from this value and the holder namespace key, and rejects the value when the recomputed key does not equal the key it was read from.

subject.description: Closed identity of the remarked Contact. It is principal-scoped on purpose: a remark is holder-private display data and never takes part in authorization or subject equality, so it carries no Station or actor role.

petname.description: Holder-authored global alias for this Contact. Absence means no alias; an empty string is not the way to clear one, because the display profile rejects it.

note.description: Free-form holder note, at most 4096 Unicode code points. It may be empty and it may span lines, so it does not reuse the single-line display profile.

tags.description: Private grouping tags. The reserved and vendor namespace rule of section 3.1 governs the values, and a client validates it as a domain rule: an array of strings passing this schema is not evidence that the namespace rule holds.

pinned.description: Whether the holder pinned this Contact in local ordering.

verified_handle_at_save.description: Canonical wire form of the verified handle seen when the remark was written or last updated, kept for anti-impersonation comparison. The typed input form with a leading marker is not stored.

confirmed_display_name.description: Profile display text the holder saw the last time it explicitly confirmed this Contact identity. It shares one display profile with the Actor Profile field it snapshots, so the two can never drift to different limits. An ordinary petname, note, tag or pin edit preserves it; only an explicit confirmation refreshes it.

saved_at.description: When the remark was first saved.

updated_at.description: When the remark was last modified.

contract.description: Canonical content-block schema for ak.content.poll and ak.content.poll.response.

poll_body.description: Poll configuration. max_selection_count is validated against responses by reducers because JSON Schema cannot compare a response to its referenced poll message.

poll_answer.description: One visible answer option. answer.id values MUST be unique within a poll; reducers and conformance vectors enforce that cross-item constraint.

contract.description: Closed domain result selected without protocol current state IDs. Every result names the last authority commit that affected the typed target.

direct_conversation_binding_value.description: One immutable confirmation; binding_event_ref is the exact Event producing this revision. Its original covering Commit remains source. Never a collection.

current_direct_conversation_binding.description: Write-once current inside the one Direct Conversation Realm, keyed by its verified founding pair_key; uniqueness still comes from founding admission.

realm_authority_root_value.description: Closed value of the lifetime-stable Realm authority root. Every member is derived by the registered ak.realm.create value_projection from the signed envelope and create payload; an author-supplied member is a realm_authority_root_conflict, never an accepted write.

controller_actor_id.description: Current root controller. At genesis it is exactly the create envelope actor_id.

controller_epoch.description: Increments only on a root controller rotation. Genesis is 0.

authority_generation.description: Realm delegation-root generation. Genesis is 0 and only accepted ak.realm.authority.reset increments it; owner transfer and planned governance Station handoff preserve it, so neither invalidates existing grants.

authority_event_ref.description: Exact create Event at delegation generation zero or the accepted authority reset Event establishing the current nonzero generation. Owner transfer and Station handoff preserve this anchor. It is not the current state revision and grants no historical Event read.

current_realm_authority_root.description: Singleton authority-root current state. The selector carries no component beyond its kind, so (realm_id, selector) is the Realm's lifetime-stable authority root identity.

member_state_value.description: Closed value of the member_state current state: the materialized membership register of one complete ActorId. models/common-fields.md section 4.5 fixes it as a four-state register over join/knock/leave/ban. It is a named def rather than an inline object because registry/contract-registry.json cites it as the value_schema_ref of ak.member.state; an enclosing _result envelope names the selector and revision beside the value, so citing the envelope would let a value_projection member be checked against the wrong object.

selector.description: Section 9.8 keys the set per target: the subject is the reacted-to object, and the payload carries no other target field. v1 core additionally requires an ak:message: target in the same effective scope (section 9.8.2), which a reducer enforces on admission; profiles MAY register further reactable kinds, so the wire type stays the generic object_ref of reaction_payload.

current_message_reactions.description: Registered projection of one reaction target. models/strand-and-message.md section 9.8.3 is authoritative and says this family is a keyed-set projection of the closed enum in models/common-fields.md section 2, whose join that section defines: ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove each project exactly one keyed_set_add, so a remove is itself an asserted element rather than an explicit revocation. The (target_ref, key, members[], count) summary of that section is the default view folded above this set, never the stored value.

message_reactions_value.description: Closed value of the message_reactions current state: the canonically sorted dot set of reaction assertions on one target. The join is the keyed-set union of models/common-fields.md section 2, which stays commutative, associative and idempotent; remove-wins convergence is a default-view fold above it and MUST NOT be implemented as a sixth state model. The set keeps both sides of a concurrent (add, remove) pair because models/strand-and-message.md section 9.8.3 requires the audit view to rebuild them.

reaction_assertion_entry.description: One asserted element of the message_reactions keyed set. The tag is the canonical dot of the accepted Event write that produced it; the value is the complete reaction payload of that Event. The asserting actor and the polarity -- whether this is an add or a remove -- are deliberately NOT element fields: section 9.8.3 reads both from the signed envelope of the Event the dot names, because event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 forbids a projection from assembling, renaming or trimming fields.

canonical_event_dot.description: Stable tag of one registered reducer write: the canonical <event_id>:<write_index> dot of zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. A bare event_id is never a valid tag. Canonical dot-set order compares the complete event_id by unsigned UTF-8 bytes, then write_index as an integer (2 before 10). Index encoding has no leading zeros. Duplicate dots and conflicting values for one dot are rejected; sorting is not winner or causal ordering.

agent_key_authorization_entry.description: One tagged entry of the agent_key current state. The tag is the canonical dot of the accepted Event write that produced it; the value is the complete authorize or revoke payload of that Event.

current_agent_key.description: Registered reducer projection of one Agent signing key. It is the single state source a portable state witness may quote; a service-private key table is not an alternative.

selector.description: Composite subject derived from (agent_id, agent_key_id). Producers MUST NOT spell it by string concatenation.

current_agent_status.description: Registered Agent lifecycle projection. The first active value has exactly one provenance: the delegated PCR genesis ak.realm.create conditional write of zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1.

agent_key_value.description: Closed value of the agent_key current state.

authorizations.description: Canonically sorted active tagged-set entries. A revoke entry is a witnessed revocation boundary marker, never an active authorization.

current_realm_genesis.description: Singleton create-locked identity/security core. Written once by the registered ak.realm.create result write (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1); the value is the closed ak.schema.realm_genesis.v1 object.

current_realm_history_access.description: Singleton Realm history-access FSM current state (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1). Initialized by the conditional ak.realm.create write and moved only by ak.realm.history_access.

current_identity_resolution.description: Singleton Realm identity-resolution projection. The PCR reducer initialises it from the genesis object's initial_resolution on the conditional ak.realm.create write and ak.identity.resolution.update is its only post-genesis writer (zh/identity/identity-did.md section 4.2). The stored value is the five-member resolution_projection, not the three-member commitment the owner signs: resolution_event_ref and updated_at are reducer-derived from the carrying envelope and are read back off this result by section 5.

current_identity_accountability.description: One accountability endorsement (family identity_accountability). zh/models/actor.md section 3.3.1: there is one record with two writers, and its identity is (Realm, issuer principal, subject principal, normalized exact scope set) -- the Realm component is the scope this result lives in, so it is not a selector member. A grant that changes a provision endorsement MUST be written into the original controller PCR; the same tuple in another Realm is a different record and cannot revoke this one.

selector.description: Composite subject. Producers MUST NOT spell it by string concatenation; the registered composite derives its third component as string_set_digest(accountability_scope, ak.accountability_scope_set.v1), so the scope set carried here is the normalized set that digest is taken over.

current_capability_grant.description: Registered projection of one Capability Grant. The subject GrantId is derived by retyping the accepted ak.capability.grant Event id; the value is the complete projected grant, including reducer-inserted id and the registered derived members authority_depth / authority_root_refs (zh/authz/capabilities.md section 10).

call_recording_id_component.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript segment handle, canonical byte-for-byte (crypto-media/call-state.md section 5.1).

call_recording_state_value.description: Capture permission state of one recording segment: ak.call.recording.start opens it as recording, a committed ak.call.state recording_transition.to=stopped closes it. ready/failed artifact details live in the separate call_recording_artifact family.

call_transcript_state_value.description: Capture permission state of one transcript segment: ak.call.recording.start opens it as transcribing, a committed ak.call.state transcript_transition.to=stopped closes it.

current_call_state.description: Commit-ordered projection of the ak.call.state state_transition axis (crypto-media/call-state.md section 4.1).

value.description: Creation initializes from=null with an allowed initial state; later accepted lifecycle deltas have a non-null predecessor.

current_call_focus.description: Commit-ordered projection of the ak.call.state focus axis. The first committed session_focus is binding (MEDIA-2); later writes MUST restate it verbatim.

current_call_recording_state.description: Capture permission state current state of one recording segment (family call_recording_state), keyed by the (call_id, recording_id) segment key so several captures in one call never collide.

current_call_recording_artifact.description: Published artifact current state of one recording segment (family call_recording_artifact): the ready/failed details published from stopped, referencing the exact confirmed stop Event. It grants no capture, key or read authority.

current_call_transcript_state.description: Capture permission state current state of one transcript segment (family call_transcript_state), keyed by the (call_id, recording_id) segment key.

current_call_transcript_artifact.description: Published artifact current state of one transcript segment (family call_transcript_artifact): the ready/failed details published from stopped, referencing the exact confirmed stop Event.

current_call_moderation.description: Complete effective Call axis with original sources and independent whole-axis revision, bound by the enclosing authenticated authority Snapshot. Not a portable grant or independent omission proof.

current_call_roster.description: Complete effective Call axis with original sources and independent whole-axis revision, bound by the enclosing authenticated authority Snapshot. Not a portable grant or independent omission proof.

current_call_mute_override.description: Reserved call-only shape for the ak.call.state mute_override axis. v1 rejects every mute_override write; this single-leg value cannot establish per-leg media authority (crypto-media/call-state.md section 4.1).

strand_position_value.description: The registered value shape of strand_position, pinned by models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6 as list_space_id with rank, or null. The null branch is the pre-placement state of a Strand that has been created but never moved onto a Board.

current_realm_schema.description: Per-Realm declaration of the Realm-scoped Morph kind tightening (models/governance-objects.md section 4). Singleton: the Realm is given by the Event envelope, which conformance/encoding.md section 9.5.1 forbids repeating in the subject.

current_realm_link.description: One directed Realm-to-Realm link. models/realm-links.md section 5 makes the subject the (target_realm_id, link_kind) tuple with the source Realm given by Event scope, and the current value the last accepted write.

current_realm_join_rule.description: The Realm default_join_rule enum. models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3 makes ak.realm.join_rule its sole canonical carrier.

current_realm_alias.description: The Realm-local alias declaration or its tombstone. The tombstone branch is retained rather than collapsed to null so durable withdrawal remains distinguishable from never-declared; Directory does not resolve aliases.

current_realm_policy_bundle.description: The Realm policy components that have no facet Event kind of their own. models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3 restates the whole bundle on every policy_revision.

current_realm_asset_privacy_policy.description: The Realm asset metadata and download policy (crypto-media/media-and-blob.md section 6). It is deliberately not a policy_bundle component and is excluded from key_access_revision.

current_realm_plaintext_visible_services.description: The declared set of services that may see plaintext in this Realm (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3).

current_realm_media_service.description: The single settled media service binding of the Realm. crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 4 calls it a single-valued commit-ordered projection; section 2.1 pins the closed field set.

current_mimi_room_binding.description: One MIMI room binding (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3). The subject is the MIMI room URI, not an Arkret id: the family records how one external room is bound, and the same Realm or Strand may be bound into more than one room. The binding is a projection into MIMI and is never canonical truth about the Arkret side.

current_moderation_franking_proof.description: The receiving-service proof that one encrypted target Event was received (governance/content-moderation.md section 3.4). The subject is the proven Event id. Installing an authorized signed current row is independent of a later report and does not itself establish moderator verification or an existence-time verdict.

current_moderation_report.description: The accepted moderation report itself (governance/content-moderation.md section 3.3). The subject is the report Event's own EventId, which is the same value ak.moderation.decision carries in payload.target_ref for decision=dismiss. The value is the complete report payload. The queue item is a read-side View over this family and the dismiss records in moderation_state, not a second stored state.

current_realm_preview_policy.description: The Realm preview / peek policy (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3). It is the projected source of the query field preview_policy_id and is a per-Realm singleton like every sibling facet in that sentence. The value is payload.value only: payload.reason is audit provenance carried by the Event, not projected state.

current_realm_tombstone.description: The terminal tombstone of the Realm, with its required successor_realm_id (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.6). Commit-ordered and written at most once.

current_realm_destroy.description: The terminal destroy of the Realm, which MUST NOT carry a successor (models/realm-and-space.md section 2.6). Commit-ordered and written at most once.

realm_set_default_strand_value.description: The registered value shape of realm_set_default_strand. models/strand-and-message.md section 2 makes the authoritative current value the Realm projection field default_strand_id and normalizes absent and explicit null to one null before a whole-value comparison, so the value is the one-member object carrying that field rather than a bare pointer: only a member can be absent.

current_realm_set_default_strand.description: The authoritative default_strand_id pointer of the Realm (models/strand-and-message.md section 1). The current value is the last accepted write on the stream.

current_strand_position.description: The position of one Strand on one Board. models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6 pins the subject to the reversible typed_pair of board_space_id and strand_id and forbids a hash subject, so both typed-ID components MUST be validated on parse.

invite_lifecycle_value.description: Closed value of the invite_lifecycle current state: the one process-state register of one Invite. zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 declares the state set and the edge set, and registry/contract-registry.json carries the edges as event_kind_registry.transition_contracts.invite_lifecycle, so this def holds the state names only. The register carries nothing else on purpose: a transition projection writes one axis, and every other Invite fact that has to be checked against the pre-state is its own registered family (invite_directed_invitee, invite_live_target). A mirrored copy here would be the drifting second truth that section removed join_rule_snapshot for.

current_invite_lifecycle.description: Registered projection of one Invite's process state. The subject InviteId is the create Event id retyped (zh/models/common-fields.md section 6.0), so a directed ak.invite.create and a third-party ak.invite.third_party each open exactly one of these and every later Event names it through payload.invite_id.

invite_live_target_value.description: Closed value of the invite_live_target slot: the record of the directed Invite that currently occupies this account's slot, or null for an empty slot. zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 fixes the occupant as create_event_id in the verbatim ak:event: spelling rather than the ak:invite: retype, because the projection grammar has no retype source; the slot carries no process state, since occupancy itself is what live means. null is the reusable empty state a registered release write returns it to, not a read-only sentinel.

create_event_id.description: envelope.event_id of the ak.invite.create that occupies this slot, in the verbatim ak:event: spelling. It is the same 33-octet token as that Invite's InviteId under a different typed prefix, and the two spellings are never interchangeable on the wire.

current_invite_live_target.description: The one live directed Invite slot of one invitee account inside one Realm. zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 makes it the single source of truth for directed-invite liveness deduplication, keyed by the invitee AccountId alone: the Realm is already given by the Event envelope, so carrying realm_id in the subject is forbidden by zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4.

invite_directed_invitee_value.description: Closed value of the invite_directed_invitee record: the exact account one directed Invite is addressed to, written once by ak.invite.create from that same Event's payload and never updated. It is the reverse index of invite_live_target, and the two together are what make the slot release checkable: the slot answers "which Invite holds this account", this record answers "which account does this Invite hold". ak.invite.third_party writes no record at all, so a third-party Invite's stored invitee is absent rather than null -- that absence is what the stored_field_matches_payload pre-state requirement of zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 reads.

current_invite_directed_invitee.description: Registered create-locked projection of one directed Invite's invitee. The subject InviteId is the create Event id retyped, the same subject invite_lifecycle uses, so a later Event that names payload.invite_id reaches both the state register and this binding without carrying either of them on the wire.

pin_assertion_entry.description: One asserted element of the pin keyed set. The tag is the canonical dot of the accepted Event write that produced it; the value is the complete pin payload of that Event. The asserting actor and the polarity -- add, remove or reorder -- are deliberately NOT element fields: models/pins.md section 4.1 reads the polarity from `kind` and the asserter from `actor_id` on the signed envelope of the Event the dot names, because event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 forbids a projection from assembling, renaming or trimming fields. The value branch is an anyOf and MUST NOT be read as a discriminator: pin_add_payload and pin_reorder_payload share the required {pin_scope, target_ref, rank} triple, so an add and a reorder that carry no optional member are byte-identical and only the envelope tells them apart.

pin_value.description: Closed value of the pin current state: the canonically sorted dot set of pin assertions in one pin scope. The join is the keyed-set union of models/common-fields.md section 2, which stays commutative, associative and idempotent. Every one of the three pin kinds adds an assertion, including remove and reorder, so the set keeps both sides of a concurrent pair; the ordered roster, the remove-wins fold, the note inherited by a reorder and the conflict view are all read-side folds above this set, defined in models/pins.md section 4.1, and MUST NOT be implemented as further stored state.

selector.description: models/pins.md section 4.1 keys the set per pin scope: the subject is the whole closed pin_scope object, kind and id together. The id alone would not do -- pin_scope is a four-branch oneOf, so two scopes of different kinds carrying the same id would collide into one subject, and the subject would not be reversible into the object the payload signed. target_ref is a field on the element value, not part of the subject.

current_pin.description: Registered projection of one pin scope. models/pins.md section 4.1 is authoritative and spells this projection verbatim: ak.pin.add, ak.pin.remove and ak.pin.reorder each project exactly one keyed_set_add, so a remove and a reorder are themselves asserted elements rather than explicit revocations. The reason is in that section: keyed_set_remove_observed without a match would remove every target in the scope, and with a match it would only remove add dots alive in the frozen prior state, which silently converges a concurrent (add, remove) pair to add instead of surfacing it.

space_parent_value.description: The registered value shape of space_parent, pinned by models/realm-and-space.md section 3.5. It is the one-member object carrying the parent pointer, with a nullable member, and it is never a bare null: only a member can be absent, which is the same argument realm_set_default_strand_value makes, and here a bare null would also make the family's own compare-and-set inexpressible, because a pre_state requirement is a predicate over a stored FIELD and a null value has no fields. null in the member is the root state, a Space with no structural parent, written explicitly by the ak.space.create genesis write when the signed object omits parent_space_id.

current_space_parent.description: The structural parent of one Space. models/realm-and-space.md section 3.5 is authoritative: the subject is the SpaceId alone, the projection is an ordinary current value, and the current value is the last accepted write on the stream, ordered only by stream_position. The Space metadata projection deliberately excludes parent_space_id, so this family and not the object is the truth source models/relation.md and sync/views.md read the derived contains edge from. A directed cycle among current parents makes every edge in it domain-unresolved; it MUST NOT reselect a register value, fake a root, or produce a live contains.

space_child_scope_policy_value.description: The registered value shape of space_child_scope_policy: the closed placement policy object of models/circle.md section 7.1, or null. null is the undeclared state; that section says a Space MAY declare a policy, and an undeclared policy adds no constraint, which is what allow_any also means. The reducer MUST NOT synthesize the allow_any object out of an absent member: a projection may only write a value the signed Event or the envelope supplies, and null is the one registered spelling of the absent state.

current_space_child_scope_policy.description: The child placement policy of one Space, keyed by SpaceId. models/circle.md section 7.1 is authoritative for the enum and for the four reducer obligations it creates on ak.strand.create, ak.strand.move, ak.space.parent and structural contains writes; section 6.3 is authoritative for why it is not interchangeable with Space.scope_circle_id. It is a family rather than a create-locked object member because space_patch_payload carries a dedicated top-level child_scope_policy command whose own description makes it select security execution, while the generic metadata patch is forbidden from reaching the path at all.

agent_provisioning_value.description: The registered value shape of agent_provisioning, pinned by zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3. These are exactly the create-locked members every later authorization reader needs when all it holds is the Agent DID: the controller it is bound to, the Agent PCR that carries its lifecycle and key state, the delegation that authorized the controller, and the immutable requested-scope commitment zh/authz/capabilities.md section 9.1 recomputes a disclosure against. Nothing else from the payload belongs here -- agent_slug and the selector members are agent_selector_claim's, the endorsement members are identity_accountability's, and created_at is already the endorsement's not_before. requested_scope itself is controller-private and MUST NOT appear; only the digest does.

controller_principal_id.description: The managed-principal controller. The create-locked ArkretPrincipalControlRealm serviceEndpoint spells the same DID as controller_did; entry 1 admission compares the two, so this member is that comparison's registered left-hand side.

principal_control_realm_id.description: The forward-declared Agent PCR. Until its ak.realm.create is accepted this names a Realm that does not exist yet; that is the registered class C preimage exemption of zh/conformance/encoding.md §3.1 and not an inconsistency.

current_agent_provisioning.description: One Agent provisioning fact (family agent_provisioning), the first of the four typed results one accepted ak.agent.provision writes atomically. zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3 is authoritative.
