Sigil-free: the display forms #general:acme.example and general@acme.example MUST NOT reach the wire. <domain> is the issuing authority and MUST be an authority domain of this Realm's trust_domain; a foreign-domain claim MUST be rejected with reason realm_alias_authority_mismatch.

realm_alias_payload.description: Closed payload for ak.realm.alias, the ONLY wire carrier of a Realm alias. A declaration writes the complete canonical alias; {tombstone:true} is a durable value tombstone that removes the alias from effective resolution without erasing the current state history. realm-genesis.schema.json and realm-profile.schema.json are closed and have no alias property, and ak.realm.create / ak.realm.profile payloads MUST NOT carry one.

realm_create_payload.description: Minimal identity and security-root payload for ak.realm.create. User-visible, mutable, policy and reducer-derived Realm state is carried only by registered bootstrap facets. Every genesis, including Principal Control Realm and Agent PCR, requires a canonical 32-octet genesis_salt.

realm_organization_payload.description: Organization-side endorsement or revocation for a Realm relationship. Reducer validation MUST require realm_id to match the top-level Event.realm_id, organization_id to identify an Organization principal in accepted registration state, the Realm-side writer to hold ak.realm.admin, and authorization to verify against current organization DID control evidence or a delegated service whose purpose covers this relationship and control_scopes. The stable organization_id is not itself resolvable DID material.

statement_id.description: Stable id of this organization statement. It is audit identity, not the reducer current state subject; the reducer current state subject is (organization_id, relationship).

realm_id.description: Realm the organization statement is bound to. MUST equal the enclosing Event.realm_id.

organization_id.description: Stable Organization principal identity that endorses, governs, sponsors, certifies, or revokes the Realm relationship. This did_core_id is bound to current Organization DID evidence through accepted registration/resolution state; it is not itself resolvable.

relationship.description: Relationship being asserted or revoked for this organization and Realm.

control_scopes.description: Machine-readable scopes covered by the organization's consent. A scope here is an endorsement boundary only; actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy, governance-Station authority, capability, or service-binding Event.

expires_at.description: Administrative review/renewal hint only. It does not auto-transition account status; a later AccountStatusRecord is required and remains subject to sequence and terminal rules.

realm_commit_ref.description: Optional RealmCommitId naming the authority commit whose current Realm state the organization evaluated when issuing this statement.

organization_policy_ref.description: Optional DID-document delegation URL, policy object, governance decision, or attestation reference used to evaluate the statement.

authorization.description: Organization-side authorization proof. This is independent of the Realm-side ak.realm.admin authorization required to write the event into Realm history.

issuer_id.description: Stable Organization or delegated-service principal identity that issued this statement. The issuer_id is a did_core_id; verification_method and accepted registration/delegation state carry the DID evidence required to verify the issuer.

delegation_ref.description: Required when issuer_role is governance_service or account_authority. It MUST resolve to a live organization DID delegation whose purpose covers ak.realm.organization and the requested relationship/control_scopes.

executed_by.description: Optional exact ActorId of the human administrator or service actor that initiated the organization-side decision. This does not become the organization principal.

proof.description: Signature, threshold transcript, or governance-service attestation over the canonical organization statement binding statement_id, realm_id, organization_id, relationship, status, control_scopes, issued_at, validity window, and statement replacement/revocation fields.

realm_owner_transfer_payload.description: ak.realm.owner.transfer — rotate the controller binding of the Realm authority-root current state. It changes controller_actor_id and increments controller_epoch only: authority_generation, the current state ref and every existing grant are untouched, so the whole authority tree issued by the previous controller stays valid. This is not a reparent — the root never moves.

expected_state_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the authority-root current state value this Event expects to replace. The reducer MUST compare-and-swap against it and reject a stale value rather than overwrite.

controller_actor_id.description: Exact ActorId of the successor that becomes the root controller. Its control proof MUST bind this complete identity; a bare principal DID or parallel Station sidecar is insufficient.

patch.description: The authority-root member selected by the author. The reducer also increments controller_epoch from the CAS-frozen pre-state; every other member is preserved verbatim.

successor_acceptance.description: Independent acceptance proof from the successor. The current controller proof, this proof, the payload and expected_state_digest MUST all enter the same signing transcript. The successor controller_epoch is uniquely computed from the expected pre-state, so neither party signs a producer-supplied counter.

realm_policy_bundle_payload.description: Enabled Realm policy component set, written wholesale into the realm_policy_bundle commit-ordered projection current state: every revision restates the complete enabled component set and the Realm object's derived policy fields re-derive from the latest accepted bundle. policy_revision starts at 1 and every later authoritative reducer admission MUST equal previous.policy_revision + 1: rollback uses top-level policy_revision_rollback; a forward gap uses failed_precondition with reason_code policy_revision_gap and produces zero current-state writes. policy_revision MUST cover policy_revision (see contract-registry event-kind row and models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3).

policy_revision.description: Strictly monotonic bundle revision; rollback or gaps are rejected.

federation_policy.description: The sole producer carrier of the effective Realm federation policy. High-assurance Realm reducers require closed, restricted, or quarantine and reject open.

media_service_decryption_allowed.description: Whether a media service listed in plaintext_visible_services may decrypt call media. Defaults to false when absent. It is one of three conditions that MUST all hold (ak.realm.media_service declaration + plaintext_visible_services grant + this toggle). Because it changes who may receive media keys, it enters the media scope key_access_revision; a generation that does not cover the current value cannot authorize media decryption. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 8.2.

handle_issuer_policies.description: Ordered Realm handle-issuer trust policy used by primary-handle resolution. Earlier entries have higher tie-break priority; every issuer is domain-scoped.

member_action.description: How this Realm disposes of a principal's membership when the account enters deactivated. Defaults to leave_self_initiated when the component is absent. Unrecognized values fail closed to retain_membership with a policy parse warning and MUST NOT silently fall back to the default. The single authority for the closed enum and its disposition semantics is identity/account-lifecycle.md section 7.1.

consent_required.description: When true, every invite into this Realm MUST pass the holder consent admission gate in identity/consent-model.md section 6.1 before the invite Event is submitted. It MUST NOT be read as permission for a cross-Realm authority-commit precondition.

allowed_third_party_invite_verification_.description: Complete current allow-set of service DIDs trusted to attest 3PID ownership for ak.invite.third_party / ak.invite.claim. The array is whole-value replacement state in this policy-bundle revision, not an incremental patch. Absence and [] both deny every third-party invite verification service. Removing a DID in a later policy_revision revokes it for every later claim re-check; no separate tombstone exists. Reducers MUST evaluate the current accepted bundle current state on a fresh basis before accepting ak.invite.claim.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

realm_set_default_strand_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.set_default_strand. Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. Reducer projects strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify strand_id references a projected, non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm; a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. The Strand projection is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage. expected_default_strand_id compiles to a current state expected_revision precondition for optimistic concurrency (CAS). Absent and explicit null are normalized to the same null value before comparison, so omission asserts expected_revision null and is only valid while the current state is still in its initial no-default state; once a default is set the field MUST be present, otherwise the reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition and MUST NOT overwrite unconditionally.

expected_default_strand_id.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard compared as a whole value after absent and explicit null are normalized to null. The reducer accepts the write only if the Realm's current default_strand_id equals this value (null asserts no default is currently set). Omission therefore asserts expected_revision null and MUST fail once a default exists. Mismatch MUST be rejected (failed_precondition).

relation_create_payload.description: Create or replace the Relation current value at one registered primary conflict domain. primary_conflict_domain is the signed current-state subject and MUST exactly match payload.relation's registered relation_kind/from_ref/to_ref shape. payload.relation is the closed six-field relation_definition authoring region; its optional relation.rank is the only create-time rank carrier, and materialized Relation members are forbidden. expected_revision is null only when the domain has never been written; after a tombstone, a new event-derived RelationId MAY replace that tombstoned value only at its exact revision. An active current value cannot be replaced by create.

relation_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.relation.tombstone. primary_conflict_domain is the signed current-state subject; relation_id MUST equal the current value's id at that domain, and expected_revision MUST equal its exact revision. The transition is irreversible for that RelationId. When supplied, reason is retained on the Event and is not copied into the materialized Relation object.

relation_update_payload.description: Relation patch payload. primary_conflict_domain is the signed current-state subject; relation_id MUST equal the current value's id at that domain, and expected_revision MUST equal its exact revision. relation_kind/from_ref/to_ref are create-locked because they define the subject; changing them requires an explicit tombstone followed by create. effective_scope and every effective_scope.* descendant path remain reducer-managed.

rsvp_encrypted_response.description: Encrypted RSVP response envelope. The content_type is pinned so a receiver can route the ciphertext to exactly one decrypted schema; the plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response.

rsvp_entry.description: Complete RSVP current state value. The whole entry is the current-value projection set value, so the deterministic winner carries the schedule source the responder observed plus the response itself.

schedule_basis_refs.description: The unique schedule revision the responder actually observed, retained in the existing array wire shape as exactly one ak:event: typed id. It is the sole carrier of that association: the payload holds exactly one entry, so no envelope mirror is required and none is defined. Shape admission is decidable from this field alone, without resolving the referenced Event.

response.description: Plaintext response branch. Only admissible while the target Strand scope has no accepted ak.mls.genesis and the receiving service declares the rsvp_response plaintext data class; after activation it MUST be rejected with mls_activation_required.

encrypted_response.description: Encrypted response branch; content_type is pinned to application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json and the decrypted plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response. Required once the target Strand scope has an accepted ak.mls.genesis.

rsvp_response.description: RSVP response object. Used directly by rsvp_entry.response and as the decrypted plaintext of rsvp_entry.encrypted_response, whose content_type is application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json. status and comment always share one encryption boundary; a plaintext status with an encrypted comment is not a valid shape.

comment.description: Optional responder comment. An empty response is expressed by omitting the field, never by an empty string.

event_ref.description: Calendar event Strand id; encoded as a ak:strand: typed id.

occurrence.description: JSON null for the whole series, or the canonical recurrence instance key: YYYY-MM-DD for all-day events and YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[Zone] for timed events. The date component MUST be a real proleptic-Gregorian date, not merely match the digit pattern. The producer MUST canonicalize before signing; receivers MUST reject non-canonical keys instead of rewriting them.

schema_define_state_payload.description: Schema definition payload. value is a JSON Schema 2020-12 document validated by the executable ak.validator.json_schema_2020_12_definition.v1 profile; value.$id is the stable definition current state subject.

sidecar_context_attach_payload.description: Controller-signed versioned attachment of a source Realm context to an existing native Sidecar. It creates no Strand or Relation protocol object.

sidecar_create_payload.description: Minimal native Sidecar genesis intent. The payload is empty: sidecar_id is derived from the Event id; realm_id, controller_account_id, state and timestamps are reducer-derived from the accepted envelope, and the Sidecar scope activates standard RFC 9420 through its own accepted ak.mls.genesis.

space_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Space object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

space_object_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.tombstone. Realm tombstone uses its separate Realm lifecycle payload; Space tombstone targets payload.space_id.

space_parent_payload.description: Reparent one Space. All three members are required. parent_space_id is nullable and explicit null is the one spelling of "no parent" on this payload, so the space_parent register stays total and an omitted member can never mean the root by accident; the Space create object spells the same fact by absence and the genesis write normalizes it. expected_parent_space_id is the declared prior parent this producer read, not an optional compare-and-set: zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 3.5 registers it as a pre_state requirement on the space_parent family, and making it optional would give one Event kind two admission semantics selected by a member's presence.

space_patch_payload.description: Space metadata patch and optional separate child scope policy command. A policy member selects security execution; the patch cannot touch policy, identity, scope or lifecycle, including dotted paths. A combined Event is atomic and requires security finality.

space_state_transition_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.archive and ak.space.restore. The target Space is expressed on payload.space_id; top-level target_ref is a rejected field on Event envelopes.

service_id.description: Media service principal. Every issued participant_binding.issuer_kid and service_signature.kid MUST project onto this DID (media-service-binding.md section 3).

ice_configuration_url.description: ICE / TURN credential endpoint. Part of the section 2.1 integrity binding.

foci.description: Non-empty multi-focus list. A descriptor carrying a single flat sfu_endpoint, or no foci at all, MUST fail closed with media_service_foci_required; a server MUST NOT normalize or infer one in the realtime path.

focus_id.description: Stable focus id inside this Realm media service. It enters the signed canonical bytes and the session_focus election (call-state.md section 4.1).

focus_kind.description: Backend binding id. It sits on the kind axis rather than being spelled `type`, because the value set is an Arkret-owned closed registry and classification-field-registry.json reserves the type axis for fields inherited verbatim from an external standard. Only livekit and arkret_native have a normative binding in v1; a client meeting an unknown or unsupported focus_kind MUST fail closed with unknown_focus_type rather than hand the token to an arbitrary SDK.

token_endpoint.description: Token exchange endpoint (section 3). Shared abstraction across every backend; only backend_token differs. Part of the section 2.1 trust root, so a client MUST verify the exact current state value against the current confirmed RealmCommit state before anchoring it.

connect_url.description: Backend connection entry point; the concrete protocol is fixed by the type-specific binding appendix.

health_url.description: Client pre-flight endpoint, usable only for ordering foci_preferred before a session_focus is committed. Once call_focus carries a session_focus, a connect failure MUST surface as focus unavailable and MUST NOT silently switch focus.

cascade_group.description: Backend cluster this focus belongs to, for user-visible disclosure that a cross-region conference is cascaded inside the backend. The protocol does not standardize SFU-to-SFU cascading.

realm_discovery_payload.description: Closed whole-value payload for ak.realm.discovery. Preview field selection is owned exclusively by ak.realm.preview_policy.

ratio_basis_points.description: Integer basis points: exact ratio = ratio_basis_points / 10000; permitted range 1000..10000 inclusive. Compare using exact integer arithmetic.

realm_schema_payload.description: Closed whole-value payload for ak.realm.schema. value.schema_refs is the complete replacement set of activated schema ids; it is not merged with any previous set. Every member MUST be a registered ak.schema.*.vN id, and the core member ak.schema.realm.v1 MUST be present in every update, so the set can never drop self-contained Realm validation. The Realm structural role is carried only by the signed ak.schema.realm_genesis.v1 purpose and is not writable here; policy and deployment profiles have their own carriers.

schema_refs.description: Complete replacement set of activated schema ids. Members MUST be registered ak.schema.*.vN ids; unknown or unregistered ids fail closed. ak.schema.realm.v1 MUST be a member of every accepted value.

strand_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the Strand object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance. stage and stage_changed_at are forbidden on create; the optional business stage axis is initialized only by ak.strand.stage.set.

board_space_id.description: Board Space that owns the position edge; deduplication key (board_space_id, strand_id) MUST be unique among active edges.

from_space_id.description: Source List Space (optional; reducer infers from current active edge if omitted).

target_space_id.description: Target List Space after move. This is the ONLY payload-level field for the destination; the reducer compiles it into the current-value projection value as 'list_space_id' on the current state at ak:result:strand_position:<board_space_id>:<strand_id>. Writers MUST NOT put 'list_space_id' directly on the ak.strand.move payload (additionalProperties=false enforces this) — there is exactly one destination input field on the wire.

expected_position.description: Optional exact whole-value compare-and-set preimage of strand_position. It must equal the placed current value in canonical JSON bytes; omission does not add a CAS. The unplaced first move omits this member.

strand_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.update. Patches ordinary Strand fields on the Strand identified by target_ref.

patch.description: Only the two exact Synthesis content paths may reach tracks; replacing tracks, a track entry or configuration is forbidden.

space_id.description: List Space within which the reorder happens.

expected_position.description: Optional exact whole-value compare-and-set preimage of strand_position. It must equal the placed current value in canonical JSON bytes; omission does not add a CAS. The unplaced first move omits this member.

strand_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.stage.set. Mutates Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see the shared stage-set contract in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3 and zh/models/strand-and-message.md §3.2.

strand_watch_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.strand.watch.set. Writes the (strand_id, watcher_actor_id) watch current state. The new current state value is computed from payload.level + payload.level_public: when level is null the effect is set null (clear, equivalent to mentions_only); when level is a string the effect is set { level, level_public? }. Reducer invariants: (1) watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope.actor_id unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others; (2) when watcher_actor_id != envelope.actor_id (.others write), level MUST be one of {mentions_only, participating, all} and level_public MUST be omitted or false — writing muted or level_public=true on behalf of another actor MUST failed_precondition; (3) .others writes MUST have exactly one ak.audit.accessed Event as the second slot of the registered audit_paired_event unit pointing to the watch Event with semantic_refs[role=audit_pair], and its payload access_kind=watch_set_others must bind writer_actor_id, target_actor_id, target_ref=strand_id and paired_event_id. The Station validates current watch state and atomically commits both Events; no caller-authored result head is carried. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

level.description: Watch level. Required. null clears the current state (equivalent to mentions_only / no record); in that case level_public MUST be omitted.

level_public.description: Opt-in publication of the level value to non-self projection consumers. Default false. muted MUST NOT be exposed even with level_public=true. MUST be omitted when level is null.

expected_value.description: Ordinary watch predicate evaluated only against the signed causal basis. null asserts an unwritten basis; a concrete value must match the selected exact base head. It does not serialize independent offline writes or pick a winner.

allOf.description: level_public MUST be omitted when level is null (clearing a current state does not carry a public-level setting).

track_name.description: Strand track key carried by Message Event payloads. In v1 Message payloads are restricted to 'discussion'; the materialized Message resolves its track through the referenced Strand and does not duplicate this payload-only field.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a concrete verification method. Bare DIDs are not valid where a key binding is required.

view_reconcile_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.reconcile. view_id is the view current state subject -- zh/models/views.md section 3.2 is normative that all three View kinds write ONE family, so the family is named for the View, not for this payload. definition is the complete author-editable definition (view.schema.json #/$defs/view_definition), not an author-overwritable copy of the materialized object: identity, Realm, schema, creation metadata and lifecycle state are retained from the target pre-state, and update provenance is derived from this Event. Reconcile is neither create object snapshot nor update patch: it replaces the definition wholesale.

relation_create_object.description: Relation create input: the closed six-field authoring region of relation.schema.json, not the materialized object. Its optional rank is the only create-time rank carrier. See that definition for why reducer-owned members are absent.

expected_governance_generation.description: Station tenure the producer observed. The handoff is a compare-and-set on the governing Station tenure, never on the Realm authority-root delegation generation.

realm_governance_station_change_payload.description: Admission requires verified transfer eligibility under the PCR profile pcr_governance_policy; Human PCR rejects without effects even with valid signatures. The payload has no subject-role override.

device_authorize_possession_transcript.description: Candidate-device possession transcript of the registration_anchor branch: the second Event of a PCR genesis unit. The signing input is UTF8("ak.device_authorize_possession_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json(this object); the signature it produces is the payload's device_signature, which is why device_signature is not a member here. authorized_generation_ref is fixed to 1, the value the same pcr_genesis_unit initializes. recovery_session_id and scopes are the normalized nulls of a branch whose payload carries neither.

device_authorize_recovery_possession_tra.description: Candidate-device possession transcript of the pcr_recovery branch. The signing input is UTF8("ak.device_authorize_recovery_possession_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json(this object); the signature it produces is the payload's device_signature, which is why device_signature is not a member here. recovery_session_id is narrowed to the non-null accepted recovery session, so the transcript cannot be replayed outside the unit that authorized it, and authorized_generation_ref MUST equal the sibling ak.device.reanchor new_device_generation.

realm_authority_reset_payload.description: ak.realm.authority.reset — invalidate every capability grant that descends from this Realm's authority root in one accepted Event. It increments authority_generation only: controller_actor_id and controller_epoch are preserved verbatim, so the reset is not a controller change and never moves the root. Every realm_root grant ref carries the generation it was issued under, so advancing the generation is exactly what makes a whole delegated authority tree stop evaluating; ak.realm.owner.transfer preserves the generation and therefore leaves every child grant valid. The current controller is the only possible author: the compare-and-set below requires the frozen pre-state digest, so this is a deliberate act by the holder of root control, never an automatic takeover of a lost authority.

expected_state_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the authority-root current state value this Event expects to replace. The reducer MUST compare-and-swap against it and reject a stale value rather than overwrite. The successor generation is uniquely computed from the pre-state this digest freezes, so no counter is carried on the wire.

view_create_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.create. zh/models/views.md section 3.2 gives the three View kinds three different author loads over one current state family; one shared def with an anyOf of the three branches and no event_kind discriminator admitted every shape on every kind -- an ak.view.update could carry an unconstrained definition object, and an ak.view.create could carry {view_id, patch}. Each kind now binds exactly one closed payload.

object.description: ak.view.create author definition: the same closed authoring region ak.view.reconcile replaces wholesale, NOT the materialized object. The earlier shape was the materialized View minus four banned members, which still handed the author schema, realm_id, created_by, created_at and state -- the create-locked members every later write retains verbatim, so a self-reported creator or realm became permanent truth, and a create could start a View outside its initial state. Those five are now produced by the registered create-lock derivations of zh/models/common-fields.md section 3.3, which also removes the prose-only cross-check that created_by and created_at had to equal the envelope: there is nothing left to cross-check when the reducer is the only writer.

view_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.update: the incremental patch surface, and the only shared-View removal path (zh/models/views.md section 3.1). It MUST NOT carry an object snapshot or a whole definition -- those are create and reconcile -- and view_id is required because it is the current state subject.

expected_state_digest.description: Signed frozen pre-state guard. It names the exact committed current value this patch was authored against: the single value the target current state holds at the position the write is applied, per the accepted order of its own stream. A mismatch fails the Event; it MUST NOT be resolved by choosing an older historical candidate that does match. contract-registry.json registers nothing for it because the v1 state_projection grammar has no expected_prestate member, so it is an admission rule beside the projection rather than part of it.

device_authorize_recovery_session_id.description: Accepted recovery session this device authorization is admitted beside. One form, referenced by the device_authorize_payload member and by the possession core so the transcript cannot drift to a second spelling.

device_authorize_possession_core.description: Shared signing-input core of the three candidate-device possession transcripts: registration_anchor, pcr_recovery and applet_managed_delegation. This object is not a wire member of any Event: it is the object the candidate device signs, and the signing input is UTF8("<domain>\n") || canonical_json(this object) with canonical_json per conformance/encoding.md section 2 (JCS) and <domain> the variant's x-arkret-signature-domain. The resulting signature is what the ak.device.authorize payload then carries as device_signature, so this core MUST NOT contain device_signature, any Event id, any Event or envelope digest, pairing_challenge_transcript_digest or any other proof material: those are outputs of this transcript or carriers for it, and signing them would be circular. account_id is present and is injected from the Event envelope actor_id rather than mirrored by the closed payload. Every authorization member the payload may omit is required here and normalized to null, so 'absent' and 'present as null' cannot both encode the same authorization (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.2.1). The core is deliberately not closed; each registered variant closes itself with unevaluatedProperties false after narrowing its branch, so exactly the members that variant registers may appear.

account_id.description: Complete account AccountId subject of the ak.device.authorize Event this transcript authorizes, injected from that Event envelope's account actor_id. It is NOT a payload member: device_authorize_payload is closed and MUST NOT mirror a principal_id or an account_id, so a verifier MUST rebuild this member from the envelope actor_id.account_id it already authenticated and MUST NOT take it from a payload member, a route, a session audience or any unsigned body member.

device_id.description: Candidate device identity, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.device_id.

device_public_key_did.description: Candidate device Ed25519 signing key in did:key form, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.device_public_key_did. It is the key that verifies this transcript's own signature.

hpke_key.description: Candidate device HPKE public key, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.hpke_key. Signing it here is what forbids a service from substituting it.

algorithms.description: Canonical sorted unique algorithm ids, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.algorithms. The producer MUST sort and deduplicate them by UTF-8 bytewise order before signing.

authorized_by.description: Byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.authorized_by. Under registration_anchor it MUST equal account_id.principal_id; that is an equality between two members of this same object, which JSON Schema cannot express, so it is a normative requirement of crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.2.1 that the accepting side checks. Under pcr_recovery the same principal is selected by the accepted recovery policy and the account-local lineage, not by current DID controller state. Under applet_managed_delegation it is the Applet-managed principal's own principal_id.

authorization_binding_kind.description: The branch this transcript is signed for. accepted_device is absent by construction: that branch's candidate signs device-pairing.schema.json#/$defs/device_pairing_target_proof under its own domain instead, because at stage time it does not yet know the approving sibling. A verifier MUST select the domain from this member and MUST NOT accept a transcript reused across binding kinds.

authorized_generation_ref.description: PCR-local device generation this authorization is bound to, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.authorized_generation_ref. The candidate device signs it, so a relay cannot move an authorization to another generation without invalidating this signature (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.5.2).

expires_at.description: Required here and null when the payload omits it. Making it required is what makes the section 5.2.1 normalization executable: if it were optional, an omitted member and an explicit null would be two canonical byte strings for one authorization and the normalization could not be enforced.

scopes.description: Required here and null when the payload omits it, for the same reason as expires_at.

recovery_session_id.description: Required here; non-null only on the pcr_recovery branch and normalized to null on the two branches whose payload forbids the member.

strand_tracks_update_payload.description: Closed configuration-only payload for ak.strand.tracks.update; content writes use ak.strand.update.

agent_interaction_set_payload.description: Realm-scoped controller-only Agent interaction mode. Signed plaintext control, not membership or private participation selection. CAS and authority admission are defined in zh/models/agent-interaction.md section 1.

applet_managed_device_scope.description: One exact scope/action pair of a managed Device authorization. Only Realm and Circle are supported; no ancestor, Sidecar, wildcard or cross-entry action inheritance. Actions MUST be registered CapabilityActionId values, sorted in UTF-8 byte order and unique. See device-lifecycle section 16.1.

applet_managed_device_scopes.description: Non-empty canonical managed Device scope pairs. Exactly one entry per effective_scope; entries MUST be sorted by UTF-8 bytes of RFC8785 JCS(effective_scope). Receivers reject unsorted or repeated scopes, unknown actions and cross-entry combination; they never normalize signed bytes.

hpke_key.description: Device HPKE public key used for secret/key envelope encryption. It is covered by the possession transcript and by the surrounding root anchor or accepted-device Event proof; services MUST NOT substitute it. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_proof, which the approving device reads only after that attestation verifies.

algorithms.description: Canonical sorted unique algorithm ids supported by this device. Enters device trust binding transcript together with device_public_key_did and hpke_key. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_proof, not any service-supplied or staged copy.

authorized_generation_ref.description: Exact actor-local accepted generation, bound by the signed control and Device CAS. Never inferred from a DID version, Station epoch or PCR.

applet_id.description: Exact owning Applet from accepted Realm actor identity; every authorized business scope independently requires its current active installation and grant.

consent_permission.description: One concrete permission. A peer set contains at most one entry per scope, ordered invite, voice_call, video_call, presence. Complete optional-member presence is signed and preserved.

constraints.description: Optional consent-specific constraints (rate limits, time-of-day windows, device restrictions). v1 does not standardise constraint types beyond capability constraint vocabulary.

evidence_ref.description: Optional reference to claim disclosure, presentation response, or invite proof that triggered this consent (audit trail).

contract.description: Exact authorized Relation, moderation or Agent interaction current read at one governing-Station cut. It is non-enumerating and binds never-written to the exact selector. Includes the original issuer-only exact owned_agent capability_grant read, including ineffective and terminal rows; no never_written for grants. Also supports exact Agent/Applet Policy CAS reads by the authorized policy setter and exact Applet/Service registration CAS reads by a Realm administrator, including authoritative never_written. No enumeration or new permission.

exact_current_state_read_request_body.description: One exact, non-enumerating selector in one Realm. The caller cannot supply a revision, stream or governance Station.

exact_current_state_read_response_body.description: One authorized same-cut answer. never_written is an affirmative Station result, never an inference from omission, timeout or invisibility.

registry_id.description: Versioned registry symbol for a dependency, payload schema, or conformance vector.

retrieval_url.description: Optional retrieval hint only. The registry_id plus digest, not this URL, identifies the referenced content.

reducer_contract_ref.description: Digest-bound registered reducer contract. Execution, state models and conditional writes come only from that contract; the manifest cannot choose a different synchronization class or state profile.

contract.description: Plaintext shape that MUST be encrypted before writing ak.profile.file_transfer.v1 account-data values.

blob_size_bytes.description: Size of the stored blob bytes, usually ciphertext plus AEAD overhead.

media_type.description: Original file media type. This field lives inside encrypted account data; encrypted blob metadata SHOULD use application/octet-stream.

plaintext_size_bytes.description: Original file byte length before client-side encryption.

content_key.description: Fresh per-transfer content key carried only inside encrypted account-data plaintext.

key_envelope.description: HPKE base-mode authority commit of the content key for one recipient device. The HPKE info and AAD are the same JCS bytes projected from the authenticated DeviceMessageEnvelope and the message transfer_id (zh/models/file-transfer.md section 4.2); they are rebuilt by the recipient and never carried as an aad_digest.

enc.description: HPKE KEM encapsulated key for the recipient device.

constraint_id.description: Optional stable identifier of this constraint within the grant; used for diagnostics and overrides.

constraint_kind.description: Constraint family discriminator. v1 collapses what were 15 types into 8 by absorbing narrowly-scoped types into their conceptual parent: edit_window â†’ temporal; container_move â†’ scope_limitation; rate_limiting + resource_limit â†’ quota; approval_workflow + accountability + device_session â†’ claim_based (with constraint_subkind); encryption_requirement + visibility_control â†’ confidentiality (with constraint_subkind). Use the optional 'constraint_subkind' field to indicate the original specialization where evaluation logic differs.

effect.description: Unknown predicates do not satisfy allow and do apply deny, quarantine and require_review. Proven nonmatches do not apply refusal effects; see constraint-schema section 15.0.

evaluation_class.description: Cacheability/dependency hint for the authorization evaluator. stateless = pure function of (constraint, op, now); grant_local = depends on the grant object only; realm_state = depends on the exact Realm authority revision (membership, policy_version, etc.); external = depends on data outside that authority state (claim revocation status, rate-limit counts, async approval). Each constraint_kind has a canonical evaluation_class declared in constraint-schema.md Â§2.3; implementations MAY tighten (e.g. grant_local â†’ stateless) but MUST NOT loosen (e.g. external as stateless). Auth evaluators SHOULD use this hint to gate fast-path caching.

constraint_subkind.description: Optional discriminator within a constraint_kind. Standard values: claim_based.{claim,approval,accountability}; quota.{rate,resource}; confidentiality.{encryption,visibility}; temporal.{window,edit_window,redact_window,session}; authority_control.{applet_authority}. Per constraint-schema.md Â§2.2, device/session binding is NOT an independent constraint_subkind: it is the claim_based constraint_subkind=claim sub-case expressed via an accepted PCR device issuer. Implementations MAY require constraint_subkind for these families and fail closed on unknown values.

applies_to_actions.description: Optional restriction of a temporal constraint to specific capability actions (e.g. ['ak.message.revise.own', 'ak.message.redact.own']). Action mismatch is neutral in the effect fold: satisfied for effect=allow and not matched for deny/quarantine/require_review.

recurrence.description: Daily/weekly recurrence is core. Unsupported frequency, unknown IANA timezone and necessary unresolved DST boundaries are unknown predicates, never implicit nonmatches.

max_duration.description: From original authorization acceptance, never producer Event time, first use, refresh or not_before. Realm grants use their original RealmCommit.committed_at. Local predicate failure does not log out the account. Nonnegative integer components, at least one; UTC calendar months clamp before elapsed components. Zero expires immediately. Empty components are forbidden; overflow is unknown.

max_session_duration.description: From the issuer-ledger original authenticated session start. Refresh, reconnect and restart preserve the same lineage and start. Verified sessionless operations make only this predicate neutral. Nonnegative integer components, at least one; UTC calendar months clamp before elapsed components. Zero expires immediately. Empty components are forbidden; overflow is unknown.

inactivity_timeout.description: From issuer-confirmed last qualifying business activity, initially session start. No refresh, heartbeat, presence, replay or caller-supplied time. Verified sessionless operations make only this predicate neutral. Nonnegative integer components, at least one; UTC calendar months clamp before elapsed components. Zero expires immediately. Empty components are forbidden; overflow is unknown.

expires_after.description: ISO 8601 duration; used by approval_workflow constraint instead of expires_after_ms.

condition.description: Conditional predicate for field_access and similar constraints. The `kind` value is a registered named condition from constraint-schema.md Â§4.1; unknown kinds MUST fail closed. Implementations MUST NOT introduce ad hoc string DSL predicates.

allowed_space_kinds.description: Allowed Space kinds (e.g. 'board', 'list', or profile-registered kinds like 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket'). Reducer/profile MUST validate kind value.

allowed_circle_ids.description: Limits Circle-scoped capability actions to the listed Circle ids. Used by ak.circle.manage / ak.circle.member.manage style grants; unconstrained Realm-wide Circle management grants are not a normal permission shape.

allowed_session_ids.description: Limits applet interop-session operations to the listed applet-defined session correlation ids.

blob_presign_scope.description: Scope limiter for ak.self.blob.command.presign.v1 grants: allowed purposes plus optional blob/realm restrictions.

allowed_data_labels.description: Data classification labels this grant may read, export, transform, or send to external endpoints.

allowed_endpoints.description: Allowed outbound endpoint origins or deployment-approved endpoint patterns for applet / agent / connector operations.

max_authority_depth.description: Maximum remaining authority hops. Bounded by the canonical authority-chain depth ceiling (4) defined in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md Â§3 and zh/authz/capabilities.md Â§10.2; reducers MUST reject grants declaring a larger value at accept time rather than only truncating during DFS.

applet_id.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the accepted Applet registration.

executed_by.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the concrete Applet service, bot, or provisioned ghost ActorId that may execute the grant. A proof verification_method remains a DID URL; its adapter projection MUST equal the ActorId principal component, while the complete ActorId is verified from accepted authorization evidence.

registration_epoch.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the canonical Applet registration epoch.

blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum TTL, in seconds, that this grant permits for ak.blob.presign. The service must clamp requested max_age_seconds to the smaller of this value and deployment policy.

max_artifact_bytes.description: Maximum artifact size in bytes for applet / agent / export operations.

max_operation_count.description: Maximum number of distinct accepted idempotency identities in one UTC epoch-aligned fixed period. Enforcement is a linearizable check-and-reserve at one logical quota authority shared by every node in the enforcing service; per-node duplicated budgets and overshoot are forbidden.

period.description: ISO 8601 duration. For quota constraints, a stricter conditional schema permits only a non-zero fixed-length week/day/hour/minute/second duration; year/month durations are forbidden so every authority derives the same UTC epoch-aligned window id.

burst.description: Optional token-bucket capacity at the same logical quota authority, capped by max_operation_count and refilled at max_operation_count/period. It never increases the fixed-window total budget.

constraint_scope.description: Closed v1 quota counting scope. Unknown values are schema violations and MUST fail closed. Quota counters are actor-bound; the enum selects the additional slicing dimension: actor only, actor+space, actor+realm, or actor across all nodes/regions of the enforcing service's global quota domain. global is not an implicit federation-wide counter. Every node in the service domain MUST share one logical linearizable quota authority.

approval_mode.description: The only approval mode of v1. The approved write MUST NOT take effect before the approval evidence is verified and accepted in the same transaction (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.7). There is no second mode and no path that first materializes a proposal object and then approves that object.

approval_relation.description: Responsibility classification of this grant explicit approval_actor_ids roster. It never creates a second dynamic roster or supplies action/scope capability. Missing explicit roster cannot satisfy approval.

timeout.description: Positive fixed ISO 8601 duration (week/day/hour/minute/second, no calendar year/month). Each approval vote is valid only when the target covering committed_at <= that vote input.approved_at + timeout, inclusive and with zero tolerance. The same rule applies to Event and operation targets; receiver clocks and first-seen timestamps never anchor it. Omission adds no grant-local age limit.

approval_threshold.description: Closed executable vote threshold: majority means floor(N/2)+1, unanimous means N, and a positive integer is the exact quorum. N is the distinct eligible approver set at the accepting authority cut. Omission means unanimous. A missing or empty eligible set, or an integer greater than N, cannot satisfy approval. Repeated signatures by one approver count once. Parameterless quorum/custom strings are schema violations.

required_claims.description: Conditional claim requirements. resource-selector-grammar.md Â§3.3 caps this array at 32 entries as a normative DoS guard; the schema enforces maxItems:32 so condition-selector grants cannot smuggle in unbounded claim objects.

subject_matches_actor.description: If true, the credential subject did_core_id MUST match the actor did_core_id after each proof's DID is independently validated and projected through its registered method adapter.

value_constraints.description: Per-field equality / membership constraints on credential claims.

min_encryption_level.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static floor: the minimum content-encryption mechanism the grant requires. Pure static declaration evaluated as stateless unless cross-checked against the scope's current MLS activation state (see constraint-schema.md section 12).

plaintext_fallback_allowed.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant permits plaintext in a scope that has no accepted ak.mls.genesis. After activation the flag cannot restore plaintext; the write MUST be rejected with mls_activation_irreversible. See constraint-schema.md Â§12.

audit_trail_required.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant requires an audit trail (e.g. active Audit Applet Binding). See constraint-schema.md Â§12.

depends_on_moderation_state.description: Cache-invalidation hint: when true, this grant's authorization decisions depend on the moderation_state current state (see capabilities.md Â§18.1) and the grant's cache entry MUST be invalidated when that current state changes. Default false: ordinary grants (ak.strand.update / ak.message.create / organization membership grants) do NOT take a cache hit on every moderation decision. v1 capabilities.md Â§18.1 lists three conditions where MUST be explicitly true (moderator-role grants, condition-selector subjects referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue / current state). Schema-side enforcement of condition (2) is in capability-grant.schema.json via if/then on actions[]; conditions (1) and (3) are reducer-side lint. Cache invalidation hint outside the eight constraint families; it does not participate in allow/deny evaluation and is documented in capabilities.md Â§6 / constraint-schema.md.

allowed_managed_actor_roles.description: Ordinary authority_control permits only these accepted roles of the Applet bound by the parent applet_authority constraint; no arbitrary third-party regrant.

contract.description: Shared authority proof family for service operations that key-management.md designates as high-risk material destruction or equivalent (first consumer: active-series key backup tail deletion, key-management.md section 7.8). Exactly one closed branch: recovery_unlock, device_quorum, or trusted_recovery_service, discriminated by `kind`. Every branch reuses the common detached-JWS leaf (event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof) over the operation's single canonical delete-intent transcript; branches never restate the leaf fields. An ordinary current-device session proof is deliberately NOT a branch of this family — operations that accept it for low-risk paths must say so in their own normative text. This is one wire leaf with per-consumer domain separation: the transcript context is owned by the consuming operation, never by the leaf, so x-arkret-proof-contexts below enumerates every registered consumer context and proof-context-registry.json carries the matching consumer_operation on each row.

detached_proof.description: Common detached-JWS leaf. `payload_digest` MUST be the digest of the operation's canonical transcript, whose first member is the consuming operation's registered context (for key backup deletion: the delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1 under ak.key_backup_delete_proof.v1); `created_at` MUST fall inside the server-issued challenge window when the operation binds one. A signature made under another consumer's context MUST be rejected even when it verifies cryptographically.

recovery_unlock_proof.description: Recovery-unlock proof. recovery_session_id MUST select a verified, unexpired recovery session for the transcript's exact account. The session's accepted proof summary MUST be recovery_unlock and bind proof.verification_method; the verifier resolves that key only from the recovery policy frozen into the session. Current device keys, DID-document fallback keys, service keys and revoked recovery keys MUST be rejected.

proof.description: Detached-JWS leaf whose verification_method MUST resolve, at proof.created_at, to an authorized non-revoked device key of exactly this device_id under the transcript's principal_id. Every quorum member signs the same canonical transcript bytes.

device_quorum_proof.description: Device-quorum proof. The schema enforces only the minimum wire shape (threshold>=2, signatures.minItems=1). Verification is normative in the consuming operation's text: (a) every signature MUST verify over the same canonical transcript; (b) signatures MUST be deduplicated by device_id; (c) the count of valid deduplicated signatures MUST be >= threshold; (d) threshold MUST equal the currently accepted recovery policy device-quorum k — a smaller issuer-supplied threshold MUST be rejected as failed_precondition. A deployment whose policy k is below 2 cannot use this branch and must use recovery_unlock or trusted_recovery_service instead; a single current device proof is not a high-risk quorum.

threshold.description: The quorum threshold the issuer claims to satisfy. MUST equal the principal's currently accepted recovery_policy device-quorum k; receivers MUST cross-check per description rule (d).

signatures.description: minItems=1 is the schema floor only; receiver-side verification requires deduplicated valid signature count >= threshold per description rule (c).

trusted_recovery_service_proof.description: Trusted recovery service proof. The verification_method of `proof` MUST be controlled by service_id, and service_id MUST be authorized as a trusted recovery service by the recovery policy / DID delegation snapshotted into the referenced recovery session. The session MUST be unexpired, unconsumed for this purpose, and MUST have been established by recovery_unlock or device_quorum — the service alone is never a sufficient factor. v1 registers no attestation carrier on this branch: the recovery policy has no attestation_required switch, so an attestation reference here would be an unverified configuration surface rather than an enforced factor.

recovery_session_id.description: Verified, unexpired, unconsumed recovery session authenticated by recovery_unlock or device_quorum. A service-only session is not a second factor.

contract.description: Closed plaintext account-data current state value of ak.account.holder_quarantine. The recipient Station is the sole CAS writer; the current state is a pending-review pointer inbox and grants no membership, contact, or consent authority. surface_kind is the closed discriminator: invite_delivery entries reference an accepted invite Event and its introduction evidence, consent_request entries reference no Event at all. Contact delivery is not a branch here: a Contact request has its own pending_incoming state and MUST NOT get a second parallel review carrier.

updated_at.description: Instant of the accepted Station CAS write that produced this value.

quarantine_entries.description: Bounded pending-review entries, oldest first. Expired entries are purged before a write and overflow evicts the oldest entries.

last_invalidation.description: Optional diagnostic for the latest accepted consent-revoke invalidation. It is holder-private and never disclosed to the requester.

surface_kind.description: Closed discriminator for the admission surface that produced this entry. An unregistered value fails closed.

quarantine_entry.description: One pending-review quarantined admission. Membership in quarantine_entries is the only state this current state expresses: an entry is pending review until the holder reviews it or its TTL discards it, so no status member is carried. The two surface_kind branches are closed and mutually exclusive; a member declared by the other branch is a schema violation.

entry_digest.description: Recipient-service-local stable deduplication digest for this quarantined delivery.

account_id.description: Exact holder of this account-data current state and recipient of the quarantined invite. The sole CAS writer is account_id.station_id; another account with the same principal core is a different holder.

source_peer_principal_id.description: Original principal identity used only by the existing per-principal anti-abuse quota ledger; must agree with the authenticated full source actor. It is not a Consent peer selector or editor input.

source_peer_actor_id.description: Exact authenticated requester/inviter, including Account Station. Required for holder review and exact-peer permission authoring/invalidation; never infer it from source service or principal alone.

source_id.description: Authenticated transport source service DID. It never participates in the new-source quota identity key.

consent_scope.description: Requested consent scope. The invite_delivery branch pins it to invite; the consent_request branch admits every other registered scope. The enum mirrors zh/identity/consent-model.md section 4.

introduction_kind.description: Introduction evidence kind presented by the requester. invite_delivery branch only; a consent request has no introduction evidence, so any value there would be fabricated.

invite_event_id.description: Accepted invite Event identity. Its suite-tagged token is the sole wire source for the complete Event digest.

request_digest.description: Replay deduplication digest of the invite delivery request. invite_delivery branch only: ak.self.consent.command.request.v1 declares idempotency_mechanism none and carries no nonce, so its branch deduplicates by live-entry uniqueness instead.

idempotency_key_digest.description: Digest of the invite delivery Idempotency-Key. invite_delivery branch only, for the same reason as request_digest.

expires_at.description: Deployment-policy TTL. An expired entry is discarded and never converts to a grant.

consent_revoke_invalidation.description: Private quarantine invalidation when a complete peer permission replacement removes invite. Match the exact stored source_peer_actor_id; never clear another Station account of that principal. The source quota ledger remains independent and unchanged.

contract.description: Canonical RFC 9457 application/problem+json error response. The type URI is the stable machine discriminator and must resolve through error-code-registry.json. Unknown extension members are tolerated by consumers as required by RFC 9457; producers may emit only extensions registered for the selected type.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The complete object uses the RFC literal member vocabulary; instance is the standard URI-reference member rather than an Arkret wrapper role.

contract.description: Closed canonical plaintext retained only as exact historical MLS authentication material. This is not a current disclosure operation, lookup response, credential, membership grant, or a minimal_metadata_realm profile. The enclosing verified Event/Commit, MLS epoch and exact LeafNode remain mandatory authentication context.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators distinguish identity registry receipts from other receipt envelopes (e.g. audit-ryw-receipt, event-batch-receipt).

subject_did.description: Method-native bare DID whose exact accepted log entry at seq is committed by accepted_entry_digest. This identifies method history, not an Arkret business principal.

accepted_entry_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of the exact complete accepted method-native log entry, including its control proofs. It commits to immutable accepted bytes at subject_did and seq, not a PCR Event or an unsigned-operation projection. Receipts with different digests at the same position MUST NOT contribute to the same consensus quorum.

registry_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the registry service issuing the receipt. The detached proof verification_method remains a DID URL and MUST project to this value through the registered method adapter.

witness_role.description: Issuer's role in the DID registry consensus group. Required so verifiers can apply role-specific freshness / quorum rules; an absent role would force the verifier to guess writer vs replica semantics.

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

signature.description: Registry detached proof. payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with signature omitted)). The detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.identity_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, registry_id, subject_did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag and is not a wire field. signature.created_at MUST equal receipt.created_at. signature.verification_method MUST be a currently valid DID URL assertion method whose DID component is independently validated and projected to registry_id by the registered method adapter. Receipt audience and proof audience MUST either both be absent or be the same single string; array-valued proof audiences are invalid for this object family.

contract.description: Canonical did_core_id/did resolution state, owner-published evidence and service-route bootstrap contracts. A did is a standard bare DID and a did_core_id is the stable Arkret business identity projected by a registered DID method adapter.

authenticated_service_resolution.description: Public method-native service evidence. All route coordinates are derived from the independently verified DID state; this carrier creates no signed address history.

normalized_did_document.description: Exact normalized document verified by the registered DID method; project(did) equals service_id and its unique ArkretService entry selects service_kind.

method_evidence_boundary.description: Inclusive adapter-defined history interval covered by this evidence. For a method without native history the from and to values are identical synthetic values for the one verified state.

webvh_method_history_evidence.description: Complete did:webvh log, proof and witness material routed by evidence_kind webvh_log to the active did:webvh adapter. log_entries is the gap-free native history from inception through boundary.to_version_id, not a resolver summary or a partial segment. witness_records is the complete did-witness.json record set required by every witness policy active in that interval and is empty only when no entry activates a witness policy. The receiver independently verifies SCID derivation, every versionId/hash-chain link, every controller proof, rotation authorization, all applicable witness thresholds, the exact boundary endpoints and canonical equality of the terminal state with normalized_did_document. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB; an over-limit service history is ineligible for retained historical-signer and governance-Station bootstrap and fails closed rather than returning partial evidence.

evidence.description: Closed canonical evidence receipt for exactly the inclusive boundary. method MUST be webvh and method_proofs MUST carry the matching webvh_log row; the public evidence evaluator checks its history_head against boundary.to_method_history_head. This receipt summarizes the independently reverified log_entries/witness_records but never replaces them.

log_entries.description: Exact ordered native did:webvh entry objects from inception through the selected terminal entry. The adapter applies the registered did:webvh parameter-name and proof rules and rejects gaps, duplicates, surplus entries after boundary.to_version_id, or a first entry other than inception.

witness_records.description: Exact native did-witness.json record objects needed by log_entries. Records are keyed uniquely by versionId; missing, duplicate, invalid or surplus records fail closed. The array is empty exactly when the verified log activates no witness policy.

did_web_method_history_evidence.description: Bounded current DID Document retrieval evidence routed by evidence_kind did_web_document to the active did:web adapter. The boundary endpoints MUST be identical synthetic values. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB.

evidence.description: Closed canonical document-bound evidence receipt. method MUST be web and method_proofs MUST be empty; document_digest and boundary synthetic head are cross-checked by the public evidence evaluator.

did_key_method_history_evidence.description: Bounded deterministic local expansion evidence routed by evidence_kind did_key_expansion to the active did:key adapter. The boundary endpoints MUST be identical synthetic values. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB.

evidence.description: Closed canonical local-expansion evidence receipt. method MUST be key and method_proofs MUST be empty; the public evidence evaluator recomputes document_digest and the synthetic boundary directly from did.

method_history_evidence.description: Adapter-routed evidence. evidence_kind is the single-source discriminator: the receiver resolves it through did-method-adapter-registry.json method_evidence_kind, which is unique across active adapters, to exactly one active adapter for this versioned schema. The evidence carries no adapter_version; an adapter change requires a new schema/operation version rather than a registry drift under the same wire shape. Unknown evidence kinds fail closed.

resolution_commitment.description: Owner-committed current did and method-native history position. For a deterministic method, method_history_head and version_id use the adapter-defined deterministic canonical values; they are never omitted.

principal_resolution_update_payload.description: Signed PCR resolution CAS payload. expected_revision is the exact accepted identity_resolution source revision in the full Account PCR; the old projection and method boundary are read from that source at the same transaction cut before independent method-native successor verification.

principal_genesis_event.description: The accepted identity-control Realm genesis Event. It is resolution history head 0 and commits the initial resolution; its derived Realm id, actor, purpose and initial projection are cross-bound by the principal resolution evidence evaluator.

resolution_update_event.description: One accepted post-genesis resolution successor Event. payload.expected_revision binds the exact covering Commit of its immediately preceding accepted resolution Event in the same full Account PCR lineage.

principal_resolution_projection_attestat.description: Station assertion that resolution_projection is the current accepted value of this account's singleton resolution current state. It carries no PCR realm id, Event, receipt or RealmCommit: the public consumer verifies the account pair, the projection and the bounded method history, not the account's internal control stream.

account_id.description: Complete account identity covered by the Station attestation. Both principal and Station components participate in equality.

method_history_evidence_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the exact method_history_evidence object carried in the same response. It binds the attestation to the bounded adapter evidence so neither half can be swapped.

issued_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Hard freshness bound. A consumer performing a security-sensitive action MUST refetch at or after this instant; a cache never extends it.

principal_resolution_projection_attestat.description: Complete Station-signed projection attestation. The detached proof signs the canonical transcript above; proof.created_at MUST equal attestation.issued_at.

public_principal_resolution.description: Complete public resolution response for one account selected by account_id. It is the only unauthenticated resolution surface and it MUST NOT carry principal_control_realm_id, PCR genesis Event, genesis receipt, resolution Events or accepted RealmCommit; those are account-internal audit material served only by the authorized audit operation. A consumer verifies the service route for account_id.station_id, then the attestation proof, then project(did)=account_id.principal_id and the bounded method history; a set of bare unproven fields is not a valid response.

account_id.description: Complete public selector and external account identity. No PCR-derived value participates in account equality.

resolution_projection.description: Current accepted value of the singleton resolution current state. resolution_event_ref is an opaque head coordinate for staleness comparison; it is not a handle for fetching that Event through any public surface.

method_history_evidence.description: Bounded adapter-routed evidence for exactly the projected history position. It is required: without it the projection is an unverifiable server assertion.

principal_resolution_audit_request_body.description: Authorized request for account-internal resolution audit evidence. Authorization is the current holder session bound to the exact AccountId. Recovery actors first finish the existing recovery transaction and become the current holder; v1 does not create a second audit authorization path. Caller-declared intent is never authorization. Unknown account, wrong AccountId and unauthorized caller are externally indistinguishable and share the anti-enumeration outcome.

account_id.description: station_id MUST equal the serving Station DID. A different value is an unknown account, not a referral.

history_depth.description: Maximum number of post-genesis predecessor resolution Events to disclose, counted backwards from current_resolution_event. 0 discloses the current head only. A value outside the closed range is param_invalid; an implementation MUST NOT substitute a private cap.

after_resolution_event_ref.description: Known ancestor already held by the caller. The disclosed segment stops exclusively at it, so only the unknown suffix is returned. It MUST be the genesis Event or an accepted ak.identity.resolution.update in this account's current lineage; a ref outside that lineage is param_invalid with reason resolution_history_ancestor_unknown. Supplying it with history_depth 0 is param_invalid, because depth 0 discloses no predecessor and the cursor could not apply.

principal_resolution_audit_evidence.description: Account-internal resolution audit and recovery evidence for one account selected by account_id. It is served only by the authorized audit operation. PCR genesis, realm and RealmCommit material support account-local audit and recovery; they MUST NOT be compared as external identity, MUST NOT be required to validate an ordinary federated Event, which is verified from its producer proof and the RealmCommit that admitted it, and MUST NOT be republished on any unauthenticated surface.

account_id.description: Complete account selector. The remaining PCR material is recovery/audit evidence and does not change account equality.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Realm id derived from principal_genesis_event under the registered PCR derivation rule; it is not a producer-selected alternate scope.

genesis_commits.description: The two consecutive RealmCommit objects accepting principal_genesis_event and founding_device_authorize_event in that order.

predecessor_resolution_events.description: Post-genesis resolution update Events preceding current_resolution_event, ordered from the current event's immediate predecessor toward older events and contiguous with no gaps. The genesis Event is carried separately and MUST NOT be repeated here. The segment ends at whichever comes first: request history_depth items, the exclusive request after_resolution_event_ref ancestor, or head 0. A server MAY return a shorter contiguous segment than requested when a response bound applies, MUST NOT return more items than history_depth, and MUST NOT skip an intermediate Event.

accepted_commit.description: The authority-signed RealmCommit that accepted current_resolution_event in the Principal Control Realm stream.

history_complete.description: True exactly when the disclosed segment reaches its requested stop condition: head 0, or the exclusive after_resolution_event_ref ancestor. False means disclosure was truncated and next_audit_cursor is present. Omitted history is unknown rather than absent.

next_audit_cursor.description: Present exactly when history_complete is false. Resolve payload.expected_revision of the oldest disclosed resolution Event (current when no predecessors are disclosed) to its exact accepted covering RealmCommit in this Account PCR lineage, then return that Commit event_ref. No envelope precondition, whole-value guard, payload echo or unrelated Commit supplies this predecessor. Omitted history is unknown.

route_mirror_hint.description: Transport-only hint for one route-mirror service. mirror_id is only a stable lookup identity and MUST be paired with independently verifiable service_resolution first-hop material; neither the did_core_id nor the carrier authorizes target-service routing or Realm access.

mirror_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the candidate route-mirror service. A bare did_core_id is never a route or authority.

service_resolution.description: Discovery carrier for the mirror itself. The target requires independent current DID verification.

route_assistance.description: Transport-only bounded discovery hints. They do not authorize routing, extend outer token expiry, or supply current DID state.

mirror_hints.description: At most four independently routable mirror hints. Each item carries the mirror did_core_id together with a service_resolution_carrier; bare URLs and bare core ids are not valid items.

resolution_url.description: Bounded canonical HTTPS discovery URL for the public method evidence of the expected service. Fetch success supplies no authority or freshness.

service_route_projection.description: Derived route projection of one verified service DID state (sync/service-surface.md section 2.6). Every coordinate comes from the independently verified method-native state and its unique ArkretService entry; the projection creates no signed address history and carries no method evidence.

service_kind.description: Expected role selected from the DID Document; the value space is registry/service-kind-registry.json filtered to the context of the consuming result.

resolution_event_ref.description: Adapter coordinate emitted by the active did-method-adapter-registry row; it is a method-state position, never an Arkret Event handle.

base_url.description: Unique canonical absolute HTTPS service entry of the selected ArkretService entry, normalized with exactly one trailing slash.

founding_device_authorize_event.description: The founding device authorization Event immediately following the PCR realm.create Event.

contract.description: Private service-to-service request emitted by the current Realm governance Station after it commits an invite Event. The invitee Station treats included authority locations only as discovery hints.

invite_event.description: The ak.invite.create EventEnvelope being delivered. The inviter-side Station reads it from its own accepted, persisted canonical bytes; it is never rebuilt, re-signed or projected into another shape.

invite_commit.description: Realm-stream authority commit whose event_ref equals invite_event.event_id.

producer_signer_fact.description: Exact immutable original Human signer fact retained with invite_commit. Required exactly when invite_commit carries producer_signer_fact_digest; never reconstructed from current keys. Disclosure is limited to the existing exact invite recipient Station notification.

authority_locator_hints.description: One to eight untrusted locator cores, strictly sorted by service_id UTF-8 bytes. service_id is the semantic identity key; duplicate or conflicting representations of one service_id invalidate the entire array.

account_id.description: Exact invite recipient account. Delivery is sent only to account_id.station_id.

route_assistance.description: Optional transport-only hints for recovering the same Station route. This field is outside invite_event canonical bytes and MUST NOT be copied into durable Realm state; it does not extend invite/locator TTL, change AccountId, or authorize delivery.

consent_grant_ref.description: Original accepted ak.consent.replace Event issued by this exact holder for this exact peer, whose target contains invite. Historical reference only: actual delivery rechecks the current exact-peer invite entry, source and window. Does not disclose full-set value or confer Realm authority.

handle.description: Canonical handle string the inviter used as the human-readable entry point.

handle_claim.description: Signed HandleClaim status view proving that handle resolves to invite_address.account_id. The receiver MUST verify exact handle_claim.claim.subject_account_id equality, status=verified, the signed as_of/fresh_until window, null revocation fields, core/status proofs, core expiry, issuer trust, visibility/audience policy, and that handle_claim.claim.handle equals handle.

resolved_by.description: Optional stable Directory or issuer service did_core_id that supplied the handle resolution.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether the AccountId exists or whether policy quarantined/dropped the invite.
