A holder-quarantine outcome MUST be reported as deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Only a receiver policy disclosure level of outcome may add disclosed_outcome, and only with delivered|blocked.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result, closed to delivered|blocked. Present ONLY when the subject's receive policy disclosure level for this introduction trust tier is 'outcome' and the subject did not block the issuer; omitted (opaque) otherwise. delivered: the invite reached the holder surface awaiting acceptance; blocked: rejected by block list or policy. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST NOT be disclosed: it reveals holder-private consent state (identity/consent-model.md 6.1.1) and MUST be reported as status='deferred' with no disclosed_outcome, in the same response and timing equivalence class as rate-limit silent drop, timeout drop, holder-not-found and holder policy deny.

contract.description: Actor-private plaintext account-data current state value containing delivered directed-invite references and untrusted authority-bundle locator hints. It is not part of Realm history and carries no bearer credential.

updated_at.description: Instant of the accepted CAS write that produced this value.

delivery_entries.description: Bounded register of delivered directed invites, oldest first. At most one entry per invite_id; a redelivery of the same invite_id replaces the previous entry. Entries whose expires_at has passed are purged on the next write; overflow beyond 200 evicts the oldest entries.

invite_id.description: Invite ID derived from the accepted ak.invite.create Event; the deduplication key of this register.

inviter_account_id.description: Complete AccountId of the inviter, copied from the accepted invite Event and verified by the delivery chain.

authority_locator_hints.description: One to eight untrusted locator cores, strictly sorted by service_id UTF-8 bytes. service_id is the semantic identity key; duplicate or conflicting representations of one service_id invalidate the entire array. The invitee's own Station must fetch and verify a nonce-bound RealmAuthorityBundle before any preview, join preparation, or bootstrap request.

received_at.description: Instant the recipient Station accepted this delivery into the current state.

expires_at.description: Expiry copied from the accepted invite; an entry with expires_at <= now is stale and MUST NOT be used to accept the invite.

contract.description: Subject-private policy used by a Station to decide which invite delivery or first-contact request introduction evidence may notify the holder. This policy is not written into the target Realm durable event log or the public contact fact log.

account_id.description: Exact account whose private invite receive policy this object configures. The authenticated holder and the account-data current state owner MUST equal both components; another account with the same principal core MUST NOT share this policy.

holder_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Allowlist of introduction evidence kinds that may reach holder notification or review.

explicit_address_behavior.description: Default behavior for explicit_address evidence. Deployments SHOULD default to quarantine or drop, not notify.

handle_claim_behavior.description: Default behavior for handle_claim evidence. Omitted means quarantine. A subject MAY set notify to allow verified handle-based requests to reach the holder, but the effective value is capped by receive_policy_constraints.

unknown_invites.description: Behavior for invite/contact delivery requests without compliant introduction_evidence.

consent_profile.description: Holder-selected invite consent gate profile (consent-model.md section 6.1). Omitted means default. Under require_explicit_consent only verified consent_grant introduction evidence may notify the holder; every other invite or first-contact delivery without an active grant is silently dropped on the holder Station: no quarantine entry, no new-source ledger charge, no holder-private write, and the requester observes the same opaque status=deferred without disclosed_outcome regardless of trust tier or disclosure settings. The profile is subject-private: it is never advertised through ServiceDescribe and MUST NOT be observable by requesters or peer Stations. It is independent of the Realm-level realm_policy_bundle preauth.consent_required flag, which only forces the admission gate to run and selects no profile.

new_source_quota.description: Subject-private ceiling on how many previously unseen source peers may make a first contact with this holder. The ceiling is evaluated at the single holder admission chokepoint of identity/consent-model.md section 6.1.1.3 and therefore covers all three first-contact surfaces -- invite delivery, contact delivery and the identity/consent-model.md section 6.1.1 consent request -- not only the surfaces that write a holder_quarantine entry; contact delivery is charged the same way while its carrier is the Contact pending_incoming head. Each member is intersected with the deployment new_source_quota: the effective value is min(subject value, deployment max). An omitted member takes the deployment default. 0 is legal and locks the holder to zero new sources; every further first contact is silently dropped inside the existing opaque deferred equivalence class.

source_count_per_window.description: Holder ceiling for the short sliding window declared by receive_policy_constraints.new_source_quota.window_seconds.

source_count_per_retention.description: Holder ceiling for distinct new sources inside the long sliding window declared by receive_policy_constraints.new_source_quota.retention_seconds.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Optional subject-private allowlist for canonical handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty or omitted means no subject-level domain restriction; deployment constraints may still restrict the effective set.

denied_handle_domains.description: Subject-private denylist for canonical handle domains. Matches are rejected before allowed_handle_domains is evaluated.

trusted_handle_issuer_ids.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of handle claim issuers accepted for handle_claim evidence.

trusted_directory_ids.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of Directory service DIDs accepted as resolved_by for handle_claim evidence.

denied_actor_ids.description: Per-account/actor block list. Invite delivery whose exact inviter ActorId is in this list MUST be dropped, and disclosure MUST be forced to opaque regardless of the disclosure policy. Accounts with the same principal core at different Stations are distinct.

disclosure.description: Graded disclosure policy. Controls whether the invite/contact delivery outcome reveals a real result (delivered/blocked) to the requester, by introduction trust tier. Holder quarantine is never disclosable at any tier: it maps to status=deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Omitted means the default: high_trust=outcome, discovery_trust=opaque, low_trust=opaque.

domain_name.description: Canonical IDNA A-label domain. Subdomains are not implied; list each accepted domain explicitly.

disclosure_level.description: opaque: only a generic accepted-for-processing status is returned, indistinguishable across exists/not-exists/policy outcomes. outcome: the real delivered|blocked result is disclosed to the inviter. Neither level ever discloses holder quarantine.

high_trust.description: Disclosure level for the high-trust introduction tier: consent_grant, locator_ref, shared_realm. Default outcome.

discovery_trust.description: Disclosure level for public or restricted discovery evidence: handle_claim. Default opaque.

low_trust.description: Disclosure level for the low-trust introduction tier: same_station, explicit_address, and missing/non-compliant evidence. Default opaque.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound applied to subject-private receive policies. The effective receive policy is the intersection of the subject policy and these constraints; constraints can only make a subject less reachable, never more reachable.

applies_to.description: Surfaces governed by the introduction-evidence and disclosure members of this constraint object: deployment_allowed_introduction_kinds, deployment_denied_introduction_kinds, the three *_max_behavior members, disclosure_max, and the handle domain, handle issuer, directory, source and DID method lists. Omitted means both invite_delivery and contact_request. new_source_quota is NOT filtered by this member and always applies to all three first-contact surfaces (identity/consent-model.md section 6.1.1). The enum stays closed at these two values because the identity/consent-model.md section 6.1.1 consent request surface carries no introduction evidence and takes no part in graded disclosure, so the filtered members have nothing to select on it.

deployment_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Maximum set of introduction evidence kinds this deployment permits. Omitted means no deployment-level kind cap.

handle_claim_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for handle_claim evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

explicit_address_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for explicit_address evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

new_source_quota.description: Deployment ceiling and defaults for the per-holder new-source quota required by identity/consent-model.md section 6.1.1. Omitting the object does NOT disable the quota: every omitted member takes the specification default below, because the quota itself is a MUST. This object MUST NOT be filtered by applies_to: it is the threshold of the single holder admission chokepoint of section 6.1.1.3, where invite delivery, contact delivery and the identity/consent-model.md section 6.1.1 consent request share one ledger and one set of thresholds, so it applies to all three surfaces whatever applies_to says. Both windows are sliding and are evaluated against one server-internal seen-source ledger; the quota never becomes observable to the requester, whose outcome stays inside the existing opaque deferred equivalence class.

window_seconds.description: Short sliding rate window in seconds. Specification default 86400.

default_source_count_per_window.description: Short-window admission count used when the subject publishes no override. Specification default 3.

max_source_count_per_window.description: Upper bound a subject may raise the short window to. Specification default 10. MUST be greater than or equal to default_source_count_per_window.

retention_seconds.description: Long sliding window in seconds. It is also the seen-source ledger retention period; the two are one parameter. Specification default 2592000. MUST be greater than or equal to window_seconds.

default_source_count_per_retention.description: Long-window distinct new-source count used when the subject publishes no override. Specification default 30.

max_source_count_per_retention.description: Upper bound a subject may raise the long window to. Specification default 200, anchored to the quarantine current state maxItems. MUST be greater than or equal to default_source_count_per_retention.

disclosure_max.description: Deployment/admin upper bound on graded invite outcome disclosure. Each present tier caps the corresponding subject disclosure value using opaque < outcome; omitted tiers impose no additional deployment cap.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Deployment-level allowlist for handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty means no handle domain is accepted.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent invite state update.

third_party_invite.description: Wire-level 3PID/OOB invite binding. No plaintext email/phone/SMS code is allowed here. `oob_code_kind` distinguishes offline high-entropy token validation from server-side lookup short-code validation.

display_name_hint.description: Non-identifying UI hint only; MUST NOT contain plaintext 3PID.

token_commitment.description: SHA-256 of the private per-invite salt followed by the raw token UTF-8 bytes. Required in both modes; lookup uses a secret 256-bit salt in addition to its rate-limited pepper/HMAC index.

token_salt_id.description: Opaque handle for the verification service's private salt record. The salt value itself MUST NOT appear on wire.

lookup_table_ref.description: Opaque verification-service lookup table reference for short-code mode. The raw short code MUST NOT appear on wire.

pepper_id.description: Server-private pepper generation identifier for lookup mode; the pepper value itself is never on wire.

oob_code_kind.description: offline_token means the out-of-band code is itself >=128-bit entropy and validated against token_commitment. lookup means the human-readable code is only an index into a server-private lookup table protected by rate limits and pepper/HMAC storage.

token_entropy_bits.description: Required for offline_token mode. Entropy estimate excluding separators.

verification_public_key.description: Ephemeral public key or DID verification method used by the verification service to sign claim results.

third_party_invite_provisioning_id.description: Opaque verification-service handle for one private provisioning record, carrying 256 CSPRNG bits in unpadded base64url. It addresses the record on the activation and status surfaces and MUST NOT be written into a durable Realm Event, treated as invite permission, or treated as activation authority.

third_party_invite_provisioning_state.description: Verification-service-private lifecycle of one provisioning record. provisioned: material exists and is bound to no invite, so nothing may be delivered. activated: bound to exactly one accepted ak.invite.third_party and the delivery intent is durable. consumed: the token was presented and its binding_proof signed. expired: the activation window elapsed with no binding. revoked: the bound invite reached a terminal state or the inviter lost the capability. It is service-local state, never a Realm invite current state state and never a reducer input.

third_party_invite_delivery_state.description: Out-of-band delivery progress of an activated provisioning record. failed reports only that the service exhausted its retry budget; the Realm-visible transition still requires an authorized writer to submit ak.invite.revoke with target_state send_failed.

third_party_invite_delivery_target_uri.description: Private out-of-band delivery target for one third-party invite, as an RFC 6068 mailto: or RFC 3966 tel: URI. It appears only in the provisioning request body: the verification service MUST NOT echo it in any response, MUST NOT write it into a durable Realm Event, account-data current state, notification or ordinary log, and MUST keep only the salted delivery_target_digest of section 4.1 in its encrypted audit record.

third_party_invite_provision_request_bod.description: Request body of ak.open.third_party_invite.command.provision.v1 (zh/sync/third-party-invites.md section 7.2). An authenticated inviter asks the verification service to mint the private token, salt or pepper and per-invite ephemeral key for one third-party invite and to return only the public material. The verification service authenticates the caller from signature alone, applies its anti-abuse budget, and MUST NOT treat a successful provisioning as invite permission, as a pending Realm Invite, or as authority to deliver anything.

request_id.description: Caller-minted idempotency identity of this provisioning attempt. The same request_id with byte-identical canonical intent MUST return the original public material and provisioning_id; the same request_id with any different intent MUST fail with duplicate_conflict and MUST NOT mint a second set of material.

realm_id.description: Realm the invite will be authored into. It is frozen into the provisioning record and MUST equal the Realm of the accepted ak.invite.third_party at activation.

inviter_account_id.description: Complete AccountId of the inviter. It MUST equal the account the request signature resolves to, and MUST equal the author of the accepted ak.invite.third_party at activation.

verification_id.description: Verification service DID the inviter selected. It MUST equal the service serving this request and is copied verbatim into the returned third_party_invite; Realm allowlist membership is re-checked by the reducer and at activation, never established here.

oob_code_kind.description: Mode the inviter requests. A service that does not implement the requested mode MUST answer unsupported_feature instead of silently downgrading; the returned third_party_invite carries exactly this mode.

expires_at.description: Requested invite expiry. The service MUST clamp it to the profile ceiling of section 6 and return the effective value; the accepted ak.invite.third_party MUST carry the returned value verbatim.

signature.description: Inviter proof over the ak.third_party_invite_provision_request_proof.v1 transcript. verification_method MUST be a current verification method of inviter_account_id.principal_id; audience MUST be verification_id; the service MUST enforce a bounded freshness window and one-time replay protection.

third_party_invite_provision_response_bo.description: Success body of ak.open.third_party_invite.command.provision.v1: exactly the public material the inviter puts into ak.invite.third_party, plus the opaque handle that later binds the accepted invite back to this private record. It MUST NOT carry the raw token, token_salt, lookup pepper, ephemeral private key or delivery_target_uri, and it MUST NOT be presented to the invitee.

third_party_invite.description: Public material to copy verbatim into the ak.invite.third_party payload. Activation compares the accepted invite current state against this object member for member; any edit makes the invite unactivatable.

expires_at.description: Effective invite expiry after profile clamping. It is the value the ak.invite.third_party payload MUST carry.

activation_expires_at.description: Instant after which this provisioning record can no longer be activated. It MUST NOT be later than expires_at. Once it passes the record moves to expired, its material is zeroized on the section 6.1 schedule, and it MUST NOT be revived.

third_party_invite_acceptance_attestatio.description: Station-signed, purpose-scoped observation that one exact ak.invite.third_party is accepted and still pending on the Station's current accepted basis. It is the only standard carrier that lets an independent verification service activate its private record without holding Realm state; a caller-reported invite_id, invite digest, Event signature or HTTP success MUST NOT be accepted in its place. It grants no governance read access and authorizes nothing except activation of the named provisioning record.

station_id.description: Service DID of the Station that evaluated the Realm state and signed this attestation. The consumer resolves it through ak.open.service.read.resolution.v1 and MUST reject an attestation whose signature verification_method does not project to it.

verification_id.description: Exact verification service this attestation is issued to. It MUST equal the third_party_invite verification_id and the service consuming it, and signature.audience MUST equal it verbatim; any other service MUST reject the attestation. Purpose separation comes from the registered ak.third_party_invite_acceptance_attestation_proof.v1 signing context, so a signature made for another object family never verifies here.

invite_id.description: Invite id derived from the accepted ak.invite.third_party Event; it is never minted at provisioning time.

inviter_account_id.description: Complete AccountId of the accepted Event author, as the Station verified it.

provisioning_id.description: Provisioning record this attestation is scoped to. It binds the attestation to one activation request and makes it useless for any other record.

third_party_invite.description: Exact public material carried by the accepted invite current state. Together with invite_id, realm_id and invite_expires_at it is the complete preimage the consumer recomputes invite_digest from, per section 4.2.

invite_expires_at.description: The accepted invite current state expires_at. It is the fourth member of the section 4.2 invite_digest preimage and MUST NOT be confused with this attestation's own expires_at.

invite_state.description: The Station attests the invite is pending on the observed basis. There is no attestation shape for any other invite state; a non-pending invite yields no attestation at all.

observed_at.description: Instant the Station evaluated the current accepted invite and policy basis in its serializable issuance gate. A consumer uses this for audit ordering; it decides attestation validity from the signed expires_at without consulting a Realm-configured grace window.

expires_at.description: Explicit attestation validity end chosen by the issuing Station's service policy. It MUST be later than or equal to observed_at and MUST NOT exceed invite_expires_at. A later invite revoke blocks new attestations but does not rewrite an already issued attestation before this signed expiry.

signature.description: Station proof over the ak.third_party_invite_acceptance_attestation_proof.v1 transcript.

third_party_invite_acceptance_attestatio.description: Request body of ak.self.third_party_invite.read.acceptance_attestation.v1 (zh/sync/third-party-invites.md section 7.4). The authenticated inviter asks its own Station for the purpose-scoped acceptance attestation of one exact invite it authored. The Station evaluates its current accepted basis; the caller supplies no governance material and receives no governance closure.

provisioning_id.description: Provisioning record the attestation will be scoped to. The Station copies it verbatim and never resolves it against verification-service state.

verification_id.description: Verification service the attestation is issued to. The Station MUST reject a value that differs from the accepted invite current state verification_id.

third_party_invite_acceptance_attestatio.description: Success body of ak.self.third_party_invite.read.acceptance_attestation.v1. An invite that is not visible to the caller, was not authored by the caller, or is not pending on the current accepted basis returns the uniform not_found of section 6; a basis the Station cannot currently confirm returns revision_unavailable.

third_party_invite_activation_request_bo.description: Request body of ak.open.third_party_invite.command.activate.v1 (zh/sync/third-party-invites.md section 7.5). It binds one provisioning record to exactly one accepted ak.invite.third_party. The attestation is the whole authorization: the service MUST NOT accept a bare invite id, a caller-computed invite digest, or its own optimistic read of a remote Realm.

provisioning_id.description: Provisioning record to activate. It MUST equal acceptance_attestation.provisioning_id.

third_party_invite_activation_response_b.description: Success body of ak.open.third_party_invite.command.activate.v1: the immutable binding this activation established. A byte-identical retry, a concurrent duplicate and a retry after a process restart all return this same body; the current lifecycle and delivery position are read separately through ak.open.third_party_invite.read.provisioning_status.v1.

activated_at.description: Instant the binding and the delivery intent were durably committed. It is the first activation instant and never advances on retry.

third_party_invite_provisioning_status_r.description: Request body of ak.open.third_party_invite.read.provisioning_status.v1 (zh/sync/third-party-invites.md section 7.6). provisioning_id is the whole query credential and MUST travel only in this JSON body. An unknown handle, a handle belonging to another inviter, and a deleted record MUST be indistinguishable.

Lifecycle and delivery position of one provisioning record. It is the recovery surface for a lost provisioning or activation response and the only standard delivery observation point. It MUST NOT carry the raw token, token_salt, lookup pepper, ephemeral private key, delivery_target_uri or any 3PID-derived value, and it MUST NOT reveal whether the invitee has opened the invite.

invite_id.description: Invite this record is bound to. Present exactly when the record has been activated.

activated_at.description: First activation instant, identical to the activation outcome value.

delivery_attempt_count.description: Out-of-band delivery attempts made so far. An external mail or SMS gateway MAY deliver the same invite more than once; a count above one is not evidence that the invitee received more than one distinct invite.

third_party_invite_present_request_body.description: Request body of ak.open.third_party_invite.command.present_token.v1 (zh/sync/third-party-invites.md section 4.1). The invitee's client presents the out-of-band invite_token together with the exact account it wants bound and the intended Realm; the verification service atomically consumes the token and returns the binding_proof the client then carries into ak.invite.claim. invite_token MUST travel only in this JSON body: a request that carries it in the URL query string or path segment is rejected with third_party_invite_token_in_query before any lookup.

invite_token.description: Raw invite token read from the URL fragment or entered as an out-of-band code, with any user-facing separators removed. Offline tokens are >= 128 bits of entropy; lookup short codes are validated against the service-private lookup table (section 3.2).

realm_id.description: Intended Realm. MUST equal the Realm the pending ak.invite.third_party belongs to; the service binds it into binding_proof.realm_id.

subject_account_id.description: Exact account to bind. Copied verbatim into binding_proof.subject_account_id; the invitee later proves control of it with subject_proof in ak.invite.claim.

subject_did.description: Complete method-native DID whose projection MUST equal subject_account_id.principal_id; lets the verification service resolve the DID independently before signing.

claim_nonce.description: Client-generated one-time nonce; bound into binding_proof.claim_nonce and reused as ak.invite.claim claim_nonce. Re-presenting the same consumed token with the same (realm_id, subject_account_id, claim_nonce) MAY return the same binding_proof within the service's recoverable window (section 6.1); any other tuple MUST be refused.

third_party_invite_present_response_body.description: Success body of ak.open.third_party_invite.command.present_token.v1: everything the invitee's client needs to author ak.invite.claim besides its own subject_proof. Failure responses are non-enumerable (section 6): they MUST NOT reveal whether the token, invite or Realm exists.

token_commitment.description: The pending invite current state's salted commitment, copied into ak.invite.claim token_commitment.

contract.description: Signed principal-control record selecting the backup series for one actor and backup kind. Servers verify the accepted record; ordinary clients consume BackupActiveSeriesState from their Account Station instead of replaying PCR history.

series_pointer_version.description: Strictly monotonic per (actor_id, backup_kind). The first record is 1 and every successor is previous+1; receivers reject rollback, gaps and same-version forks.

previous_series_ids.description: Retained old series used only for read-old-data or erasure transition. MUST NOT be treated as a primary recovery source.

source_commit_ref.description: Principal Control Realm source RealmCommit and current identity-root device generation under which active_series_id was selected.

signature.description: base64url signature over RFC 8785 JCS(record without signature_proof.signature). The closed record shape fixes the authenticated projection.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted current-generation ak.device.authorize Event anchoring the device that signed this active-series selection.

device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic device generation. This is not a DID versionId and MUST equal the accepted current_device_generation_ref at the referenced checkpoint.

contract.description: Exact single-object backup unlock intent signed by the accepted current device or by the verified recovery session frozen replacement identity key. Current authority and immutable object identity are rechecked even on exact replay.

account_id.description: Exact authenticated account pair; both principal and Station must equal the challenge or frozen recovery session.

challenge.description: Required exact server challenge: current-device challenge record, or recovery_session.challenge. Caller-minted values are forbidden.

verification_method.description: current_device: exact current accepted device method; recovery_session: the exact frozen requesting_device_public_key_did from the session. A recovery factor signer or arbitrary DID resolver fallback MUST NOT authorize this intent.

signature.description: base64url signature over RFC 8785 JCS(unlock proof without signature_proof.signature), including every present closed-branch field.

audience.description: Exact authenticated service origin. Must equal the current-device server challenge origin or the recovery service origin bound by the authenticated recovery grant.

mixed_secret_storage.description: True only for the personal_node exception where one encrypted backup envelope contains both identity-signing material and E2EE / MLS history material. Non-personal deployment profiles MUST reject this flag. When true and recipient_method=passphrase_kdf, the stricter Argon2id floor below applies.

series_id.description: Stable identifier for one immutable chain of backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_kind). A pair MAY have multiple series during compromise rotation or migration; active series selection is outside this envelope and MUST come from the signed active-series record in identity/key-management.md §7.6. Receivers use (actor_id, backup_kind, series_id) to detect server-side rollback / withholding within the selected series.

series_sequence.description: 0-based, strictly monotonically increasing sequence number within (actor_id, series_id). Genesis envelope of a series MUST set 0. Receivers MUST reject envelopes whose sequence does not strictly exceed the previously accepted sequence in the same series. This predecessor/CAS axis is independent of the optional source_commit_ref checkpoint.

supersedes_id.description: backup_id of the immediate predecessor in the same series_id. MUST be absent for series_sequence=0; MUST be present, non-null, and reference an existing predecessor for series_sequence>0.

supersedes_digest.description: Required when supersedes_id is non-null. Hash of the canonical_json of the predecessor envelope (excluding signature_proof.signature). Receivers MUST recompute and reject mismatches as `series_chain_broken`.

source_commit_ref.description: The only canonical optional source checkpoint for genesis and successor authoring. Its exact wire and public builder shape is source_commit_ref{realm_commit_id: RealmCommitId, device_generation_ref: u64 >= 1}. Producers MUST authenticate this member under the envelope signature when present and MUST NOT accept or serialize source_ref, a nested/full CommittedEventRef, a string generation, Seal data, or a frontier digest. This checkpoint is independent of series_sequence, supersedes_id, and supersedes_digest and never substitutes for the successor predecessor/CAS chain.

device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic device generation. This is not a DID versionId and MUST equal the accepted current_device_generation_ref at the referenced checkpoint.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Required whenever encryption.recipient_method is recovery_public_key, and optional as a signed recovery-strand hint otherwise. Binds the backup envelope to the active recovery policy version under which it was produced. Receivers MUST compare this tuple to the currently accepted recovery policy before using such an envelope; mismatch fails as recovery_policy_mismatch, but the field does not replace active-series, checkpoint, Realm/MLS authorization, or device-state checks. This is intentionally separate from source_commit_ref: it binds the recovery authorization surface, not only the device trust generation or control-stream position.

recipient_key_ref.description: For recipient_method=recovery_public_key, this MUST resolve to the inline backup_hpke.key_agreement_ref of a non-revoked method signing entry in the envelope's referenced accepted recovery policy, and the selected hpke_suite MUST appear in that entry's hpke_suites. DID Document-only key agreements are not an authorization source. A method signing entry's verification_method is a signing-key ref and MUST be rejected here.

hpke_suite.description: Registered active HPKE suite (KEM x KDF x AEAD per RFC 9180) selector; the value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Applies only to recipient_method=recovery_public_key. When absent it denotes the default-MUST row ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1. aead.name MUST equal the selected suite's AEAD. An unregistered or inactive suite MUST be rejected (unsupported_hpke_suite). Absent / ignored for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key).

salt.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 16 KDF salt bytes; decoders MUST check the decoded length and canonical re-encoding.

aead_profile.description: Optional AEAD profile id that binds algorithm version, nonce length, tag length, key length, and AAD construction. Receivers that do not support the profile MUST fail closed instead of inferring semantics from name alone.

nonce.description: base64url AEAD nonce. Required for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key). For passphrase_kdf this is HMAC-SHA256(nonce_key, the exact §7.5.1 JCS nonce transcript)[0:24]; an absent aead_profile uses the effective XChaCha20-Poly1305 v1 profile in that transcript. Receivers recompute and reject mismatches. Absent for recovery_public_key (HPKE derives its nonce internally).

nonce_salt.description: Producer-generated base64url random salt (at least 128 bits before encoding) included in the passphrase_kdf nonce derivation transcript. Required when recipient_method=passphrase_kdf; not secret, signed as envelope metadata, and prevents nonce reuse from duplicate business metadata tuples.

enc.description: base64url HPKE KEM encapsulated key. Required for recipient_method=recovery_public_key; the KEM/KDF/AEAD are pinned by encryption.hpke_suite (default ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1) per artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Absent for the symmetric methods.

domain_separation.description: Signed key-backup domain separation inputs. The HKDF info and fixed AEAD/HPKE AAD base are derived exactly from the envelope by key-management.md §7.2; only the subdomain and genuine x_* AAD extensions are carried on the wire.

aead_aad_extensions.description: Optional producer-chosen AEAD/HPKE AAD extensions. Every member name MUST be x_*; implementations merge these members into the fixed derived AAD base before RFC 8785 canonicalization and MUST reject collisions.

contents.description: Signed, nonempty public index of every encrypted plaintext item. Each entry is matched by item_kind and secret_id after decryption; item_kinds for the §7.2 AEAD AAD are derived only from this closed index.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the device signing key.

signature_algorithm.description: Current-v1 raw signature algorithm name. Reserved ML-DSA-65 is not admitted until a future negotiated schema/profile activation.

signature.description: base64url-encoded signature over RFC 8785 JCS(envelope without signature_proof.signature). Every present closed envelope member, including optional and x_* members, is authenticated; no wire field list selects the projection.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted current-generation ak.device.authorize Event anchoring the device signing this backup.

contract.description: Canonical Arkret-specific evidence for ak.profile.key_transparency.v1 and high-security/sovereign log-backed witness requirements. This wire object is not an implementation of IETF KEYTRANS and MUST NOT be advertised as such; interop with draft-ietf-keytrans-protocol-05 requires a separately registered adapter/profile.

Closed request and response DTOs for self and peer MLS KeyPackage upload, claim, claim-status query, consume, and revoke operations. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

object_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

keypackage_capability_id.description: Open registered identifier from keypackage-capability-registry.json. Unknown well-formed values are preserved but treated as unsupported.

keypackage_capability_set.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted unique KeyPackage capability identifiers. Semantic registry membership and ordering are enforced after structural schema validation.
keypackage_capability_set.x-arkret-canonical-order: Sort by canonical encoded element bytes; elements MUST be unique.

keypackage_id.description: Arkret MLS-profile KeyPackage identity. This is the registered ak:mls:kp:<uuidv7> special form, not an opaque external identifier.

keypackage.description: Base64url encoding of the canonical MLS KeyPackage bytes.

cipher_suites.description: Generated from active canonical_id rows in mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.

last_resort.description: When true, this entry is a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10). It remains published across claims and never enters the single-use claimed or consumed states; rotation, expiry, or explicit revocation transitions it to revoked with a registered revocation_reason. This application-layer flag is covered by the required upload batch endpoint_signature. Optional capability gated by ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

actor_id.description: Complete holder ActorId; exact RFC 8785/JCS UTF-8 bytes equal the KeyPackage BasicCredential. Realm actor is bound to its owning Realm.

agent_id.description: Agent KeyPackage branch only. MUST equal principal_id and the current AgentSignerEvidence agent identity. It is never encoded as an ak:device identifier.

agent_verification_method.description: Agent runtime method that signed the exact KeyPackage; MUST match agent_key_authorize_event_id and the KeyPackage signature byte for byte.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted active ak.agent.key.authorize Event that binds an Agent runtime verification method to this KeyPackage. Mutually exclusive with device_authorize_event_id.

last_resort.description: When true, this claim record returns a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10) because the single-use pool was empty. The package may be reused within the same intended_realm_id and is not transitioned to consumed; the holder MUST rotate it and trigger group updates on next online. Optional capability gated by ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

keypackage_claim_record.description: Complete holder identity is actor_id. Account/Agent retains its principal projection. Realm actor carries only its full RealmActorId and Device authorization; no principal mirror or Account fallback.

actor_id.description: Complete holder ActorId whose exact RFC 8785/JCS UTF-8 bytes are carried by every uploaded KeyPackage BasicCredential. The account principal MUST equal principal_id.

endpoint_signature.description: Required authoritative batch signature over the complete typed upload request with only this top-level signature omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.upload.create.v1 domain. The selected human device or Agent runtime endpoint signs the same transcript.

keypackage_refs.description: Accepted KeyPackage refs in request order; batch upload may accept more than one entry.

requester_authorization.description: Closed Account Device, Realm actor Device or Agent authorization. Full Realm requester identity is signed in requester_actor_id on the unsigned request, never a parallel principal mirror.

target_account_id.description: Exact cross-Station AccountId for the human-device target branch. It is forbidden for Agent targets.

requester_account_id.description: Exact cross-Station AccountId for the human-device requester branch. It is forbidden for Agent requesters.

target_keypackage_ref.description: Optional exact ordinary KeyPackage selector for a normal same-group Direct Conversation Add/Welcome after accepted member rejoin. When present, the owner authority atomically claims exactly this current, unconsumed package or returns the same opaque claim_failed result as every other target-side failure; it is never a best-effort hint.

target_agent_id.description: Agent exact-target branch only. This field is the sole target identity carrier and MUST match the Agent identity in the returned claim record and current AgentSignerEvidence.

target_agent_verification_method.description: Agent exact-target branch current runtime verification method.

target_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Agent exact-target branch current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event.

peer_keypackages_claim_fields.description: Server-prepared immutable peer claim request fields before requester_authorization is attached. claim_request_id carries at least 128 bits of entropy and equals the Idempotency-Key value on the peer command.

target_account_id.description: Exact cross-Station AccountId for the human-device target branch. It is forbidden for Agent targets.

requester_account_id.description: Exact cross-Station AccountId for the human-device requester branch. It is forbidden for Agent requesters.

target_keypackage_ref.description: Optional exact ordinary KeyPackage selector for a normal same-group Direct Conversation Add/Welcome after accepted member rejoin. When present, the owner authority atomically claims exactly this current, unconsumed package or returns the same opaque claim_failed result as every other target-side failure; it is never a best-effort hint.

target_agent_id.description: Agent exact-target branch only. This field is the sole target identity carrier and MUST match the Agent identity in the returned claim record and current AgentSignerEvidence.

target_agent_verification_method.description: Agent exact-target branch current runtime verification method.

target_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Agent exact-target branch current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event.

request.description: The exact participant-authorized unsigned request fields. Together with request_digest, this lets the destination bind a later Welcome and Direct Conversation binding to the durable claim without trusting source-service assertions.

peer_keypackage_claim_receipt.description: Destination-service-signed durable receipt. source_id and request are covered by the receipt signature; request_digest additionally binds the complete transport command, including participant authorization. Realm target receipts additionally sign claim_authority_ref from the actual claim acceptance cut; it must resolve to destination_id as that Realm's authority at claimed_at. Originals remain immutable across governance handoff.

keypackage_claim_terminal_receipt.description: The KeyPackage owner service signs an immutable terminal ledger fact. never_claimed is issued only after the request can no longer succeed; expired/revoked identify every formerly claimed ordinary KeyPackage. This is the portable cleanup authority for a failed Direct Conversation attempt.

keypackages_claim_response_body.description: Privacy-preserving peer success response. It intentionally omits inventory counts and per-device failure information.

claim_id.description: KeypackageClaimId of the claim to read, byte-identical to the Welcome keypackage_claim_ref. The caller's authenticated endpoint MUST be the claim record's exact endpoint.

keypackages_claim_query_request_body.description: Self read of one claim of the caller's own KeyPackage (ak.self.keys.keypackages.read.claim.v1). The response is the byte-identical keypackages_claim_response_body first serialized for the claim request that allocated claim_id.

recipient_account_id.description: Exact cross-Station recipient AccountId for the human-device signer branch. The Agent branch carries only its branch-specific identity.

recipient_id.description: For a Realm actor recipient, the original claim_receipt.destination_id (historical claim issuer), preserved across handoff and never used as the current HTTP route. Account/Agent retains its owning Station rule.

welcome_ref.description: Exact MlsWelcomeDelivery referenced by this durable receipt. The delivery is not an Event and has no independent RealmCommit.

welcome_digest.description: sha256:-prefixed lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete MlsWelcomeDelivery named by welcome_ref, producer_proof included. The consuming Station compares it with the Welcome binding it wrote on the claim ledger when it enqueued that delivery.

recipient_mls_durable_receipt.description: Recipient signs every field except signature after durable MLS installation. Closed XOR of Account Device, Agent, or Realm actor Device. Realm recipient_id binds the original claim issuer; the current governor consumes only a completely imported exact claim ledger.

keypackage_consume_receipt.description: Recipient Station signed durable consume acknowledgement. recipient_durable_receipt is the sole carrier of claim request, KeyPackage, Welcome, Realm, MLS group, epoch, and recipient service coordinates. The service-generated request_digest, claim_id, and consumed_at plus the complete nested durable receipt are covered by signature. For an ordinary KeyPackage it is issued only after the exact single-use claim transitions to consumed. For a reusable last-resort KeyPackage it terminally acknowledges only that exact claim audit while the KeyPackage row remains published. Same exact consume replays this receipt; any claim, coordinate, signer-branch or evidence mismatch conflicts.

recipient_durable_receipt.description: Sole consume authority and coordinate carrier. Its closed device or Agent signer branch authorizes the command and binds the owner, KeyPackage, Welcome, Realm, MLS group, epoch, and recipient service.

signature.description: Signature over the typed consume request with this field omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.command.consume.v1 domain.
Signature over the typed revoke request with this field omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.command.revoke.v1 domain.

peer_keypackages_claim_command_response_.description: Closed peer claim command result. First success and direct exact replay use the same durable state view as the read-only ledger query; unknown is impossible after a command has been admitted. Existing outcome bytes never cause a second claim.

contract.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ak.keys.{upload,query,claim}, the Station-to-Station device directory read and ak.keys.backups.{put,list,delete}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

request_id.description: Client-generated idempotency id. The service keys the canonical request digest and terminal outcome by (account_id, backup_id, request_id).

keys_backups_delete_proof.description: High-risk authority proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1. Exactly one of recovery_unlock, device_quorum or trusted_recovery_service; an ordinary current-device session proof is not accepted for active-series tail deletion.

account_device_key_entries.description: One entry per exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(account_id); duplicate AccountIds MUST be rejected even when values differ.

did_key.description: Authoritative device signing key as an Ed25519 did:key (multibase base58btc, multicodec ed25519-pub). Mirrors ak.device.authorize.payload.device_public_key_did (device-lifecycle.md §5.2 / §5.4). To check SignalEnvelope and durable Event proofs, receivers resolve a verification_method DID URL under the verified principal did, validate its bare did through the registered adapter, require project(did) to equal the actor/principal did_core_id, and require its fragment to equal the full ak:device:<uuidv7> id. Constructing a verification method by appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden.

device_generation_state.description: Reducer-managed identity-root generation fence for the principal device directory.

current_device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic generation; it is not and MUST NOT be derived from a DID versionId.

account_device_generation_entries.description: Current device-generation fence for each exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

device_projection_attestation_core.description: Origin Station assertion that this exact device projection is the account's current accepted one. It is the whole verification closure of the Station-to-Station device directory read and of the account_device signer evidence: the attested body carries no PCR genesis receipt, no device authorization chain and no accepted RealmCommit, because that material is account-internal governance and is disclosed only through ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1 under exact current-holder authorization. Required device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref fields describe the closed shape of a returned usable row; they do not require an unauthorized device to have a partial projection. A device with no current accepted authorization is omitted or reported through the non-enumerating failure shape. attested_at is a monotone freshness marker and, with authorized_generation_ref, is the cache key of device-lifecycle.md section 8.3.

account_id.description: Exact account owning the device projection. The proof controller MUST project exactly onto account_id.station_id; an attestation that verifies under any other Station key is not evidence about this account.

device_status.description: This surface attests usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the attested status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh current-query cache deadline only. Expiry does not revoke the signed device authorization or prohibit ordinary publication with verified cached evidence. Security operations use their stricter registered current-state gate.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from attestation cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

device_projection_attestation.description: Complete origin-Station-signed device projection attestation. The detached proof signs the ak.device_projection_attestation_proof.v1 transcript; proof.created_at MUST equal attestation.attested_at.

verified_device_projection.description: The device projection a client receives from its own authenticated Station on the self keys/query surface. The values are the ones the Station read out of the origin Station's verified device_projection_attestation; the row therefore carries no origin proof and no wrapper whose only job was to verify that proof, and a client MUST NOT treat this projection as portable evidence about the origin. account_id and device_id are not repeated here: they are the enclosing entry's account_id and the device_keys map key, and the returning Station MUST have checked that the verified attestation named exactly that pair before projecting it. attested_at is the origin's own observation instant, forwarded verbatim; together with authorized_generation_ref it is the cache key of device-lifecycle.md section 8.3. Required device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref describe the closed shape of a usable row; a device with no current accepted authorization is omitted or reported through the non-enumerating failure shape rather than degraded into a partial projection.

device_status.description: This surface projects usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the projected status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: Origin observation instant of the verified projection, forwarded verbatim. MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh current-query cache deadline only, forwarded verbatim from the verified origin attestation. The returning Station MUST NOT extend it. Expiry does not revoke the signed device authorization or prohibit ordinary publication with verified cached evidence.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window, forwarded verbatim. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

query_device_record.description: Per-(account_id, device_id) entry in keys_query_response_body, the client-facing self surface. account_id and device_id are the device_keys entry and map keys, not row fields. The row is the restricted typed result the client's own authenticated Station produces after it verified the origin Station's device_projection_attestation, so it carries the verified projection plus the prekey material and the signer_evidence_ref the client actually uses, and never the origin proof or its verification wrapper. A device whose generation is fenced, or which is revoked, is not degraded into a partial row -- it is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so an incomplete row can never be mistaken for a usable one.

signer_evidence_ref.description: Exact account_device signer evidence the origin Station retained with its Station attester closure before the row was returned. It keeps pointing at that complete immutable evidence object: it is neither recomputed from this pruned projection nor an additional device-authority claim.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the section 5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

query_account_device_entries.description: One device-key result group per exact AccountId on the self surface. The returning Station MUST have matched each verified attestation's account_id and device_id against this account_id and its enclosing device_id key before projecting the row. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

peer_query_device_record.description: Per-(account_id, device_id) entry in peer_keys_query_response_body, the Station-to-Station surface. account_id and device_id are the device_keys entry and map keys, not row fields. Every returned row is complete and attested: the origin Station signs the exact projection, so the requesting Station can verify the row without ever seeing PCR material. This is deliberately a different type from the client-facing query_device_record: the signed attestation is the object the requesting Station verifies, and a Station MUST NOT turn an unverified peer row into a client result by dropping its proof. A device whose generation is fenced, or which is revoked, is not degraded into a partial row -- it is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so an incomplete row can never be mistaken for a usable one.

signer_evidence_ref.description: Exact account_device signer evidence retained with its Station attester closure before this row is returned. Its embedded attestation equals this row's attestation byte for byte; the ref is not an additional device-authority claim.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the §5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

device_projection_attestation.description: Origin-Station signature over the authoritative device projection. Consumers read device_signing_key_did, hpke_key, device_status, device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref from the verified attestation. Its account_id and device_id MUST match the enclosing result group and device key; its signer MUST project onto account_id.station_id.

peer_query_account_device_entries.description: One device-key result group per exact AccountId on the Station-to-Station surface. Each signed device projection MUST match this account_id and its enclosing device_id key. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

account_device_algorithm_entries.description: One claim target group per exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

query_account_device_selectors.description: Explicit account/device selectors sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(account_id). Neither AccountId component may be inferred from the target service, caller session or another entry. Duplicate AccountIds MUST be rejected; use one entry containing all selected device_ids for that account. At most 16 accounts and 32 devices per account bound the local read and its cross-Station fan-out alike; an over-limit request fails whole and is never truncated.

query_failure.description: Closed non-enumerating failure row for the device directory read surfaces. device_result_unavailable covers absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets with one indistinguishable value. device_directory_unavailable states only that the requester's own Station could not obtain or verify a current attested projection this time; it never depends on target state and MUST NOT be rendered as an omitted row or an empty device set.

retry_after_ms.description: Only meaningful with device_directory_unavailable; a target-private failure MUST NOT carry it.

encryption.description: Non-secret recipient metadata so the client can categorize a backup (recovery_public_key vs passphrase_kdf vs secret_storage_key) without downloading the ciphertext. The aead/kdf material is withheld from the list summary.

device_generations.description: Current identity-root generation fence by exact AccountId. Fenced accounts or mismatched device generations expose no usable signing/HPKE/prekey material.

peer_keys_query_purpose.description: Declared use of the requested directory rows. The destination authorizes each purpose independently and MUST NOT clear the broadest one once.

peer_keys_relationship_basis.description: Closed relationship the requester asserts. The destination re-derives it from its own accepted state; a caller assertion never authorizes by itself. The contact branch deliberately carries no realm_id: a legitimate Contact needs no shared Realm.

peer_keys_query_request_body.description: Station-to-Station device directory and published prekey-bundle read. It is the only registered carrier for a cross-Station keys/query target: the client asks its own Station, which authenticates itself with its own RFC 9421 service signature and never forwards a client SessionGrant, DPoP or any local bearer. Single authority, single hop, read only. Cross-Station single-use material stays with the MLS KeyPackage claim contract. Realm requester is restricted to MLS admission in its own Realm, with ordinary Account device targets only. The relationship realm_id MUST equal requester_actor_id.realm_actor_id.realm_id; current governor and both joined memberships are independently verified. Existing MLS capability, membership and policy rules remain unchanged.

request_id.description: Stable typed id the requesting Station mints for this fetch. The destination uses it only for correlation and rate limiting and keeps no durable ledger.

requester_account_id.description: Exact requesting account. Its station_id MUST equal the authenticated Source-Service-ID and MUST NOT be inferred from a principal component, route or session.

requester_actor_id.description: Exact Realm requester; mutually exclusive with requester_account_id. The authenticated source is its verified current governing Station. No Bot-specific MLS permission or approval is introduced.

device_keys.description: Targets for this destination only: every account_id.station_id MUST equal the authenticated Destination-Service-ID.

peer_keys_query_response_body.description: Verbatim origin-signed rows plus the closed non-enumerating failure shape. The destination does not add a response signature layer: every row carries the origin's own device_projection_attestation and signer_evidence_ref, and the requesting Station MUST verify them before projecting the restricted client-facing query_device_record. Echo request_id and the complete mutually exclusive requester branch exactly.

requester_actor_id.description: Exact Realm requester; mutually exclusive with requester_account_id. The authenticated source is its verified current governing Station. No Bot-specific MLS permission or approval is introduced.

keys_backups_page.description: Bounded Account Station metadata page with the current accepted secret_storage backup-class pointer, independent of list filters. key-management.md section 7.6.1 fixes cursor and unknown-state semantics.

keys_backups_unlock_request_body.description: Closed exact single-object unlock intent. Branch authority, current validity, exact account/device/object, challenge and signature must all verify before durable allowance/budget/result commit. An identical retry by the same still-authorized holder returns the stored object without double charge.

keys_backups_issue_delete_challenge_requ.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.issue_delete_challenge.v1. While an issued challenge for the same (account_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid, the service MUST return the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new challenge.

keys_backups_delete_challenge.description: Server-issued, durable, single-use delete challenge (TTL <= 300s). Every field is materialized by the service; the client echoes challenge_id in the DELETE body and every proof signs the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1, which embeds these exact values. Replay, expiry, path mismatch, or audience/service mismatch MUST fail closed.

challenge_id.description: Server-issued unique id of this challenge; echoed verbatim in the DELETE request body.

challenge.description: Server-issued CSPRNG challenge bytes (base64url, no padding).

nonce.description: Server-issued CSPRNG nonce bytes (base64url, no padding); distinct from challenge so the transcript binds two independent freshness values.

account_id.description: Exact account that owns the backup and challenge; both principal and Station components are signed by every delete proof.

audience.description: The service base origin this challenge is valid against; MUST match the origin the DELETE request is sent to.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.

keys_backups_delete_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete.v1. The service verifies the referenced challenge against the current caller/path/service, verifies the high-risk proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript, and consumes the challenge in the same transaction as the successful delete. A byte-identical network retry returns the stored terminal outcome without re-admitting the consumed challenge; the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

challenge_id.description: Exact echo of the server-issued challenge_id being consumed.

keys_backups_issue_unlock_challenge_requ.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.issue_unlock_challenge.v1. While an issued challenge for the same (account_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid, the service MUST return the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new challenge.

keys_backups_unlock_challenge.description: Shared-durable single-use current-device unlock challenge, TTL <= 300 seconds, scoped to authenticated account/device, exact backup/series/ciphertext, origin and service. All values are server materialized. Recovery-session unlock reuses its session challenge and MUST NOT call this operation.

challenge.description: Server-issued CSPRNG challenge bytes (base64url, no padding).

nonce.description: Server-issued CSPRNG nonce bytes (base64url, no padding); distinct from challenge so the transcript binds two independent freshness values.

account_id.description: Exact authenticated account pair.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.

account_device_event_authorization.description: Exact pre-admission real Account Device source (Human or accepted Applet-managed), independently proven from native authorization. accepted_at is the original authorization Commit time; no target Commit exists yet. All fields enter the original Station attestation payload digest. Never present in directory/current-query evidence.

forward_device_projection_attestation_co.description: Forward-only closed same-cut real Account Device (Human or accepted Applet-managed) attestation. Original current projection fields plus a required exact Event-bound immutable authorization source. This is not a directory row or a grant.

account_id.description: Exact account owning the device projection. The proof controller MUST project exactly onto account_id.station_id; an attestation that verifies under any other Station key is not evidence about this account.

device_status.description: This surface attests usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the attested status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh authority_forward first-admission deadline: now MUST be earlier than expires_at; a new attempt MUST NOT reuse cached evidence. Exact already-accepted retry returns the original outcome before freshness checks. Original accepted historical verification uses original attested_at and MUST NOT reapply current TTL.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from attestation cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

forward_device_projection_attestation.description: authority_forward real Account Device (Human or accepted Applet-managed) wrapper. Existing proof context and unique unsigned {attestation:core} projection; no new profile or proof context.

contract.description: Result shape for the WebRTC media service ICE config endpoint. Used by ak.profile.webrtc_media.v1; see crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §4.

realm_id.description: Echo of the request Realm id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-Realm replay.

call_id.description: Echo of the request call id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-call replay.

actor_id.description: Stable actor did_core_id that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

device_id.description: Device that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

ice_servers.description: STUN / TURN server entries the client may use during this call.

ttl_seconds.description: Validity window for the issued credentials in seconds. Clients MUST refresh before this expires; servers SHOULD pick a value <= 1 hour for normal calls.

refresh_lead_seconds.description: Minimum lead time before ttl expiry at which the client SHOULD initiate refresh. refresh_lead_seconds MUST be strictly less than ttl_seconds (servers MUST NOT issue refresh_lead_seconds >= ttl_seconds, otherwise the client would judge the credential stale at issuance and storm refresh). Defaults SHOULD be ttl_seconds / 4. The recommended floor (60s) applies only when ttl_seconds is large enough that floor < ttl_seconds still holds; for small ttl (e.g. the 60s minimum) the server MUST shrink refresh_lead_seconds below ttl_seconds (see webrtc-signaling.md §4.2). Required so all clients refresh at consistent cadence and servers can plan secret rotation grace windows.

issued_at.description: Server-issued timestamp (RFC 3339 UTC). Bound into the ICE config signature.

turn_required.description: When true, clients MUST disable host/srflx ICE candidates and only relay through TURN. Used by high-privacy Realms to prevent IP leakage.

next_retry_at.description: Set when the response reports a temporary service failure (e.g. turn_credential_expired). Clients MUST NOT retry before this time.

signature.description: Detached signature by the media service DID over the canonical bytes of this response (excluding `signature`).

urls.description: STUN/TURN server URL(s). Schemes: stun:, stuns:, turn:, turns:.

username.description: TURN ephemeral credential username. v1: <expiry-unix>:<per-call-pseudonym>. MUST NOT contain principal DID, handle, email, or any cross-call stable identifier.

credential.description: TURN ephemeral credential password (HMAC-SHA256 of username with per-tenant turn shared secret in REST-style).

kid.description: DID URL of the concrete media-service verification method. Bare DID is not accepted because the response must pin one already accepted service key binding.

signature_algorithm.description: Current-v1 signature algorithm. Reserved algorithms, including ML-DSA-65, are rejected as unsupported until a new negotiated schema/profile activates them while preserving the exact signing input defined in webrtc-signaling.md §4.1.

signature.description: base64url-encoded detached signature over canonical response bytes.

thumbnails.description: Bound thumbnail / preview descriptors. Producers SHOULD prefer this over preview_blob_ref for private or E2EE media.

contract.description: Closed request DTOs for realtime media service operations. ak.self.media.read.ice_config.v1 responses use media-ice-configuration-response-body.schema.json.

Own-Station verified route and signing keys for the media service anchored by one joined Realm current accepted realm_media_service current state. It resolves service identity, purpose and route only; it releases no media key, no backend token and no plaintext-visibility authorization.

service_signing_key.description: One accepted assertion-capable Ed25519 signing key of the anchored media service, taken from the same verified current DID Document as the route. The controller DID of verification_method equals the route did; the key verifies participant_binding and ICE config signatures without a per-token DID resolution.

public_key_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes. Public verification material only; it grants no media key release.

media_service_binding_request_body.description: Authenticated member request for one joined Realm. The media service identity is taken from that Realm current accepted current state; caller-supplied service ids, DIDs, base URLs, candidate origins and method evidence are not accepted.

media_service_binding_response_body.description: Complete bounded own-Station result: the accepted anchor, its verified route projection and the signing keys that verify issued media signatures. No method history evidence, witness record, normalized DID Document, describe body or third-party attestation closure is returned. expires_at bounds route and key reuse only and is never an authorization lease.

route.description: Verified route projection of the anchored issuer; service_id equals the accepted current state service_id. A Station fulfilling the media issuer role retains service_kind station and must independently satisfy the media binding profile, selected backend sub-profile and registered token HTTP operation bundle. Never relabel its DID endpoint as media_service. An independent media_service role requires its separately registered method-native identity; this result does not grant service-registration eligibility.

contract.description: Realm-scoped, actor-scoped full member_identity segment. It is carried by ak.member.identity.update in plaintext or inside encrypted-envelope.schema.json. Replacement events that name segment=member_identity MUST carry this complete object. This object discloses subject_actor_id and display_profile for Realm UI projection; handle lifecycle is intentionally excluded and is governed only by ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims. Mention / reply / quote / actor attribution MUST use the exact ActorId, never a handle string or a bare principal DID.

actor_id.description: Effective member actor did_core_id in this Realm. MAY represent a Realm-scoped pairwise identity.

subject_actor_id.description: Exact durable subject represented by a Realm-scoped or pairwise actor. Account subjects retain their station component; authorization and audit continue to use the Event actor and member state.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of this MemberIdentity object with the top-level proof field excluded. The signature MUST cover the same canonical bytes.

contract.description: Local SDK message intent, content and encryption binding. Ordinary messages are constructed and signed locally, then use the unified Event submission; no remote draft preparation operation exists.

id.description: For ak.message.create, the reducer derives this value by retyping the creating Event.event_id's full 33-byte / 44-character token from ak:event: to ak:message:. It is not independently producer-chosen.

effective_scope.description: Read-only immutable effective scope of this Message, materialized from the accepted Event.scope_ref after the receiver verifies it against the Strand's frozen pre-state (models/circle.md §6.1-§6.2). kind='realm' for Realm-default scope; kind='circle' when the Message's Strand was Circle-scoped at write time. A later Strand scope rebind MUST NOT reinterpret already-written Messages. This field MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied content payload (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Message ContentBlock.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a message_metadata object.

state.description: Top-level lifecycle state for messages. Messages do not have a separate deleted/tombstone state; retention or moderation removal uses ak.message.redact and state=redacted so the message slot and audit metadata remain stable.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.message.redact Event. Aligns with the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

revision_root_id.description: First revision in this message's edit chain. The first revision MUST have revision_root == id. Maintained by ak.message.revise reducer.

redaction_ref.description: Required when state=redacted; references the accepted ak.message.redact Event id that produced this state. A cross-object ak.redaction can never be the source: its payload class excludes Message targets, so this reference is single-valued and unambiguous (models/common-fields.md 5.1 Message exemption). MUST be absent for other states.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent materialized message update, such as ak.message.revise or ak.message.redact.

mentions.description: Structured direct mention AST nodes for this Content Block. This is the only carrier of a direct mention: authorization, notification routing and audit attribution read mention_node.subject_account_id exclusively, and compare it as a complete AccountId (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.1-§9.4.2).

audience_mentions.description: Structured broadcast mention AST nodes for this Content Block (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3).

attachments.description: Profile-defined attachment hints. At most 32; canonical durable attachment relations SHOULD use Relation attached_to.

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

sidecar_exchange_binding.description: Agent Sidecar exchange binding. Legal only inside encrypted_metadata plaintext of an event whose signed scope_ref.kind is sidecar; forbidden in plaintext metadata and shared Realm/Circle events.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Message metadata fields. Reducer-owned lifecycle and revision fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

contract.description: Provider directory, room binding, and content mapping receipt objects for ak.profile.mimi_interop.v1.

mimi_room_uri.description: Canonical MIMI room URI. It is the mimi_room_binding current state subject source, so it is a closed canonical form rather than a free URI: lowercase mimi:// scheme, host[:port] authority with no userinfo, lowercase A-label host, no leading-zero port, at least one non-empty path segment, no dot or dot-dot segment, no trailing slash, no query, no fragment, uppercase percent escapes, and no percent-encoding of unreserved octets (RFC 3986 section 6.2.2.2). A receiver MUST reject a non-canonical value with schema_violation and MUST NOT normalize it first, because two spellings of one room would otherwise each own a first accepted binding and the revoked terminal state could be bypassed by respelling. current state subject encoding is the uri subject kind of zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4.
