The pattern below expresses the structural half of the canonical form; two rules it cannot express portably -- the default port 443 MUST NOT be written explicitly, and a percent escape MUST NOT encode an unreserved octet -- are normative all the same and are closed by ak.vector.encoding.state_selector_uri.v1 plus the SDK typed validator, which every producer and receiver MUST apply in addition to this pattern. See zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md section 4.

supported_profiles.description: Sorted unique by UTF-8 byte order; the sorted array is what enters the signed projection.

endpoints.description: Sorted by endpoint_id; endpoint_id unique across rows. Effective URLs derive only via a standard URL parser under the verified HTTPS base_url with same-origin re-check and the section 3 SSRF policy (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3.1).

mls_cipher_suites.description: Generated from active canonical_id rows in mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.

proof.description: Detached JWS by a verification method whose bare controller did validates under the registered method adapter and projects exactly to service_id (did_core_id), over the canonical unsigned projection (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3.1). The projection's first member is the registered object-family context ak.mimi_provider_directory_proof.v1 (proof-context-registry.json); a signature made under any other context MUST be rejected even when it verifies cryptographically. Direct DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden. payload_digest is the projection digest; the proof object itself never enters the projection. A digest or dev placeholder is not a signature.

endpoint_id.description: The feature this endpoint serves; the id set is the same closed feature enum, and each endpoint_id appears at most once.

relative_path.description: Normalized relative path: begins with '/', no scheme, authority, query, fragment, whitespace or backslash. Receivers MUST additionally reject '.' / '..' dot segments and percent-encoded '/', '\', '.' or '..' after decoding (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3.1).

room_binding.description: MIMI room binding effect payload. In authority-commit/authority-ordered projection state, the current state subject is payload.mimi_room_uri for mimi_room_binding.

mls_group_id.description: For E2EE projection this value MUST equal the authenticated RFC 9420 GroupInfo/GroupContext group id and the sole group id derived from the current accepted MlsGroupValue.effective_scope. The five-field governance binding has no mls_group_id member; see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4 and zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.2.

status.description: Room binding lifecycle status. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are proposed->accepted, proposed->revoked, accepted->migrating, accepted->revoked, migrating->accepted (verified migration proof), migrating->revoked. revoked is the only terminal state; illegal transitions are rejected with mimi_room_binding_status_transition_invalid. Normative state machine: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

migration_outcome.description: Outcome of a migrating->accepted transition: completed (candidate topology in effect) or rolled_back (previous accepted topology restored). MUST be paired with migration_proof and absent on other transitions. Normative: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

receipt_kind.description: Interop-audit object discriminator. This object is not an Event Envelope and this value is not an event kind.

contract.description: Closed request/response DTOs for MIMI provider interop. Key-material uses the existing keypackage-operations claim request and command outcome directly, as registered by operation-registry.

consent_id.description: Opaque private request correlation only; never a native permission selector.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a verification method authorized by the issuer's current DID Document (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 5.1).

kind.description: Semantic update kind and durable-effect discriminator. It MUST equal the kind inside the decoded opaque payload. ak.mimi.room_binding selects the caller-authored Event branch; every other value selects the receipt-only branch.

room_binding_event.description: Complete caller-authored and caller-signed ak.mimi.room_binding initial submission. It is required exactly when /update/kind is ak.mimi.room_binding. The facade MUST first verify that the decoded opaque payload carries the same semantic kind, then bind the Event's exact payload to the path room, target Realm and Strand, MLS group, and authenticated MIMI operation and submit these exact bytes through authority Event submission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign the Event. Every other receipt-only branch MUST omit this field.

requester_actor_id.description: Exact Actor the requester is asking as, Station and actor role included. consent-model.md section 6.1 compares an ordinary peer by complete ActorId and forbids falling back to a bare principal. The operation proof MUST authenticate this exact Actor through its current accepted authority. Transport authentication MUST bind the complete request and authenticated source; a provider transport signature authenticates only that service and does not authorize the Actor. Proving key control under some principal does not authorize an arbitrary account of that principal.

holder_account_id.description: Exact Account the request is addressed to, chosen and signed by the requester. It is not evidence that the holder exists, is visible or has consented: creating the private correlation queries no consent current state, and a request that is syntactically valid and authenticated MUST produce an indistinguishable opaque outcome whether or not the holder exists. A correlation may freeze a target nobody can legitimately accept; it carries no authority. This operation resolves no aliases -- the external identifier to Arkret identity mapping happens before it, under the section 10 rules.

strand_id.description: Optional interop context. It grants no Realm authority and neither widens nor narrows the consent scope; when present it is covered by the unsigned-body digest like every other member.

proofs.description: Required requester operation proof over ak.mimi_request_consent_request_proof.v1. Resolve the exact Actor's current accepted Account device generation or Agent runtime authorization under mimi-interop.md section 5.1; DID controller key possession and provider transport signatures do not authorize an Actor. Agent runtime requires current controller/lifecycle, provision and key ceilings and operation-scoped authenticated runtime authority. No generic remote PCR disclosure carrier is registered for this request: missing authorized current evidence MUST fail closed before correlation creation or holder lookup.

mimi_request_consent_request_body.description: Request that a named Arkret holder grant consent to a named Arkret Actor. The signed request writes both identities in full and the facade freezes exactly those into its private correlation, so update_consent is a byte comparison rather than a re-resolution against whatever the facade's current Station or alias table happens to say.

mimi_update_consent_request_body.description: Caller signs a complete ak.consent.replace Event. body.consent_id equals private correlation.consent_id only; it is never the native selector. Exact holder Account/PCR/peer and original root/device/source gates apply. Accept adds or replaces only the correlation concrete scope; deny/revoke removes an existing entry, including expired ones. All other entries and optional-member presence remain byte-for-byte equal to the signed exact prestate. Facade compares the authenticated complete exact prestate; final PCR acceptance atomically checks that same expected revision or never_written predicate and performs the full replacement, never server merge or a distributed transaction. Wrong correlation/decision/stale new write uses opaque not_found. Exact accepted retry restores original correlation/decision/Event outcome before new-current evaluation and never replays a write.

consent_event.description: Caller signs a complete ak.consent.replace Event. body.consent_id equals private correlation.consent_id only; it is never the native selector. Exact holder Account/PCR/peer and original root/device/source gates apply. Accept adds or replaces only the correlation concrete scope; deny/revoke removes an existing entry, including expired ones. All other entries and optional-member presence remain byte-for-byte equal to the signed exact prestate. Facade compares the authenticated complete exact prestate; final PCR acceptance atomically checks that same expected revision or never_written predicate and performs the full replacement, never server merge or a distributed transaction. Wrong correlation/decision/stale new write uses opaque not_found. Exact accepted retry restores original correlation/decision/Event outcome before new-current evaluation and never replays a write.

mimi_report_abuse_request_body.description: Holder-signed MIMI report claim for a service-authored moderation Event. The body carries no provider identity, reporter identity or pre-signed Event mirror: the facade derives them from authenticated transport, reporter_authority and this exact claim.

mimi_report_claim.description: Exact reporter-signed input to the facade's service-authored ak.self.moderation.report Event. The facade derives reporter_id, provenance and source_provider_id from authenticated authority, never from a body echo.

mimi_reporter_authority.description: Holder-signed, short-lived binding from the external reporter to one complete current Arkret ActorId. The proof transcript covers the complete closed request with only reporter_authority.proof omitted: reporter_authority and report_claim. The verifier resolves the current device or authorized Agent proxy key independently, authenticates the Provider at the transport layer, and verifies both full CommittedEventRefs remain current before the facade service authors an Event; carrier fields never self-authorize.

contract.description: Atomic authority submission containing one producer-signed MLS Commit Event and every Welcome required by its Add proposals.
Station-signed historical Add authority and complete member-authorized roster read. Leaf indices and MLS secrets are never carried.

mls_member_group_state_material_read_req.description: Authenticated member read of accepted Genesis public RFC material at an exact target membership/history cut. The Account Station binds caller_actor_id to the session and forwards all selectors unchanged to governance.

mls_add_authority_attestation.description: For Account/Agent recipients, signed by the owning Account Station. For Realm actors, signed by the governance Station that actually accepts the Add; claim_authority_ref equals the original receipt's signed claim authority. Different claim and Add issuers require verified same-Realm authority succession and complete exact ledger import.

mls_add_authority_attest_request_body.description: Transport-only full claim outcome lets governance verify the destination receipt's claims_digest before retaining only the signed minimal attestation. It is never returned by roster read.

mls_member_roster_authority_read_request.description: Authenticated own-Station member selector. The Station authorizes the exact accepted target and derives Genesis from immutable accepted provenance in the same read cut; the member need not read a prejoin Genesis or a complete current baseline.

consumed_proposal_ordinal.description: Zero-based index of this inline Add in the accepted Commit PublicMessage's ProposalOrRef vector, counting every consumed Proposal kind.

proposal_wire_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of the exact TLS-serialized RFC 9420 Proposal body at consumed_proposal_ordinal in the accepted, signed Commit PublicMessage. It is never an independent Proposal handshake input or a synthetic ProposalRef.

claim_issuer_resolution.description: Required only for Realm actor Add records, even when both issuers are equal. Immutable complete Station method history frozen from the actual claim; service_id equals claim_receipt.destination_id and validates its signature at claimed_at. Not a current route.

attestor_resolution.description: Immutable complete Station method history frozen with the Add. service_id equals attestation.attestor_station_id and validates its signature at attested_at. Account/Agent also verifies the same Station claim signature using this closure; Realm actor uses its separate claim_issuer_resolution. Not a current route.

roster_manifest.description: Governance Station signature covers every member except signature, including both immutable Blob refs copied from the exact accepted Genesis. A later-joined member verifies this manifest before using those refs in the member public material request. records_digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete ordered roster_record array, independent of page boundaries.

roster_read_response_body.description: One governance-signed page containing the longest continuous prefix of 1..8 complete records that fits the 2 MiB canonical JSON response limit. Pages are cut-bound, and next_cursor identifies the next record offset; no caller-selected page size or partial record is permitted. Page boundaries also include the exact self-only signing-key projection budget; either envelope exceeding 2 MiB makes the complete roster unavailable.

roster_signing_key.description: Public key selected by the authenticated own Account Station for the enclosing exact signed object and its original timestamp. A DID URL is only a key selector; this result is not portable authority or a resolver source.

record_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of the exact complete Add record on this page, including frozen closure.

self_roster_read_response_body.description: Non-portable authenticated own-Station result. roster is the unchanged signed governance page. Exactly one key entry per Add record on that page, in the same order; no entry for Genesis. Keys bind exact signature kid, purpose, timestamp and record digest; current or remote self-asserted keys cannot substitute. Entire canonical response is at most 2 MiB.

contract.description: Producer-signed recipient delivery queued atomically with its winning MLS Commit. This is not a shared Realm Event and does not receive an independent RealmCommit.

Defs-only canonical objects shared by signed moderation reports, MIMI report mapping and durable franking-proof Events. This schema depends only on primitive/common schemas and does not reference an Event or operation request schema.

evidence_package.description: Canonical encrypted moderation evidence-package descriptor. target_refs names exactly the report target at admission; recipient_public_key_ref and encrypted_to MUST be byte-identical and resolve to an authorized moderator key for the report's exact effective scope. reporter_signature covers the descriptor and referenced ciphertext. The encrypted material MUST contain only reporter-visible evidence for target_refs and MUST NOT contain MLS epoch/exporter private material or unrelated plaintext.

franking_proof.description: Canonical receiving-service receipt used both inside a moderation report and as the complete payload of an ak.moderation.franking_proof durable Event. The local signature uses domain ak.franking_proof.signature.v1 and covers every member except signature. event_id names the encrypted Event whose receipt is proven; the enclosing proof Event has its own distinct Event.event_id.

event_id.description: Event ID of the encrypted Event whose receipt is proven; not the enclosing franking-proof Event ID.

verification_method.description: Exact receiving-service verification method used for signature. Its controller MUST project to received_by and the method MUST be authorized at received_at.

replay_nonce.description: Opaque anti-replay nonce generated by the receiving service and covered by the proof signature.

signature.description: Receiving service signature over the canonical franking-proof transcript.

id.description: The accepted ak.self.moderation.report Event id retyped to moderation_queue_item; services MUST NOT allocate an independent identifier. See governance/content-moderation.md section 3.3.

report.description: Immutable payload projection from the accepted ak.self.moderation.report Event; never the service-operation request wrapper.

status.description: Authoritative moderation queue-item lifecycle. v1 is intentionally minimal: 'submitted' = report accepted and awaiting handling; 'resolved' = handling complete (terminal). The disposition (action taken vs no violation) lives on the separate ak.moderation.decision event. Additional intermediate states MAY be introduced in a later revision if a workflow phase needs them. See governance/content-moderation.md §3.3.

priority.description: Local administrator workflow only: never carried in an Event payload, never part of the decision fold, never replicated across Stations, and never a capability. Omit when unassigned. See governance/content-moderation.md section 3.3.

visibility.description: Read-side derivation over the accepted report and the target scope, in the order given in governance/content-moderation.md section 3.3: plaintext scope -> plaintext_evidence; evidence_package present -> encrypted_evidence; franking_proof only -> franking_proof_only; otherwise metadata_only. When evidence is withheld or trimmed for an unauthorized caller, this member MUST be downgraded to the evidence shape that caller can actually receive, and MUST NOT reveal whether the trimmed evidence exists. Never written by the reporter and never hard-filled with one default.

assigned_to_ids.description: Local administrator workflow only; entries MUST already hold the matching moderation capability in this scope. Omit when unassigned. See governance/content-moderation.md section 3.3.

evidence_policy.description: Derived handling policy; omit when there is no material source. plaintext_allowed mirrors the plaintext-scope branch of visibility, franking_proof_verification_required mirrors whether the report payload carries a franking_proof. retention_expires_at and legal_hold are local retention policy and MUST NOT change the canonical decision. See governance/content-moderation.md section 3.3.

audit_refs.description: Local administrator workflow only; entries MUST be Events the caller is already authorized to read. See governance/content-moderation.md section 3.3.

contract.description: Closed signed-request DTO for ak.self.moderation.command.report.v1. Canonical evidence and franking-proof objects live in moderation-evidence.schema.json so Event payload validation does not depend back on an operation request schema.

moderation_report_event_submission.description: Direct-holder signed ak.self.moderation.report Event. The current governance Station resolves current authorization and scope, then commits the exact Event or rejects it; the request carries no RealmCommit, current state, predecessor or caller-selected authorization basis.

moderation_report_request_body.description: Carries exactly one direct-holder signed moderation report Event and no unsigned report projection.

contract.description: Reference business-field schema for the morph.md customer_risk example. It constrains the fields object carried by a ak.schema.morph.v1 container.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle that defines this Morph's effective scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope. The producer signs the corresponding Event.scope_ref; the receiver verifies scope_circle_id.realm_id == Morph.realm_id and exact equality between the derived scope and Event.scope_ref before materializing the object's immutable effective_scope.

schema_refs.description: Authoritative structural schema set for Morph fields. Reducers MUST validate fields against exactly these refs; morph_kind and facets are not a replacement for schema_refs. Generic before-to-after transition validation is not provided by JSON Schema.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a morph_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata once the enclosing scope has an accepted ak.mls.genesis; before that activation the scope is plaintext and after it the plaintext branch MUST be rejected with mls_activation_irreversible.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Morph content.

state.description: Morph lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.morph.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=morph_not_active); ak.morph.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else morph_not_archived); ak.redaction targeting the morph MUST come from {'active','archived'} (else morph_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.morph.archive / ak.morph.restore / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Optional Morph business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle). Generic mirror/data Morphs may omit it; no v1 carrier can make it required at create time (realm morph_kind_profiles only tighten fields.* / facets / capability actions, see models/morph.md §4). If absent, the first ak.morph.stage.set initializes the axis to any registered value; later changes follow the normal transition rules. ak.morph.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected. Stage transitions do not carry a reason/note; explanations belong in a referenced Message. See models/common-fields.md §5.3.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ak.morph.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions MUST NOT update this field.

morph_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Morph metadata. Morph business fields stay in the top-level fields object; metadata carries display-oriented fields such as title and summary. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

ordinary_notification_kind.description: Closed notification_kind subset of the ordinary source-Event branch. invite has its own private Invite delivery carrier and agent belongs to the account-artifact branch, so neither participates in the deterministic projection preimage.

ordinary_projection_content.description: Server-materialized current content of one ordinary source-Event notification projection, as delivered on the account subscribe notifications channel (account-subscribe-frame.schema.json#/$defs/notification_delta). It reuses the ak.schema.notification.v1 field shapes and carries only what the recipient's own Station can state authoritatively: the projection identity is the delta id, the recipient is the authenticated account, and the inbox state (unread / read / dismissed / archived) stays in holder-private account data. See spec/v1/zh/sync/client-sync.md#312-普通源-event-当前行分支aknotification_projection

contract.description: Account notification carrier, including personal Agent accounts. Realm Bot/Ghost mentions are processed through their authorized native Device content stream and MUST NOT produce this carrier or an Account notification projection.

oneOf.description: SHA-256 suite byte 0x01 followed by the complete digest of the registered notification projection preimage. Recompute against recipient AccountId, RealmId, source EventId and notification_kind.

id.description: Profile-local approval_request_id. It is an opaque_correlation value, so its lexical space is disjoint from the ak: typed-ID namespace: a value MUST NOT begin with ak:.

source_account_artifact.description: Closed account-private artifact source for notifications that are not derived from a durable Realm Event.

source_ref.description: Optional canonical-object reference for clients that want to render the notification target without resolving source_event_id. Reducers MUST treat source_event_id as authoritative; source_ref is a render-only hint.

strand_id.description: Optional Strand context for routing the notification.

track_name.description: Optional Strand track key on the source Strand.

preview.description: Render summary. Under E2EE / redaction / history-limited scopes this MUST be empty or an authorized redacted digest; sender/reducer-enforced. A notification projection MUST NOT widen the plaintext visibility of the source Message. See models/private-objects.md §3.4.

id.description: SHA-256 suite byte 0x01 followed by the complete digest of the registered notification projection preimage. Recompute against recipient AccountId, RealmId, source EventId and notification_kind.

contract.description: Canonical target descriptors and signed authorization-token claims for object-address links.

address_link_kind.description: Closed URL-resolution classification. Signed authorization tokens use only invite or preview.

contract.description: Canonical field-patch format embedded in event payloads (typically at payload.patch) for non-create updates. Its only protocol identifier is ak.schema.patch.v1. Grammar, parser responsibilities, redactable content-slot protection and reducer-managed-field protection are defined normatively in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4; the machine-readable path set an $op="unset" MUST NOT remove is registry/redactable-field-registry.json, which this schema deliberately does not restate.
Plaintext shapes that MUST be encrypted before writing ak.profile.personal_productivity.v1 account-data values.

message_payload.description: Canonical future ak.message.create payload. It MUST omit message_id and event_id. Dispatch first completes the Event canonical preimage, derives its content-bound EventId, and then retypes that same 33-byte token into MessageId.

default_operations.description: Required when a managed default is require_review: only these review-capable operations use that default; nonselected operations default deny unless an explicit rule matches.

policy_rule.description: Closed policy rule. Extension rules must carry an explicit schema_ref/profile_ref instead of adding undeclared fields to the signed policy body.

priority.description: Rule evaluation priority. Higher values are evaluated first; omitted means 0.

domain_name.description: Lowercase DNS A-label domain. Matching semantics are label-boundary based and defined by governance/content-moderation.md.

server_selector.description: Selector for federation server policy rules. Domain rules match normalized DNS labels only; service_id exact rules take precedence in policy evaluation.

contract.description: Closed decrypted plaintext shape for the principal-private ak.presence.preference account-data value. The sending client applies an unexpired preference to all of the principal's devices; services MUST NOT require its plaintext or project it into server-readable policy state.

manual_state.description: Optional pinned broadcast state. offline is expressed by stopping broadcasts and TTL expiry; invisibility is expressed by ak.presence.visibility=nobody.

status_message.description: Optional NFC status-message override, at most 256 Unicode code points. U+0009 and U+000A are the only permitted control characters; all other C0/C1 controls are rejected. NFC normalization is a semantic validation step in addition to this schema.

clears_at.description: Optional expiry instant. At or after this instant the complete preference is equivalent to absence and the sending client resumes automatic state selection without the temporary status-message override.

contract.description: Closed decrypted plaintext shape for the principal-private ak.presence.visibility account-data value. The sending client applies this policy before encrypted Signal fanout; services MUST NOT require its plaintext or project it into server-readable policy state.

presence_visibility.description: Closed sender-side policy. public permits effective-scope fanout, contacts_only requires every other active member to be an accepted Contact with current holder-to-peer presence scope, consent_only requires a fresh complete exact-peer complete Consent current with an eligible presence entry for every other active member, and nobody suppresses sends. No receiver-side filtering substitutes for whole-scope confidentiality.

contract.description: Signed online locator returned from a holder-controlled Station locator ref. It asserts an exact AccountId and current first-hop route used for private invite delivery; it is not a Realm membership grant and cannot alter account identity.

account_id.description: Exact invite recipient account; both components are proof-bound.

service_resolution.description: First-hop resolution material for account_id.station_id; it is covered by the locator proofs.

route_assistance.description: Optional transport-only route recovery hints covered by the locator proof. They MUST NOT enter an invite Event or Realm member current state, do not extend this locator's expires_at, and do not authorize delivery or route switching.

expires_at.description: Time after which the locator MUST NOT be used to initiate invite delivery.

locator_ref_digest.description: Digest of the private locator ref material. The raw locator token MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

display_hint.description: UI-only display hint. It is not identity authority and MUST NOT be used for authorization.

proofs.description: At minimum contains recipient_service_acceptance. High-assurance deployments SHOULD also require subject_locator_authorization.

proof.description: Detached proof over canonical_json(principal_locator_without_proofs). proof.payload_digest MUST equal that canonical payload digest.

locator_token.description: Opaque base64url locator token with at least 128 bits of entropy. It SHOULD be a server-side handle and MUST NOT plaintext-encode account_id, expiry, policy state, or other invitee-identifying material. It MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string.

ttl_seconds.description: Requested locator lifetime. The Station MAY shorten it but MUST NOT exceed the v1 one-hour ceiling.

one_time_use.description: When true, the first successful resolve atomically consumes the locator.

ttl_seconds.description: Requested replacement-locator lifetime. When omitted, preserve the old locator's granted lifetime (old expires_at minus old issued_at). The Station MAY shorten it but MUST NOT exceed the v1 one-hour ceiling.

one_time_use.description: Whether the first successful resolve atomically consumes the replacement locator. When omitted, preserve the old locator's one_time_use value.

display_hint.description: Replacement display hint. When omitted, preserve the old hint; null explicitly clears it.

locator_token.description: Fresh opaque bearer secret generated from at least 192 bits of CSPRNG entropy and returned exactly once. Clients MUST keep it out of logs, analytics, caches, and ordinary durable local state; an explicit user-directed out-of-band handoff is permitted and inherits the token's TTL and revocation risks.

locator_id.description: Non-secret administrative identifier used only on the authenticated self surface.

display_hint.description: UI-only display hint. It is not identity authority and MUST NOT be used for authorization.

contract.description: Closed wire carriers scoped to a single principal: PCR genesis, participation replacement, history ingress contracts, Sidecar staging and shared primitives.

agent_participation_replace_request_body.description: Controller-owned full replacement of one per-scope participation selection. The authenticated Account Authority is the sole selection authority; first write uses expected_version=0 and each accepted write increments by one.

commits.description: Exactly two consecutive RealmCommit objects in registered unit order: realm.create then device.authorize.

pcr_genesis_submit_request_body.description: Account-Authority-to-Station relay. The outer service signature authenticates transport only; content authorization is exclusively the frozen registration anchor, the identity-root control proof and the two Event proofs. The designated method fact owner verifies the primary anchor and historical evidence; the Station admits the exact frozen unit. Within one authenticated TCB, exact verified method facts are carried through the registered channel without repeating the same method history; independent trust boundaries verify independently. Historical genesis verification never substitutes current DID resolution. Exactly one registration control proof is carried: identity_creation_control_proof with accepted_at evidence, or account_registration_control_proof with validated_at evidence. For the latter the authenticated exact owner must separately validate proof.request_canonical_digest recomputed by the fact owner from the original register body with only proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted; the original body remains durable owner material. Both proof variants authorize the same complete ordered PCR unit and initial session, not a DID publication or a second lineage.

did.description: Complete registration DID. The Station independently validates method evidence and requires project(did)=principal_id before accepting genesis.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-derived registration versionId: the exact accepted did:webvh entry versionId. It MUST equal the value the Station re-derives from principal_registration_anchor and the same field in identity_creation_control_proof.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the registration root control key committed by the identity root proof: the accepted did:webvh entry's active update key.

principal_registration_anchor.description: Exact frozen closed registration anchor. Its canonical digest MUST equal the selected control proof registration_anchor_digest. The responsible verifier derives did, version, history head and active root key from this primary material; same-TCB consumers carry the authenticated exact result and independently compare their own account, operation, unit and state bindings. It is historical input and MUST NOT be replaced with current resolver output.

registration_did_evidence.description: Complete Account-Authority-accepted historical evidence. Its canonical digest is reverse-bound by the pcr_genesis_unit receipt.

pcr_genesis_unit.description: Exact ordered, atomic PCR genesis unit. The first Event is identity-root signed ak.realm.create; the second is founding-device signed ak.device.authorize. Neither signer has an accepted Arkret signer projection before this unit, so neither producer proof is resolved through the ordinary device directory. The first key is resolved only from principal_registration_anchor, registration_did_evidence and the selected registration control proof; the second key is resolved only from the root-signed founding descriptor, authorize payload and unit-local candidate overlay. For the second Event proof.verification_method, the verifier parses the DID URL, requires the registered adapter to project its bare DID component to principal_id, and requires its fragment to equal device_id (the complete ak:device UUID string); constructing a DID URL by appending to did_core_id is forbidden, and did:key is not accepted for this slot. The verifier MUST NOT consult or mutate the durable device directory until every check succeeds. These Events are replayable only inside this complete unit and its accepted receipt closure, never as standalone shared-history Events. No partial acceptance is permitted.

authority_refs.description: Sorted ownership, Agent lifecycle, authorization, Realm participation and key-readiness refs. Circle membership and Sidecar selection refs are forbidden.

prepared_event_draft.description: Service-built canonical producer Event digest-payload bytes with producer_proof and reducer-managed fields absent. The client MUST decode these exact bytes under the suite carried by event_digest, add only the required producer proof, and return the resulting signed Event. Event id and kind are derived views, never parallel wire inputs.

event_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of unsigned_event_base64url under the fixed current-v1 Event identity suite. The value MUST use the sha256 prefix; no Realm state selects or changes it.

contract.description: Closed WebVH registration anchor for a v1 human principal. It is the single primary method-native material that human registration and PCR genesis both consume. v1 human registration supports exactly the active did:webvh adapter and anchor_kind=webvh_registration; every other DID method, including did:key and did:web, fails closed with unsupported_did_method before method-specific parsing. The anchor carries originals, never receipts: a verifier reconstructs did, method_history_head, version_id, the exact normalized DID document and the root verification method/key from the branch material alone, offline, without a current resolver, a database row or an Account Authority attestation. registration_did_evidence and identity_creation_control_proof keep their own registration anti-replay and control-intent roles and never substitute for this object. Adding another branch requires a separately registered publication-proof or independent-witness trust model, threat model and conformance vectors. Complete canonical anchor bytes MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB.

webvh_registration_anchor.description: did:webvh registration anchor. log_entries is the gap-free native history from inception through the registration entry: log_entries[i].versionId MUST carry version number i+1, and registration_did_operation adds only the did/did_method/seq wrapper around the terminal entry; new-DID publication matches the registry-accepted wrapper, while published-DID registration verifies existing native material without asserting a prior Arkret registry submission. witness_records is the complete did-witness.json record set every witness policy active in that interval requires. The verifier re-executes the registered did:webvh:1.0 adapter over log_entries - SCID derivation, every entry-hash link and predecessor versionId anchor, every controller proof, rotation authorization against the preceding nextKeyHashes commitment, and every applicable witness threshold - and only then derives, from the verified terminal entry alone: did from registration_did_operation.did, version_id from terminal versionId, method_history_head as sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of that terminal entry, the root control key from terminal parameters.updateKeys[0], and the root verification method from the terminal entry proof whose multikey is that same key. The derived did, method_history_head and version_id MUST equal the PCR genesis initial_resolution values byte-for-byte, and the derived root verification method and key MUST be the ones the genesis root producer proof used. A resolver summary, a partial log range, a bare current DID document or a caller-asserted head is not this anchor.

registration_did_operation.description: Exact registration-time did:webvh operation wrapper. For identity_creation it matches the registry-accepted operation; for published_identity it wraps the existing verified native terminal entry as frozen primary material and MUST NOT be submitted to a registry or treated as a registry receipt. did_method MUST equal webvh, did MUST be the canonical did:webvh identifier this anchor establishes and is the anchor's only copy of that DID, seq when present MUST equal the version number of the terminal entry, and operation MUST be canonically equal to the last log_entries element. previous_event_digest MUST be absent: inside an anchor the predecessor is carried as the preceding log_entries elements, so a digest of it would be a mirror of material already present. The wrapper therefore states an invariant rather than offering a second, independently choosable copy of the registration entry.

log_entries.description: Exact ordered native did:webvh entry objects from inception through the registration anchor entry. Element i MUST be the entry whose versionId version number is i+1, so a missing predecessor, a duplicate, a surplus entry after the registration entry, or a first entry other than inception 1 fails closed.

witness_records.description: Exact native did-witness.json record objects required by log_entries. Each record is the closed {versionId, proof} pair, at most one record per versionId, and its proof array MUST satisfy that version's effective witness policy threshold with distinct listed witnesses. Every record MUST name a versionId present in log_entries: unlike a fetched did-witness.json, this anchor's log ends at the registration entry, so a record for any other version is surplus and fails closed. The array is empty exactly when the verified log activates no witness policy.

normalized_did_document.description: Exact normalized DID document projection of the verified terminal entry state. Its did MUST equal registration_did_operation.did. The verifier recomputes the normalized projection from the terminal entry state and rejects any divergence instead of trusting this member; it holds the principal's own published verification methods, not the method-native update key, so a root key MUST NOT be selected from here.

contract.description: Canonical wire shape of a public key carried in Arkret DTOs. It is defined in its own document so that device, agent and account surfaces reference one shared definition instead of reverse-referencing each other's bundles. Prose examples MUST use this exact shape: kty/kid/algorithm/key, no public_key alias.

public_key.description: Canonical public key. key carries the base64url key material; kid is the typed identifier of the key holder (for a device key, ak:device:<uuidv7>). There is no public_key member: that spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected.

contract.description: Closed request and response DTOs for Station device registration, trusted public-Gateway registration handoff, and push notification delivery.

push_route_token.description: Opaque service-generated routing token. It MUST NOT contain, encode, or be reversibly derived from a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Circle id, Strand id, Message id, Event id, handle, platform push token, or stable cross-context correlation key.

registration_id.description: Station-generated, high-entropy, pairwise registration identity scoped to one exact AccountId/device/push route and destination Gateway. It is not an Arkret typed ID, MUST NOT begin with ak:, MUST NOT encode account or provider material, and MUST never be reused after terminal revocation. A replacement allocates a new registration_id and names the exact predecessor through supersedes_registration_id.

badge.description: Coarse unread indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute unread count (activity side channel); only a boolean presence flag or a policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

missed_call.description: Coarse missed-call indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute count; only a boolean presence flag or the policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

device_route.description: Per-notification device selector only. The gateway obtains provider token, application, platform and explicit visible-notification opt-in solely from authenticated durable registration, and derives timing from source service, selected route and declared profile.

route_tokens.description: Gateway-internal opaque routing fragment shared by blind and visible notifications. Every field here drives gateway-side routing / dedup / circuit-breaker state and MUST be stripped before the gateway calls any push provider; it MUST NOT be forwarded to a provider. Tokens are issued by the destination Principal Service and bound to that service DID, push gateway service DID, purpose, scope, and salt epoch.

realm_route_token.description: Opaque token for Realm-level routing / dedup / circuit-breaker keying.

scope_route_token.description: Opaque token for the effective Realm or Circle scope of this wakeup.

audit_envelope.description: `ak.audit.accessed` envelope routing fragment carried alongside a notify request. When present, the request is an audit-pipeline event (e.g. an `e2ee_late_recovery` access notice), not a push notify: the gateway writes the audit event, acks 200, and skips the push pipeline.

access_kind.description: ak.audit.accessed.access_kind. The gateway branches on `e2ee_late_recovery` to skip the push pipeline.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: REQUIRED (at the application layer) when access_kind == e2ee_late_recovery. References the original encrypted event for audit only; this marker does not prove historical membership or authorize plaintext disclosure.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key". MUST be an l10n key token, never plaintext body or any identifying metadata.

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved (E2EE client-side rule fallback). Pure local-evaluation signal; carries no metadata. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

devices.description: Nonempty unique device_id set. Routes, platform, application and visible-notification opt-in are resolved exclusively from authenticated current device registrations.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key".

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

devices.description: Nonempty unique device_id set. Routes, platform, application and visible-notification opt-in are resolved exclusively from authenticated current device registrations.

visible_notification_opt_in.description: Receiver device authorization state for ak.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1. Missing or false means this device MUST receive only blind_wakeup output even if the caller service is plaintext-visible; visible metadata requires an explicit per-device opt-in.

push_register_device_request_body.description: Account Station self-service registration. The authenticated exact AccountId supplies registration scope and its station_id must equal the receiving Station service identity. A push_gateway role cannot accept this operation on its own authority.

push_target_id.description: Server-derived pairwise pseudonym for this registration, derived per push-notifications.md section 2.2 (HMAC-SHA256 over the service-private push secret and canonical account_id / device_id / push_route_id / salt_epoch_id inputs). account_id is taken from the authenticated session and is not repeated in this self-service request. The caller and the device MUST use this exact value as the notify target; they MUST NOT mint their own push_target_id.

registration_id.description: Station-generated immutable identity for this exact registration. The Station uses it for trusted public-Gateway handoff and terminal revocation; the client MUST treat it as opaque.

push_unregister_device_request_body.description: Account Station self-service unregistration under the same exact authenticated AccountId/device authority as registration; gateway notify authority is insufficient.

push_key.description: Provider route secret disclosed only to the destination Gateway's authenticated Source-Service-ID tenant partition. It MUST NOT enter notify, receipts, logs, metrics, traces, cross-tenant indexes, or provider payload fields other than the provider address required for delivery.

visible_notification_opt_in.description: Exact device opt-in derived by the source Station. False restricts the installation to blind wakeup even when the Gateway also advertises the visible-notification profile.

supersedes_registration_id.description: Exact current predecessor replaced by this installation. The Gateway atomically tombstones that predecessor with installing this registration. It MUST be absent for an initial installation.

push_registration_handoff_active.description: Immutable active installation submitted by the authenticated source Station to one trusted public Gateway. Source and destination service identities are carried only by signed HTTP headers. The source Station is the only notify source authorized by this minimal handoff contract; delegation is not inferred from profile claims or body fields.

push_registration_handoff_revoked.description: Terminal handoff tombstone. It carries no provider route, application metadata, opt-in, account identity, or replacement value. The Gateway retains the minimal (source Station, registration_id, request digest, outcome) high-water needed to reject a delayed active install after private material is erased.

push_registration_handoff_request_body.description: Station-to-Gateway desired registration state. The HTTP Message Signature binds exact Source-Service-ID, Destination-Service-ID and Content-Digest. The Gateway keys state by authenticated source tenant plus registration_id; a byte-identical replay returns the original receipt, different content for the same key is duplicate_conflict, and revoked is terminal.

request_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of the complete handoff request body. It binds provider route bytes without repeating them in the receipt.

proof.description: Gateway detached-JWS proof. payload_digest hashes this complete receipt with proof omitted. The signed binding is canonical_json({context:'ak.push_registration_installation_receipt_proof.v1',payload_digest,registration_id,push_target_id,device_id,state,request_digest,source_station_id,destination_gateway_id,verification_method,created_at,audience}); created_at equals stored_at and audience equals source_station_id.

push_registration_installation_receipt.description: Gateway-signed durable confirmation that the exact active installation or terminal tombstone was committed in the authenticated source Station tenant before success. The receipt grants no Account authority and contains no provider token.

push_notify_request_body.description: Closed Arkret notify body. Product-private notification bodies, provider adapter payloads, APNs/FCM/WebPush data dictionaries, `content`, `content_*`, `provider_payload`, DND/snooze state, and push-rule plaintext are outside this wire surface and MUST be consumed before this body is built. Provider-facing payloads are reconstructed by the gateway from this closed shape and MUST strip route_tokens / reason_code / event_kind / audit_envelope before provider dispatch.

event_kind.description: Originating Event kind (e.g. `ak.message`) used by the gateway to route Phase-P2 `ak.agent.*` lifecycle / actor-private kinds to a no-fanout aak. Coarse routing selector; carries no Realm / sender / event identifier.

reason_code.description: Caller-supplied wire-safe reason code. The well-known value `historical_only` marks a diagnostic replay that MUST NOT trigger a fresh push fanout (the gateway answers a 200 idempotency-style ack). Other values are honored only where the operation defines them.

push_gateway_submission_outcome.description: Gateway acceptance result for exactly one input device route. Identity is the (push_target_id, device_id) pair already carried by the request; no third route identifier exists. Provider delivery state, provider message ids, raw push tokens and token hashes MUST NOT appear here.

gateway_status.description: Closed gateway acceptance result. accepted = this request durably took the device route over. duplicate = an earlier request already took it over, or the operation explicitly requires a no-fanout acknowledgement, and this request produced no new delivery. A no-fanout acknowledgement does not assert provider acceptance, queueing or new durable route ownership. rejected = the gateway did not take it over. accepted and duplicate both mean the caller MUST NOT resend this device; only rejected may be resent, and only when retry_after_ms is present. See push-notifications.md §5.2.

reason_code.description: Closed rejection reason, all registered in error-code-registry.json. The first four are target-level or policy rejections; push_token_unknown / push_token_invalid tell the caller to drop this device registration; the last two are the only caller-retryable reasons. REQUIRED when gateway_status=rejected and MUST be absent otherwise.

retry_after_ms.description: Caller-facing backoff. Present only when the gateway did not take the route over AND the reason is one the caller can retry; its presence is the sole wire signal that the caller — not the gateway — owns the next attempt. A durably accepted route is retried by the gateway and never carries this field.

push_notify_response_body.description: Closed notify response. outcomes[] is conserved against notification.devices[]: every input device_id appears exactly once, no device_id appears twice, and no device_id appears that was not requested. A target-level failure is expanded into one same-reason rejected outcome per input device rather than collapsing into a second response shape, so the conservation invariant holds unconditionally. Counts, if a deployment surfaces them, are derived from outcomes[] and are never an independent truth source.

push_target_id.description: Echo of notification.push_target_id. MUST equal the request value.

outcomes.description: One entry per unique device_id in notification.devices[]. device_id MUST be unique across the array.

contract.description: Canonical wire schema for client query / projection and search request bodies and their reusable building blocks (filters, sort, relation query). The OpenAPI document references these $defs so there is a single source of truth. Human-readable semantics: zh/conformance/query-schema.md. facet_name / view_renderer are copies of the shared OpenAPI enums (kept local so this file is self-contained); the authoritative facet / renderer enums also live in the OpenAPI components and MUST stay in lockstep.

context_ref.description: Optional timeline / renderer context object reference. This is not a RealmCommit.

wait_for.description: Unique body wait carrier only for an operation/binding explicitly registered in operation-registry.wait_for_bindings. No current generic query operation is registered. Header or consistency aliases are forbidden.

contract.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface read cursor operations (ak.self.read_cursor.*). Advance carries the authenticated holder's exact signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event; the service validates and forwards it without rebuilding or co-signing. The durable cursor object model and read_scope / position field shapes are read-cursor.schema.json; that object has no updated_at, and the outcome updated_at here is the derived envelope created_at of the winning advance. See spec/v1/zh/discovery/read-receipts.md.

read_cursor_advance_request_body.description: Carries one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance Event and nothing else. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 object; actor_id is both envelope ownership and payload ownership, while payload device_id must equal the authenticated session device. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through authority Event submission and MUST NOT rebuild the payload or sign under a service identity. The cursor object carries neither an id (there is no read_cursor typed ID kind; identity is the (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) tuple) nor an updated_at: a cursor is never updated in place, so the update time of an advance is the submitted Event envelope created_at and MUST NOT be restated in the payload.

updated_at.description: Derived, not caller-supplied: the envelope created_at of the ak.read_cursor.advance Event that currently wins the causal-first merge for this (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope). The cursor object itself carries no updated_at.

kind.description: Read-scope object kind per zh/models/private-objects.md §2.2. Track-scoped read cursors use kind='strand' plus track_name. Thread cursors use kind='thread' with container_ref = the thread root message id (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector over the reply sub-timeline, not a first-class protocol object. Shares the read-scope discriminator family with read-receipt.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset.

container_ref.description: Required when kind is circle, space, strand, or thread; omitted for kind='realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' AND the cursor scopes a single track (e.g. 'discussion', 'synthesis', or any profile-registered track name). Track names MUST match the Strand's registered tracks; unknown tracks MUST be rejected with schema_violation.

contract.description: Actor-private multi-device read cursor. Stored in encrypted account data or actor-private stream; NEVER published into a shared Realm Event history. Bound to (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position, HLC, device_id) per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §6.6. Multi-device merge is causal-first per §6.5: the position that causally dominates wins regardless of HLC; HLC max decides only causally concurrent positions, and device_id only breaks equal HLCs. The object carries NO typed id and NO update timestamp. A cursor is never updated in place: its identity is the (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) tuple, each advance is a freshly authored ak.read_cursor.advance Event (event-kind-registry id_source=not_an_object_id), and the time of that update is that Event envelope created_at. There is no read_cursor typed ID kind, no id-addressed read surface, and capability selectors address read cursors only as read_cursor:<realm>:*. Derived views that need a time (read-cursor-operations.schema.json#/$defs/read_marker_response_body, the ak.read_cursor.update device-message content ak.schema.read_cursor_update.v1) take updated_at from the winning advance envelope.

device_id.description: Originating device. Required for multi-device convergence: when two devices race on the same (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) the receiver first picks the later position when both position Events are committed on the same CommitStreamRef; only when neither dominates (different streams or the same Event) does it pick the greater HLC, and device_id provides a deterministic actor_id-scoped tiebreaker when those HLCs are equal. device_id MUST NOT be used to select a position that another position dominates.

contract.description: Closed decrypted Signal plaintext payload profile for ak.receipt.read, carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session. It is a Strand timeline UI hint, NOT canonical truth, NOT a durable Event, and NOT a multi-device cursor (see read-cursor.schema.json for that). MUST NOT generate push notifications. Realm scope, sender identity and send time come from the enclosing signed envelope and are not duplicated here. Privacy is governed by Realm policy: Realms MAY allow public, members-only, or actor-private receipt sharing. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md sections 2.1 / 6.2 and zh/sync/signal.md section 1.1.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_actor_id, sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref), including the complete ActorId. Arbitrary forward gaps are accepted; a repeated or lower value is stale.

event_id.description: ID of the most recent Event the actor has read. Causality implies all causal predecessors are also read.

hlc.description: Optional. HLC of the read position; required when the Station sync surface compares receipts under merge / debounce rules across devices for the same actor.

kind.description: Read-scope discriminator from the same family as read-cursor.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset (receipt additionally supports view/message/morph; cursor additionally supports circle/space). kind='thread' selects the reply sub-timeline rooted at a message (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector, not a first-class protocol object.

object_ref.description: Required when kind is anything other than 'realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' and the receipt scopes a single track.

track_scope.description: Only valid when kind='strand'. Use track_scope='all' for an entire Strand regardless of track.

source_ref.description: Original accepted source of this selector at the same private read cut; stream and revision equal the row.

webvh_recovery_plan.description: Recovery-begin planning carrier only. Complete signed inception-to-target native log, with available witness records; all accepted-prefix witnesses remain mandatory. Missing witness records for unaccepted successor entries are allowed at begin only. No evidence receipt or claim of published currentness. Validate signatures, pre-rotation, accepted-prefix extension and exact next_resolution independently. Finish requires complete published webvh_method_history_evidence. Canonical size at most 1 MiB.

log_entries.description: Exact ordered native did:webvh entry objects from inception through the containing recovery.begin payload.next_resolution.version_id. Apply registered native parameter/proof rules and reject gaps, duplicates, surplus entries after that exact target, or a first entry other than inception. The separately supplied next_resolution commitments must independently recompute from this target.

witness_records.description: Available native witness records, unique by versionId. Accepted prefix must satisfy its witness policy; successor records may be absent until finish. Any supplied record must verify; no surplus or invalid records.

contract.description: Public genesis-to-current authority certificate chain plus a nonce-bound online assertion. It exposes only the Realm stream and never enumerates Circle or Sidecar streams. Human PCR accepted registration genesis binds the complete Account and its account Station permanently under ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 pcr_governance_policy. A Human genesis governor mismatch, authority transition or foreign current governor rejects without effects; provenance is independently verified and is not a caller-supplied flag. User-managed Agent PCR is also fixed to its original full Agent/controller Account Station at generation zero with no authority transitions; accepted agent_control genesis and controller provision must bind that Station. Existing generation-zero Agent disclosure retains its own gates. Other proven subject branches retain their existing rules. The public operation MUST NOT disclose a Human PCR bundle: indistinguishable not_found under pcr_governance_policy; its private native authority checks remain mandatory. Non-Human managed-device verification retains this carrier. Direct Conversation fixes the accepted genesis governance_station_id for life at generation zero: authority_transitions is empty and current_service_id equals that genesis Station, including the current assertion. Same-Station endpoint/key/deployment changes remain legal; normal generation-zero Direct bundles retain existing disclosure gates.

authority_transition.description: The Event must be ak.realm.governance_station.change in the Realm stream; all IDs and consecutive generations must match the handoff.

contract.description: Closed planned transfer from one Realm authority generation to its unique successor. Both service signatures and the controller-authored change Event are required; this is not a quorum vote. Eligibility is derived from verified accepted genesis provenance: Human and user-managed Agent PCRs are forbidden at every handoff stage by the PCR profile pcr_governance_policy; valid signatures or schema shape cannot override it.

historical_signer_facts_digest.description: New handoffs require SHA256(JCS complete sorted {target,producer_signer_fact} inventory); existing_original-only schema absence cannot transfer new digest-bearing history. Both original handoff contexts sign it.

pcr_private_state_digest.description: Required exactly for eligible Organization PCR planned handoff: SHA256 of the complete canonical private handoff manifest, including its undisclosed CSPRNG nonce. Both original signatures cover it; no private archive or manifest enters the public authority bundle.

change_commit_id.description: The Realm-stream commit for change_event_ref; it is not a cross-stream final commit.

management_private_state_digest.description: New eligible handoffs require SHA256(JCS of the private management handoff manifest), including empty state, independent of Applet/review presence. Both existing handoff signatures cover it. Historical originals remain immutable. No private manifest/archive enters public authority bundles.

contract.description: The only shared Realm acceptance, ordering, finality and replication record. Every visibility scope has an authority-signed predecessor chain.

governance_generation.description: Tenure counter of the governing Station that signed this Commit; it advances only on an accepted ak.realm.governance_station.change. It is not the Realm authority-root delegation generation of current-state.schema.json#/$defs/realm_authority_root_value, which advances only on ak.realm.authority.reset.

producer_signer_fact_digest.description: Fixed SHA256(JCS(original immutable producer signer fact)), before Commit identity/signature. The fact excludes its target Commit coordinate. Human, Service, realm_device and private realm_control facts retain their exact original verification sources through replay and handoff.

stream_ref.description: Closed independent stream selector: Realm, Circle, Sidecar or private realm_control. realm_control is not a business, membership, capability or MLS scope.

genesis_salt.description: Canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of exactly 32 CSPRNG octets. It distinguishes event-derived creation intents and has no replay, ordering, authorization, freshness, or winner semantics.

founding_device_descriptor.description: Human Principal Control Realm genesis only. The identity root commits to the exact founding device material and the canonical founding authorize payload digest. The enclosing pcr_genesis_unit requires it; Agent PCR genesis MUST omit it.

initial_resolution.description: Root-committed initial did and DID method history position for a Principal Control Realm or Agent control Realm. The admitting service MUST verify that project(did) equals the genesis actor_id before accepting the closed genesis unit.

allOf.description: founding_device_descriptor is exclusive to human Principal Control Realm genesis. agent_control, collaboration and direct_conversation genesis MUST omit it. genesis_salt is required for every purpose since PCR genesis is event-derived like any other Realm.
Only identity-control Realm genesis carries initial_resolution, and every such genesis carries it. Collaboration/direct-conversation Realms MUST omit it.
Human Principal Control Realm genesis uses the independently closed human-principal DID method set.
Agent PCR genesis commits the already accepted did:webvh inception head. The later PCR service binding update is continuous from this head and does not participate in the create Event preimage.

founding_device_descriptor.description: Closed founding-device commitment embedded in the root-signed human Principal Control Realm genesis payload and required by pcr_genesis_unit. It is not an independent signed object. Agent PCR creation omits this human-device descriptor.

device_public_key_did.description: did:key form of the founding device Ed25519 signing key. The descriptor carries the raw key inside the root-signed genesis payload, so it carries no key digest; the receipt pcr_genesis_scope.device_key_digest is SHA-256(UTF-8(canonical multikey)) over this value with the did:key: prefix removed.

hpke_key.description: Founding device X25519 HPKE public key as the canonical multibase base58btc multikey of the X25519 multicodec (0xec), always starting with z6LS. It is the same encoding discipline as device_public_key_did without the did:key: prefix and the same value the founding ak.device.authorize payload carries; the receipt pcr_genesis_scope.hpke_key_digest is SHA-256(UTF-8(this exact string)).

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the proof-free founding ak.device.authorize payload. It MUST NOT be an Event id or envelope digest.

contract.description: Human PCR accepted registration genesis binds the complete Account and its account Station permanently under ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 pcr_governance_policy. A Human genesis governor mismatch, authority transition or foreign current governor rejects without effects; provenance is independently verified and is not a caller-supplied flag. Other proven subject branches retain their existing rules.

A closed, untrusted locator core for obtaining a nonce-bound RealmAuthorityBundle. Realm scope and freshness belong to the enclosing carrier and current assertion. The core carries no proof, authority assertion, governance history, operation advertisement, preference, or trust level; only a verified genesis, continuous handoff chain, and valid nonce-bound current assertion can identify the current governance Station.
Join discovery and bootstrap through the verified current governance Station. An inviter Station and Directory provide only routing hints; neither is an authority source.

authority_locator_hints.description: One to eight untrusted locator cores, strictly sorted by service_id UTF-8 bytes. service_id is the semantic identity key; duplicate or conflicting representations of one service_id invalidate the entire array.

governance_generation.description: Station tenure the intake descriptor was answered under.

self_preview_response_body.description: Pre-join disclosure relayed by the caller's own Station. authority_bundle is the RealmAuthorityBundle that Station fetched with its own nonce and verified before asking the current governance Station for the preview; the preview is not membership, a join commitment or verified governance state.

peer_preview_response_body.description: Disclosure answered by the verified current governance Station. It carries no authority bundle: the caller Station has already verified this Station through its own nonce-bound RealmAuthorityBundle and authenticates it as Destination-Service-ID.

self_prepare_response_body.description: Current context for authoring a producer-signed join Event. It does not reserve a position or authorize admission.

membership_commit_id.description: RealmCommit of the member's own join that opened the caller's held stream, or re-anchored it after the caller had no joined hosted member left: ak.member.state{join} or ak.invite.accept for a directed Invite on the Realm stream, or ak.circle.member.state{join} on the Circle stream. Circle bootstrap requires current parent-Realm membership; a parent-Realm join Commit cannot replace the Circle join Commit (zh/sync/federation.md section 4.1.1).

history_stream_ref.description: Optional exact target stream for a stream_history original instead of a full recovery baseline. The same accepted current membership and authenticated member Station checks apply. The response signed Account/stream coverage must match this request, and cannot bootstrap or overwrite current state.

peer_bootstrap_response_body.description: The verified current authority returns a snapshot whose retention_and_history_floor for the membership Commit's exact stream is that join position, with a visible head at or above it. Other authorized streams retain their own history floors. The caller verifies that prefix evidence, installs the disclosed snapshot current_state_entries as its typed current anchored at their stream heads, then scans each permitted stream from its own floor to its advertised head (zh/sync/federation.md section 4.1.1). After an already accepted registered atomic unit has completed member-station materialization, a governing Snapshot refresh preserves that caller's canonical history floor proved under zh/governance/history-visibility.md section 3.1 and its complete authorized current cut. Under since_join, floor zero requires the exact current founding join and position zero to belong to the same proven accepted atomic unit, with its complete originals and continuous Commit chain; later rejoin, missing originals, Realm purpose or low position alone cannot supply this exception. Direct Conversation four-item founding is never four independent single-join bootstrap exceptions. This clarification does not change the initial ordinary single-join bootstrap prefix, Circle gates, signatures, governance tenure, exact scope, membership or continuous-prefix verification, and adds no operation or DTO.

contract.description: Closed response DTOs for the self-surface cross-Realm link read operations (ak.self.realm_link.*). Writes use caller-signed ak.realm.link Events submitted through the authority Event submission surface. General link-graph cycles are legal; traversal uses a visited set and does not reject a write merely for forming a cycle. The durable link payload is the canonical ak.realm.link; see spec/v1/zh/models/realm-links.md.

link_kind.description: Core value or machine-registered extension kind using x.<reverse-dns>.<name>; unregistered extension values fail closed.

commitment.description: Optional opaque commitment / proof reference linking this edge to an external attestation.

contract.description: Closed response DTO for the self-surface Realm organization-relationship read operation (ak.self.realm_organization.read.list.v1). Returns the projected ak.realm.organization statements (active / revoked / expired) for a Realm plus the declared owning_organization_ids hints that have no verified statement. The verified rows mirror the canonical realm_organization_payload field order; lifecycle_phase is reducer-derived. A row here is a projection only: an organization relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active, and actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy, governance-Station authority, capability, or service-binding Event. See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.3.0 and schemas/event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/realm_organization_payload.

lifecycle_phase.description: Reducer-derived lifecycle phase of the projected statement. verified_active = latest accepted statement for (organization_id, relationship) is status=active and within its validity window. revoked_or_expired = the relationship has been revoked or is outside its not_before/expires_at window. Declared-only organization hints with no statement are carried in declared_organization_hint_ids, not as rows.

delegation_ref.description: Resolved authorization.delegation_ref for delegated issuer roles (governance_service / account_authority).

relationships.description: Projected ak.realm.organization statement rows (verified_active and revoked_or_expired), latest-per-(organization_id, relationship).

declared_organization_hint_ids.description: owning_organization_ids declared hints (realm-and-space.md §2.3.0) that have NO verified ak.realm.organization statement. These are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

contract.description: Closed response DTOs for the self-surface Realm read operations (ak.self.realm.*). Realm read returns the lifecycle projection, stream enumeration returns the visible authority streams of one Realm, and export returns a full event-log + operation dump. See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md.

realm_stream_view.description: One authority stream of the Realm that this caller is permitted to know exists and whose Commit chain is already established. Progress uses the same {head_commit_ref, next_position} shape as zh/sync/service-surface.md section 4.6, and readable_floor is the same anchor the scan surface returns, so a client can enumerate, bind its permitted prefix and continue the tail without a second vocabulary.

head_commit_ref.description: Head Commit of this stream as known to the server when the page was served. A stream with no Commit yet MUST NOT appear in this list at all rather than appear with an empty head.

next_position.description: Next stream_position this stream expects, i.e. head stream_position + 1. Positions are never compared across streams.

readable_floor.description: Bottom of this caller's readable range on this stream. Omitted only when the caller may read no Commit of the stream while still being permitted to know that it exists.

realm_stream_page.description: ACL-filtered, paginated enumeration of one Realm's authority streams (ak.self.realm.read.streams.v1). It is the discovery surface that positional scan cannot be: scan requires a stream_ref the caller already knows, so without this list a stream outside the bounded subscribe window would be undiscoverable. Pagination is a fixed snapshot: the page sequence is taken against one server-side generation, so a stream that appears after the first page is NOT inserted into the earlier pages and is therefore never skipped; it is discovered by a later enumeration or by the visible discovery delta. Permissions are re-checked on every page, so a page MAY be narrower than its predecessor, and a stream the caller has stopped being permitted to know about MUST disappear rather than be served from the frozen generation.

streams.description: Rows sorted by unsigned bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(stream_ref), the same order the subscribe frame truncates in, so enumeration and delivery agree on which streams a bounded window kept. The Realm stream is a row like any other.
