next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation of this enumeration. Absent means the current page is the last one.

has_more.description: The only field a client may use to decide whether to keep paging (zh/sync/api-conventions.md section 7.1).

operations.description: Operation dump rows {operation_id, realm_id, object_kind, operation_type, payload, created_at}.

events.description: Event-log dump rows {event_id, realm_id, event_kind, operation_type, operation_id, sender, payload, created_at}.

contract.description: Closed signed inline Snapshot with signed purpose and complete same-cut coverage. full_recovery includes all caller-disclosable rows/heads/floors and retains the 8 MiB admission capacity. stream_history contains all disclosable target-stream rows excluding circle/sidecar definition selectors (which are scope-local despite their parent Realm source), plus exactly the required parent MemberState and Circle/Sidecar selector rows, and heads/floors only for their source streams. Its signed history_basis binds full Account identity (including Station), exact target, anchor and accepted cross-stream dependency refs. It is a new original with its own content ID, issued before the window ref, never a clipped signed original. Current disclosure rechecks every included component; unrelated scopes absent from this object do not invalidate it. Narrow objects never replace current/bootstrap/handoff or imply omitted state is absent. Existing signer-tenure, retention/redaction, cursor lifetime and atomic Account-frame checks remain mandatory.

governance_generation.description: Station tenure this snapshot is bound to. Current /head MUST equal the fresh current authority generation. Exact historical by-ref MUST equal its requested basis generation and may precede current authority after a valid handoff; the consuming Account Station or independent auditor resolves that tenure and its exact signing-time service key from the fresh genesis-to-current chain. Unknown/future tenure, wrong signer, old tenure presented as current head, or rollback of saved current/checkpoints MUST be refused. Ordinary clients apply the bound own-Station consumption contract rather than independently resolving governance history.

purpose.description: Signed installation purpose. Only full_recovery can replace a Realm current baseline. stream_history is bound to one Account historical window and MUST NOT clear omitted selectors or advance current checkpoints.

visible_stream_heads.description: Exactly the covered source streams at the signed cut. full_recovery covers every disclosed stream; stream_history covers its target plus only sources of necessary selector dependencies. No hidden directory.

current_state_entries.description: Complete disclosable selector set within the signed coverage, read at the same cut as covered heads and floors. Omitted selectors outside stream_history coverage do not mean empty or deleted.

retention_and_history_floor.description: Caller-authorized per-stream history floors and Realm history policy at the same durable cut as visible_stream_heads and current_state_entries; no floor for a hidden stream may be disclosed.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

security_class.description: Optional security class. 'high_assurance' forbids federation_policy=open and SHOULD use stricter resolver/E2EE/audit defaults. Omitted = 'standard'.

trust_domain.description: Immutable deployment trust domain captured by ak.realm.create. Receivers MUST require this to match the current Realm trust domain before accepting cross-domain replay-sensitive proofs.

owning_organization_ids.description: Declared or projected stable Organization principal identities associated with this Realm. Each value is a did_core_id and is not itself resolvable DID material; Organization classification and current DID evidence are established by accepted registration/resolution state. This field alone is not a verified ownership/governance endorsement; clients and directories MUST require an active ak.realm.organization statement for verified badges or organization-controlled semantics.

schema_refs.description: Currently activated registered schema id set. It carries no Realm structural role: the signed ak.schema.realm_genesis.v1 purpose is the only authority for Realm class (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3), so a profile id here would be a second, editable class discriminator. The core member ak.schema.realm.v1 is initialised by the genesis reducer, is always present and can never be removed. Every other member MUST be a registered ak.schema.*.vN id; third-party namespaces are not accepted and no registered Event mints a non-ak. schema id. ak.realm.schema replaces this whole set (realm_schema_payload); policy, deployment conformance and operation-local profiles have their own carriers and are forbidden here.

fields.description: Product/profile fields. purpose and collaboration_role are reducer-managed read-only projections of the signed genesis purpose and MUST equal it (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3); they are schema constrained below so a producer cannot mint a Realm class here. Other product fields remain extension-defined.

purpose.description: Projection of genesis purpose for the three identity-control classes. genesis purpose=collaboration and purpose=direct_conversation project no value here. Authorization MUST verify the genesis, never this field.

collaboration_role.description: Projection of genesis purpose=direct_conversation. No other genesis purpose projects this field, and authorization MUST verify the genesis rather than this projection.

preview_policy_id.description: Optional materialized pointer to the effective preview / peek policy. Canonical writes use ak.realm.preview_policy; absence means directory card / stripped state only, no history stub/snippet preview.

default_strand_id.description: Derived ordinary default-Strand selection from current-value projection realm_set_default_strand. The deterministic (depth, EventId) winner selects the candidate; it is effective only when the selected Strand is eligible, non-terminal, and in the same Realm. Selection grants no authority.

history_access.description: Scope-local history range ratchet initialized by Realm create. Only all_history_for_current_members to since_join may change state; widening back to all_history is permanently forbidden. Standard MLS requires since_join.

governance_station_id.description: Current governance Station service identity, derived from generation-0 genesis and the verified consecutive handoff chain. It is the authority that signs RealmCommit records for every independent Realm, Circle, and Sidecar stream in this Realm generation.

agent_participation.description: Realm five-bit Agent participation ceiling. It may only tighten the target-service safety ceiling and is itself the parent of Circle and Strand ceilings.

max_authority_lifetime_ms.description: Maximum fixed child-chain lifetime only for actions explicitly required to be finite by their risk/constraint contract. Defaults to 24 hours for those actions; first use freezes the bound and redelegation cannot renew it. It does not impose expiry on unbounded ordinary chat/read/organizer authorization.

contract.description: Closed recovery completion attestation and Standard-grant issuance carriers. Device recovery is authorized by the accepted PCR recovery policy; an optional DID-root proof is only one explicitly enabled factor. When deployment policy permits reactivation, the same completed closure is the only operation that may atomically author a deactivated-to-active successor for the original account before issuing its new-generation Standard grant.

issue_recovery_completion_grant_response.description: Exact durable outcome for one completed recovery transaction. If the original account was deactivated, successful issuance also means the Account Authority atomically restored that same account and authored its deactivated-to-active successor; no replacement account or second PCR is created.

recovery_completion_grant_request_body.description: Closed request proving completed PCR recovery and the exact current replacement device generation. The Account Authority checks the committed re-anchor through its RealmCommit.

initial_session.description: The Standard grant to issue after recovery. device_id MUST equal the attested replacement device and the RFC 7638 thumbprint of session_public_key MUST equal the Bound AccountHandoff and HTTP DPoP key.

canonical_request_digest.description: SHA-256 of JCS(request object with only canonical_request_digest omitted). The Bound AccountHandoff authorization and RFC 9449 HTTP DPoP proof authenticate the account and holder outside this closed business body.

recovery_completion_attestation.description: Coordinator-signed proof created after one atomic recovery commit accepted the two producer-signed recovery Events, issued one PCR-stream RealmCommit for each of them, advanced the device generation, activated the replacement device, consumed the recovery session and completed the transaction. A RealmCommit accepts exactly one Event, so the two CommittedEventRef values MUST name two different Commits at consecutive positions n and n+1 of the same PCR Realm stream; their commit_id and their event_id MUST both differ.

account_id.description: Exact recovered account. Its station_id is the coordinator: the service signer/route authority of the Station-local recovery transaction. No separate coordinator field exists on wire or in the signed projection.

completed_at.description: Server-side linearized commit time of the single atomic recovery commit. It MUST NOT be earlier than the terminal receipt completed_at, which is only an authoring time.

signature.description: Base64URL signature over the closed completion projection, including reanchor_event_ref, device_authorization_event_ref and new_model_generation_ref.

reanchor_event_ref.description: CommittedEventRef of the recovery re-anchor Event in the account PCR stream. It sits at position n, immediately before device_authorization_event_ref, in its own RealmCommit.

device_authorization_event_ref.description: CommittedEventRef of the replacement-device authorization Event. It sits at position n+1 of the same PCR Realm stream as reanchor_event_ref, in its own RealmCommit accepted by the same atomic recovery transaction.

contract.description: Normative grammar for an account's PCR recovery policy. Bound through signed control events to one exact AccountId and its local unique PCR lineage; receivers reject recovery and pcr_recovery device authorization whose proof family or optional DID-root factor is not allowed by the currently accepted policy.

version.description: Monotonically increasing counter scoped by the exact account_id. Receivers MUST reject a publish whose version is not strictly greater than the currently accepted policy.

supersedes_id.description: Predecessor policy_id. Null only for the genesis policy of an exact account.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier the policy applies to. Cross-domain proofs MUST fail.

cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wall-clock delay, in seconds, between recovery session creation and acceptance of a recovery proof for that session. Receivers MUST reject a proof submitted earlier. Absence is no delay; the value is a signed policy constraint and MUST NOT be ignored.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the authorized issuer: founding device after genesis; current-generation accepted device for later updates; identity root for re-anchor; or a coordinator satisfying the superseded policy quorum. Receivers resolve this semantic authority from accepted principal-control state, not from arbitrary DID Document membership.

signature.description: base64url signature over UTF8('ak.identity.recovery_policy.signature.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of all present top-level policy members except signature_proof. The closed policy shape fixes the projection; absent optional members are omitted and null is retained only where the schema explicitly admits null.

methods.description: Single signed source of recovery acceptance and derived publication authority. Each kind occurs at most once (semantic MUST). Entries are independent OR alternatives; device_quorum.k counts distinct eligible member devices within that entry and MUST NOT exceed its member count. Empty methods is explicit policy revocation. did_root is an opt-in to validated DID history/pre-rotation authority, never an accepted device key. Every published entry MUST be executable by the receiving deployment; no constraint may be silently discarded.

recovery_policy_set_payload.description: Canonical ak.policy.set payload for recovery-policy publication. policy_id MUST equal value.policy_id; state and reason are intentionally unavailable on this operation.

recovery_policy_publish_request_body.description: Recovery policy publication through the ordinary first-publication Event ingress. Cross-field validation additionally requires payload.policy_id=value.policy_id and actor/scope/lease to bind value.account_id's exact Principal Control Realm.

recovery_key_entry.description: Recovery proof signing key with its distinct, inline backup-only HPKE recipient. The signing verification_method and backup_hpke.key_agreement_ref MUST be unique within the policy. Public material, algorithm, validity and revocation are checked independently for the two roles.

verification_method.description: Exact and sole recovery signing-key selector used by recovery_unlock proofs. It resolves only within this accepted policy entry, never through arbitrary DID Document membership or a caller-provided fallback.

public_key_multibase.description: Multikey for the recovery proof signature algorithm. MUST NOT equal or be converted into the paired HPKE key.

signature_algorithm.description: Current-v1 signature algorithm used by the recovery key. Reserved algorithms, including ML-DSA-65, fail closed as unsupported until a future negotiated schema/profile activation.

not_before.description: Earliest instant this recovery key may authorize a recovery_unlock proof.

expires_at.description: Instant after which this recovery key MUST NOT authorize a recovery_unlock proof.

revoked_at.description: When set, the entry is revoked from this instant onward and MUST NOT satisfy any recovery_unlock proof whose binding time is at or after it.

recovery_key_agreement_entry.description: Dedicated X25519 HPKE recipient for key-backup envelopes. It cannot verify recovery_unlock or authorize DID/Event operations.

key_agreement_ref.description: Stable identifier used by key-backup encryption.recipient_key_ref.

recovery_policy_summary.description: Read-model summary of the currently accepted recovery policy. `policy` carries the original ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object when the service can disclose it to the caller.

acceptance_basis_ref.description: RealmCommit that accepted this exact recovery policy version.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple equivalent to `{policy_id, policy_version: version}`. When present, it MUST match policy_id/version.

policy.description: Full accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object. Omitted only when the caller is authorized to learn that a policy exists but not to receive the accepted method entries.

methods.description: Single signed source of recovery acceptance and derived publication authority. Each kind occurs at most once (semantic MUST). Entries are independent OR alternatives; device_quorum.k counts distinct eligible member devices within that entry and MUST NOT exceed its member count. Empty methods is explicit policy revocation. did_root is an opt-in to validated DID history/pre-rotation authority, never an accepted device key. Every published entry MUST be executable by the receiving deployment; no constraint may be silently discarded.

authority_stream_head.description: Optional account control-stream checkpoint under which the active policy was observed.

recovery_policy_status_view.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.resource.get.v1. `active_policy=null` is a successful read meaning no accepted recovery policy currently exists for the resolved exact account.

account_id.description: Resolved exact account. Required when the request used an explicit account_id selector; SHOULD be present on all authenticated reads.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple for the active policy. MUST be absent or null-equivalent when active_policy is null, and MUST match active_policy.policy_id/version when active_policy is present.

recovery_policy_publish_response_body.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.command.publish.v1 after accepting a ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 publish or rotation.

acceptance_basis_ref.description: RealmCommit that accepted this exact recovery policy version.

authorization_verification_method.description: Exact accepted policy method authorized for this service; both method and audience MUST match verbatim. DID membership or recursive string mention is insufficient.

services.description: Recovery authorization issuers accepted by this policy. Entries are independent OR alternatives: exactly one entry MUST match the submitted authorization verbatim on service_id, authorization_verification_method and audience. There is no threshold across entries and no deployment-level issuer.

contract.description: Replacement-device-signed terminal intent for one RecoveryTransaction. It binds the two exact producer Event ids, recovery session/policy/proof snapshot and resulting device generation expectation. It is signed before authority admission and therefore does not contain a RealmCommit id; successful completion is proven separately by the coordinator-signed recovery completion attestation and its CommittedEventRef values.

transaction_id.description: RecoveryTransaction that reserved this receipt id. It MUST equal the transaction whose binding.terminal_receipt_id is this receipt_id, which is what lets a verifier holding only the receipt resolve the authorizing transaction; binding.terminal_receipt_id alone is one-way. See zh/identity/security-transactions.md section 2.

transaction_request_digest.description: Stable request_digest of the RecoveryTransaction. It is signed by the replacement device so the terminal attestation cannot be rebound to a different transaction plan even if an identifier is substituted.

prepared_plan_digest.description: Digest of the closed typed prepared_plan stored by the RecoveryTransaction. It MUST equal transaction.prepared_plan_digest and is signed to prevent substituting different prepared bytes under the same reserved ids.

account_id.description: Exact recovered AccountId. The replacement-device method proves only its principal projection; the accepted recovery session and device authorization independently bind this complete account, including station_id.

recovery_session_id.description: Stable session identifier used by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof, and MLS Welcome replay during this recovery. A byte-identical resubmission of an already accepted receipt is idempotent and MUST return the stored receipt; only a SECOND, DIFFERENT receipt for the same session id and exact account is a conflict. Rejecting the byte-identical replay would make a lost response unrecoverable, which zh/identity/security-transactions.md section 1 invariants 3 and 4 forbid.

recovery_authority_kind.description: did_root is valid only when the accepted PCR policy explicitly enabled that optional factor.

previous_model_generation_ref.description: PCR device generation snapshotted at recovery-session creation.

new_model_generation_ref.description: Accepted monotonic PCR device generation after completion.

proof_digest.description: Canonical-JSON digest of the proof transcript used to satisfy the active recovery policy. Auditors recompute against the originating proof event to verify.

quorum_participant_count.description: Required for device_quorum; equals the number of distinct participating member devices.

welcome_count.description: Number of MLS Welcomes successfully replayed for the recovering device.

outcome_reason_code.description: Free-form reason code; MUST be present when outcome != 'completed'.

completed_at.description: Authoring time at which the replacement device signed 'complete this recovery if every check passes'. It is not proof that anything was committed. The durable, linearized commit time is the completed_at of the paired ak.schema.recovery_completion_attestation.v1, which MUST NOT be earlier than this value.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the new_device_id device key frozen by the recovery session and authorized by the recovery unit of this same transaction. Receivers MUST resolve it through the principal control stream and verify that the paired completion attestation reports the accepted ak.device.authorize; service keys and unrelated fresh-device keys MUST NOT sign a recovery_receipt.

signature_algorithm.description: v1 fixes the recovery-strand replacement device possession proof to Ed25519 (zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md sections 5.2 and 14; transaction binding in zh/identity/security-transactions.md section 2). The three-algorithm set in zh/identity/key-management.md section 7.9 belongs to recovery_policy.method signing entries.alg and MUST NOT be reused as a reason to widen this one.

signature.description: base64url signature over UTF8('ak.identity.recovery_receipt.signature.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of all present top-level receipt members except signature_proof. The closed receipt shape fixes the projection; absent optional members are omitted and every present optional member is authenticated.

contract.description: Wire contract for the device recovery session state machine. The root object is the recovery session state shape; request body/result helper shapes and kind-specific recovery proof transcripts live in $defs. Completion is owned by the bound RecoveryTransaction; see zh/identity/security-transactions.md §2 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.

challenge.description: base64url(no padding) encoding of 256 bits from a CSPRNG. The value is single-use and bound to one recovery_session_id.

identity_model.description: The v1 base recovery model: an accepted PCR recovery policy directly authorizes the next device generation. Current DID control is not implicit.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that satisfied this session.

publication_authority_context.description: Server-snapshotted PCR recovery authority evaluated by the current governance Station.

session_grant_id.description: Exact recovery_session grant that created and owns this session.

session_grant_cnf_jkt.description: Exact cnf.jkt of session_grant_id. All subsequent recovery requests and proof transcripts must use the same DPoP key.

account_id.description: Exact account authority pair frozen for the session lifetime. station_id MUST equal the authenticated server serving this recovery session.

current_device_generation_ref.description: Reducer-managed PCR device generation snapshotted at session creation.

publication_authority_context_digest.description: SHA-256 of JCS(publication_authority_context). Recovery proof transcripts and RecoveryTransaction session snapshots bind this exact digest.

transaction_id.description: Unique durable RecoveryTransaction bound by CAS after verification. Absent until transaction create succeeds.

rejection_reason_code.description: Closed enum. proof_failed: proof verification failures reached the server policy limit; operator_rejected: explicit operator/admin rejection; risk_policy: server risk policy rejection; superseded: replaced by a newer recovery session for the same principal/device.

expires_at.description: Session expiration. Default TTL is 900 seconds; deployments MAY shorten it and MUST NOT lengthen it unless a future recovery_policy field explicitly permits the override.

created_at.description: Recovery session creation/signing time. This is the created_at value used in the recovery proof transcript.

request_id.description: Client-stable idempotency identity. The server binds it to the presented recovery_session grant id, cnf.jkt and canonical create intent; same identity with different intent fails duplicate_conflict.

account_id.description: Required exact authority selector. The receiving server MUST require station_id to equal its own service DID and select the single lifetime PCR lineage by the complete pair; an unknown or mismatched pair fails closed.

requesting_device_signature.description: Ed25519 proof of possession, base64url without padding. Signs UTF8(ak.identity.recovery_device_possession.v1 plus LF) concatenated with JCS(recovery_device_possession_transcript); the authenticated grant supplies session_grant_id and session_grant_cnf_jkt.

expected_recovery_policy_ref.description: Optional client CAS hint. Servers MUST snapshot the currently accepted policy; if this hint is present and differs, the request fails with recovery_policy_mismatch.

challenge.description: Echo of the server-issued session challenge. Mismatch fails as recovery_session_challenge_mismatch.

verification_method.description: Current DID-root verification method, accepted only when the frozen PCR recovery policy explicitly enables this revocable factor.
Sole recovery signing-key selector. It MUST uniquely and exactly match one in-window, non-revoked recovery_unlock key entry in the session's frozen accepted policy/version.

proof.description: Kind-specific recovery proof. Receivers reconstruct the canonical transcript from stored session state and the proof body, then verify that the active recovery policy allows this proof kind and that the proof satisfies that entry exactly.

recovery_session_proof_submit_response_b.description: Success outcome of ak.root.identity.recovery_session.command.submit_proof.v1. A 2xx reply means the proof verified and the session entered state=verified; a proof that does not verify is an error reply, so no state member is echoed.

model_generation_ref.description: Accepted PCR generation fenced by this recovery. DID method versioning is orthogonal.

created_at.description: Session creation/signing time, not client proof creation time.

recovery_unlock_proof_body.description: Signature-independent recovery_unlock projection. Only signature is deleted, never replaced by null, before transcript canonicalization; verification_method remains the exact frozen-policy key selector.

verification_method.description: Sole recovery signing-key selector, bound by the transcript signature and resolved only in the session's frozen accepted policy/version.

device_quorum_proof_body.description: Signature-independent device_quorum projection. Each nested signature member is deleted while its device, key and algorithm coordinates remain bound.

trusted_recovery_service_proof_body.description: Signature-independent trusted_recovery_service projection. Only the carrier signature is deleted.

generic_recovery_transcript.description: Canonical transcript field set shared by recovery_unlock, device_quorum and trusted_recovery_service proofs before adding kind-specific proof_body. Producers and receivers MUST bind exactly this session tuple.

model_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic device generation accepted for this recovery session; it is never a DID method versionId.

proof_body.description: Closed signature-independent projection selected by kind. Carrier signatures and commitments identified by the selected branch are deleted before canonicalization.

requesting_device_public_key_did.description: Canonical fragmentless did:key carrying the replacement Ed25519 device identity public key. This exact value, not the DPoP grant-binding key, is frozen before factor verification and must equal replacement authorize device_public_key_did. The multicodec and 32-byte key must validate; other key kinds fail closed.

recovery_device_possession_transcript.description: Closed create-time replacement identity-key PoP transcript. Grant id/JKT come from authenticated recovery_session credentials. expected_recovery_policy_ref is included exactly when the create request includes it; absent is not null. No signature, recovery_session_id or server-issued challenge is present because this proof precedes session creation.

request_id.description: Client-stable idempotency identity. The server binds it to the presented recovery_session grant id, cnf.jkt and canonical create intent; same identity with different intent fails duplicate_conflict.

account_id.description: Required exact authority selector. The receiving server MUST require station_id to equal its own service DID and select the single lifetime PCR lineage by the complete pair; an unknown or mismatched pair fails closed.

expected_recovery_policy_ref.description: Optional client CAS hint. Servers MUST snapshot the currently accepted policy; if this hint is present and differs, the request fails with recovery_policy_mismatch.

contract.description: Account-onboarding historical DID evidence retained inside the Station account/PCR boundary. It is not federated signer-key evidence and does not identify an external principal account-local lineage.

registration_did_evidence_draft.description: Client-authored historical DID evidence before Account Authority acceptance. control_proof signs canonical_json({context:'ak.registration_did_evidence_control_proof.v1',principal_id,did,adapter_version,method_history_head,version_id,control_key_digest,method_evidence_digest,verification_method,created_at}); method_evidence_digest is sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of method_evidence. accepted_at is deliberately absent: the Account Authority adds it only after the exact did_operation has been accepted by the registry. For published_identity the same draft binds evidence re-derived from the complete terminal anchor, including every applicable witness proof; its completion adds validated_at instead of accepted_at. Signing and verification cannot be restricted to seq=1 or an empty witness set.

registration_did_evidence.description: Account-Authority-accepted form of registration_did_evidence_draft. accepted_at records the trusted registry's own original acceptance time for the exact did_operation and is not retroactively inserted into the client signature, while control_proof.created_at records the instant the proof signer committed inside its own signature. The two timestamps come from independent Authority clocks and establish no dependable causal order, so verifiers MUST NOT accept or reject this evidence by comparing them numerically. The pcr_genesis_unit receipt commits the canonical digest of this complete object.

control_proof.description: Registration control signature whose transcript digest is committed by the pcr_genesis_unit receipt.

published_registration_did_evidence.description: Historical evidence for complete published-DID registration. validated_at is the designated fact owner durable first acceptance time for this exact current-validated registration evidence, retained by the Account Authority through an authenticated exact result. It is not DID publication time, versionTime or a registry receipt. No accepted_at member is permitted. Replay preserves validated_at and the original draft signature. Full evidence digest is committed by PCR genesis acceptance.

control_proof.description: Registration control signature whose transcript digest is committed by the pcr_genesis_unit receipt.

accepted_registration_did_evidence.description: Closed complete historical registration evidence, discriminated by accepted_at for new registry publication or validated_at for existing-DID validation. Exactly one branch, never caller-authored timing.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional intra-Realm Circle (models/circle.md) defining this Relation fact's effective scope, supplied in the submit payload. For confidential_discussion_of it points to the private Strand's Circle. For structural relations the resulting effective_scope MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope (circle.md §6.1). Sidecar context mappings are native sidecar.context typed results, not Relation objects.

effective_scope.description: Read-only immutable effective scope of this Relation fact, materialized from the accepted Event.scope_ref after the receiver verifies it against scope_circle_id and endpoint pre-state (circle.md §6.1-§6.2). For structural relations it MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope. It remains immutable across any later scope rebind and MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied content payload (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).

relation_kind.description: Relation semantic. The standard kind vocabulary (kind list, cardinality class, truth-source class, weak_semantic flag) is machine-indexed in artifacts/registry/relation-kind-registry.json; detailed dedupe/scope/conflict semantics in models/relation.md §3-§6. Cross-Realm constraint: the current governance Station's authoritative reducer MUST resolve both endpoints and reject structural relations 'contains' and 'belongs_to' when either endpoint realm differs from this Relation realm, with failed_precondition reason cross_realm_structural_relation and zero commit/projection effect; producer or SDK prechecks are non-authoritative. weak_semantic=true kinds per the registry MAY cross Realm subject to two-sided authorization. Stays a free string so extension profiles can add kinds; unregistered kinds are opaque edges (unknown_relation_kind), never container/visibility semantics.

rank.description: Top-level rank string for ordered relations (e.g. contains-list-strand position). Encoding follows the ak.rank.lexofractional.v1 grammar in zh/conformance/encoding.md section 9.1. Aligned with Space.rank so all rank-bearing canonical objects expose rank at the top level instead of fields.rank.

fields.description: Edge metadata. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key — rank moved to the top level in v1 to align with Space.rank.

state.description: Relation state. 'tombstoned' covers both deletion and redaction; the originating reason is preserved on the ak.relation.tombstone / ak.redaction event, not on the materialized object.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.relation.tombstone / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

object_ref.description: Typed canonical object reference. Allowed kinds: realm, space, actor_profile, strand, message, morph, relation, event, view, blob metadata ID and content-addressed blob ref (sha256 / blake3). Actor endpoints use the structured ActorId branch of relation_endpoint, never a DID or serialized JSON string.

relation_endpoint.description: A typed object-reference string or a structured full ActorId. Equality and deduplication preserve the complete ActorId including Station. This branch represents an actor.

relation_primary_conflict_domain.description: The unique current-state subject for one directly writable Relation domain. Realm comes from the Event envelope and Circle is not a key component. domain_kind MUST equal the matching relation-kind-registry.json shape's registered primary_conflict_domain: tuple keys on (relation_kind, from_ref, to_ref), while from keys on (relation_kind, from_ref). truth_source shapes have no directly writable Relation domain.

relation_kind.description: The current Relation's create-locked relation_kind. It MUST resolve to a directly writable relation-kind-registry.json shape whose registered primary_conflict_domain equals domain_kind; a derived_projection shape is rejected with schema_violation (reason=relation_kind_contains_derived / relation_kind_watches_derived).

to_ref.description: Present exactly when domain_kind=tuple. A from domain already identifies the single current Relation for the from_ref, so carrying to_ref there would create a second spelling of the subject.

relation_definition.description: The author-editable Relation definition: the edge itself and its metadata, and nothing else. It is deliberately NOT relation.schema.json. A materialized object schema used as an authoring input hands the author the schema identifier, the Realm binding, the creation metadata, the most-recent-update metadata and the lifecycle state -- the create-locked members every later write retains verbatim, so a self-reported creator or a Realm the Event was never committed into becomes permanent truth. The old relation_create_object banned only id, type and effective_scope and left the rest to a prose sentence asking semantic validation to cross-check created_by and created_at against the envelope; a prose cross-check is not a gate, and there is nothing left to cross-check once the reducer is the only writer. Those members now come from the registered create-lock derivations of zh/models/common-fields.md section 3.3, and the lifecycle state from object_initial_state. `type` stays absent because the object kind comes from the typed-id prefix, `id` because it is derived from the create Event's own event_id, and `effective_scope` because it is the reducer-materialized projection of the verified Event.scope_ref (zh/models/circle.md section 6.2).

scope_circle_id.description: Optional intra-Realm Circle (models/circle.md) defining this Relation fact's effective scope, supplied in the submit payload. For confidential_discussion_of it points to the private Strand's Circle. For structural relations the resulting effective_scope MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope (circle.md §6.1). Sidecar context mappings are native sidecar.context typed results, not Relation objects.

relation_kind.description: Relation semantic. The standard kind vocabulary (kind list, cardinality class, truth-source class, weak_semantic flag) is machine-indexed in artifacts/registry/relation-kind-registry.json; detailed dedupe/scope/conflict semantics in models/relation.md §3-§6. Cross-Realm constraint: structural relations 'contains' and 'belongs_to' MUST NOT cross Realm (resolved from_ref and to_ref MUST share the same realm_id); weak_semantic=true kinds per the registry MAY cross Realm subject to two-sided authorization. Stays a free string so extension profiles can add kinds; unregistered kinds are opaque edges (unknown_relation_kind), never container/visibility semantics.

rank.description: Top-level rank string for ordered relations (e.g. contains-list-strand position). Encoding follows the ak.rank.lexofractional.v1 grammar in zh/conformance/encoding.md section 9.1. Aligned with Space.rank so all rank-bearing canonical objects expose rank at the top level instead of fields.rank.

fields.description: Edge metadata. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key — rank moved to the top level in v1 to align with Space.rank.

object_ref.description: Canonical object reference. Acceptable typed-id kinds match the v1 resource selector kind enum (see resource-selector-grammar.md §3.1). Notably MUST NOT include 'actor_profile' (use the 'actor' selector with did pattern), nor non-canonical 'board' / 'list' / 'card' / 'subject' / 'room' kinds — board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket are Space objects and MUST use the 'space' kind together with the 'allowed_space_kinds' constraint to restrict which Space kinds the grant covers.

actor_id.description: Concrete principal / service / agent did_core_id. v1 forbids actor:*; actor selectors MUST NOT use a wildcard subject.

match_scope.description: Authorization selector breadth. exact matches only the named resource; realm_wide is valid only for the registered resource kinds with an explicit realm_id. Neither current navigation ancestry nor creation ancestry expands authorization. Hierarchy traversal belongs to queries, not grant matching. The normative algorithm is zh/authz/resource-selector-grammar.md section 6.

contract.description: Signed, artifact-bound SDK release claim. The proof covers RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the object with proof omitted, prefixed by the UTF-8 domain separator arkret-sdk-conformance-claim-v1 followed by LF.

build_variants.description: Optional per-build profile inventory for source or multi-variant SDK distributions. Each complete features/configuration inventory is covered by the claim proof and the existing AK-SDK-015 build_variant_inventory digest. Variant IDs MUST be unique; no separate per-feature digest is carried.

features.description: Complete enabled feature names, sorted in strictly increasing ASCII order. An empty array explicitly represents no enabled optional features.

configuration.description: Complete non-secret behavior-affecting build configuration, including target, compiler/toolchain, profile, default-feature policy and relevant flags. Keys are tool-qualified stable names, values are exact canonical build inputs. Defaults MUST be expanded. Secrets MUST NOT be included. The publisher MUST fail closed if the inventory cannot reproduce the claimed configuration.

covers_vectors.description: Exact conformance vector ids this run produced results for. REQUIRED when kind is vector_result; the verifier checks the union against the clause's expanded vector_evidence.vectors and its decision_points.

evidence.description: One evidence reference. A vector_result entry MUST name the exact vectors it covers; the other kinds MUST NOT carry covers_vectors.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

contract.description: Closed Station-local durable RecoveryTransaction and SecurityRotationTransaction resource. The prepared plan is the sole canonical intent source; accepted outputs form a durable ordered prefix. account_id is the exact account owner; the coordinator role is account_id.station_id, the service core identity of the executing Station, and no separate coordinator field exists on wire. Every prepared Event and backup ActorId must equal this account actor.

account_id.description: Exact account owner. Its station_id is the coordinator: the service core identity of the executing Station, not an arbitrary external coordinator. Process separation is deployment-private and creates no public coordinator role.

authorizing_device_id.description: SecurityRotation only. Exact device from the fresh high-risk authenticated create session. The coordinator binds it to that session and persists it before any side effect; the worker rechecks that the account and this device are still active immediately before old-material erasure.

prepared_plan_digest.description: SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(prepared_plan)). Implementations MUST recompute it and persist both bytes and typed value before the first side effect. This cross-service CAS coordinate is fixed independently of any domain-selectable Blob or KDF digest suite.

accepted_steps.description: Durable accepted prefix. Entry i has the step kind at index i of the fixed order selected by kind; entries never carry a duplicate step label.

revoke_proposal.description: SecurityRotation only. Immutable exact PCR proposal Event/Commit binding, persisted when that accepted proposal becomes visible.

revoke_command_outcome.description: SecurityRotation only. Immutable Station-local decision for the exact accepted revoke proposal; absence is pending only while the authoritative transaction and result ledger are complete at the read cut.

accepted_step.description: Accepted position in the kind-specific fixed step order. The index determines the step; execution evidence is verified against the typed plan and durable outcomes, never inferred from reserved IDs or digests alone.

new_backup_envelopes.description: Complete signed KeyBackup envelopes in canonical ascending backup_id order, with distinct IDs. Each envelope's backup_id and ciphertext_digest MUST equal the corresponding binding.new_backups entry; signatures and ciphertext digests MUST be verified.

output_ref.description: Exact echo of prepared_plan.binding.terminal_receipt_id for commit_recovery_unit or prepared_plan.local_commit_digest for local_commit. The verifier MUST compare the value against the selected transaction's closed plan.

verification_method.description: Canonical current Account DID URL with fragment #<device_id>. The verifier resolves the device's authorized signing key, generation, revocation and pending state at the same accepted PCR cut and binds the device and artifact exactly.

signature.description: base64url signature over RFC 8785 JCS of the fixed projection {step,output_ref,transaction_id,transaction_request_digest,prepared_plan_digest,attestation_digest}. attestation_digest is not a wire field: the signer and the verifier each recompute it as SHA-256(JCS(artifact)) from the typed artifact carried in this object and fill it into the projection, so artifact is authenticated transitively and is not duplicated in the outer projection. For commit_recovery_unit the artifact is the complete recovery receipt; this outer signature authenticates that receipt and never contains, signs or precomputes a RealmCommit.

security_transaction_continue_request_bo.description: Submits the client-attested terminal step only. The resource-aware validator derives the next step from transaction kind and accepted prefix, accepts recovery index 0 or security-rotation index 4 only when that terminal step is ready, and rejects every coordinator-owned prefix with failed_precondition. Coordinator-owned steps are executed and recovered by the durable worker, never driven by this request. Recovery has no coordinator-owned prefix: commit_recovery_unit is its single step; its client artifact carries only the recovery receipt, while the governance Station issues the two PCR-stream RealmCommits inside the atomic admission.

expected_accepted_step_count.description: CAS coordinate. It MUST equal the current accepted_steps length. The schema intentionally has no kind-blind maximum or {0,4} coupling; the service resolves the transaction resource, derives the next fixed step, and accepts only a terminal-ready index.

prepared_event_unit.description: Exact typed Event submit request plus its suite-bearing canonical digest. Operation, request schema, destination and audience are fixed by this unit type and the parent account_id.station_id; canonical request bytes are RFC 8785 JCS(request), not a second wire input. A PCR recovery unit contains exactly reanchor plus replacement authorize for the same account-local lineage/session/sequenced revision guard. Both producer proofs use the same session-frozen replacement key resolved through the unit-local candidate possession overlay before mutation; they cannot be submitted or replayed outside the complete recovery unit. Current human DID or device-directory resolution cannot authorize either slot.

request.description: Exact nested two-Event recovery unit shape. The parent security transaction fixes its operation, slot order and authority; this array is not an ordinary self Event-submit batch.

recovery_create_request_body.description: Closed typed recovery intent. The caller states what it wants recovered and supplies the two complete signed Events, the exact current PCR-stream predecessor and their ordered digests; it never supplies a finished prepared_plan or a RealmCommit. The Station derives the snapshots and every reserved id inside its own durable prepare transaction, which produces no recovery effect.

pcr_policy_recovery_intent.description: Caller-authored recovery intent fixing the verified recovery session, replacement device, generation CAS, terminal receipt id, two exact signed producer Events, current PCR stream head and their ordered digests. It contains no Station-signed RealmCommit.

recovery_commit_intent.description: Closed authority-commit expectation for the PCR stream. predecessor_ref is the exact current stream head and unit_event_digests fixes the two producer Events that the governance Station must commit atomically after all recovery checks succeed.

predecessor_ref.description: Exact current RealmCommit id of the Principal Control Realm stream; genesis-null is invalid.

unit_event_digests.description: Exactly [reanchor_digest, authorize_digest] in RealmCommit event order.

recovery_terminal_commit.description: Sole client-attested terminal artifact of a RecoveryTransaction. It carries the exact replacement-device-signed recovery receipt. The governance Station validates it and the two prepared producer Events, then atomically issues their two consecutive PCR-stream RealmCommits; the client artifact never contains or signs either authority record.

recovery_receipt.description: Complete replacement-device-signed recovery receipt binding the transaction, plan, both producer Event ids, generation CAS and recovery proof snapshot.

pcr_policy_accepted_steps.description: Accepted prefix for the canonical pcr_policy step order declared by pcr_policy_recovery_step. PCR-policy recovery has exactly one accepted step, the client-attested commit_recovery_unit terminal commit. The recovery unit stays transaction-private prepared material until that commit, so no coordinator-owned prefix entry exists.

pcr_policy_recovery_binding.description: Reserved producer identities of one RecoveryTransaction. The replacement-device-signed Event ids and terminal receipt id are frozen before admission; the resulting RealmCommit is created only by the governance Station during the atomic terminal step.

pcr_policy_recovery_plan.description: Station-derived closed plan frozen with the canonical request in a durable prepare transaction that produces no accepted Event, RealmCommit, generation advance, active device, consumed session or terminal result.

reanchor_commit_intent.description: Exact caller-stated PCR stream head and ordered Event digests; it MUST equal the create request recovery_intent.reanchor_commit_intent byte for byte.

pcr_policy_recovery_step.description: The enum array order is the canonical PCR-policy recovery step order addressed by accepted_steps indexes. PCR-policy recovery has a single client-attested step at index 0: the Station prepare transaction that freezes the plan belongs to create, not to the accepted-step ledger, so no coordinator-owned prefix precedes the terminal commit.

security_rotation_accepted_steps.description: Accepted prefix for the canonical rotation step order declared by security_rotation_step.

authorizing_device_id.description: Must equal the device in the fresh high-risk authenticated create session; caller text alone is not authoritative.

security_rotation_local_commit.description: Client-authored terminal artifact. The device copies transaction_id, transaction_request_digest and prepared_plan_digest from the authoritative SecurityTransaction resource, copies local_commit_digest from its closed prepared_plan, and supplies its own device_id and canonical committed_at. No server-issued signed artifact or separate supply operation exists; the enclosing client_step_attestation authenticates this complete object.

backup_rotations.description: The single secret_storage entry; its nested binding is the sole source of the reserved series and object references.

erase_confirmation_digest.description: Must equal the non-circular projection digest over transaction_id and this plan's nested backup rotation bindings.

local_commit_digest.description: Must equal the non-circular projection digest over transaction_id, new_secret_commitment and this plan's nested backup rotation bindings.

security_rotation_step.description: The enum array order is the canonical security-rotation step order addressed by accepted_steps indexes.

contract.description: Canonical role-scoped ServiceDescribe response. Runtime operation availability is the union of registered supported_operation_bundles intersected with usable transport_bindings; supported_features is the sole feature claim set. Profile claims remain conformance evidence and never add operations. Exact source-tree, generated-registry, SDK, service-build, or release-artifact fingerprints are not compatibility carriers and MUST remain outside this document and all protocol decisions.

service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the service making this describe claim. It cannot be resolved without service_resolution or another verified AuthenticatedServiceResolution.

service_resolution.description: Read-only current did commitment for this service role. Describe is a second-hop endpoint confirmation surface, not a did_core_id resolver: callers already need a candidate URL before fetching it and MUST verify the did projection, method evidence and endpoint reverse binding before updating a route cache.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain for this service. Receivers use it as the canonical receive-context replay boundary for cross-deployment proofs and federation transactions.

service_kind.description: One logical role this service plays on the wire. Each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role; co-located roles sharing a public binding use separate role-scoped responses selected by GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>. The value space is registry/service-kind-registry.json filtered to active rows whose valid_in contains service_describe.

protocol_version.description: Arkret protocol-family bootstrap discriminator. A consumer first extracts this field before applying the version-specific ServiceDescribe schema: a well-formed value other than 1.0 yields unsupported_protocol_version, while missing or non-string values yield schema_violation. The const keeps an object admitted as ak.schema.service_describe.v1 closed to Arkret/1.

supported_profiles.description: The sole complete-profile self-declaration for this exact build and role endpoint. Every declared profile MUST satisfy its full applicable contract. Feature-only support belongs in supported_features. verified_profiles supplies independent evidence, never an alternate activation set; each verified profile MUST also occur here.

profile_bindings.description: Profile-specific carrier declarations keyed by profile id. A profile that mandates one interoperable private carrier must bind it here rather than relying on a product-local route.

supported_features.description: Canonical-sorted exact registered feature ids this role endpoint currently supports. This is the sole public runtime feature claim set.

calendar_tzdb_versions.description: IANA TZDB release tags this service can execute for calendar schedules, taken from calendar-timezone-registry.json. Required when the service claims a calendar profile. A schedule whose signed tzdb_version is absent here MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or project its instants as unresolved; the service MUST NOT fall back to a nearby or newer release.

authentication_metadata.description: Authentication and session metadata needed by clients before calling protected operations. Unregistered keys are limited to safely ignorable x_* metadata.

methods.description: Authentication methods offered for this principal/account surface. Methods describe proof providers, standard discovery, and the proof kind accepted by the Account Authority. Arkret gate/account routing is always derived from account_authority.

did_binding_methods.description: session_dpop is the mandatory default SessionGrant presentation; session_http_signature is only an additional high-security body/transcript binding layer. did_http_signature denotes separately registered DID proofs and is never a SessionGrant fallback.

limits.description: Operational limits such as body size, batch size, TTL, pagination or retention bounds.

plaintext_visibility.description: Plaintext boundary declaration. Omission is not allowed: callers use this object to decide whether the service may be registered as plaintext-visible. An empty object means the service claims no plaintext classes; Realm plaintext_visible_services entries MUST match non-empty data_classes here.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service is implemented to receive.

max_visibility.description: Maximum plaintext visibility class the service claims it can receive. Omitted is treated as none unless data_classes is non-empty.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound for subject-private invite/contact receive policies. Stations SHOULD expose this in describe so clients can show which user reachability preferences are capped by server policy.

rate_limit_policy_id.description: Identifier for a cacheable, verifiable rate-limit policy object with the same minimum fields as rate_limit_policy. See zh/sync/api-conventions.md §8.

rate_limit_policy.description: Inline rate-limit policy. If the service can return rate_limited, entries[] MUST expose at least endpoint or operation_id, rate_limit_scope, a window/limit tuple or a retry hint; an empty entries[] explicitly means no predictable endpoint-level rate limit beyond generic abuse protection.

endpoint.description: Closed endpoint selector: either an absolute HTTP(S) URL or an absolute-path endpoint on this service.

egress_network_policy.description: Coarse outbound-network policy for SSRF protection. Public describe MAY omit sensitive allowlist entries; authenticated operator describe MAY return the complete policy. Normative semantics are defined in zh/sync/api-conventions.md §11.2.

resource_kinds.description: Directory-service resource classes indexed by ak.find.directory.read.describe.v1. Required when service_kind=directory_service.

verified_profiles.description: Profiles for which a Conformance Verifier run (conformance-suite.md §6.2) has produced a passing verification artifact. Each entry MUST identify the verification run, artifact hash, artifact retrieval reference, verifier DID, verifier signature, and verification timestamp. When the service is in `development_mode=true` this array MUST be empty. Each profile_id MUST occur in supported_profiles and be unique within verified_profiles; consumers MUST verify this relationship and applicable artifact evidence before displaying a verified badge. Evidence alone MUST NOT activate a profile.

artifact_ref.description: URI or transparency-log reference from which the verification artifact can be fetched.

verifier_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Conformance Verifier that signed the artifact statement. The artifact's DID URL signing key is verified separately and its canonical bare did MUST project through the registered adapter to this value.

signature.description: Signature over profile_id, verification_run_id, artifact_digest, artifact_ref, verifier and timestamp.

interop_surfaces.description: Surfaces this service exposes outside its claimed Arkret v1 conformance: bridged third-party protocols and delegated resolver postures. A service MUST NOT declare its own product-private route root here — a private API is neither a bridged foreign protocol nor a delegation, and declaring one would grant it a conformance-adjacent standing it does not have. The object is closed so such a declaration cannot be smuggled in through extension keys.

kind.description: matrix_passthrough / mimi_passthrough: bridged foreign protocol surface. delegated_resolver: a DID document / key-log surface served on behalf of a canonical authority this service does not claim to be (conformance-profiles.md §9). external_interop: any other non-Arkret interop surface. This list is exhaustive; product-private APIs have no member here.

development_mode.description: Mirror of the service's development_mode flag. When true, `verified_profiles` MUST be empty.

supported_operation_bundles.description: Canonical-sorted registered bundle ids this role endpoint fully implements. The local registry expands each id to exact (operation_id,binding_kind) pairs; unknown ids never grant availability.

transport_bindings.description: Transport endpoints in descending server preference. Operation coverage is not repeated here and comes only from supported_operation_bundles.

invite_addressing.description: Registered invite-addressing negotiation. Required when ak.feature.invite_addressing.v1 is advertised.

cidr.description: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR string. Parsability and address-family semantics are enforced by the egress policy evaluator.

origin.description: Absolute origin of the client-visible Account Authority.

gate_account_base_url.description: Absolute base URL from which all client-visible /_arkret/gate/account/* endpoints MUST be derived.

kind.description: Every advertised interactive authentication method terminates in the AccountHandoff exchange. For OIDC, authentication-handoffs is the unique authorization-code consumer; SessionGrant issue never consumes the code.

transport_binding_websocket.description: WebSocket transport descriptor. kind=websocket fixes the required binding profile ak.profile.binding.websocket.v1, the arkret.v1 subprotocol and the challenge_dpop_session_v1 authentication through binding-kind-registry and the profile itself; the descriptor carries only the connection coordinates and transport limits.

contract.description: Verifiable disaster-recovery bundle for one service DID. Private key bytes are never carried; key references resolve through the configured key backend.

identity.description: Stored service identity, DID document and current registration receipt. Consumers must verify their cross-bindings before restore.

contract.description: Canonical DTOs reachable from current authority-commit operations. Every definition is part of the current operation closure.

StrandWatchCurrentRequestBody.description: Exact own-account watch selector shared by the self and authenticated peer current read. The complete account Actor equals the authenticated self effective Actor, or is asserted by its own Account Station whose identity equals account_id.station_id. Service actors and other-account requests have no read authority. It cannot enumerate watchers or supply an expected CAS value. Authorization and delivery follow strand-and-message section 8.3.1.

StrandWatchCurrentResponseBody.description: One governing durable cut shared by self and peer. Affirmative never_written requires complete accepted watch provenance, including a fully verified handoff import; a cleared null remains current with revision. Generation/head and the exact selector bind the observation, not a future write lease. Snapshot omission, generation zero and member replicas do not prove absence.

AccountCursorRevokeRequestBody.description: Revoke an immutable local cursor issuance owned by the authenticated exact account and current device. Validate the canonical token and durable binding before writing. same_session requires the exact private issuing-session identity; it is not a same_device alias. Repetition is idempotent without extending the horizon. Expired, unknown, foreign, altered and unauthorized targets produce zero writes. See client-sync sections 12.2 and 12.2.1.

revoked.description: Whether a live device session was revoked.

grant_chain_terminated.description: Whether the grant rotation chain is now unable to refresh, including the already-terminated idempotent case.

authentication_session_logged_out.description: Whether the underlying Auth-side browser/auth session is now logged out, including the already-logged-out idempotent case.

AuthenticationSessionLogoutRequestBody.description: Service-to-service Account Authority to Auth Server request that logs out the Auth-side session owning a ak.session.grant rotation chain.

grant_jwt.description: Session grant used to locate the Auth-side session and its rotation chain.

logout_request_digest.description: Optional digest of the validated client-visible account /logout request that caused this S2S sub-operation.

validated_at.description: When the Account Authority validated the client-visible account /logout request.

reason_code.description: Reason for logging out the Auth-side session. v1 defines only account_logout for this S2S sub-operation.

AuthorizationCheckResponseBody.description: ak.self.authz.read.check.v1 diagnostic/preflight decision. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §18. This response is advisory; canonical Event admission remains authoritative.

decision.description: `allow` / `hard_deny` are terminal decisions. `soft_deny` is an evaluated policy soft refusal. `quarantine` / `require_review` are local moderation outcomes. Transient dependency or freshness failures are reported through `freshness_state`, `reason_code`, and `retry_after_ms`, not as policy decision values.

freshness_state.description: Checkpoint freshness classification for revocation-sensitive decisions; see zh/authz/capabilities.md §18.2.

last_known_checkpoint_age_ms.description: Age of the newest revocation/auth checkpoint evidence used for this decision. Present when freshness_state is stale or unknown.

authority_status.description: Coarse status of the current governance Station and committed-stream source used to diagnose stale or unknown revocation freshness.

reason_code.description: Registered reason code. High-risk stale or unknown revocation freshness returns revocation_freshness_unknown.

retry_after_ms.description: Set when `freshness_state ∈ {stale,unknown}` or a retryable `reason_code` is present; client SHOULD back off this amount before retry.

obligations.description: Additional local preflight obligations the caller MUST satisfy before the action proceeds.

AuthorizationCheckRequestBody.description: ak.self.authz.read.check.v1 advisory local authorization preflight. It is never a cross-service authorization fact and cannot replace the current governance Station's admission decision.

actor_id.description: Subject did_core_id whose authorization is being checked.

resource.description: Optional resource selector (Realm / Strand / Space / Morph / etc.).

context.description: Optional decision context — claim presentations, checkpoint reference, request metadata.

url.description: Fully-qualified URL clients can pass to browser primitives. Contains the `presign` query parameter, `blob_ref`, and a presign envelope bound to `realm_id` for Realm-owned blobs.

expires_at.description: Server-determined expiry; SHOULD be earlier than `now() + max_age_seconds`.

blob_ref.description: Target blob. MUST be a content-addressed ref or visible blob metadata id.

realm_id.description: Realm binding for Realm-owned blobs. Servers MUST include the same realm_id in the presign envelope and reject mismatches with blob metadata; only deployment-public/global blobs may omit this field.

max_age_seconds.description: Client-requested TTL upper bound. Server clamps to the smaller of this value, the issuing grant's `blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds` constraint, and the deployment-level cap.

purpose.description: Intended rendering / download mode. Servers MAY apply purpose-specific Content-Disposition or rate limits.

backend_token.description: Closed branch selected by backend_kind: arkret_native uses the typed signature object; every other v1 backend uses a non-empty opaque string.

participant_id.description: SFU-local short handle, scope `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`. UUIDv7-form rtc_participant typed ID.

backend_kind.description: Backend binding type identifier (livekit / arkret_native / etc.).

media.description: Complete actual issued media range, covered by participant_binding and copied unchanged into the accepted roster.

device_id.description: Stable protocol endpoint identifier. REQUIRED for agent_key_proof and covered by request_canonical_digest; the Account Authority MUST persist and return the same value in the issued grant so Stations can bind MLS KeyPackage ownership, Welcome routing, consume/revoke operations, refresh, and restart recovery to one endpoint. It MUST NOT be derived from a session or grant id.

device_message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity copied unchanged into DeviceMessageEnvelope.device_message_id. Reusing the same sender-scoped device_message_id with different canonical target content MUST fail with duplicate_conflict (reason device_message_id_conflict).

pruned_count.description: Number of recipient deliveries acknowledged by this token: DeviceMessage rows deleted plus Welcome rows marked delivered and retained for audit; zero is legal for a repeated or older token.

acknowledgement_token.description: Acknowledgement token previously issued to the same authenticated recipient endpoint by account subscribe or the recipient-delivery list. It cumulatively prunes both DeviceMessage and MlsWelcomeDelivery queue items through the bound position, only after every covered item was durably processed. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens MUST be rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything. Naturally idempotent; no Idempotency-Key required.

deliveries.description: Ordered recipient-private queue items, each discriminated as an unchanged DeviceMessageEnvelope or MlsWelcomeDelivery. These are not shared Event Envelope objects.

acknowledgement_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever deliveries[] is non-empty. Covers both delivery kinds in this page and earlier items for the authenticated recipient endpoint. Queue deletion happens only through ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1 with this token, never through the after= read cursor (client-sync.md §10.1).

next_cursor.description: Read-only continuation position; advancing it MUST NOT delete queued messages.

lost.description: SHOULD be true only for a durably evidenced historical gap or failure since this recipient endpoint's last acknowledged position; normal expiry and capacity MUST NOT delete unacknowledged deliveries of either kind. Clients MUST re-establish MLS/key readiness when true.

delivered.description: Principal-id to device-id map for messages accepted for delivery.

unknown_devices.description: Principal-id to device-id map for recipient targets that are not deliverable. Membership alone is the whole result: unknown, revoked, fenced or otherwise undeliverable devices are indistinguishable. A sender-side invalid expires_at never lands here; it fails the whole request.

messages.description: Station-local did_core_id -> device_id map. The authenticated addressed Station supplies the AccountId Station component; this body carries no cross-Station route and MUST NOT use ActorId JSON as a key.

accepted_at.description: Stable registry decision time for this exact accepted or duplicate operation. A duplicate returns the original acceptance time.

sequence.description: New method sequence number when available.

operation_ref.description: Exact method-native immutable operation identifier. For did:webvh this is did + "?versionId=" + the submitted entry versionId. The authenticated response acknowledges the exact complete submitted operation, including proofs; accepted/duplicate MUST match the locally frozen typed request and its method-native version and sequence. A registry MUST NOT normalize or replace accepted entry bytes. A duplicate returns the original result for the same bytes.

did_method.description: DID method discriminator without the did: prefix (e.g. web, webvh, key). It MUST exactly equal the method component of did; verifiers dispatch method-specific validation only after that equality check.

sequence.description: Optional method sequence number when the DID method exposes one.

previous_event_digest.description: Optional previous operation hash / key-log head, when required by the DID method.

operation.description: Complete DID method-native operation, including every controller/update/recovery proof required by that method. This is not a generic JSON Patch. The selected adapter MUST validate the immutable native operation and its full history before any state mutation; transport authentication never substitutes for method-native control proof.

DirectConversationFoundingAuthorityEvide.description: Closed XOR authorization evidence for one Direct Conversation founding unit, matching the two registered ak.realm.create admission variants. The human branch feeds direct_conversation_genesis; the controller_agent branch feeds direct_conversation_agent_genesis. Carrying both, neither, or mixed branch fields rejects the whole unit.

contact_round_evidence.description: Current round with immutable initial identity, original establishment and two independently authenticated directional scope-instance currents. No history chain; initial identity alone does not authorize founding.

agent_provision_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted Agent provision Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel agent_provision_digest is carried.

EventDeliveryTargetState.description: Closed lifecycle for one frozen distinct Realm fanout target. Authority loss is terminal and a later rejoin never revives the old target.

EventDeliveryTargetStatus.description: Authorized projection of one frozen Realm fanout target. target_id is opaque and stable. service_id is present only when the caller can currently read at least one exact joined-member ActorId that contributed the target.

target_id.description: Service-generated opaque target identifier. It MUST NOT encode the target service DID.

EventDeliveryStatusRequestBody.description: Authenticated, non-enumerating request for the durable fanout state of one caller-visible accepted Event.

EventDeliveryStatusResponseBody.description: Complete frozen target set for one visible Event. Rows are sorted byte-wise by unique opaque target_id. Consumers derive the pending count by counting pending_route and pending_delivery rows, and derive aggregate state as pending iff that count is non-zero.

ActorPrivateEventSubmitRequestBody.description: Request of ak.self.actor_private_events.command.submit.v1: exactly one caller-signed actor-private Event of a kind that has no dedicated submit operation. The service validates the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT rebuild the payload or co-sign. No approval sidecar exists because no approval layer applies to these kinds. zh/models/actor-private-effects.md section 2.1.

ActorPrivateEventSubmitResponseBody.description: Closed outcome of ak.self.actor_private_events.command.submit.v1, discriminated by event_kind. accepted_event_id is the event_id of the accepted Event, and an exact retry returns the first stored outcome. Only ak.device.push_route carries the accepted per-route revision its next write must name as expected_server_revision. No RealmCommit exists for these writes.

EventAdmissionSubmission.description: One complete original producer-signed Event plus applicable external approval signatures. Realm actor private control admission is resolved from its owning Realm accepted state, with no foreign Account/PCR source package. No arbitrary atomic Event list.

approval_signatures.description: One ak.schema.approval_signature.v1 object per approver. An event-target signature binds approval_target.event_id equal to event.event_id. An operation-target signature is allowed only when capability-action-registry.json resolves its action to this exact carrier operation and binds request_canonical_digest to the original typed request with approval_signatures omitted. Every ingress that wraps EventAdmissionSubmission -- ordinary self submit, batch submission, control transactions, facade hand-off -- reuses this one field and MUST NOT define its own DTO. The array is omitted when no approval layer demands evidence; it MUST NOT be present and empty. The governance Station persists the evidence, the verification basis, the nonce consumption and the binding to this submission inside the same atomic acceptance transaction, and the shared Realm Event store keeps the original Event bytes unchanged.

EventSubmitEnvelope.description: Actor-supplied ak.self.events.command.submit.v1 input envelope. It reuses the complete canonical Event shape, including the required producer-signed scope_ref. Object payload schemas independently forbid actor-supplied effective_scope where that name is reserved for a read-only materialized object projection.

EventsSubmitBatchRequestBody.description: Legacy-named typed array retained only as the nested prepared_event_unit request in security-transaction.schema.json. It is not an ak.self.events.command.submit.v1 request: that operation accepts only authority-commit-operations.schema.json#/$defs/self_submit_request_body, including its closed ordinary_realm_bootstrap branch. The parent security transaction fixes the recovery unit type, slot count, order and authorization; this array alone grants no generic Event batch admission.

EffectiveCapabilityGrantView.description: One active effective capability grant and the exact revision of that same capability_grant current state, read atomically by the governing Station. This revision is the only valid authoring basis for a subject-signed ak.capability.relinquish Event; state_digest, evaluated_at, Event ids and locally folded history MUST NOT substitute for it.

EffectiveGrantSnapshot.description: Atomic subject-visible snapshot of active effective grants. Each row carries its own exact current-state revision; state_digest authenticates the list as a whole and is never a per-grant CAS operand.

state_digest.description: Digest of the complete effective-list snapshot. It MUST NOT be copied into expected_revision or otherwise treated as one grant's revision.

IdentityDocumentView.description: Result of ak.root.identity.document.resource.get.v1 — current DID Document plus normalized view hints.

did_document.description: Raw DID Core document with W3C field names preserved.

normalized_view.description:
Optional Arkret normalized principal view (snake_case) — derived
projection only, NOT a re-publishable DID Document. See
zh/identity/identity-did.md §6.

method_evidence.description: Closed adapter-discriminated proof material (e.g. did:webvh history head and canonical witness receipt). This is the registered supply surface for portable principal resolution evidence.

IdentityLogListResponseBody.description: Result of ak.root.identity.log.read.list.v1. Entries are returned in the DID method's own native log form: for did:webvh each entry is a verbatim did.jsonl log entry with its native versionId, entryHash chain and Data Integrity proof.
