Arkret defines no parallel entry envelope, sequence numbering, hash chain or proof transcript over DID logs — the method already provides all of them, and a second signed representation of the same history could disagree with the first. Methods without a native history (did:web) MUST report that rather than being wrapped in a shape that implies one.

method.description: DID method of the returned log, e.g. did:webvh. Consumers dispatch parsing and verification on this value.

native_history.description: False when the method has no native key history at all (did:web). Such a response MUST return an empty entries array; the server MUST NOT synthesise entries, sequence numbers or a chain the method does not have.

entries.description: Verbatim method-native log entries in method order. Arkret does not reinterpret, renumber or re-sign them; verification follows the method specification.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor for the next page when has_more=true.

IdentityReceiptListResponseBody.description: Result of ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list.v1. receipts[] is a tagged union over two distinct object families discriminated by their schema constant: ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1 records a role inside a DID registry consensus group (writer / witness / replica) and binds seq + accepted_entry_digest, while ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1 records a did:webvh method witness observed at a specific versionId. The two say different things with the same English word, so the discriminator is mandatory and a verifier MUST branch on it rather than infer intent from which optional fields happen to be present.

threshold_met.description: True when the returned receipt set satisfies the effective witness threshold for the requested head. The effective threshold is the strictest intersection of the method-native parameters.witness.threshold and the deployment / Realm policy minimum (identity-did.md §3.4.2), and distinctness is counted over controlling_organization_did where policy requires distinct organizations. Omitted when the registry cannot evaluate threshold policy for this query; an omitted value MUST NOT be read as true. A true value is an Arkret-layer convenience and MUST NOT replace verifying the standard did-witness.json proofs.

DidWebvhIdentityMethodEvidence.description: Method-native pins derived only after fail-closed verification of the complete did:webvh history. control_key_digest is SHA-256 over the decoded canonical multikey bytes of parameters.updateKeys[0] at version_id.

InitialSessionGrantIntent.description: Initial Standard SessionGrant intent embedded in either complete Human registration branch. It reuses the DPoP holder key established by account handoff; Account Authority recomputes RFC 7638 thumbprint of session_public_key and requires equality with the handoff/control-proof dpop_jkt. It is not a separate authorization or credential.

session_public_key.description: Exact RFC 8785 JCS public JWK for the existing handoff DPoP holder key. Private members are forbidden.

MlsGroupStateMaterialResponseBody.description: Exact RFC 9420 public group-state material. *_bytes_b64 use unpadded base64url. Consumers MUST decode each content-addressed Blob ref's embedded suite, hash the raw bytes under that suite, compare the digest, verify GroupInfo and ratchet_tree consistency, then derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified tree. Blob suites are independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite.

group_info_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

ratchet_tree_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

MlsGroupStateMaterialRequestBody.description: Read-only service request for the exact public MLS epoch-0 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. Every Genesis selector is copied from that Event. When caller_actor_id is present, target_commit_event_ref and target_epoch are mandatory; governance checks current and target-cut member/history authority and source Station replication right at the target accepted Commit cut. Without caller_actor_id this remains the original Station replication-only read, with source Station replication right checked at the Genesis Commit position.

group_info_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

ratchet_tree_ref.description: Copied byte-for-byte from the accepted ak.mls.genesis payload; the embedded Blob digest suite is the sole wire carrier of the material digest and is independent of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite (encoding.md 4.0.1).

routed_to_ids.description: Stable core_ids selected as moderation routing destinations. MUST be omitted for an ordinary reporter and MAY be serialized only when the caller independently holds moderation/governance capability for the report's exact scope. Endpoint discovery and DID verification remain separate resolution steps.

OrganizationControlProof.description: Method-native proof that the caller controls the external Organization DID at the pinned version. proof_kind is a closed discriminator with exactly two members, both of which describe a MATURE, already-published DID. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception / governance ceremony and deliberately has no member here: a receiver must never have to guess whether a proof asserts control of existing state or creation of new state. This object never carries an Arkret-issued challenge signature in place of method-native control evidence.

proof_kind.description: resolved_verification_method: a single signature by a verification method that is in the organization DID's control relationship at version_id. governance_quorum: a threshold of signatures from the organization's governance key set. Witness attestation is neither of these and MUST NOT be substituted for control evidence (identity-did.md §8.1).

quorum_threshold.description: Required when proof_kind=governance_quorum and forbidden otherwise. The number of distinct valid governance signatures the organization's own policy demands. proofs[] MUST contain at least this many entries signed by distinct verification methods; JSON Schema cannot compare the two, so the receiver MUST enforce it and fail closed when short.

proofs.description: Detached proofs over canonical_json({context:'ak.organization_registration_control_proof.v1', challenge_id, organization_id, organization_did, local_admin_subject, version_id, log_head_digest, verification_method, created_at}). The verifier independently validates the published organization_did and requires project(organization_did)=organization_id before checking the DID URL verification_method. Binding the challenge, stable core, DID, beneficiary admin and exact version together prevents replay across deployments, resolutions or beneficiaries.

OrganizationRegistrationChallenge.description: Single-use control challenge. Every binding field exists to close one replay path: purpose separates this proof from any other signature the organization makes, audience and trust_domain pin it to this deployment, origin pins the HTTP surface, nonce makes it unrepeatable, and the expiry window bounds how long a captured proof stays useful. A registry MUST consume the challenge on the first successful use and atomically persist (challenge_id, canonical_request_digest, outcome). Only a byte-identical retry may return that stored outcome; the same challenge with any different digest is invalid.

organization_did.description: Current published bare DID for the external organization. The registry MUST independently validate it and require the registered method adapter to project it to organization_id before issuing the challenge.

purpose.description: Fixed purpose tag, identical to the signing context of OrganizationControlProof.proofs[]. A proof produced for any other purpose MUST NOT verify here.

audience_id.description: Stable service did_core_id of the issuing registry. A proof bound to one registry MUST NOT be accepted by another; the proof verification method remains a DID URL projected to this value by the registered method adapter.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes will be delegated to. It is fixed at challenge time and signed over by the control proof, because a proof that binds only the organization and the version says nothing about who benefits from it: anyone who obtained such a proof could submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. ensure MUST reject a request whose local_admin_subject differs from the one in the referenced challenge.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after created_at. A longer window buys nothing and widens the interval in which a captured proof remains usable.

OrganizationRegistrationChallengeRequest.description: Request a single-use control challenge for an external Organization DID. Two phases are mandatory: the registry issues the challenge and remembers it, then the caller proves control against it. Folding this into ensure would let the caller supply its own challenge, at which point neither freshness nor single use can be established by the receiver.

organization_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the external Organization to be registered. Resolvability alone confers nothing; this request only opens a proof window.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID submitted for first registration. The registry MUST independently resolve and validate it and require project(organization_did)=organization_id.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes will be delegated to. It is fixed at challenge time and signed over by the control proof, because a proof that binds only the organization and the version says nothing about who benefits from it: anyone who obtained such a proof could submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. ensure MUST reject a request whose local_admin_subject differs from the one in the referenced challenge.

OrganizationRegistrationEnsureRequestBod.description: Register an external Organization identity with this deployment by submitting both its stable organization_id core and current published organization_did. Idempotent on organization_id: replaying the same registration returns the existing binding with created=false. This operation registers a reference and a local administrative binding; it does not host the DID's method history, does not make this deployment its controller, and does not create Realm state.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID whose method history and control proof are pinned by this request. MUST equal the organization_did bound into the referenced challenge and project to organization_id.

version_id.description: The exact resolved DID version the control proof was made against. Pinning the version is what makes the receipt auditable later: without it, a receipt asserts control at an unknown point in the DID's history.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes are delegated to. MUST equal the value bound into the referenced challenge and signed over by control_proof; a mismatch means the proof was made for a different beneficiary and MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.

requested_scopes.description: MUST be identical to the set carried by the referenced challenge; a mismatch means the proof was made for different authority than is being claimed.

handle_attestation.description: Optional supporting attestation only. An organization handle or domain claim may improve discovery and display, but MUST NOT substitute for DID control or quorum proof: whoever operates a domain is not thereby the controller of the organization's DID. Named attestation rather than evidence because it carries exactly one material family (common-fields.md R6).

subject_id.description: Stable organization did_core_id the handle is claimed for. MUST equal organization_id; the attestation proof's DID URL is independently projected to its issuer did_core_id.

status.description: The issuer's assertion at signing time. It is a floor, not a guarantee: a receiver MUST still consult the issuer's current revocation state before relying on the handle for display, because a self-asserted active is exactly what a revoked attestation would also carry.

OrganizationRegistrationResponseBody.description: Result of every organization registration command and of the read surface. Identity, DID, generation and version are read from the signed registration_receipt. created is true exactly on a call that opened a new generation.

created.description: True exactly when this call opened a new generation: the first registration, a re-registration after revoke, or an ensure that changed local_admin_subject or the scope set. False for a byte-identical ensure retry that matches the consumed challenge's canonical_request_digest and stored outcome, and for every read, refresh and revoke. Reusing the challenge with a different digest is an error, not created=false.

OrganizationRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed record that this deployment accepted an external Organization DID binding. receipt_claims is exactly the object formed by removing registration_receipt_id and proof from the receipt; registration_receipt_id is ak:organization_registration_receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims))>. proof.payload_digest hashes the complete receipt after registration_receipt_id is inserted and proof is removed, so neither digest is self-referential. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.organization_registration_receipt_proof.v1 binding object. The receipt proves acceptance of one generation of one local binding and nothing else: it is not a Realm capability, not membership, not a governance-Station designation, and not a service delegation.

registration_receipt_id.description: ak:organization_registration_receipt: plus lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted)).

organization_did.description: Published Organization DID whose pinned version and control proof were accepted for this receipt. Consumers MUST independently validate it and require project(organization_did)=organization_id.

registration_generation.description: Monotonic generation of the binding for this stable organization did_core_id, starting at 1. A same-core did refresh does not create a different organization identity; terminal registration states remain per generation.

control_proof_kind.description: Mirrors OrganizationControlProof.proof_kind so a later auditor can tell which commitment control_key_digest is over without re-fetching the original request.

control_key_digest.description: Under resolved_verification_method, the digest of the active control/update public key at version_id. Under governance_quorum, the digest of the canonical governance key set head that satisfied the threshold. It is never a next-key commitment and never private material.

status.description: Closed lifecycle. active: control evidence is current. stale: the pinned version no longer reflects current control (controller rotation) or the evidence has aged out; low-risk reads may continue but high-risk paths MUST fail closed until a successful refresh. revoked: terminal for this generation, whether withdrawn locally, atomically superseded by a new generation, or forced by deactivation of the external DID. A signed historical receipt can retain status=active as an immutable audit artifact, but it authorizes only while its generation is the registry current generation and that registry state is active.

expires_at.description: After this instant the binding MUST be treated as stale regardless of stored status. A receipt without a bounded life would let a single first-time proof authorise an organization relationship indefinitely.

proof.description: payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with proof omitted)). detached_jws signs canonical_json({context:'ak.organization_registration_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, issuer_id, registration_receipt_id, organization_id, organization_did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); created_at MUST equal issued_at. Consumers validate the registered organization's organization_did and project it to organization_id, then independently obtain the issuer service's verified resolution, require its service_did to project to issuer_id, and verify verification_method as a signing-time assertionMethod.

OrganizationRegistrationRefreshRequestBo.description: Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt. Scopes are not re-negotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control the moment the organization rotates its controller.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID at the refreshed version. MUST project to organization_id before the refreshed proof is accepted.

OrganizationRegistrationRevokeRequestBod.description: Withdraw the local binding. This is a local act with local effect only: it does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history, which this deployment does not control.

reason_code.description: Closed reason set. superseded: replaced by a new binding for the same organization. withdrawn: the deployment or the organization ended the relationship.

OrganizationRegistrationScope.description: Closed set of local administrative scopes a registration may delegate. organization_profile_manage covers this deployment's local organization profile and display; organization_realm_endorse permits issuing ak.realm.organization statements on the organization's behalf; organization_service_delegate permits declaring organization-to-service delegations locally. The set is closed because an open scope vocabulary would let a deployment mint authority the organization never consented to. Holding a scope is a permission to act later, not an action: registration by itself creates no Realm, membership, governance-Station authority, capability or service delegation.

ProjectionAssignedToRelation.description: Read-model edge backing a Strand assigned_to Relation. relation_id is needed by clients to tombstone the assignment; actor_id mirrors the Relation to_ref.

stage.description: Business-progression stage from the domain current state; null or absent when the object has never been written by ak.<kind>.stage.set. Orthogonal to the physical lifecycle in state (common-fields.md 5.3).

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition; MUST NOT be present without stage (common-fields.md 5.3.1).

kind.description: Space kind such as `board`, `list`, `folder`, or a profile-registered kind.

stage.description: Business-progression stage from the domain current state; null or absent when the object has never been written by ak.<kind>.stage.set. Orthogonal to the physical lifecycle in state (common-fields.md 5.3).

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition; MUST NOT be present without stage (common-fields.md 5.3.1).

summary.description: Derived display summary from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.summary; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

board_space_id.description: Derived board Space id from strand_position; not canonical Strand object state.

list_space_id.description: Derived list Space id from strand_position; not canonical Strand object state.

rank.description: Derived rank within list_space_id from strand_position.

assigned_actor_ids.description: Derived current full ActorIds from visible active Relation(relation_kind=assigned_to, from_ref=strand_id), preserving Station identity. Empty or absent means the Strand is unassigned for this projection caller. This is read-model state, not canonical Strand object metadata.

assigned_to_relations.description: Read-only active assigned_to Relation edges backing assigned_actor_ids. Clients use relation_id to tombstone assignments.

is_default.description: DERIVED, not independent storage: true iff strand_id == the parent Realm projection's default_strand_id (the authoritative pointer written by ak.realm.set_default_strand). The projector computes this from Realm.default_strand_id; a stale/dangling pointer never resolves to is_default=true because the reducer rejects set_default_strand against a non-existent Strand. Clients identify the Realm's default discussion Strand deterministically from this flag (or equivalently from Realm.default_strand_id) and MUST NOT infer the default from any Strand-reuses-Realm-token or other implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: W3C DID Core 1.0, DID document core properties
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: A raw DID document is emitted and resolved verbatim, so its property names belong to the DID Core lexicon; identity-did.md forbids re-spelling them as snake_case.
A DID document service entry keeps the DID Core lexicon for every member it declares, including the Arkret-defined serviceKind extension property that sits beside serviceEndpoint.
A verification method is resolved and verified verbatim from the DID document, so publicKeyMultibase keeps the DID Core spelling.

did.description: Complete service DID. It MUST equal inception_operation.state.id and the adapter projection MUST equal the resulting service_id.

idempotency_key.description: Bounded opaque caller-chosen correlation string used only to relate audit records for one ensure attempt. It is deliberately outside the ak: typed-ID namespace and MUST NOT be parsed by the typed-ID parser or treated as an object identity. Registration identity is the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) key that Provider persistence enforces with UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base_url), and the single idempotency authority for this operation is the operation registry's idempotency_mechanism=object_id; this field never establishes a second one.

public_base_url.description: Canonical service base URL: lower-case scheme and host, no query or fragment, normalized path, and exactly one trailing slash. Production deployments MUST use https; explicit development deployments MAY use http.

ServiceRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed stable service-registration receipt. registration_receipt_id is ak:service_registration_receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims))>. service_id is the projected did_core_id and did is the verified DID. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.service_registration_receipt_proof.v1 binding object; consumers verify the provider through its own resolution evidence.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the active control/update public key at version_id; this is not the next-key commitment or private recovery material.

proof.description: payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with proof omitted)). detached_jws signs canonical_json({context:'ak.service_registration_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, provider_id, registration_receipt_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); created_at MUST equal issued_at. Consumers resolve the provider did, require project(did)=provider_id, and verify verification_method as a signing-time assertionMethod of that did.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: W3C Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0, proofs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The proof is verified byte-for-byte against the external DID log, so every member keeps the Data Integrity spelling.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: did:webvh v1.0, the DID log file
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: A DID log entry must round-trip byte-for-byte with the external log, so versionId and versionTime keep the did:webvh spelling.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: did:webvh v1.0, did:webvh DID method parameters
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The parameters object is hashed and verified as part of the external DID log entry, so scid, method, updateKeys and nextKeyHashes are mirrored verbatim.

updateKeys.description: Exactly one active service-controlled update key. On a rotation entry it MUST open the previous entry's sole nextKeyHashes commitment; spent keys MUST NOT be reused.

nextKeyHashes.description: Exactly one sha2-256 multihash/Base58BTC commitment to a next update key generated and durably held by the service. Missing or mismatched commitments fail closed as service_prerotation_invalid.

SessionGrantCredentialClass.description: Closed credential class. recovery_session is a <=15 minute, non-refreshable, DPoP-bound candidate-device grant restricted to the exact recovery operation set; recovery completion issues a distinct standard grant.

SessionGrantDeviceBinding.description: Authorization state committed into a standard device grant. An Account Authority MUST populate it verbatim from the Station TCB current-device decision, which is the only source of the origin-derived authorization Event and generation; it MUST NOT be taken from client input, a local cache or a private lookup. Stations compare it with the current active device generation on admission.

model_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic generation. It MUST NOT equal or be derived from a DID versionId.

proof_jwt.description: Frozen initial holder proof authenticated by the Agent request digest. HTTP DPoP is fresh per attempt and must bind the same public JWK thumbprint, not necessarily identical JWT bytes. First validation checks both proofs; completed exact ledger replay reuses validated body proof while revalidating fresh HTTP DPoP. See key-management section 3.6.1.

SessionGrantIntrospectGrant.description: Non-secret grant metadata returned to the validating Station. Never includes the grant JWT, refresh token, or session private key.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service this grant is valid for.

session_public_key.description: Session signing key (JWK) for RFC 9421 PoP verification on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.2). Server-to-server only.

cnf_jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256 thumbprint of the holder (DPoP) key the grant is bound to (cnf.jkt); the Station uses it to verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3). Server-to-server only.

holder_binding.description: Required closed accepted human-device, recovery candidate-device, or Agent-runtime holder binding.

device_binding.description: Exact origin-derived device authorization preimage taken from the revocation gate's allow receipt. Required only for standard human_device grants and forbidden for recovery candidate-device and Agent grants.

scope_details.description: Exact immutable Agent scope_details from this credential's issuer-ledger claims, returned only over authenticated introspection. Required for Agent runtime grants and forbidden for human and recovery grants; preserves resource, constraint and participation ceilings without client claim parsing. This ceiling is not a current content authorization source. Literal capability_grant_refs may be empty for legitimate membership, Direct or Sidecar reading. All actual profile/current/endpoint gates are revalidated at use.

capability_grant_refs.description: Literal grants actually used at issuance only. An empty array is valid for registered non-grant read authority and MUST NOT be interpreted as no reading eligibility or replaced by synthetic grants.

active.description: Whether the grant is currently valid for the requested audience. READ-ONLY: introspection never consumes the grant.

proof_required.description: Whether an additional S2S holder proof is required to confirm the grant active for this introspection request. Default Station grant+DPoP validation uses the request DPoP instead of this field.

one_time_use_consumed.description: Always false: introspection is read-only and never consumes single-use state (rotation is the refresh endpoint's job).

SessionGrantIntrospectRequestBody.description: Server-to-server session-grant introspection request. Exactly one of id / grant_jwt identifies the grant.

id.description: Grant id. Mutually exclusive with grant_jwt.

grant_jwt.description: The signed grant JWT to introspect. Mutually exclusive with id.

audience_id.description: Stable service did_core_id the caller is validating the grant for; a mismatch yields status audience_mismatch.

proof.description: Optional S2S holder confirmation signed by the session key bound into the grant. Stations validating /_arkret/self/* grant+DPoP requests do not require a client-carried introspection proof; they verify the request DPoP locally against the returned cnf_jkt.

proof_jwt.description: JWS over ak.session_grant.introspection_proof.v1 claims (session_grant_id, grant_jwt_digest, audience, challenge, issued_at, expires_at).

account_id.description: Exact protocol account bound to this grant. Both components are signed; clients and resource services MUST NOT reconstruct either component from local state.

session_grant.description: Short-lived bearer/session grant bound to the requested principal, device and audience.

session_grant_id.description: Stable id of the issued or rotated session grant. Returned for every grant so the client can reference, refresh, introspect or revoke this exact grant without re-parsing the opaque session_grant.

session_public_key.description: JWK of the holder/session key the grant is bound to (the device holder key). The client needs this to perform RFC 9421 PoP and to derive the DPoP cnf.jkt for /_arkret/self/* requests (api-conventions.md §3.2 / §3.3); returning it avoids a mandatory introspect round-trip before the first self-path request.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Station or resource service the grant is valid for. MUST equal the grant's bound audience.

previous_session_grant_id.description: Present only on refresh. The predecessor grant atomically superseded by this successor.

AcceptedDevicePossessionProof.description: Accepted-device Ed25519 possession proof shared by human SessionGrant issue and refresh. The signature covers utf8('ak.session_grant_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of this complete object with signature omitted. It is not a server challenge: freshness comes from the <=300 second signed window, the one-time account handoff or predecessor grant, the issuer request identity, and issuer-ledger exact replay. The origin Station MUST verify this proof with the durable current accepted-device key in the same linearization that evaluates current authorization.

account_handoff_grant_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the exact opaque DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant presented in Authorization; the credential itself MUST NOT enter the proof or logs.

account_id.description: Exact account whose accepted device signs this proof. The verification method controller is projected only to account_id.principal_id; the accepted AccountHandoff or predecessor grant independently binds account_id.station_id.

holder_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the DPoP holder key for the handoff or predecessor SessionGrant.

session_intent_digest.description: Digest of the complete canonical immutable issue or refresh intent.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the accepted device key; its fragment MUST identify device_id and its bare did MUST project to account_id.principal_id.

signature.description: 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature encoded as canonical unpadded base64url.

AgentSessionRefreshProof.description: Current Agent runtime-key proof for SessionGrant rotation. It is a distinct branch from accepted human-device PoP and carries no client-generated challenge or polymorphic proof_kind.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

grant_jwt.description: Near-expiry human DPoP-bound SessionGrant presented as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof.

audience_id.description: If present, MUST equal the predecessor grant audience.

AgentSessionGrantRefreshRequestBody.description: Agent rotation binds the predecessor grant's agent_id, accepted agent_key_authorization_ref and proof.verification_method. Agent MLS endpoints have no device_id; a refresh carrying one is invalid. Rotation preserves the predecessor action/resource/constraint ceiling and accepts no requested_scope or agent_scope_request. Current authority is revalidated; scope additions or narrower recovery use a fresh AgentSessionGrantRequestBody with a new signed intent.

grant_jwt.description: Near-expiry Agent DPoP-bound SessionGrant presented as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof.

audience_id.description: If present, MUST equal the predecessor grant audience.

SessionGrantRefreshRequestBody.description: Closed human-versus-Agent SessionGrant rotation union. Neither branch accepts a client-generated challenge or a generic proof_kind enum.

HumanSessionGrantRequestBody.description: Returning-human issuance from an already bound account. Authorization is the DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant plus matching per-request DPoP; the body deliberately carries neither a second holder signature nor requested_scope.

RecoverySessionGrantRequestBody.description: Fresh-device existing-principal recovery issuance. Authorization is the Bound AccountHandoff plus matching per-request DPoP. The Account Authority binds this request to its account/principal mapping and does not consume the handoff on success.

AgentSessionGrantRequestBody.description: Agent runtime session issuance is bound to principal_id (agent_id), proof.verification_method and the current accepted agent_key_authorization_ref. This closed branch MUST NOT carry a device_id or derive one from the Agent key.

requested_scope.description: This issuance request action/operation ceiling is distinct from the immutable provision requested_scope. Content additions require fresh issue intent and current legitimate resource authority within provision/key ceilings; refresh cannot add scope.

agent_key_authorization_ref.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Event ref of the accepted
`ak.agent.key.authorize` that authorized the runtime key. REQUIRED when
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST be omitted for human session grants.

agent_scope_request.description: Narrowing-only Agent Auth overlay. Content issuance requires a non-empty verified Realm or Strand selector and intersects each action/resource with its complete registered authority path: literal grant, ordinary membership/history reading, Direct participant authority or dedicated Sidecar reading. Service scopes confer no content authority. Realm selection does not bypass Circle/Sidecar profile gates; exact Sidecar/endpoint binding is derived from accepted facts. Typed constraints and action-time current gates remain independent. No literal read grant is required for legitimate profile reading. track_names materializes only as allowed_tracks.

approval_evidence_refs.description: Optional narrowing pins to accepted controller-authored ak.capability.grant Events actually used for this exact Agent content session. Sorted by canonical EventId UTF-8 bytes and covered by request_canonical_digest. Each referenced grant must still be current, bind the exact controller/Agent/action/resource and satisfy every existing authority gate. An opaque approval_request_id is not evidence and MUST NOT appear here. No approval-only authority or normal-refresh scope expansion is introduced.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Optional only for the agent_key_proof branch. A runtime includes this controller-signed private disclosure when the Account Authority does not yet hold verifier-private ceiling evidence established by pairing or an authenticated private evidence transfer. If absent, the authority MUST resolve an already verified disclosure keyed by the same agent_id, DID commitment digest, verifier and audience; a service-local Agent row alone is insufficient.

dpop_binding_proof.description: `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DPoP proof JWT for the holder key that the issued session grant will bind to. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the Account Authority verifies the proof and materializes the resulting JWK thumbprint into the issued grant's `cnf.jkt` / session_public_key binding.

challenge.description: Runtime-generated canonical unpadded Base64URL challenge with at least 128 bits of cryptographic randomness. Frozen for exact issuance retry; not a pairing handle or a server-issued challenge.

audience_id.description: Verified target resource service identity; independent of HTTP Host and transport issuer routing.

verification_method.description: `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DID URL of the runtime signing key. REQUIRED when `proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the verifier MUST parse and adapter-validate its canonical bare did component, require project(did)=principal_id, and then validate the referenced key at the accepted method-history position. A did_core_id MUST NOT be used as a DID URL prefix or concatenated with a fragment. Projection mismatch returns `verification_method_principal_mismatch`. MUST be omitted for human proof kinds.

signature.description: Canonical unpadded Base64URL raw Ed25519 signature over RFC 8785 JCS of the entire proof with signature omitted; no Event JWS wrapper or extra prefix.

proof.description: Closed initial Agent proof. Require 0 < expires_at-issued_at <= 300 seconds, issued_at <= now+30 seconds, and now < expires_at for first validation. No additional nonce. Exact completed issuer-ledger replay reuses durable one-shot verification, with fresh matching-holder HTTP DPoP.

SessionGrantRequestBody.description: Closed returning-human, Agent runtime or fresh-device recovery issuance union. OIDC authorization codes are consumed only by account_handoff_request_body and never by this operation.

SignalSubmitResponseBody.description: Result of transient Signal admission. accepted=true means the service placed the encrypted envelope on the short-lived rail; it creates no Event, RealmCommit, authority-stream position or durable delivery receipt.

envelope_digest.description: Digest of the admitted complete encrypted envelope, used only for short-lived replay suppression and local correlation.

dispatched_recipient_count.description: Optional implementation hint for fanout recipients queued locally.

status.description: Retained on purpose: DeviceMessagesSendResponseBody dispatches this item by its position in the delivered map, and the status member keeps a detached item self-describing against DeviceMessageUnknownEntry. It is a positional discriminator, not a success-only outcome constant.

Retained on purpose: DeviceMessagesSendResponseBody dispatches this item by its position in the unknown_devices map, and the status member keeps a detached item self-describing against DeviceMessageDeliveredEntry. It is a positional discriminator, not a success-only outcome constant.

SignedSessionGrantClaims.description: Canonical signed claims carried by an ak.session.grant JWT. Except for the fixed kind and derived jti, the closed issuance preimage fields are copied from these claims. credential_class and holder_binding are signed and jointly determine the authorization profile; recovery_session is never refreshable or upgradable and recovery completion issues a distinct standard credential. Verifiers MUST RFC 8785-canonicalize the complete claim-derived preimage, recompute SHA-256, prepend the active sha256 suite wire code, derive ak:session_grant:<44-char-token>, and require byte equality with jti. Changing either binding therefore changes the ID.

issuance_nonce.description: Canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of the issuer-generated 256-bit issuance nonce. Exact replay reuses the same nonce, issuance preimage, grant ID and JWT.

account_id.description: Exact AccountId bound into this signed grant and its derived session_grant_id.

session_public_key.description: A supported public JWK serialized as its exact RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 string. Producers MUST parse and canonicalize input before signing; consumers MUST reject strings whose parsed JWK re-serialization is not byte-identical. Private JWK members are forbidden.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service. HTTP origins are bound separately by DPoP htu and MUST NOT be used as the SessionGrant audience.

SessionGrantReplayExpiredProblemExtensio.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details extension members for session_grant_replay_expired. The named issuer-ledger record remains authoritative and no replacement grant is created under the same request identity.

state.description: Retained on purpose: this is an RFC 9457 Problem Details extension member on the failure path and names the issuer-ledger state that caused the rejection, so the problem document stays self-describing next to SessionGrantReplayTerminalProblemExtensions. It is not a success-only outcome constant.

SessionGrantReplayTerminalProblemExtensi.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details extension members for session_grant_replay_terminal. The state is an exact durable issuer-ledger terminal state and no replacement grant is created under the same request identity.

EventDisclosure.description: Caller-scoped marker stating that canonical Event bytes are withheld. It carries no Event identity, reason, digest, preview or reducer input.

CommittedEventView.description: Caller-scoped, non-durable read representation pairing one RealmCommit with either the exact producer-signed Event or a minimal withheld marker. It has no independent identity, signature or persistence semantics and is never reducer input.

PublicRealmMetadata.description: Closed public metadata deliberately published by a Realm. It grants no membership, join, history, capability or current-authority status.

contract.description: Encrypted-only broadcast signal envelope. Exact product payload type and target are inside encrypted_payload. This object is never a durable Event and never advances RealmCommit coverage or reducer state.

sender_device_id.description: Closed sender discriminator: required exactly for an ordinary account-device sender and absent exactly for an Agent sender. null and sentinels are forbidden. Absence only selects the candidate Agent branch; source and recipient still verify accepted Agent classification and current runtime authority.

parent_realm_authority_commit_id.description: Required exactly for Circle Signal: independent exact accepted parent Realm stream cut for membership and capability. Enters envelope proof digest and pre-encryption AAD; never inferred from another stream position or wall clock.

expires_at.description: Semantic validation requires sent_at < expires_at and a class-specific TTL no greater than 120s for setup, 60s for moderation, and 30s for session.

encrypted_payload.description: AEAD ciphertext. The AAD is the JCS bytes of the closed pre-encryption header projected from the envelope top level, this object's scheme/key_ref/purpose/aead_profile/epoch/nonce and the verified group state (zh/sync/signal.md section 1); it is rebuilt by the recipient and never carried as an aad_digest. Exact payload kind, product target, and sender sequence exist only in plaintext after recipient decryption. The scheme names the construction, never the algorithm: aead_profile carries the algorithm and MUST equal the active MLS ciphersuite the group at key_ref.group_state_ref actually negotiated (zh/conformance/encoding.md section 10.1), so key_ref carries no algorithm mirror. Activating a further ciphersuite therefore reaches Signal with no wire change.

group_state_ref.description: Accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit for the scope's MLS group, or an equivalent group state proof hash. It is what fixes which ciphersuite aead_profile must equal.

purpose.description: AEAD purpose for this domain. It is a nonce-derivation and AAD input, so it keeps a Signal nonce from colliding with a content-encryption nonce under the same key and epoch.

aead_profile.description: canonical_id of an active row of artifacts/registry/mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. It MUST equal the ciphersuite the group at key_ref.group_state_ref actually negotiated; a reserved suite, an unregistered suite, or a mismatch MUST fail closed.

signal_proof.description: Detached sender proof over canonical_json({context:'ak.signal_proof.v1', envelope_digest, sender_actor_id, sender_device_id?, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). sender_device_id exists only for the ordinary branch and is omitted for Agent. envelope_digest hashes the complete SignalEnvelope with proof removed. The transcript member created_at is injected from the outer sent_at (x-arkret-binding-field-sources) and is not a wire member of this proof. Source and recipient authenticate current endpoint authority and verify this producer signature. Peer destination validates closed proof/transcript structure and recomputed digest, not the producer signature or remote authority; recipient must independently authenticate before display or effects (zh/sync/signal.md section 3).

verification_method.description: The DID URL bare DID component MUST project through its registered adapter to the signing principal component of sender_actor_id (account_id.principal_id for account). Ordinary requires fragment == sender_device_id. Agent requires the complete method byte-identical to the current accepted Agent signing-key binding and forbids sender_device_id. Constructing a method by appending to did_core_id is forbidden. The projection does not establish Station, Agent classification, or authority. Source and recipient independently bind current exact endpoint authority; destination validates projection and transcript structure but does not query remote authority or verify the producer signature as a relay prerequisite.

contract.description: Closed decrypted plaintext payload profile for transient Message generation previews carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1. It is not a durable Event or Content Block.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous sequence within (sender_actor_id, sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref), including the complete ActorId. It is independent of the per-stream seq and participates in generic Signal replay handling.

message_id.description: Predeclared final Message identity, derived by retyping the complete 33-octet token of the planned ak.message.create Event.event_id.

preview_text.description: Authoritative limit is 16 KiB of valid UTF-8, enforced after decryption by a byte validator. maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. LF, CR and TAB are allowed; other C0 controls and DEL are forbidden.

contract.description: Closed decrypted Signal plaintext payload profile for ak.presence, carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session. Presence is never a durable Event; the exact kind, actor, state and activity time MUST stay inside the ciphertext. Realm scope and sender identity come from the enclosing signed envelope and are not duplicated here; receivers MUST require actor_id == envelope sender_actor_id. See zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md section 3.3 and zh/sync/signal.md section 1.1.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_actor_id, sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref), including the complete ActorId. Multi-device presence accepts arbitrary forward gaps and only considers signals that advance the Actor/device/scope high-water.

actor_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the actor whose presence this is. MUST equal the enclosing envelope sender_actor_id.

state.description: Closed v1 presence state set. Unknown values MUST be dropped or rejected as schema_violation; receivers MUST NOT map them onto an approximate state. Invisibility is not a state value: it is expressed by ak.presence.visibility=nobody.

status_message.description: Optional NFC status text, at most 256 Unicode code points. U+0009 and U+000A are the only permitted control characters; all other C0/C1 controls are rejected. NFC normalization is enforced after decryption by the receiver.

last_active_at.description: Optional and omitted by default. Either an RFC 3339 UTC instant or a Unix-epoch-aligned ISO 8601 <start>/<end> interval bucket. The bucket duration MUST be at least PT60S and MUST match the Realm policy granularity; that bound and the epoch alignment cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced by the receiver, which MUST fail closed on malformed values.

ttl_ms.description: Plaintext presence lifetime. It MUST NOT widen the outer Signal TTL, whose session-class ceiling is 30 seconds (zh/sync/signal.md section 2); receivers treat the effective lifetime as the minimum of this value and the envelope expires_at.

contract.description: Bounded single-hop peer relay request for encrypted SignalEnvelope values. The request is short-lived, best-effort, non-idempotent, and never creates durable Event, RealmCommit, checkpoint, receipt, or delivery state.

realm_id.description: The only Realm represented by this request. Every signals[].realm_id and signals[].scope_ref.realm_id MUST equal this value.

signals.description: Original producer-signed encrypted envelopes. The source and destination services MUST NOT alter, re-sign, decrypt, or re-encrypt an item.

contract.description: One frame emitted by ak.self.signal.stream.subscribe.v1. Signal data is encrypted-only and ephemeral. Control frames never create a cursor, replay position, delivery receipt, or durable acceptance.

delivery_authority.description: Own-Station current admission for only the exact envelope in this authenticated stream frame. Bound to the receiving account and live connection generation; never a transferable or reusable current grant. The client independently binds key and exact authorization_ref to its verified MLS leaf.

product_authority.description: Own-Station complete authority-qualified Typing and MessageStream evidence for this exact envelope, maximum 32768 canonical JSON bytes. Original basis and sent_at equal the envelope. Historical and current grants are independently complete for all three registered product actions, including negative constraints. Absence disables these product projections without disabling authenticated decryption of other profiles.

historical_product_policies.description: Complete applicable access/moderation policies at this cut, including parent Realm and Circle restrictions; no narrower allow overrides a parent denial.

current_product_policies.description: Complete applicable access/moderation policies at this cut, including parent Realm and Circle restrictions; no narrower allow overrides a parent denial.

agent_product_authority.description: Accepted exact controller and live owned-Agent join source, ordinary controller authority, historical/current public management bounds and the accepted signing key ceiling projected into this Realm. Private participation preferences remain producer intent gates.

contract.description: Closed decrypted Signal plaintext payload profile for ak.typing, carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session. The target Strand and the exact kind MUST stay inside the ciphertext and MUST NOT be exposed to Station transport or sync surfaces. Realm scope and sender identity come from the enclosing signed envelope and are not duplicated here. See zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md section 3.5 and zh/sync/signal.md section 1.1.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_actor_id, sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref), including the complete ActorId. Receivers apply the high-water rule only after proof, scope, RealmCommit/MLS basis, AAD and plaintext validation; arbitrary forward gaps are accepted and repeats or rollback are stale.

strand_id.description: Target Strand. It MUST lie inside the Realm/Circle security scope named by the signed outer scope_ref.

typing.description: True while the sender is composing; senders SHOULD emit at most one update every 3 seconds and MUST send typing=false when composition stops.

ttl_ms.description: Optional plaintext indicator lifetime. It MUST NOT widen the outer Signal TTL, whose session-class ceiling is 30 seconds (zh/sync/signal.md section 2); clients clear the indicator once it expires.

contract.description: Closed own-Station signing-key results for one current invocation or one exact authority-committed historical Event. Historical coordinates come only from a verified committed_event_view delivered by account subscribe or per-stream scan. Receiver is the authenticated recipient Station, never a caller-selected remote service. No portable evidence or reusable current grant.

signing_account_actor_id.description: Complete account ActorId of the exact verified signer, preserving its Station for either an ordinary device or Agent.

public_key_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes; this is public material, not reusable current authorization.
Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes; this is public material, not reusable current authorization.

authorization_ref.description: Exact accepted authorization Event for this key. For a historical query this is independent of the selector's target committed_event_ref: the two MAY be equal but equality is not required.

revision.description: Verified current revision of the authorization stream at resolution. The revision belongs to authorization_ref.stream_ref, is not older than authorization_ref.stream_position, and is never inferred from arrival order, a cursor or a current projection.

query_signing_key.description: Shared resolved key shape for existing current Agent and historical Agent/Account Device roles; each enclosing selector/outcome retains its own authority and source rules. Only new ordinary Human and accepted Applet-managed Device historical delivery uses original governance Commit-bound immutable facts. Independent original authorization coordinates/revision/PCR governance generation remain mandatory where the enclosing role requires them; no current fallback or new target source.

committed_event_ref.description: Exact committed coordinate of the historical Event being verified. Its stream_ref.realm_id MUST equal the enclosing request realm_id. It is constructed only from a verified committed_event_view, never from a bare Event, current projection, cursor, time or cache order.

Exact committed coordinate of the historical Event being verified. Its stream_ref.realm_id MUST equal the enclosing request realm_id. It is constructed only from a verified committed_event_view, never from a bare Event, current projection, cursor, time or cache order.

accepted_at.description: Effective time of the referenced historical authorization fact; not an Event arrival or permanent-history acceptance timestamp.
Effective time of the referenced historical authorization fact; not an Event arrival or permanent-history acceptance timestamp.

public_key_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes; this is public material, not reusable current authorization.

current_device_signing_key.description: Own-Station verified ordinary human current key, valid only for the frozen invocation and exact enclosing selector. No PCR coordinates or portable evidence are disclosed.

committed_event_ref.description: Exact committed coordinate of the historical Event being verified. Its stream_ref.realm_id MUST equal the enclosing request realm_id. It is constructed only from a verified committed_event_view, never from a bare Event, current projection, cursor, time or cache order.

public_key_base64url.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes; this is public material, not reusable current authorization.

accepted_at.description: Original target governance Commit committed_at; frozen before signing its fact digest.

contract.description: A Space is a structural grouping object inside a Realm. Boards, lists, swimlanes, calendar buckets, document outline groups, etc. are all Spaces. Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership/policy/E2EE group; its metadata may be placed in an existing Realm/Circle effective scope via scope_circle_id.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

realm_id.description: Immutable Realm of this Space and of resources structurally placed under it. Producers explicitly bind new resources to this Realm; scope and capability checks remain independent.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional Circle scope for this Space object's own metadata and scoped structural relation facts. Space still does not own a security boundary; it only places its metadata into an existing Circle scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope.

child_scope_policy.description: Reducer-enforced placement/encryption policy for child resources created in or moved into this Space.

parent_space_id.description: Optional canonical parent, which MUST belong to the same actual realm_id. Cross-Realm parent is forbidden, including at creation, with failed_precondition / space_realm_mismatch. Missing or unverifiable parent evidence fails closed with space_parent_unreadable before disclosing Realm differences.

kind.description: Space kind. v1 standard kinds include 'space', 'project', 'folder', 'board', 'list', and 'topic'. Profile-defined kinds (e.g., 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket', 'page_group') MAY be added via Realm schema/profile and MUST be registered. Unknown kind MUST schema_violation.

rank.description: Fractional-index rank within parent. See encoding.md §9.

schema_refs.description: Optional schema/profile references that further constrain this Space's contained Strand types, fields, or position invariants.

fields.description: Space kind-specific fields. For kind=list, wip_limit is an integer 1..100000 and wip_limit_enforcement is required with enum warn|reject|require_review whenever wip_limit is present; these are the sole write-policy source and MUST NOT be read from View. For kind=board, view_id may identify a default presentation. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key (rank is a top-level Space field; see relation.md §2 for the symmetric Relation constraint and forbidden-wire-fields.json `fields.rank/space_payload`).

encrypted_metadata.description: Whole MLS metadata envelope; decrypted plaintext is #/$defs/space_metadata. Mutually exclusive with plaintext title, summary, labels and avatar_blob_ref. Public fields in this branch contain only registered structural policy. No plaintext title mirror on current/read/snapshot/replica, search or notification surfaces.

state.description: Space lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. State transitions are reducer-enforced per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.space.archive MUST come from state=='active' (else failed_precondition reason=space_not_active); ak.space.restore MUST come from state=='archived' (else failed_precondition reason=space_not_archived); ak.space.tombstone MUST come from {'active','archived'} AND must have no live dependents (failed_precondition reason=space_already_terminal for terminal source, space_has_live_dependents for live refs). Same-state self-transitions (archive on archived, etc.) MUST fail; clients re-archive by restore-then-archive. Tombstoned is irreversible (MUST NOT be restored). The transition timestamp lives on the writing Event and on state_changed_at.

state_changed_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent state transition. Required when state != 'active'.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle (see models/circle.md) that defines this Strand's effective scope. When set, ALL Strand tracks (synthesis, discussion, etc.) share that Circle's membership, history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and MLS activation state. When unset, the Strand lives in Realm-default scope. The producer signs the corresponding Event.scope_ref; the receiver verifies that the Circle belongs to this Realm and that the derived scope equals Event.scope_ref before materializing the object's immutable effective_scope. Rebinding scope_circle_id is forbidden by default (failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden). For 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion' scenarios use two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation (circle.md §7.2).

schema_refs.description: Optional authoritative schema set for profile-defined metadata.fields subtrees. Unlike Morph, a plain Strand carries no profile subtree and omits this field entirely; when present it MUST list at least one profile schema id. The container self-schema ak.schema.strand.v1 MUST NOT appear here. Every listed profile schema and its metadata.fields namespace MUST co-occur in both directions: the ref without the subtree and the subtree without the ref are both schema_violation, evaluated on the post-patch object by the registered event-kind payload class and reducer. Current-v1 has no per-Event requirements.schema[] carrier.

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped five-bit Agent ceiling. When present every bit is explicit and may only tighten the enclosing Circle or Realm ceiling.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a strand_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata once the enclosing scope has an accepted ak.mls.genesis; before that activation the scope is plaintext and after it the plaintext branch MUST be rejected with mls_activation_irreversible.

topic.description: Optional single Topic classification for a stably bound Direct Conversation Chat. Root same-Realm Topic Space(kind=topic) only. Whole set/unset via ak.strand.update requires the exact current digest CAS. Omitted means unclassified; no Board position or canonical Relation mirrors this field.

content.description: Strand description body. This is base Strand content and is independent of the synthesis and discussion tracks.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Strand description ContentBlock. Exclusive with content.

tracks.description: Active Strand collaboration surfaces, keyed by an active name in track-name-registry.json. The synthesis entry may carry its own content / encrypted_content; the discussion entry configures a Message timeline and may not carry either field. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE: the entire Strand shares a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md). At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/strand-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; propertyNames fails closed for names outside the registry-backed TrackName enum.

state.description: Strand lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.strand.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=strand_not_active); ak.strand.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else strand_not_archived); terminal state is reached only via a ak.redaction event targeting the strand (MUST come from {'active','archived'} else strand_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.strand.archive / ak.strand.restore / ak.redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Optional Strand business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle): archive does NOT change stage; stage=done does NOT auto-archive. ak.strand.create MAY omit stage; when present it must be one of the protocol-level enum values and has no protocol-level default. The only wire path that mutates stage after creation is the dedicated ak.strand.stage.set event; ak.strand.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the ak.strand.stage.set event log is the audit source, and human-readable explanations belong in a Message on the discussion track that references the event. v1 has no per-Realm workflow profile carrier: the core reducer hard invariants (terminal state freeze, non-active reject) defined in models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 are the complete transition rule, and receivers MUST NOT narrow admission from Realm-private configuration (§5.3.4). See models/strand-and-message.md §3.2 for full semantics and models/common-fields.md §5.3 for the protocol-level enum / bucket mapping.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST NOT appear without stage. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ak.strand.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions (stage value unchanged) MUST NOT update this field.

strand_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Strand metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Strand metadata fields. Reducer-owned fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

calendar.description: Calendar event schedule subtree activated by ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 in Strand.schema_refs. See zh/models/calendar-event.md.

track_name.description: Closed active TrackName set mirrored from registry/track-name-registry.json. The artifact gate requires exact set equality; an unregistered map key is a schema violation.

strand_track.description: Strand track entry. The stable name is the map key in Strand.tracks. The synthesis entry may carry its own narrative content / encrypted_content in addition to config; the discussion entry is config-only because its authored content is carried by Message objects. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The whole Strand has a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. To represent 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion', create two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation per models/circle.md §7.2.

enabled.description: Whether this track currently accepts new writes (synthesis edits / discussion messages). Default true when omitted. Setting enabled=false MUST cause the reducer to reject subsequent writes to this track with 'track_disabled' until enabled is set back to true. Disabling a track does NOT delete prior history; it freezes new writes only. UI MAY hide a disabled track or render it read-only.

metadata.description: Track-local UI metadata only. The reducer NEVER interprets its keys; it does not create membership, history visibility, access, or E2EE scope. Access-like keys are rejected at the wire layer to prevent a pseudo-access surface (tracks have no independent access — see models/strand-and-message.md §4.4).

content.description: Track-owned ContentBlock. In the active v1 registry only tracks.synthesis may carry this field; tracks.discussion content is carried by Message objects.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted counterpart of track-owned content. In the active v1 registry only tracks.synthesis may carry this field.

contract.description: Shared coarse-grained JSON Schema shapes for Arkret v1 string profiles. Custom format validation and UTF-8 octet limits are normative and require the SDK validator; JSON Schema patterns do not implement PRECIS, IDNA, or UTS #39.

human_identifier_localpart.description: Canonical RFC 8265 UsernameCaseMapped-derived localpart. Maximum 128 Unicode code points in prepared form.

agent_slug.description: Canonical controller-scoped Agent Agent selector slug. Maximum 64 Unicode code points in prepared form.

canonical_domain.description: Lowercase UTS #46 Nontransitional A-label domain with at least two labels; normative validation includes STD3, Bidi, Joiner, hyphen, DNS-length, and round-trip checks.

canonical_handle.description: Canonical <prepared-localpart>:<lowercase-A-label-domain> handle or realm alias. The prepared localpart maximum is 128 Unicode code points; the domain maximum is 253 ASCII octets.

acct_uri.description: RFC 7565 acct URI with UTF-8 localpart octets percent-encoded using uppercase hex when required, canonical A-label host, and no port.

single_line_display_text.description: NFC multilingual single-line display text; mixed scripts, emoji, and symbols are allowed.

display_text_128.description: Single-line display text limited to 128 Unicode code points in prepared form.

display_text_256.description: Single-line display text limited to 256 Unicode code points in prepared form.

display_text_512.description: Single-line display text limited to 512 Unicode code points in prepared form.

short_text.description: NFC multilingual short text. LF is allowed; CR, other C0/C1 controls, BOM, and bidi embedding/override controls are rejected.

audit_reason_text.description: Human-readable audit reason limited to 1024 Unicode code points. It is explanatory text only and never a machine-readable reason code or authorization source.

content_text.description: NFC multilingual content text; rendering contexts must escape markup and apply bidi isolation.

non_typed_identifier_floor.description: Lexical floor of every identifier value category that does NOT own the ak: namespace (opaque_correlation, document_local_symbol, external_system_identifier, registry_catalog_symbol, unregistered_object_identifier); see common-fields.md 2.1. The negative lookahead IS the floor: it mechanically proves the value cannot be an ak: typed id, which maxLength alone can never prove, while admitting every other value the field already accepted. It deliberately constrains nothing else - the per-field convergence direction (a registered typed kind, or a tighter opaque profile) is decided per object family, so a pattern-only floor composes with whatever profile the field already carries instead of pre-empting it.

contract.description: Defs-only shared time primitives. Arkret-owned absolute instants use the single fixed UTC millisecond spelling YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ. Duration, external-protocol NumericDate, local wall time, and algorithm-internal epoch values are different semantic types and do not reference this definition.

timestamp.description: Canonical Arkret-owned absolute instant. UTC Z form with exactly three millisecond digits. Whole seconds MUST use .000Z; offsets, missing/finer fractions, lowercase separators, leap seconds, and invalid Gregorian calendar dates are forbidden. Shape validation by this pattern is supplemented by semantic date validation.

local_date.description: Proleptic Gregorian calendar date with no time, offset, or zone. Not an absolute instant: it resolves to an instant only through an explicitly carried IANA time zone plus TZDB version. Shape validation by this pattern is supplemented by semantic date validation.

local_date_time.description: RFC 8984 LocalDateTime narrowed to whole seconds. Wall-clock time with no offset, no Z suffix, no bracketed zone, and no fractional seconds; it resolves to an instant only through an explicitly carried IANA time zone plus TZDB version. Producers MUST NOT spell whole seconds as .0 or .000. Shape validation by this pattern is supplemented by semantic date validation.

contract.description: Standalone entry point for the closed ServiceDescribe transport_bindings union. Operation coverage is supplied only by registered operation bundles.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

visibility.description: View sharing visibility. Private views are actor-private account data; shared views are canonical Realm objects.

state.description: Required View lifecycle state. Shared View removal is an ak.view.update patch to tombstoned; tombstoned is terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the ak.view.update that transitioned state to tombstoned. Actor-supplied values MUST be rejected.

stream_heads.description: Authority stream heads from which state_digest was derived.

collection_grouping.description: Grouping / lane / time-bucket / matrix configuration; mirrors models/views.md §3.3. Conditional required-ness is enforced per mode.

item_order_by.description: Stable item ordering; mirrors models/views.md §3.2. Drag-ordered collections SHOULD sort by rank.

display_fields.description: Display columns (dot path + format); see models/views.md §3.2.

view_definition.description: The author-editable View definition: the members zh/models/views.md section 2.1 calls the View own canonical state, and nothing else. It is deliberately NOT view.schema.json. A materialized object schema used as an authoring input hands the author id, the create metadata, the most-recent-update metadata and the lifecycle output fields, which is exactly the ownership the reducer-managed path registry exists to protect on the patch surface; ak.view.reconcile reached that surface through its definition member and lost it. Identity, Realm, schema and creation metadata are retained from the target pre-state, update provenance is derived from this Event, and lifecycle state is never author-requested: removal is an ak.view.update patch (section 3.1) and reconcile MUST NOT tombstone or resurrect.

contract.description: Closed side-effecting audited-read commands. Reuses producer Event, signer evidence, RealmCommit and Watch current types. Authority-commit-log section 5.3 is the normative transaction/replay boundary.

watch_audit_read_request_body.description: One caller-signed audit Event plus its required approval evidence. Realm, Strand and watcher derive only from the signed Event, not duplicated selector fields. Its actor is the authenticated complete effective Account. The Event ID is a single-use read fence and full canonical request bytes identify exact replay; purpose and accessed_at do not authorize access.

producer_device_evidence.description: Fresh complete Account Device signer evidence for the signed audit Event, following authority-forward original authorization and per-attempt live gates. Exact command replay uses the durable original read binding before checking new evidence freshness; current disclosure and final delivery still apply.

peer_watch_audit_read_request_body.description: S2S first-admission broker to the nonce-verified current governor for one audited read. Same signed audit_submission as self; no bearer, DPoP or session grant is forwarded. Source-Service-ID binds the complete auditor Account Station and actual producer evidence. Proof presence, fresh device/Agent and controller checks follow authority_forward; both proof alternatives together are forbidden. Audit command actual producer is a Device or Agent runtime Account, never a substituted Service producer; exactly one fresh evidence alternative is required.

watch_audit_read_response_body.description: One original audit Commit and the frozen exact target Watch observation from the same governance transaction. current.stream_head equals the audit Commit coordinate, and generation, Realm and target derive from the request. No roster or extra head. Exact replay returns the original frozen value only under current disclosure/delivery checks; it never reads a newer value using the old audit. An audit records authorized governing read, not guaranteed client receipt.

contract.description: Decoded protected header and claims for challenge_dpop_session_v1. This is an Arkret application-level proof carried in an authenticate frame, not an RFC 9449 DPoP HTTP header. Its wss htu and ARKRET-WEBSOCKET-AUTH htm are accepted only in this proof context.
Closed union of all application frames for ak.profile.binding.websocket.v1. Duplicate JSON member names and the advertised UTF-8 byte limit are enforced before JSON Schema validation.

error_code.description: Must resolve to a registered code in error-code-registry.json codes[]. This closed transport error body is not the HTTP RFC 9457 Problem Details.

info.summary: Canonical Arkret service surface and admin/account bindings
info.description:
Authoritative source for operations and error codes is the contract registry at
`artifacts/registry/contract-registry.json` and the error registry at
`artifacts/registry/error-code-registry.json`.

This OpenAPI document is the canonical HTTP binding for registered service
operations.

**Typed vs generic schema policy**:

Stable core operations on the events / account / snapshot / identity / authz data path
carry **typed request/response schemas** so SDK generators can derive
operation-specific required fields directly from OpenAPI without consulting
prose. The typed surface currently covers `ak.self.events.{command.submit, resource.get,
read.scan, stream.subscribe}`, `ak.peer.events.{command.submit, read.scan}`, `ak.self.account.{read.viewer, stream.subscribe, command.update_profile}`, `ak.gate.account.{command.register, command.revoke_session}`, `ak.self.realm_state_snapshot.read.manifest_head.v1`,
`ak.root.identity.{read.resolve, document.resource.get, receipts.read.list, command.submit_did_operation}`, `ak.self.authz.{read.check,
grants.query.effective}`, and the ServiceDescribe envelope. The corresponding
Event-submit schemas are the endpoint-specific `self_submit_request_body` / `self_submit_response_body`
and `peer_submit_request_body` / `peer_submit_response_body` definitions in authority-commit-operations.schema.json; Event reads use `EventView`,
`stream_scan_request_body` / `stream_scan_response_body` (authority-commit-operations.schema.json),
