`RealmCommit`, `SignalSubmitResponseBody`,
`IdentityResolveResponseBody` / `IdentityDocumentView`, `DidOperationSubmitRequestBody` / `DidOperationSubmitResponseBody`,
`AuthorizationCheckRequestBody` / `AuthorizationCheckResponseBody`, `EffectiveGrantSnapshot`,
`ServiceDescribe`.

Security-sensitive extension operations such as MLS KeyPackage lifecycle,
Directory, Applet, MIMI, Push, Blob and media bindings also carry typed DTO
schemas. The current v1 OpenAPI document does not publish generic
`OperationRequest` / `OperationResponseBody` components. Any future profile that
reintroduces a generic binding must declare `generic_binding` in the
operation registry, carry an explicit profile gate and migration plan, and
must not claim generated-SDK completeness until a typed DTO lands.

Default authentication: bearer token plus HTTP Message Signature for
service-to-service calls (see `zh/sync/service-http-binding.md` §2.2). Public
metadata endpoints explicitly noted as `public_metadata` may be unauthenticated;
every other path requires at least one of the declared securitySchemes.

Path namespace convention: every path is absolute under the negative-space
root `/_arkret/` and carries NO version segment. The first segment after
`/_arkret/` is a trust-surface classifier encoding the caller-to-server trust
relationship and attack-surface class. The "trust circle" terminology is an
explanatory metaphor, not an authorization result. The current classifiers are: `self` (the authenticated session of the caller), `gate` (authentication entry), `root` (identity /
DID trust root; not root/admin privilege), `find` (directory discovery), `peer` (federation server-to-server
wire; reserved namespace branch), `open` (external protocol interop or out-of-band handoff, e.g. MIMI / invite locators; not public/no-auth access),
`edge` (push / bridge gateways).
Reading the URL therefore reveals the attack surface, but each operation still
enforces its own session, capability, DID proof, Realm policy, visibility,
service-delegation, rate-limit, and disclosure checks. The pre-auth capability
advertisement lives at the root meta position `/_arkret/describe`.

Versioning is NOT expressed in the path. The protocol version is negotiated via
`*.describe` / exact `supported_operation_bundles` (and optionally a `Arkret-Protocol-Version`
request/response header); schema ids carry their own `.v1` suffix. The
corresponding `operation-registry.json` `http` field records the full absolute
path verbatim.

bearerAuth.description:
Non-SessionGrant bearer used only by operations whose own contract
explicitly registers a bearer credential (primarily deployment S2S).
An ak.session.grant MUST NOT use this scheme, even when a DPoP proof
header is also present. S2S federation / inter-service calls MUST
also satisfy the httpMessageSignature + sourceServiceId +
destinationServiceId AND group (see service-http-binding.md §2.2).

sessionGrantAuth.description:
The only current-v1 Authorization scheme for ak.session.grant. It MUST
co-occur with dpopProof; Bearer plus DPoP is invalid under RFC 9449
section 7.1 and MUST fail closed.

accountHandoffAuth.description:
Opaque, short-lived account-authentication handoff returned by
ak.gate.account.exchange.create_handoff.v1. The Authorization scheme on
the wire is `DPoP`, not `Bearer`, and the credential MUST co-occur with
dpopProof whose key thumbprint matches the handoff's cnf.jkt. It is not
ak.session.grant and is accepted only by the three operations listed in
AccountHandoffResponseBody.allowed_operations.

httpMessageSignature.name: Signature
httpMessageSignature.description:
RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature applied with the source service DID's
verification key. When present, the request MUST also include
Source-Service-ID / Destination-Service-ID / Content-Digest (the
latter only for requests with a body); federation event push also MUST
include Source-Trust-Domain / Destination-Trust-Domain. These are modeled as separate apiKey
securitySchemes and MUST appear in the same security AND group as
httpMessageSignature when required by the operation.

sourceServiceId.name: Source-Service-ID
sourceServiceId.description:
Required companion to httpMessageSignature. Identifies the originating
service DID and MUST be covered by the signature transcript. SDK
generators MUST treat the absence of this header on S2S endpoints as
an authentication failure, not a 400.

destinationServiceId.name: Destination-Service-ID
destinationServiceId.description:
Required companion to httpMessageSignature. Identifies the intended
recipient service DID (anti-misdirection / cross-tenant guard). MUST
match the deployment-resolved service identity; mismatched requests
MUST be rejected before reaching reducer / business logic.

sourceTrustDomain.name: Source-Trust-Domain
sourceTrustDomain.description:
Federation companion to httpMessageSignature. Identifies the source
deployment trust domain (`ak:trust_domain:<scope>`) and MUST be covered
by the signature transcript.

destinationTrustDomain.name: Destination-Trust-Domain
destinationTrustDomain.description:
Federation companion to httpMessageSignature. Identifies the receiver
deployment trust domain (`ak:trust_domain:<scope>`) and MUST match the
destination service / Realm receive context before reducer logic runs.

contentDigest.name: Content-Digest
contentDigest.description:
Required companion to httpMessageSignature on requests that carry a
body (POST / PUT / DELETE-with-body). RFC 9530 digest header bound
into the signature transcript so that body tampering is detected
before any verification of structured fields. Omitted on body-less
requests (GET / HEAD / DELETE-without-body).

presignParam.name: presign
presignParam.description:
Single-blob, short-TTL pre-signed authorization (ak.self.blob.command.presign.v1).
Carries a server-signed envelope binding blob_ref / TTL / scope /
issuance nonce. The nonce is an envelope/audit/revocation key, not a
one-use media-load replay guard unless a single-use profile is declared.
Permitted ONLY on ak.self.blob.resource.get.v1 and ak.self.blob.resource.head.v1, and MUST NOT
co-occur with bearerAuth — implementations enforce mutual exclusion.
See media-and-blob.md §5.4 and server-threat-model.md §2.1 #21 for the
carve-out's normative constraints.

dpopProof.name: DPoP
dpopProof.description:
RFC 9449 DPoP proof JWS signed by the holder key. On account-handoff
issuance it establishes the cnf.jkt binding and omits ath because no
credential exists yet. On account-handoff or session-grant use, it
carries htm / htu for the exact endpoint and ath for the presented
credential. SessionGrant issue uses AccountHandoff or Agent body proof;
refresh, revoke, logout and resource presentation use
Authorization: DPoP <ak.session.grant> plus this header. See
account-lifecycle §2.1.2 / §4.1 and
device-lifecycle §3.3.

mutualTls.description:
Reserved for deployment-controlled internal channels (sovereign /
enclave operator surfaces). Not used by any registered v1 operation
in this OpenAPI document; deployments MAY require it on product-local
management APIs outside the Arkret protocol namespace.

realmActorControlMetadata.name: Arkret-Realm-Actor-Control
realmActorControlMetadata.description: base64url_no_pad(JCS) metadata defined by realm-actor.schema.json control_http_metadata; current subject method signature required.

managedDeviceMetadata.name: Arkret-Managed-Device
managedDeviceMetadata.description: Covered RFC9421 canonical closed managed Account/Device/authorization/Applet/scope metadata; only registered operations, never a SessionGrant.

XArkretWaitFor.description: Causal checkpoint token the caller is waiting on.

MethodNotAllowed.description: Pre-dispatch router failure for a registered path with an unsupported method; Problem code method_not_allowed (HTTP 405). No operation is entered.

NotFound.description: Not found or not visible; an unregistered /_arkret/* path instead uses the pre-dispatch unrecognized_endpoint response (HTTP 404).

UnrecognizedEndpoint.description: Pre-dispatch router failure for an unregistered /_arkret/* path; Problem code unrecognized_endpoint (HTTP 404). No operation is entered.

PsiBatchUnavailable.description: The match batch is unknown, belongs to another device, or expired (error code psi_batch_unavailable). Causes are intentionally merged and use the match-phase Class B shape. The pinned epoch is retained for the full advertised completion TTL.

PsiDuplicateConflict.description: The device-scoped batch_id was reused with different canonical blind or match bytes (error code duplicate_conflict). No evaluation is performed.

PsiPolicyDenied.description: Requester/batch-level policy denial (error code policy_denied). This is a PSI Class B failure and uses the request phase's exact body bucket and advertised delay distribution; it contains no per-target information.

PsiQuotaExhausted.description: PSI window quota exhausted (error code psi_quota_exhausted), returned only at first blind admission. The body has the exact blind-phase Content-Length bucket and advertised delay distribution. Retry-After is decimal seconds until quota-window roll, rounded up to a 300-second multiple with minimum 300. See discovery-directory.md §6.4.

Retry-After.description: Decimal seconds, a positive multiple of 300.

Opens a streaming subscription scoped by `realms[]` / `actors[]`. Returns
events from `after=<cursor>` (exclusive) forward. Subscribe naturally
moves only toward newer events; there is no `before` / `order`
parameter.

With `catchup=true` and `after=<cursor>` the server first replays
the bounded catch-up range from that cursor up to the current checkpoint,
then emits `catchup_complete` per Realm and continues with live frames.
This is not a request for all historical events; full history is read
through `QUERY /_arkret/self/events` pagination / range queries.

post.summary: Resolve verified MLS epoch-0 public group-state bytes.
post.description:
Resolves one accepted `ak.mls.genesis` Event and returns its exact RFC
9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes. Before disclosure the
provider verifies every request selector against the Event, recomputes
SHA-256 over both raw byte strings, compares explicit digests and the
hashes embedded in the content-addressed refs, and validates
GroupInfo/tree consistency. The response is all-or-nothing and never
contains private tree material, MLS secrets or inferred leaf DTOs. A forwarded self member read includes caller_actor_id and target Commit/epoch; governance independently verifies current and target-cut member/history authority and the calling Station replication right at the target accepted Commit cut. It does not gate a later-joined member Station at the Genesis Commit position. An absent caller_actor_id is only the original Station replication read; source Station replication right is checked at the Genesis Commit position.

200.description: Digest-verified public MLS GroupInfo and ratchet tree bytes.

before deletion or acknowledgement. Idempotency-Key is
covered by the HTTP Message Signature; an identical retry returns the
original byte-identical signed acceptance and a different body is
duplicate_conflict with zero writes.

post.summary: Relay encrypted Signal Extension envelopes to one peer.
post.description:
Optional `ak.profile.signal_peer_relay.v1` single-hop, best-effort
relay. The request contains 1..128 original producer-signed encrypted
SignalEnvelope values for one Realm and has a 1 MiB canonical body
ceiling. The peer signature expires-created window is at most 5
seconds. Idempotency-Key is forbidden; uncertain outcomes are dropped.
This operation never creates a durable Event, receipt, RealmCommit, producer_revision
or Realm checkpoint update, and the destination cannot forward a received
envelope to a third peer.
Source authenticates current exact-account device authority and the
producer signature. Destination authenticates peer source/body, sender
routing, proof transcript/digest and outer scope/MLS admission without
a remote device directory or producer signature verification. Recipient
independently verifies device trust, producer signature and MLS/AEAD
binding before display or effects. A schema-valid invalid item is
silently dropped; malformed request schema is rejected as a whole.

204.description:
Opaque request takeover result. It does not reveal whether any
Realm, scope, sender, binding or recipient exists and does not
promise delivery. Successful responses have no body.

403.description:
Unified minimally disclosing outer peer authentication, trust-domain,
destination-endpoint or request-policy rejection. Per-envelope
sender/member binding and delivery-policy failures are silently
dropped behind the opaque 200 outcome.

verification and secret distribution use the to-device queue instead.

signal, or TTL/body above the hard ceiling.

403.description:

declared signal_class in the signed scope.

post.summary: Exchange Arkret capability proof for a backend media token.
post.description:
Media service token exchange operation defined by
zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3. Issues a short-lived
(TTL ≤ 600s, SHOULD ≤ 300s) backend_token + participant_binding for
joining a focus declared in `ak.realm.media_service.foci[]`.

Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus /
arkret_native); only `backend_token` shape is type-specific and opaque
to the protocol layer (parsed by backend SDK only).

Token issuer MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs;
clients MUST reject otherwise (`token_issuer_unauthorised`). Issuer
MUST validate: device proof, `ak.call.join` capability, focus_id
membership in current `foci[]`, session_focus persistence, MLS
MLS media key-access-revision freshness, and `media_service_decryption_allowed`
pre-conditions (§10.5.1).

200.description: Token exchange accepted; backend_token + participant_binding returned.

403.description:
`capability_denied` — actor lacks `ak.call.join` or
requested `desired_media` exceeds granted sub-capabilities; or
`token_issuer_unauthorised` when the issuing DID is not registered
in `ak.realm.media_service.service_id`.

409.description:
`focus_mismatch` — requested `focus_id` differs from the
already-committed `ak.call.state.session_focus`; clients MUST
re-target the established focus rather than retrying; or
`mls_governance_binding_stale` — the current MLS group has not yet
covered its current key_access_revision; or
`media_plaintext_service_not_authorised` for SFUs negotiating
decryption role without `plaintext_visible_services` entry.

422.description:
`unknown_focus_type` — `focus_id` resolves to a `foci[]` entry
whose `type` is unsupported by this token issuer; or
`media_service_foci_required` when `ak.realm.media_service` does
not declare explicit media foci.

get.summary: Holder-bound one-shot read of the current account projection.
get.description:
Returns the authenticated principal's account projection: principal_id,
lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed
handle-claim evidence or refs. This endpoint is distinct from
ak.self.account.read.describe.v1, which describes service capabilities.

account authority pair. profile, when present, is the current accepted Actor
Profile from that pair's single lifetime-local PCR lineage; the service MUST
NOT merge or select state from another Station carrying the same core DID.

The response MUST NOT use an unsigned bare handle as authoritative
identity. When present, primary_handle_claim is a complete
ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 object; otherwise clients use
primary_handle_claim_ref and handle_claim_digests to refresh their
local claim cache.

See client-sync sections 2.3, 3.1 and 13.

post.summary: Update the authenticated principal's Actor Profile projection.
post.description:
Carries exactly one holder-signed profile_event EventAdmissionSubmission.
event.realm_id is the account-local PCR Realm selector, and
accepted-profile presence is evaluated only in that PCR lineage. With no
accepted Actor Profile there the Event is ak.profile.create and its
materialized actor_profile ID is derived from the Event ID; payload.object
omits id. With an accepted Profile there the Event is ak.profile.update,
payload.target_ref equals that create-derived ID, and patch paths are limited
to display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>.

Both branches use the authenticated session's account authority pair and local
PCR as event.realm_id and realm scope, bind event.actor_id to the session
principal, and use direct holder proof. On create payload.object.principal_id
equals that principal; on update the accepted target Profile's materialized
principal_id equals it. Event preconditions are empty; update concurrency
uses only optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service submits the exact Event
through ordinary admission without authoring, rebuilding, co-signing, choosing
an ID, or adding a concurrency guard. Until accepted RealmCommit coverage is available
it returns revision_unavailable; exact retry then returns the stored outcome
without a second account-aggregate delta. No Directory or account-data Event is
synthesized.

MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, wait-for barrier state,
or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from
cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

get.summary: List the holder's contact projection.
get.description:
An accepted row also carries the closed next_prepare_input cursor. Its
contact_round_id, version and predecessor_event_ref are copied verbatim into the
prepare phase of /_arkret/self/contacts/scope-update or
/_arkret/self/contacts/tombstone; version is the version the next Event
carries and predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head. Every
other contact_state omits the cursor, and the projected request,
response and tombstone event refs are never authoritative lineage heads.
A pending_incoming row carries request_event_ref and the exact optional
request_message from the verified request. The client submits peer and
request_event_ref to respond/reject prepare; its own Station loads the
durable receipt and checks the current slot. The client checks the
prepared intent and signs, without resolving the request Event or
verifying foreign receipts. Glare is never pending_incoming.
Current Contact authority uses fixed first identity and source-certified scope
instances. No cross-round continuity export is defined.

post.description:
Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff. The new
device submits a canonical new_device_public_key and a client_nonce and MUST
NOT submit a challenge proof; the Station forwards the exact DTO through
the registered internal operation, and the Account Authority
mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id and 8-character Crockford-style
40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code and
stores the sole bounded-TTL account-less record in state staged, with a code that
is unique across the whole live pending set, so a user-driven refresh is
just another call here and always mints a distinct request and code.
The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no
challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving
device only over the out-of-band channel, and MUST NOT be mirrored here.
The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an
authenticated device authorizes it. Each call mints a fresh request, so
blind retries duplicate staged records.

post.summary: Resolve a device-pairing short-link token.
post.description:
Resolves an out-of-band device-pairing token into a
DevicePairingBootstrap. The token is sent in the JSON body; QR/link
handoff SHOULD carry it in the URL fragment so HTTP servers, proxies,
and Referer logs do not receive the token in path or query string.
The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: never the
challenge proof, never the target attestation, and never the hpke_key
and algorithms that attestation signs.
Only a record already finalized to ready_for_claim and not protected by
a pair_device admission fence can be resolved.
Unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a record that is not
ready_for_claim all return an indistinguishable not_found.

post.summary: Poll the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record.
post.description:
Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged
device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code
pair is the query credential and is sent in the JSON body, never in the
URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch are
indistinguishable (both not_found). Once an authenticated device has
authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus
required device_id and authorized_event_ref. authorized_event_ref is
the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check: the target device
MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical
device_signature, byte-identical key material and an expected
principal_id before assembling the identity locally. A valid credential
for an expired record reports state expired during a bounded cleanup
retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. A record that a
later successful finalize for the same AccountId superseded reports the
same expired for that retention period and is indistinguishable from a
naturally elapsed TTL. A private prepared or commit_recorded fence
returns not_found until completed; in_progress is not a public state.

200.description: Current authorization status for the staged pairing record.

post.summary: Exchange account authentication for a holder-bound onboarding handoff.
post.description:
Exchanges an OIDC authorization code at the issuer token endpoint and
returns an opaque short-lived account_handoff_grant. The handoff is not
ak.session.grant and has no refresh-token semantics. It can be used only
at the operations in allowed_operations.

For an unbound service account this operation atomically acquires or
renews the current holder's identity-creation lease. A different holder
receives identity_creation_busy while the lease is live. After expiry,
a newly authenticated holder for the same service account fences the old
lease and inherits any reserved DID-operation checkpoint. For a
bound account the response carries principal_id so the handoff can be
exchanged at /session-grants.

post.summary: Reserve a DID inception operation and issue a fresh root-control challenge.
post.description:
Validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id
and its canonical digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, and
issues a server-generated single-use challenge with a freshness window
no longer than 300 seconds. Challenge state is durable shared state and
binds the authenticated service account, handoff holder key, lease and
fence, principal, operation digest, audience, origin, trust domain,
purpose, and expiry.

Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge.
Reissuing with a new request_id invalidates any older unconsumed
challenge for the same lease/fence without changing the reserved DID
operation.

post.description:
Resolves the supplied already-published DID at the high freshness tier
(synchronous refresh or fail closed), derives did_version_id,
log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry,
and issues a server-generated single-use challenge with a freshness
window no longer than 300 seconds.

Caller-supplied DID history is never accepted. Deployments that do not
host the DID additionally require method-native witness or freshness
evidence, because co-locating the registry with the Station
does not extend that trust to third-party DIDs.

This operation reserves no principal and performs no PCR genesis; it
only proves current control of an existing DID. Repeating the same
request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge.

post.summary: Explicitly abandon a provisional identity whose PCR was never accepted.
post.description:
Consumes the abandonment challenge and performs the abandonment in one
transaction: record the orphan-anchor tombstone / audit reservation,
suppress the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every
holder-readable surface, and release the identity-creation lease. Any
step failing means zero writes.

If the PCR was accepted between challenge issuance and confirmation the
request fails with identity_creation_already_accepted and abandons
nothing: an established identity is removed through account deletion,
not through provisional-identity abandonment.

Replaying the same request_id returns the recorded terminal outcome and
never produces a second tombstone. The abandoned entry 0 remains a
permanently unusable orphan anchor that cannot be deactivated; whether
it is annotated on a discovery surface, when its handle and namespace
are released and how long the reservation is retained are deployment
governance.

than did and never accepts a bare handle. display_name is only a

In the account-first identity_creation branch, the client sends the
exact reserved unpublished DID operation. The Account Authority verifies
the current holder/lease/fence and a fresh proof signed by the
did:webvh entry-0 parameters.updateKeys[0] root, then submits the DID
operation internally and writes the service-account binding only after
accepted or byte-identical duplicate resolution. Identity root material
is never accepted. The operation is idempotent by account, principal_id,
and canonical operation digest.

Register MAY return signed handle-claim evidence or digest/ref in the
AccountRegisterResponseBody, but handle issuance, approval, assignment, re-signing,
and revocation remain issuer/coauth/deployment-governance strands.

post.summary: Account Authority hard logout.
post.description:
Ordinary hard logout at the Account Authority (account-lifecycle §4.1),
and the only client-visible logout endpoint. The Account Authority
validates the current ak.session.grant plus DPoP, terminates the
Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain (via
auth-sessions/logout when Auth-side is split out), then terminates or
durably schedules Principal-side local account/device session cleanup,
to-device drop, and push registration removal. Does not emit
ak.device.revoke, does not erase durable device authorization (re-login
restores the device), and does not create an AccountStatusRecord. Distinct
from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). A not_found
introspection result is an idempotent retry state only after the
Auth-side auth-sessions/logout sub-operation confirms completion; an
audience_mismatch remains an authentication failure and MUST NOT be
treated as already logged out.

post.summary: Record the authenticated holder's explicit account erasure request.
post.description:
The only client entry point for self-initiated account erasure
(zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1), accepted directly by
the Account Authority on the gate surface. The Account Authority
treats this as a high-risk action and requires fresh high-risk action
authentication (recent login, WebAuthn, recovery key or a deployment
equivalent), judged locally by the Account Authority — the only party
holding the relevant facts; a session that does not satisfy the
deployment policy is rejected with reauthentication_required.

Success is an acceptance confirmation only: the erasure intent is
durably recorded and the Account Authority continues its existing
erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord issuance flow within the same
service; there is no cross-service handoff. The response proves
neither record issuance nor physical completion; the current status is
observed through the existing account-status read surface and physical
completion only through the erasure receipt rail. When the deployment
grants a withdrawal window the outcome echoes withdrawal_window_ends_at
and the record is not signed before that time; once the record is
signed the request is irreversible and no withdrawal is possible.

Replaying the same request_id returns the recorded acceptance outcome;
the same request_id with different canonical bytes is
duplicate_conflict with zero writes; a different request_id while a
live unsigned-record intent exists is failed_precondition with
reason_code erasure_request_already_pending.

200.description: Erasure request accepted and the intent durably recorded.

x-arkret-auth.notes: The candidate device authenticates with `DPoP <account_handoff_grant>` plus matching DPoP for a bound pending account handoff. That handoff is the only source of the exact AccountId the body proof signs; the service MUST NOT read account membership from a request member or a server-side side channel.

post.summary: Bind a staged pairing record to an exact AccountId.
post.description:
The one authenticated step between the account-less stage and any
approval. The candidate holds the exact request id and pairing code, holds
the staged candidate key, and supplies the exact AccountId from its own
sender-constrained pending account handoff. It signs a target proof over
the complete transcript including that AccountId, and this call attaches
that public, signature-protected proof to the pending request.

The service recomputes the challenge transcript from its own durable
stage, verifies the target signature with the staged new_device_public_key,
and requires the signed account_id to equal the AccountId the handoff is
bound to. Only then does the record move from staged to ready_for_claim.
The transition is one-way, and authorized is unreachable without it.

Unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, an expired record and a record that is
no longer staged all return an indistinguishable not_found. Exact retry of
the same canonical intent returns the same outcome; the same request id
with different content conflicts.

A successful call also supersedes. In the same durable transaction it
moves every other unaccepted ready_for_claim record of that AccountId to
terminal expired, keeping the bounded tombstone that preserves exact
retry and blocks replay, so the account never holds two approvable
records at once. This is how v1 retires the code of an earlier pairing
attempt; there is no cancel operation. The key is the AccountId alone, so
a refreshed pairing page and a different new device retire the earlier
record identically and two devices cannot be added in parallel.
Supersession adds no request or response member, authors no Event, grants
nothing, never rewrites an outcome pair_device already accepted, and an
exact retry performs no second supersession.

200.description: Pending pairing record finalized and ready for claim.

x-arkret-auth.notes: The caller MUST be a current accepted, non-pending-revocation device of an exact AccountId. The pairing code is the whole input and MUST stay in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string, so it never reaches an access log or an analytics event.

post.summary: Claim one pending pairing request by its eight-character code.
post.description:
Lets an already authorized device find the exact pending pairing
request behind the code shown on a new device, so a desktop browser with
no camera can complete a join by typing eight characters.

A result is returned only when the code hits a unique unexpired
ready_for_claim unconsumed request whose signed account_id and gate
audience equal the caller account, and when proof, staged key, request id,
code and transcript digest all agree. Unknown, wrong, expired,
cross-account, not yet finalized and already consumed codes all return the
same not_found, so no error shape says whether a code exists or which
account it belongs to.

The response carries the bootstrap and the byte-equivalent target proof
needed for local verification, and no private key, session credential,
recovery material, or information about any other device of the account.
Claiming retrieves a request and grants nothing: an accepted device still
reviews it and signs ak.device.authorize. Calls are rate limited per
caller device, per AccountId and per service, and a request locks out
after its cumulative failure budget.

post.description: Agent provisioning. The controller first publishes a signed PCR-independent did:webvh entry 0. phase=prepare requires the authenticated controller account's controller_station_id, validates the pair against the current session, then verifies caller-supplied did and returns its exact accepted initial_resolution, controller PCR, delegation ref, scope digest and allocation without generating a DID/private key or choosing a PCR id. The controller freezes the PCR create with that commitment, derives principal_control_realm_id from its event_id and commits one controller-signed ak.agent.provision Event. Ordinary admission atomically projects provision/accountability/selector/realm-id-claim and returns awaiting_pcr_genesis. Separate PCR acceptance returns awaiting_did_binding; only the controller-signed continuous DID entry 1 carrying the exact create-locked binding exposes Agent/pairing/list/get and returns complete. requested_scope is an immutable ceiling, not a grant; the service creates no Agent DID/PCR/MLS private state.

post.description: Re-open pairing on any non-terminal agent with a fresh single-use pairing handle and the unchanged requested_scope_digest DID commitment. All previously issued handles stay permanently unresolvable. An Agent without an active accepted runtime-key authorization uses bootstrap; an Agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle active or paused) uses replacement while lifecycle intent, existing keys and grants stay untouched until one controller-signed authorization atomically supersedes the prior keys. Generic views expose the handle and active authorization set with independent readiness blockers and never expose runtime_state or backup readiness; that diagnostic is pairing-poll-local. Neither branch creates, revokes, or re-issues Realm grants. Pair commit does not depend on history-only backup availability; deactivated rejects.
